40ec187fa3c41791.title: Colloquium : A renormalisation group perspective on functional inequalities
40ec187fa3c41791.speaker: Thierry Bodineau
40ec187fa3c41791.abstract: In this talk, we will describe a multiscale analysis for decomposing high-dimensional measures into simpler structures. The strategy is based on the renormalization group method used in statistical physics to study the distribution of interacting particle systems. We will first apply this framework to Gibbs measures, showing how it can be used to derive functional inequalities. We will also discuss how this decomposition can be understood from the perspective of transport of measures, and survey other related developments, including numerical methods for sampling from high-dimensional probability distributions.

411ce0b01c5578b8.title: A Counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture in Dimension Three
411ce0b01c5578b8.speaker: Thomas Mordant
411ce0b01c5578b8.abstract:
Seed Seminar of Mathematics and Physics
AI and the Future of Mathematics and Physics
The Jacobian conjecture states that for any polynomial map from to itself, if it is everywhere a local diffeomorphism, then it admits a polynomial global inverse. In this talk, I will present the three-dimensional counterexample to this conjecture posted by L. Alpöge on and credited to Claude.
After stating the conjecture and the counterexample, I will explain the geometric interpretation of the counterexample which was posted by A. Jiang and credited to ChatGPT. Finally I will give some observations about the history of the conjecture and its significance.
We answer this problem coming from representation theory using topological tools. On the representation theory side we define extensions of Habiro type rings. On the topological side, we construct a universal Jones link invariant and a universal Alexander link invariant. Putting these together, our universal invariants of geometrical nature take values in the extended Habiro rings that we construct.
More information: https://seedseminar.pages.math.cnrs.fr/program/#november-4-2026

4201edc0ce8aedc6.speaker: Nicolas Guès
4201edc0ce8aedc6.abstract:
In a series of papers from the 2010s, Church, Ellenberg and Farb developed the notion of representation stability, aimed at understanding the asymptotic behavior of natural sequences of representations of the symmetric groups S_n, particularly those arising from homological invariants. Such phenomena typically occur for FI-modules, i.e., functors from FI (the category of finite sets and injections) to abelian groups.
In this talk, I will propose a homotopical refinement of representation stability: a derived version adapted to (co)FI-spaces. This viewpoint sheds light on how the phenomenon of representation stability can arise from the high (co)cartesianity of certain cubical diagrams. With this point of view, I will show how one can deduce polynomial growth results for the homotopy groups of ordered configuration spaces on closed manifolds, recover the best known bounds on their cohomology, and generalize stability results of Palmer concerning moduli spaces of submanifolds.

420f8bb1d8144cf4.title: Diffuse Interface Models and their Sharp Interface Limits
420f8bb1d8144cf4.speaker: Helmut Abels
420f8bb1d8144cf4.abstract:
CANCELED – For personal reasons, Helmut Abels has unfortunately been forced to cancel his seminar. – CANCELED
Speaker: Helmut Abels (Universität Regensburg)
Interfaces separating two or more species or components of a material are omnipresent in applications in the sciences. Nowadays there are two main classes of models to describe interfaces, both from a theoretical and practical point of view: In classical so-called « sharp interface models » the species or components under consideration fill disjoint domains that are separated by lower dimensional surfaces of a certain regularity. On the other hand in « diffuse interface models » a partial mixing of the species or components on a small length scale is taken into account, which leads to an interfacial layer of small but positive thickness. This has the advantage that the interfaces do not need to be resolved explicitly and singularities in the interfaces can be described consistently.
In the first part of the talk we will give an overview of some basic diffuse interface models with applications to material sciences. Moreover, we will discuss some analytic results on the relation between diffuse and sharp interface models, when the interfacial thickness of the diffuse interface tends to zero. The analysis is based on formally matched asymptotic expansions (in a rigorous manner) together with uniform estimates for the linearized operator. In this part we will focus on the Allen-Cahn equation as basic model.
In the second part we will discuss a Navier-Stokes/Allen-Cahn system, which describes the flow of two macroscopically immiscible viscous incompressible fluid, separated by a diffuse interface. We will present some recent results on novel higher-order estimates for the sharp interface limit of this system. With the aid of a suitable weight taking the distance to the interface and the interfacial thickness into account we obtain optimal regularity estimates, which are uniformy in the interfacial thickness. This enables to improve previous convergence results in two space dimensions significantly and extend results to three space dimensions. This is a joint-work with Mingwen Fei, Yadong Liu, and Maximilian Moser.

456ce1bf0416a7ce.title: The Diederich–Fornæss index and global regularity of the $\overline{\partial }$-Neumann prblem
456ce1bf0416a7ce.speaker: Bingyuan Liu
456ce1bf0416a7ce.speaker_affiliation: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
456ce1bf0416a7ce.abstract: Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^{n} $ be a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain. The $\overline{\partial }$-Neumann problem is Hodge theory with boundary on Ω. Its solution operator $N_{q}$ is globally regular, i.e. preserves $C^{\infty}(\Omega)$ , on strongly pseudoconvex domains (Kohn), but not on the worm domains (Christ). Since the 1990s it has been conjectured that global regularity follows when the Diederich–Fornæss index of $\Omega$ equals 1. This index is the supremum of $η \in]0,1]$ such that $-(-ρ )^{η}$ is plurisubharmonic near $b\Omega$ for some defining function ρ. I will present joint work with Emil Straube. Suppose that, for some $1\leq q_{0}\leq n-1$, the $q_{0}$-sums of the Levi eigenvalues are comparable, and the index is 1. Then $N_{q}$ and the Bergman projections $P_{q-1}$, for $q_{0}\leq q\leq n,$, are continuous in every Sobolev space $W^s(Ω)$. In particular, the conjecture holds in $C^2$, and there having index one is preserved under biholomorphisms. The key point is that index one gives a self-bounded gradient condition, which is weak pointwise but suffices in an integrated $L^2$ form.

4710e3f777ad09bb.speaker: Marius Goguet
4710e3f777ad09bb.abstract:
Categories are often seen as very abstract mathematical objects that are hard to grasp. However, in the case of module categories of finite dimensional algebras, we can understand and represent them in a very concrete way by drawing their Auslander-Reiten quiver.
The general strategy is to break down the category into appropriate building blocks: indecomposable objects, irreducible morphisms and almost split sequences. We will define all these notions and illustrate them on examples of algebras given by quivers with relations.

49b03c6a0f17eb48.title: Near-horizon Collisions at the Extreme: Naturalness and Observability of Critical Near-horizon Collisions around Near-extremal Black Holes
49b03c6a0f17eb48.speaker: Delilah Gates
49b03c6a0f17eb48.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
In principle, rapidly rotating black holes could naturally act as particle colliders because geodesics particles that collide can exhibit center-of-mass (CM) energies that diverges in the limit that the black hole approaches extremality and the collision radius approaches the horizon, provided that one particle has a critically tuned angular momentum. In this talk, I present work to understand the naturalness and observability of these critical-particle collisions around near-extremal BHs. I will highlight 1) the landscape of conditions under which these critical-particle collisions occur, 2) the CM energy achievable for critical-particle collision where one particle falls from in from infinity and the other particle is part of an accretion disk, and 3) the observability as measure by the escape probability and expected energy of emission born of a critical-particle collision.

4b4b6dae159dc939.title: Diameters and box spaces
4b4b6dae159dc939.speaker: Alain Valette
4b4b6dae159dc939.abstract:
Le séminaire d'algèbres d'opérateurs aura lieu à l'IHP le temps du trimestre "algèbres d'opérateurs : approximation, ridigité et dynamique"
Résumé : Consider a sequence $(X_k)_{k>0}$ of finite, connected, d-regular graphs with size going to infinity. It is known that, if $(X_k)_{k>0}$ is an expanding sequence, then the diameter of $X_k$ is exactly logarithmic in the number of vertices of $X_k$. On the opposite, for $0<\alpha \leq 1$, say that $(X_k)_{k>0}$ has property $D_\alpha$ if the diameter of $X_k$ grows at least like $|X_k|^\alpha$: this is a strong form of non-expansion. For a finitely generated, residually finite group $G$, let $(N_k)_{k>0}$ be a filtration of $G$. The box space associated with $(N_k)_{k>0}$ is the sequence of finite Cayley graphs $(Cay(G/N_k,S))_{k>0}$ where $S$ is a fixed finite generating set of $G$. It turns out that property $D_\alpha$ for a box space is related to interesting algebraic properties of $G$, and we will survey results by Breuillard-Tointon, Khukhro-Valette, and Guo-Tointon. Now, assuming that $G$ can be realized as a subgroup of $GL_n(A)$, where $A$ is a unital, commutative ring, we have filtrations given by congruence subgroups, giving rise to arithmetic box spaces. Sometimes the growth of the diameter is more constrained on arithmetic box spaces then on general box spaces, i.e. non-arithmeticity can be detected purely metrically. We will illustrate this with lamplighter groups $L_F:=F\wr\Z$, where $F$ is a finite abelian group. This is joint work with Etienne Grezet.

4c2bbaa6c0d111af.title: Doubling modulo odd integers
4c2bbaa6c0d111af.speaker: Jean-Paul Allouche
4c2bbaa6c0d111af.abstract:
Once upon a time, there was a mathematical journal which was "almost'' a journal in the
sense that one could find there either papers in final form, or reports of talks given at a local
(but well-known and welcoming international researchers) Seminar, or papers that were not
necessarily in final form and could even stay forever in an almost unfinished state. This journal
was the Séminaire de Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux, that became later a more
classical journal, the Journal de Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux.
Among the many papers that were not in a final form in the Séminaire (and that were
not necessarily followed by a "real paper'' appeared later elsewhere), one can find a quite
modest paper entitled "Suites infinies à répétitions bornées'' (in the 1983--1984 issue).
In that paper there was a short study of the number of cycles of a family of permutations
related to the Toeplitz transform of sequences.
Up to notation the number of cycles of the same family of permutations appeared in 2021 in
a paper by Y. Guo, G. Han, and W. Wu about "apwenian sequences''.
The formulas given in these two papers were distinct, though---of course---equivalent.
Thus it was tempting to prove directly their equality.
This possibly frivolous question lead to unexpected discoveries: the family of permutations
above or a variation of it are linked to numerous subjects, not only in mathematics (combinatorics
of words, dynamical systems, number theory, correcting algorithms), but also in card-shuffling,
juggling, change-ringing, poetry, and music composition.
The details can be found in a paper by J.-P. A., M. Stipulanti, and J.-Y. Yao, appeared in
The Mathematical Intelligencer in 2026.

4d7eec8a6e9177c1.title: Sur les points fixes des sous-groupes de Moy-Prasad dans les représentations admissibles irréductibles de groupes réductifs p-adiques (Travaux en cours avec Marie-France Vignéras et Rachel Ollivier)
4d7eec8a6e9177c1.speaker: Guy Henniart
4d7eec8a6e9177c1.abstract:
Soit p un nombre premier et F une extension finie de Q_p.
Soit G un groupe réductif connexe sur F, et C un corps algébriquement
clos. Dans une C-représentation admissible irréductible π du groupe
G(F), les points fixes par un sous-groupe ouvert K forment un C-espace
vectoriel de dimension finie d(K, π). Si π est de dimension infinie,
il est intéressant de savoir comment d(K, π) croît quand K devient de
plus en plus petit. Par exemple, on peut partir d’un sous-groupe de
Moy-Prasad G_x,r (pour x dans l’immeuble de G sur F et r un nombre
réel positif), et faire croître r. Grâce à des résultats de
Harish-Chandra (1978) et T.-C.Tsai (2025), nous prouvons que si la
caractéristique de C n'est pas p, alors pour tout entier n assez grand,
d(G_x,r+2n, π) a la forme P(p^n), où P est un polynôme à
coefficients rationnels, dépendant de x, r, et π. Nous soupçonnons
que cela reste vrai si C est de caractéristique p, mais seul le cas où
G est GL₂ et F=Q_p est connu. Pour G général, même le cas
particulier où π est la représentation de Steinberg de G(F) est
difficile. Cependant, nous obtenons un résultat asymptotique plus
faible, valable pour tout π. Au passage, nous examinons la condition
que G_x,r soit un pro-p groupe uniforme.

4da9456f5a8ed2e4.title: Plongements conformes de surfaces de Riemann
4da9456f5a8ed2e4.speaker: Alaa Mohamed BOUKHOLKHAL
4da9456f5a8ed2e4.abstract: Étant donnée une surface riemannienne, il n’est pas toujours possible de la plonger isométriquement dans une variété riemannienne donnée M, notamment en raison de contraintes telles que la courbure. Cependant, la situation devient beaucoup plus flexible si l’on cherche un plongement conforme. Dans cet exposé, on montre l’existence de plongements conformes dans le cas où M est une variété pseudo-riemannienne. De plus, on montre que l’inclusion de l’espace des immersions lisses et conformes dans l’espace des immersions induit une bijection entre les composantes connexes par arcs de ces deux espaces.

4dac8adbfe225827.title: Marco Plazzogna - Endogenous Dynamic Networks for Heteroscedastic Outcomes
4dac8adbfe225827.abstract:
Many economic and financial systems are naturally represented as networks: the outcome of one unit may depend on those of other units through relationships that evolve over time. A central difficulty is that these relationships need not be exogenous. The network itself may react to the same shocks that affect the variables of interest, creating an endogeneity problem that cannot be addressed by treating network weights as fixed or predetermined.
We study a dynamic spatial model in which the interaction network is time-varying and generated by an auxiliary formation process. Dependence between innovations driving network formation and the structural outcome shock is explicitly incorporated through a control-function approach.
The framework is further extended to allow for conditional heteroskedasticity. In particular, we distinguish between two potentially different dynamic networks: one governing the transmission of outcomes in the conditional mean, and another governing the propagation of past shocks in the conditional variance. This makes it possible to separate network effects on the level of the process from network effects on its risk and volatility.
The resulting model provides a framework for studying systems in which both interactions and uncertainty evolve endogenously over time.

4e5cf45a9394ddf3.title: Les relocalisations préférentielles améliorent la survie
4e5cf45a9394ddf3.speaker: Jean Bertoin
4e5cf45a9394ddf3.abstract:
Nous étudions une modification de l’évolution d’une chaîne de Markov sous-stochastique qui consiste en des relocalisations aléatoires en des états visités précédemment, et son impact sur la survie.
Le résultat central est que de telles relocalisations préférentielles augmentent le taux de persistance, c’est-à-dire que la probabilité de survie décroît plus lentement que pour la chaîne de référence dépourvue de relocalisations, et que cette amélioration est stricte sous des hypothèses très générales. Nous établissons des minorations explicites du rapport des taux de persistance lorsque la loi de relocalisation est fortement dispersée. L’analyse repose sur les propriétés ergodiques de chaînes dites à connexions complètes, ainsi que sur une approche de Feynman--Kac pour estimer la persistance.
Travail en collaboration avec Martin Minchev

4e8b508ceb426af1.title: [mini-cours] Combinatorics and Geometry: Crossing paths—in the age of AI. (Part 1)
4e8b508ceb426af1.speaker: János Pach
4e8b508ceb426af1.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
4e8b508ceb426af1.abstract:
Crossing numbers: Dead or alive. The crossing
number of a graph G, denoted by cr(G), is the smallest number of
edge crossings in any drawing of G in the plane. Clearly, cr(G)=0
if and only if G is planar. Garey and Johnson proved that
determining cr(G) is an NP-complete problem. Over the past forty
years, crossing numbers have proven to play a vital role in
various fields, including discrete and computational geometry,
number theory, and circuit layout (such as providing lower bounds
on the chip area required for a graph's physical layout). Yet,
many of the foundational questions that inspired research in this
area remain open, and new mysteries continue to emerge. Quo
vadis?

55607a7d512a37dc.title: Système d’Euler biparti pour les points de Drinfeld–Heegner
55607a7d512a37dc.speaker: Yichao Tian
55607a7d512a37dc.abstract:
Le système d’Euler biparti classique associé aux points
de Heegner a été introduit par Howard, basé sur des travaux pionniers
de Bertolini et Darmon. Il est un outil puissant pour l’étude de
l’arithmétique des courbes elliptiques sur le corps des nombres
rationnels.
Dans cet exposé, on expliquera un analogue de ce système d’Euler
biparti pour les points de Drinfeld–Heegner sur les courbes de
Laumon–Rapoport–Stuhler, qui sont des analogues des courbes de
Shimura sur un corps global de fonctions (i.e. le corps de fonctions
d’une courbe projective lisse sur un corps fini). Ces résultats
pourraient avoir des applications à l’étude des groupes de Selmer
des courbes elliptiques non isotriviales sur de tels corps. Comme un
ingrédient technique de la démonstration, on obtient également un
analogue du lemme d’Ihara classique pour les courbes de
Laumon–Rapoport–Stuhler.

55a678e9c2da4d53.title: The Simplicial Cylinder DG Ring
55a678e9c2da4d53.speaker: Amnon YEKUTIELI
55a678e9c2da4d53.speaker_affiliation: Ben Gurion University, Israel et Université Paris 7
55a678e9c2da4d53.abstract:
The Keller cylinder DG ring encodes homotopies between DG ring homomorphisms f_0, f_1 : A --> B.
Recently we discovered the higher cylinder DG rings Cyl_q(B), which assemble into the simplicial cylinder DG ring Cyl(B). For q=1 this recovers Keller's original construction.
The sets SHom_q(A,B) of DG ring homomorphisms A \to Cyl_q(B) form the simplicial Hom set SHom(A,B). Our main result is that when A is a semi-free DG ring, the simplicial set SHom(A,B) is a Kan complex.
We prove several results about the fundamental groupoid SHom_{\leq 1}(A,B), including invariance under quasi-isomorphism B' \to B, and that the automorphism groups are abelian. We also indicate some applications of this work, including to DG categories.
This talk will take place on Zoom only.

56258b78a2e0566c.title: A mathematical perspective on Transformers
56258b78a2e0566c.speaker: Borjan GESHKOVSKI
56258b78a2e0566c.abstract: Physics has long supplied mathematics with some of its central equations. I will argue that Transformers, the engine of large language models, are becoming a source of the same kind. Starting from raw code, under various scaling assumptions, one can interpret Transformers as an interacting particle system in continuous time; tools from PDE and kinetic theory then explain empirically observed phenomena such as representation collapse and “lost in the middle”. Unlike in physics, however, the laws here are designed rather than given, so mathematical understanding can be written back into the architecture. I will close with some thoughts on what this two-way exchange means for applied mathematics.
56258b78a2e0566c.organizer: G. Franz, L. Hauswirth, P. Laurain, R. Petrides, R. Souam

565a9a9df1453759.title: Singularities of the critical wave equation and the Keller-Segel system formed by the collision of collapsing solitons at a point
565a9a9df1453759.speaker: Charles Collot
565a9a9df1453759.abstract: Critical evolution PDEs may have solutions forming a singularity in finite time with anomalous self-similarity. There are now numerous examples where a soliton (here a stationary state or a traveling wave) collapses at a point due to its interactions with the remainder of the solution. Much less is known about singularities formed by several solitons collapsing simultaneously at a single point, especially in the non-radial case. The first example was constructed for the nonlinear Schrodinger equation by Martel-Raphael [Ann. Sci. ENS 2018]. I will present examples of such solutions for the parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system in two dimensions [joint work with Ghoul-Masmoudi-Nguyen 2024] and for the cubic wave equation in four dimensions [ongoing joint work with Li to appear]. The associated patterns are caused by different effects for each equation: the solitons' own dynamics, their interactions, and their interactions with the remainder of the solution which is affected by the presence of the multiple nearby potentials from the solitons. I will present ideas for the construction of an approximate solution, and its stability analysis based on the control of its modulating parameters and of suitable norms for the remainder, adapted to the multiscale feature of the problem.

56b6da91a344dc66.title: Compilation of pattern-matching by small inversion
56b6da91a344dc66.speaker: W. Ait Moussa
56b6da91a344dc66.abstract:
Dependent inductive data types are an essential part of type theory based proof-assistant, where they close the gap between theorem proving and functional programming. Their meaning and computational behavior are given by dependent recursors, but those are tedious and unintuitive to work with in a dependent setting. Today, the established practice in dependent settings is to have an expressive high-level dependent pattern matching construct with the same logical power as recursors but which is more natural to work with.
This talk will be split into three parts. First, I will go over the history and established theory of dependent-pattern matching and its correspondence to recursors. Then I will present an alternative translation of the non-recursive part of pattern matching to recursors using small-inversion. Finally, I will present an implementation for Rocq of the latter, written by Thierry Martinez a few years back ; in addition to its value as a basis for a specification for this translation, of particular interest is its extensive use of Ocaml's GADTs in order to formalize a notion of intrinsically well-formed Rocq terms.

57d85c3090d1bbdd.title: Families of G-Curves, Monodromy, and Tannaka Groups
57d85c3090d1bbdd.speaker: Irene Spelta
57d85c3090d1bbdd.abstract: Maximality results for the monodromy of families of algebraic varieties are widely studied in algebraic geometry. In this talk, we study the monodromy group of families of Galois G-coverings of curves. The action of the Galois group G on cohomology induces a decomposition of the associated variation of Hodge structures. Under suitable assumptions on this decomposition, we discuss results on the maximality of the algebraic monodromy group. We also present ongoing work exploring the relationship between this group and the Tannaka group associated with sheaf convolution on a single fiber of the family.

587da5bbe15d97a3.title: David Bessis – La chute de l’économie du théorème

587da5bbe15d97a3.abstract:
Si les machines démontrent les théorèmes, que reste-t-il aux humains ? En quelques mois, les progrès des modèles d’IA ont fait entrer la recherche mathématique mondiale dans une crise sans précédent, remettant à la fois en cause ses critères de valeur, son organisation pratique et son image publique. En dépit de sa nouveauté radicale, la crise actuelle nous confronte à des questions anciennes, jamais résolues, dont les mathématicien(ne)s ont longtemps cru qu’elles étaient purement théoriques : que sont les mathématiques ? Comment créent-elles de la valeur ? Quel rôle jouent-elles dans la cognition humaine ?

589081130f46d8df.speaker:
Mickael Matusinski
Silvain RIdeau
589081130f46d8df.abstract:
14h Mickaël MATUSINSKI (Université de Bordeaux)
Résolution d'équations différentielles algébriques sur et dans les corps de séries généralisées de rang 1 à coefficients réels.
(Travail en commun avec Nicolas Martinez)
Étant donnée une équation différentielle algébrique à coefficients séries généralisées de rang 1, nous présentons un algorithme de résolution en temps au plus omega qui permet de décrire explicitement l'espace des solutions sous la forme d'une famille finie de séries généralisées (au sens de Hahn) paramétriques. On en déduit qu'un tel espace de solution constitue un ensemble semi-algébrique dont nous bornons la dimension et nombre de composantes connexes. Nous utilisons à l'instar des travaux récents de Cano et Fortuny une méthode du dit polygone de Newton-Petrovic-Fine.
16h Silvain RIDEAU (École normale supérieure (Université Paris Sciences et Lettres))
Groupes définissables dans les corps géométriques avec une différentielle générique.
(Travail en commun avec Anand Pillay et Françoise Point)
La théorie géométrique de la stabilité se concentre en grande partie sur les structure algébriques (et non pas seulement les ensembles) définissables dans une structure donnée, et l'un des problèmes récurrent est leur classification. Par exemple, un résultat d'A. Pillay énonce que les groupes définissable dans les corps différentiellement clos sont des sous-groupes de groupes algébriques.
Cet énoncé reste en partie vrai dans un cadre instable. Étant donné une théorie de corps --- potentiellement enrichi, par exemple d'un ordre --- on peut considérer les modèles de cette théorie munis d'une différentielle qui sont existentiellement clos. On parle alors de corps muni d'une différentielle générique. Sous certaines hypothèses (la théorie de corps est géométrique), on comprend très bien ces structures et l'on peut y classifier les groupes définissables. Ceci repose sur une version abstraite du résultat de Weil sur la reconstruction d'un groupes à partir d'une loi de groupe définie birationnellement.

5bdba800cbc040e7.title: Nonexistence of homomorphisms between matrix algebras over spheres which are injective on K-theory
5bdba800cbc040e7.speaker: Chris Phillips
5bdba800cbc040e7.abstract:
Résumé : This is joint work with Ilan Hirshberg.
In 1993, Blackadar asked for which $n$, $k$, $d$, and $r$ there is a unital homomorphism $C (S^{2 n}, M_r) \to C (S^{2 k}, M_{d r})$ which is injective on $K_0$. There are "obvious" examples constructed as follows. For $m \in {\mathbb{N}}$, $K^1 (S^{2 m - 1})$ is generated by the class of a unitary in $C (S^{2 m - 1}, M_m)$, and from this one gets homomorphisms $C (S^{1}) \to C (S^{2 m - 1}, M_m)$ which are injective on $K_1$. One can then take (odd) suspensions, increase the matrix size in the codomain, and tensor everything with $M_r$. Ordered $K_0$ suggests that many more might exist. In particular, Blackadar asked whether there is a unital homomorphism $C (S^{2 n}, M_{2 n}) \to C (S^{4 n}, M_{4 n})$ which is injective on $K_0$.
The answer is no. We prove that the only choices of $n$, $k$, $d$, and $r$ for which such a homomorphism exists are those which occur in the examples above. The proof uses indecomposability in the rational cohomology ring of the space of homomorphisms from $C (S^{2 n})$ to $M_d$.
This material is based upon work partially supported by the US National Science Foundation under Grant DMS-2400332.

603614eaa9063139.title: Irregularities in Uniform Distribution
603614eaa9063139.speaker: Omri Sarig
603614eaa9063139.abstract:
Suppose \(a\)is an irrational number. Weyl proved that the frequency of visits of \(na\;{\rm mod}\; 1\) to a subinterval of [0,1] tends to the length of the subinterval ("uniform distribution"). It has long been known that the error term in this limit theorem can exhibit strong bias (“irregularity in uniform distribution"). This bias depends on the fine number theoretic properties of \(a\). For example, the square roots of two and three do not behave in the same way (!)
I will explain how infinite ergodic theory can shed light on this phenomenon, and describe some recent joint work with Dmitry Dolgopyat on the equidistribution of the error term. There are amusing connections to the geometry of translation surfaces with infinite genus, and to local limit theorems of inhomogeneous Markov chains.

60cef684c741f359.title: Minimal model for localization of topological Fukaya categories of surfaces
60cef684c741f359.speaker: Pierre BODIN
60cef684c741f359.abstract:
In the first half of this talk, I will present the construction of the topological Fukaya category of a graded marked surface, as introduced by Haiden, Katzarkov, Kontsevich, and present some of its main properties.
In the second half, I will present a minimal model for the localization of this category at a spherical object corresponding to a simple closed curve on the surface. This new description will then be used to describe the indecomposable objects of the localization in terms of graded curves on the singular surface obtained by collapsing the simple closed curve to a point.

628df6c4380c2afa.title: FAMED triangulations will live forever
628df6c4380c2afa.speaker: Antonin Guilloux
628df6c4380c2afa.abstract:
I will present a joint work with Fathi Ben Aribi and Ka Ho Wong around volume conjectures. Roughly, a volume conjecture describes a link between the semiclassical limit of a quantum invariant of a triangulated hyperbolic knot complement and the hyperbolic geometry of its complement. There are several flavors and we will focus of a version by Andersen and Kashaev.
Recently, arguments by Fathi and Ka Ho reduce essentially this conjecture to a combinatorial property of the triangulation, called FAMED. I will explain this condition and how to extensively test this condition, and a path toward a proof of the volume conjecture.

66e2752f075b4eff.title: Topological freeness for minimal actions of groups with the rapid decay property
66e2752f075b4eff.speaker: Joseph Gondek
66e2752f075b4eff.abstract: We apply an operator-algebraic property of finitely generated groups, called rapid decay (RD), to topological dynamics. We show that the compact, minimal G-spaces of an RD group G with amenable neighbourhood stabilizers have some rigidity properties; under general conditions, all such actions are topologically free. 67c0840d946bbf68.title: Proliferation Transitions for Non-Abelian Anyons
67c0840d946bbf68.speaker: Andrea Antinucci
67c0840d946bbf68.abstract:
Phases of matter and the transitions between them are famously characterized within the Landau paradigm and Landau–Ginzburg theory: phases are labeled by broken or unbroken symmetries, while phase transitions are described in terms of scalar order parameters. There are, however, phases beyond the standard Landau paradigm that are distinguished not by the realization of ordinary symmetries, but by that of generalized global symmetries. Among these, topologically ordered phases in (2+1)d possess non-invertible 1-form symmetries described by anyon lines. In this talk, I will present a framework for describing transitions between topologically ordered phases related by anyon proliferation, which can be viewed as a non-invertible generalization of the choice of the unbroken symmetry. The resulting theories involve scalar fields coupled to gauge fields. A crucial ingredient in this construction is the (3+1)d Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), which allows to separate symmetry from dynamics and will be employed in a rather unconventional way.

68dd5494a0651231.speaker: Konstantinos Kartas
68dd5494a0651231.abstract: the almost purity theorem is a foundational result about perfectoid algebras which, as the name suggests, holds only in an “almost” sense. We show that suitable completeness hypotheses on the algebras allow us to remove the “almost”. More precisely, spherically complete perfectoid algebras satisfy non-almost purity for Galois p-extensions and countably saturated perfectoid algebras satisfy non-almost purity for all finite étale extensions. 69aa1cc5302c19af.title: Dynamique des tourbillons visqueux dans un demi-plan
69aa1cc5302c19af.speaker: Thierry Gallay
69aa1cc5302c19af.abstract:
ANNULÉ – En raison de la fermeture du campus Pierre-et-Marie Curie le séminaire est ANNULÉ.
Speaker: Thierry Gallay (Université Grenoble Alpes)
Le but de cet exposé est de définir un cadre mathématique permettant de décrire les interactions entre tourbillons et parois pour des écoulements plans à grand nombre de Reynolds. Les phénomènes typiques que l’on souhaite étudier à terme sont le mouvement auto-induit (pour un tourbillon isolé) et l’effet de rebond (pour une paire de tourbillons).
Dans la première partie, à caractère tout à fait élémentaire, on explique comment résoudre les équations de Navier-Stokes incompressibles dans un demi-plan en exploitant l’équation d’évolution pour le tourbillon du fluide. Si l’on suppose que la vitesse s’annule sur la paroi, le tourbillon vérifie une condition au bord non linéaire et non locale qui est difficilement utilisable en pratique. On peut toutefois la remplacer par une condition intégrale permettant une formulation élégante du système, lequel se résout alors par un simple argument de point fixe dans un cadre fonctionnel approprié.
Dans la seconde partie, en cohérence avec l’objectif affiché, on suppose que la donnée initiale est une collection finie de tourbillons ponctuels, dont les circulations peuvent être arbitrairement grandes. Ce cas ne peut pas être traité comme précédemment par un simple argument de point fixe, mais on peut tout de même montrer l’existence et l’unicité de la solution en utilisant une décomposition appropriée, qui permet de traiter la partie la plus singulière de la solution dans le plan tout entier où l’on dispose d’outils plus affûtés. En fonction du temps disponible, on présentera également quelques résultats concernant le comportement asymptotique en temps de la solution, ses propriétés de localisation, ou la question difficile de la limite non visqueuse.
Cet exposé repose entièrement sur un travail en collaboration avec Anne-Laure Dalibard.
Thierry Gallay (Université Grenoble Alpes)

6d4efbf05c9ff8b3.speaker: Simone Maria Giancola
6d4efbf05c9ff8b3.abstract:
Le séminaire des doctorants se propose de fournir aux doctorants une occasion de s'ouvrir aux autres domaines des mathématiques que le leur. A chaque séance, un intervenant réalise un exposé sur un fait standard de leur domaine d'étude, de niveau adapté à l'ensemble des doctorants.
----
The PhD students seminar aims to provide PhD students with an opportunity to explore other areas of mathematics beyond their own. At each session, a speaker gives a presentation on a standard topic in their field of study, at a level suitable for all phd students.
This talk starts with an example in real life. We will see that there is a natural way to model it with graph theory, called planted clique. With first principles it is already possible to do a partial statistical analysis of it. Complementing the analysis with some comments reveals an interesting phenomenon about solutions that can be found efficiently, i.e. techniques that are applicable in real life problems.

6f95359338f3c096.title: Séminaire 09/10/2026 - Gabriel Peyré and Vianney Perchet
6f95359338f3c096.abstract:
14h15-15h15 Gabriel Peyré (ENS)
The Expressive Power of Large Language Models
Abstract: Large language models process vast sequences of input tokens by alternating between classical multi-layer perceptron layers and self-attention mechanisms. While the approximation capabilities of perceptrons are relatively well understood, those of attention mechanisms remain less explored. In this talk, I will compare the proof techniques and approximation results associated with these two types of layers, emphasizing key open questions that connect large language models with approximation theory in infinite-dimensional spaces representing input token distributions.
15h30-16h30 Vianney Perchet (Criteo et ENSAE)
AI-powered AI. Robustness, Consistency and Smoothness of Algorithms.
Abstract: AI systems no longer operate as isolated algorithms, machines, or agents; instead, they
interact with each other. An algorithm designed for a specific task might use the output or
prediction of another as its input. This has serious consequences: blindly relying on another
algorithm can be extremely helpful if it is accurate, but devastating if it is not, as a single error -
even the tiniest one - could break down the whole system. New algorithms will need to incorporate
these predictions to improve their consistency, while remaining robust against errors. We will use
simple toy examples to show how the generic framework of learning-augmented algorithms (LAA) is
perfectly suited for this challenge, highlighting the complexity of designing practical and potentially
vastly more efficient algorithms.

702c137c490164b6.title: What does it mean to formalize a proof? Can we really trust a formalized proof, even if written by an LLM?
702c137c490164b6.speaker: Riccardo BRASCA
702c137c490164b6.abstract: Formalization of mathematics began in the 1970s with various goals. Verifying the correctness of proofs was only one of them and, for most researchers, not the most important. With the rise of AI-assisted and AI-generated proofs, however, the need for reliable verification tools has become increasingly important. In this talk, we will use examples from differential geometry and other areas to explain what it means for a proof to be formalized, whether by a human or by a large language model. We will explain which problems formalization can, and cannot, solve. Finally, we will discuss its role in recent announcements, including the claimed solution to the Navier–Stokes problem.

72002ba2e502d205.title: Algèbres de von Neumann de réseaux arithmétiques et ensembles de Kakeya
72002ba2e502d205.speaker: Mikael de la Salle
72002ba2e502d205.abstract:
Une forme de la conjecture de rigidité de Connes prédit que les algèbres de von Neumann de $\mathrm{PSL_n}(Z)$ sont toutes distinctes. Au moment où j'écris ces lignes, cette conjecture est toujours ouverte. Des anciens travaux avec Vincent Lafforgue et Tim de Laat (ainsi que d'autres travaux de Uffe Haagerup et Tim de Laat) suggèrent une approche possible à cette conjecture, en terme de propriétés d'approximation.
J'expliquerai pourquoi cette approche est difficile: elle implique aussi une forme de la conjecture de Kakeya en toute dimension.
La conjecture de Kakeya en dimension d affirme que toute partie de l'espace euclidien de dimension d, qui contient un segment dans toute direction, est de dimension de Hausdorff égale à d. Au moment où j'écris ces lignes, cette conjecture est prouvée uniquement en dimension 2 (Davies, Cordoba) et 3 (Wang et Zahl).

73fb95623682fbb0.title: Height one phenomena in p-adic Hodge theory
73fb95623682fbb0.speaker: Tasos MOULINOS
73fb95623682fbb0.abstract:
The syntomification of the integers (Z_p^syn) acts as a parameter space for p-adic cohomology theories. By the work of Drinfeld and others, it is known to carry a canonical formal group, and hence a map to the moduli stack of formal groups. Pulling back along this map gives rise to a certain line bundle equipped with a distinguished section "v_1". On the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups, the nonvanishing of v_1 defines the substack parametrizing "height-1" formal groups. Yet the preimage of this locus on Z_p^syn, when computed in p-adic formal stacks, is empty. There is a mismatch here because inverting v_1 on syntomic cohomology gives p-adic étale cohomology, but inverting it on the stack itself before passing to global sections gives nothing.
I will explain how passing to analytic stacks brings this missing locus into view. By realizing the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups as an analytic stack, we construct an algebro-geometric shadow of K(1)-localization. Applied to syntomification, this produces an analytic stack whose dualizable quasi-coherent sheaves recover p-adic Galois representations, and more generally lisse étale sheaves on the generic fiber of a p-adic formal scheme. I will explain how a perfected version of this construction depends only on the generic fiber, providing a geometric counterpart to purity results for K(1)-localized K-theory.
This is joint work in progress with Greg Andreychev.

7482b5e5a45584bc.title: Grégoire Sempé - Marginal Propensities to Decarbonize
7482b5e5a45584bc.abstract: This research project characterizes the cost-effective climate policy on households’ direct emissions. Heterogenous households abate through lumpy decisions on their durable goods holdings and their usage intensity. I study theoretically whether liquidity constraints justifies combining carbon pricing and subsidies or credit lines. I propose a quantitative heterogenous agent model to find the optimal climate policy mix.

754692a68d6f0070.title: Spectre des longueurs marquées et aire des surfaces dont le flot géodésique est Anosov
754692a68d6f0070.speaker: Stéphane SABOUREAU
754692a68d6f0070.abstract: Il y a plus de vingt ans, Croke et Dairbekov ont montré qu'une métrique g_0 à courbure négative sur une surface fermée possède une aire minimale parmi toutes les métriques riemanniennes g à courbure négative sur la même surface dont le spectre des longueurs marquées est supérieur ou égal à celui de g_0. Nous montrons que l'hypothèse de courbure sur la seconde métrique peut être supprimée et nous étendons ce résultat aux métriques de Finsler réversibles. Plus précisément, nous prouvons qu'une métrique de Finsler réversible F_0 sur une surface fermée dont le flot géodésique est d'Anosov possède une aire minimale parmi toutes les métriques de Finsler réversibles F sur la même surface dont le spectre des longueurs marquées est supérieur ou égal à celui de F_0. Travail en commun avec Marcos Cossarini.

75dd6faa50cbe660.title: An equivariant version of Gabber’s lemma
75dd6faa50cbe660.speaker: Filippo Belfiori
75dd6faa50cbe660.abstract: Gabber’s preparation lemma is a fundamental result in algebraic geometry, originally established by Gabber in 1994 in his work on the exactness of certain Gersten complexes. Following the work of Morel, Gabber’s lemma has become a cornerstone of motivic homotopy theory over fields, the homotopy theory of algebraic varieties. When algebraic varieties are equipped with an action of an algebraic group G, one can similarly define an equivariant motivic homotopy category, providing a framework for studying the homotopy theory of varieties with G-action. In this talk, I will first recall Gabber’s preparation lemma and discuss some of its main consequences. I will then propose and study an equivariant version of Gabber’s lemma for a finite constant abelian group G, based on the C2-equivariant version introduced by Bachmann. If time permits, I will also discuss some applications of this equivariant version of Gabber’s lemma.

75ff18b604345dc7.title: Finiteness and density problems for (positive) integral points on Mordell–Schinzel surfaces
75ff18b604345dc7.speaker: Robin Zhang
75ff18b604345dc7.abstract: In 1952, Mordell erroneously claimed that the surface $xyz = G(x,y)$ has infinitely many integral points for any $G \in \mathbb{Z}[x,y]$. I will discuss a classification for finiteness and Zariski density of (positive) integral points on these log K3 surfaces when the coefficients of $G$ are non-negative. This combines a dynamical argument proposed by Mordell, the theory of generalized cluster algebras, and the Killing–Cartan classification of semisimple Lie algebras. This talk is partially based on joint work with Antoine de Saint Germain.

772d2a8890f92411.title: Anti-classification results in dynamical systems
772d2a8890f92411.speaker: Matthew Foreman
772d2a8890f92411.abstract:
Thematic 3-weeks programme at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris, May 18th to June 4th, 2027.
Beware: It was reported to us that scammers are sending to participants fraudulent e-mails about accommodation/fees. Please be particularly cautious about e-mails not coming from the organisers nor from an @ihp.fr address.
REGISTRATION IS FREE, HOWEVER MANDATORY.
Presentation of the programme
In recent years, there have been major advances using techniques from Descriptive Set Theory to show, in a rigorous way, that many classical problems in Dynamical Systems are impossible to solve. In this context, a problem that can be set in a Polish space is said to be impossible to solve if it cannot be settled using inherently countable techniques. These groundbreaking results mostly lie in Ergodic Theory, with further significant advances in Topological and Smooth Dynamical Systems.
One main goal of this program is to further enhance interactions between Descriptive Set Theory and Dynamical Systems. It brings together researchers from different fields to settle some of the most famous problems in dynamics dating to the mid-20th century.
A second main goal is to expand applications of the techniques from Descriptive Set Theory to other areas of mathematics.
Week 1
The program begins with lectures introducing the basic impossibility techniques and lectures explaining fundamental concepts in areas of potential applications.
We plan to have tutorials on:
Impossibility Results
Ergodic Theory
Symbolic Dynamics
Smooth Dynamical Systems
Additionally, there will be Research Talks and Expository Lectures (primarily in Ergodic Theory and Descriptive Set Theory).
Week 2
Research talks in Descriptive Set Theory, Ergodic Theory, Smooth and Symbolic Dynamics, as well as Expository Lectures, including on:
Impossibility Results in Ergodic theory
Complexity Theory
Flexibility and Rigidity
Moreover, we will have Problem and Discussion Sessions.
Week 3
Topical Days (particularly Complex Dynamics with tutorial); Problem Sessions

777bc7e241eb1487.title: Importance Sampling
777bc7e241eb1487.speaker: Simon Coste
777bc7e241eb1487.abstract: Importance sampling is a technique for estimating integrals of the form E[φ(X)], where X has a density g that may be difficult to sample from or otherwise handle. The simplest Monte Carlo method would consist of generating i.i.d. samples X_1,...,X_n from g and averaging the values φ(X_i). By contrast, Importance Sampling (IS) consists of using samples Y_1,...,Y_n from another density, say f, and averaging the reweighted values φ(Y_i) * g(Y_i)/f(Y_i). This works provided that f is positive when g is positive, but there is no free lunch: the price to pay can be high variance and poor accuracy. In this expository talk, I will (1) explain when and how to use IS, with practical examples from chemistry and combinatorics; (2) explain how to measure the accuracy of IS and determine the sample size n needed for an accurate estimation of E[φ(X)], locally for a specific φ; and (3) explain how to measure this accuracy globally using Wasserstein distances, even in infinite dimensions for stochastic diffusions, where "importance sampling" is known under the name of "Girsanov theorem".

7a33ca7d22b5f94e.title: HOMFLY Homology for Oriented Tangles
7a33ca7d22b5f94e.speaker: Luke Conners
7a33ca7d22b5f94e.abstract: We introduce an extension of Khovanov and Rozansky's categorification of the HOMFLY polynomial to oriented tangles. Unlike previous such extensions, ours is invariant under the full suite of oriented Reidemeister moves, including the "misoriented" Reidemeister IIb. For oriented links L, this removes the preliminary step of presenting L as a braid closure. Our construction admits an interpretation in terms of Bar-Natan's "canopolis" framework, allowing for local computations. Based on joint work with William Ballinger.

7bdc1c8b6f385022.title: [ANNULÉ] Xenia Flamm, raconte-moi le spectre réel (de variétés de caractères) !
7bdc1c8b6f385022.abstract:
Le spectre réel est un outil de la géométrie algébrique réelle qui permet de compactifier les ensembles semi-algébriques en ajoutant, à l’infini, leurs k-points, pour tout corps k ordonné non-archimédien. J’en présenterai la construction ainsi que les principales propriétés.
Dans une deuxième partie, nous nous intéresserons aux variétés de caractères, c’est-à-dire des espaces de modules de représentations d’un groupe de type fini dans un groupe semi-algébrique G. Ces espaces permettent notamment de décrire de nombreuses structures géométriques sur les variétés. Nous verrons comment le spectre réel permet d’étudier leurs dégénérescences : les points à l’infini peuvent être interprétés comme des représentations à valeurs dans G(k), où k est un corps ordonné non-archimédien. À travers quelques exemples, j’expliquerai en quel sens ces dégénérescences peuvent être vues comme des structures géométriques « non-archimédiennes ».

7d7b9b0a954106bb.title: Homological construction of non-semisimple TQFTs
7d7b9b0a954106bb.speaker: Aleksei Andreev
7d7b9b0a954106bb.abstract: In the 1990s, Lawrence initiated a program to interpret quantum invariants homologically in order to understand their topological nature. Within this framework, twisted homology of configuration spaces of surfaces forms representations of mapping class groups. Recently, De Renzi and Martel showed that, for a specific choice of local system, this construction recovers the projective version of Lyubashenko’s representation for quantum sl_2. Since this representation is part of the non-semisimple Kerler--Lyubashenko TQFT, it is natural to ask whether the homological construction extends to cobordisms. I will answer this question by constructing a homological action of cobordisms via their multi-trajectory spaces and Juhász’s presentation of cobordism categories. As a basic example, I will reformulate Donaldson’s TQFT in these terms, and then sketch how the (projective) Kerler--Lyubashenko TQFT arises as its natural deformation.

7e64db0a59eb01df.title: Surfaces Browniennes et Explorations Métriques
7e64db0a59eb01df.abstract:
Les surfaces browniennes sont des surfaces aléatoires continues qui apparaissent comme limites de grandes surfaces discrètes choisies au hasard. Elles constituent aujourd’hui des modèles fondamentaux de géométrie aléatoire.
Dans cet exposé, je présenterai ces objets et quelques-unes de leurs propriétés fondamentales. Nous reviendrons sur plusieurs résultats marquants de la théorie, en partant des modèles discrets dont ces surfaces émergent. On verra notamment comment certains processus stochastiques apparaissent naturellement lorsqu’on explore ces surfaces à partir d’un point, et comment ils permettent de mettre en évidence certaines propriétés de Markov spatiales.
Aucun prérequis particulier n’est nécessaire : l’objectif sera surtout de donner une intuition des objets et des méthodes, plutôt que d’entrer dans les détails techniques.

7f90cfd61645f286.speaker: Tasos MOULINOS

80313ab580ded52f.title: Murmurations de zéros de fonctions $L$
80313ab580ded52f.speaker: Didier Lesesvre
80313ab580ded52f.abstract: Les murmurations sont un phénomène inattendu récemment découvert : les moyennes de coefficients automorphes présentent des oscillations structurées lorsque les nombres premiers croissent proportionnellement aux conducteurs d'une famille de fonctions $L$. Elles peuvent être interprétées comme des corrélations entre les signes des équations fonctionnelles et les coefficients automorphes, et ou encore comme des phénomènes de transitions dans les statistiques des petits zéros de fonctions $L$. Dans cet exposé, j'introduirai le phénomène des murmurations et les heuristiques qui permettent d'en comprendre les mécaniques, puis je présenterai le cas particulier des fonctions $L$ des carrés symétriques de formes modulaires. L'approche dans ce cas repose de manière centrale sur la formule des traces d'Eichler-Selberg.

81f5130d919a8aaf.title: On supercuspidal representations in the l-adic cohomology of some local Shimura varieties
81f5130d919a8aaf.speaker: Yoichi Mieda
81f5130d919a8aaf.abstract: A local Shimura variety is a p-adic analogue of a Shimura variety. Its l-adic cohomology is expected to be related to the local Langlands correspondence. In the Lubin-Tate case, a supercuspidal representation appears only in the middle degree. In the GSp(4) case, a supercuspidal representation appears only in the degrees 3,4, and it appears in the degree 4 if and only if its L-parameter has non-trivial SL(2)-part. In this talk, I will explain my recent results in this direction for more general cases.

825091c772259bd3.title: Global lower resolvent estimate for damped waves
825091c772259bd3.speaker: Arthur Yax
825091c772259bd3.abstract:
In this talk, we will discuss the decay rates of damped waves when the Bardos-Lebeau-Rauch-Taylor Geometric Control Condition (GCC) fails, roughly speaking "there is a geodesic that does not enter the damped region".
Since decay rates are related to resolvent growth (Batty-Duyckaerts), we provide and present a result of global lower resolvent bound, as well as applications of it in various settings.

8342a404054eacb7.title: Lissage par peignes et trivialité locale pour les espaces homogènes au-dessus d’une courbe relative
8342a404054eacb7.speaker: Margot Bruneaux
8342a404054eacb7.abstract:
Soit $R$ un anneau local hensélien, de corps résiduel $\kappa$, soit $C$ une courbe projective lisse sur $R$, à fibres géométriquement connexes, soit $G$ un $C$-groupe réductif dont le tore radical $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, et soit $E\to C$ un $G$-torseur.
Nous montrons que, si le noyau de l'isogénie centrale
\[
G_{\mathrm{sc}}\times_C \operatorname{rad}(G)\longrightarrow G
\]
est étale sur $C$, ou bien si $\kappa$ est un corps suffisamment grand, alors la trivialité de $E_\kappa\to C_\kappa$ pour la topologie de Zariski implique la trivialité de $E\to C$ pour cette même topologie.
Nous démontrons également une version « moyennée » de ce résultat, en supposant seulement que $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, ainsi qu'une variante concernant les espaces homogènes projectifs, sans aucune hypothèse restrictive sur $G$.
Ces résultats ont notamment pour conséquences un principe local-global pour les torseurs sur les corps de fonctions de courbes au-dessus d'anneaux de valuation discrète henséliens, renforçant des travaux de Gille--Parimala--Suresh, ainsi qu'une version hensélienne d'un théorème de Drinfeld--Simpson.
Nos démonstrations sont de nature géométrique. Elles reposent sur des compactifications de torseurs et sur une technique de lissage par peignes, dans une version relative et arithmétique que nous développons en détail, en nous appuyant sur les travaux de Kollár et de Graber--Harris--Starr.
En collaboration avec Federico Scavia.

83b6ce1f8bc4646c.title: Dynamique de Aut(F_n) sur G^n, pour G compact et n grand
83b6ce1f8bc4646c.speaker: Florestan Martin-Baillon
83b6ce1f8bc4646c.abstract:
Donnons nous un groupe de Lie compact G et un entier n.
Un n-uplet (g_1, …, g_n) étant donné, on peut changer l’un des g_i en son inverse, ou multiplier l’un des
g_i par g_j (avec j différent de i) : ces opérations élémentaires ne changent pas le sous-groupe de G
engendré par les g_i. Ces opérations engendrent un groupe de difféomorphismes de G^n, et le problème
que nous aborderons est d’étudier la dynamique de ce groupe. Pour n suffisamment grand, nous verrons
qu’il est possible de classer les fermés et les mesures invariants.

848c2764cc76482e.title: Mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties
848c2764cc76482e.speaker: Martin Ortiz
848c2764cc76482e.abstract: The weight part of Serre's conjecture studies the modularity of certain spaces of mod p automorphic forms. In the case of Shimura varieties, this is usually done by considering their etale cohomology, with Serre weights as coefficients. One can also propose a similar conjecture for mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties, and I conjecture that the two approaches are equivalent. I can prove this generically for G=GL3, and some cases in GSp4. Moreover, for GSp4 this approach produces a generic entailment of Serre weights, which is completely invisible from the etale cohomology perspective.

8680b2f106b96358.title: Cohomological invariants of hermitian pairs over central simple algebras
8680b2f106b96358.speaker: Alexandre Lourdeaux
8680b2f106b96358.speaker_affiliation: Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China
8680b2f106b96358.abstract:
In this talk we adapt the Witt theory of hermitian forms over a central simple algebras over fields of characteristic not 2, to hermitian pairs over fields of characteristic 2. Hermitian pairs are hermitian forms with an extra datum that is necessary to describe all simply connected simple groups of type $D_n$ in characteristic 2. In order to define useful and well-behaved cohomological invariants for hermitian pairs, we define them using unramified cohomology attached to the function field of the Severi-Brauer variety associated to the central simple algebra which is the base of our hermitian pairs. We obtain classifying invariants and related them to classical invariants in small degrees.
(This is a joint work with Yong Hu.)

86e7c3606d9ebbed.title: Sard’s theorem in infinite dimension: from real algebraic geometry to sub-Riemannian geometry
86e7c3606d9ebbed.speaker: Antonio Lerario
86e7c3606d9ebbed.abstract:
Sard’s theorem can fail in infinite dimension, even for polynomial maps with finite-dimensional targets. I will explain how quantitative estimates in real algebraic geometry, combined with finite-dimensional approximation, yield Sard criteria in this setting. I will then show how Kupka’s classical counterexample can be realized inside a sub-Riemannian endpoint map. This produces a smooth bracket-generating distribution whose endpoint map has no regular values, disproving the sub-Riemannian Sard conjecture in the smooth category.
Based on joint works with Luca Rizzi and Daniele Tiberio.

879740ae91d3b179.title: Training deep Transformers: mean-field models and convergence analysis
879740ae91d3b179.speaker: Raphael Barboni
879740ae91d3b179.abstract:
Transformers have become the dominant architecture in modern machine learning, yet the theoretical understanding of their training dynamics remains limited, especially for deep architectures with many layers and Attention heads. I will present a rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing gradient-based training of Transformers in the overparameterized regime, where depth, width and context length tend to infinity. This mean-field model features two types of measure representations: token distributions evolving through layers (measures over the token space), and Attention parameters at each layer (measures over the parameter space). Our contributions are twofold: (i) We prove the well-posedness of gradient flow curves in a conditional Wasserstein metric space, establishing a rigorous foundation for gradient-based Transformer training. (ii) We prove convergence of gradient flow towards global minima when the initial training risk is sufficiently low. A key technical contribution is providing necessary and sufficient conditions for injectivity of the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) for Attention mechanisms: we show that NTK injectivity is equivalent to linear independence of log-sum-exp functions modulo affine functions, a condition satisfied by diverse token distributions, including discrete distributions, uniform distributions, and Gaussian mixtures.
These results builds on joint works with M. de Hoop, T. Furuya, G. Peyré and F.-X. Vialard.

892203e7a7e511fe.title: Nonrelativistic Conformal Collider Physics of Multiparticle Point Production
892203e7a7e511fe.speaker: Dam Thanh Son
892203e7a7e511fe.abstract:
Motivated by nuclear experiments where a few neutrons are produced by a local source, we develop a formalism of "nonrelativistic conformal collider physics." We define detector operators in the nonrelativistic conformal field theory describing fermions at unitarity. We reduce the problem of computing the momentum distribution and correlation between final particles produced by a local source ("point-produced") to the computation of correlation functions involving the detector operators. The general formalism is applied to the point production of three unitary fermions, where we find the momentum and angular distribution of final particles, and point production of a large number of fermions. We discuss a nonrelativistic version of celestial holography, which maps the asymptotic out-state to a quantum wave function in the so-called "oscillator frame." Based on arXiv:2608.18202 with Cyuan-Han Chang, Subham Dutta Chowdhury, and Ian Moult.

8c608e98e501a176.title: Beyond crystalline cohomology, rigid cohomology
8c608e98e501a176.speaker: Thomas Serafini
8c608e98e501a176.abstract: Crystalline cohomology is not a "good" cohomology for non-proper varieties - for instance, the crystalline H1 of the affine line is not finite-dimensional. Following ideas from Monsky and Washnitzer, Berthelot defined rigid cohomology on general varieties in characteristic p > 0, which provides the "right" extension of crystalline cohomology to arbitrary varieties. The central idea is that of overconvergence, i.e. considering analytic functions that converge not on a p-adic lifting of the variety, but rather on a neighborhood of it. Following and detailing the example of the affine line, we will build to the definition of rigid cohomology and explain its relation to p-adic differential equations.
8c608e98e501a176.location_text: Salle Pierre Grisvard, IHP - Bâtiment Borel

8caedad483f08113.title: Uncertainty and unique continuation for dispersive PDEs at two time points
8caedad483f08113.speaker: Diego Fiorletta
8caedad483f08113.abstract:
Imposing too strong simultaneous decay or localization constraints on a function and its Fourier transform causes the function to vanish identically (Uncertainty Principle). The same applies to a solution to some dispersive evolutionary PDE if similar constraints are imposed on its profile at two different time points.
In the first part of the talk, I will introduce a manifestation of the Uncertainty Principle, the Benedicks-Amrein-Berthier Theorem. The $L^2$ norm on $\mathbb{R}^n$ of a function is controlled by the sum of the $L^2$ norms of the function and its Fourier transform observed outside sets of finite Lebesgue measure (Amrein-Berthier). In particular, no non-zero function supported on a set of finite Lebesgue measure can have a Fourier transform with the same property (Benedicks).
In the second part I will show how the above statements translate into qualitative and even quantitative unique continuation results when the Fourier transform is replaced by the propagator, evaluated at a non-zero time T, associated to some dispersive PDE, in particular considering linear and non-linear instances of the Schr\"odinger equation.

8cf2a51d13cfb6c4.title: 14e séminaire ITZYKSON - Dualité markovienne : méthodes algébriques et applications
8cf2a51d13cfb6c4.abstract:
14e séminaire ITZYKSON : Dualité markovienne : méthodes algébriques et applications
Le 14e séminaire Itzykson est organisé par Jean-René Chazottes (CPHT), Guillaume Dubach (CMLS), Ruben Minasian (IPhT) et Julio Parra-Martinez (IHES).
Depuis bientôt une quinzaine d’années l’axe math-physique de la FMJH organise un séminaire Itzykson tous les ans à l’IHES. Il s’agit d’une journée consacrée à un thème de physique mathématique, avec un cours et deux ou trois exposés spécialisés (en français ou en anglais selon le choix des orateurs).
Le prochain séminaire Itzykson portera sur la dualité markovienne, et ses liens avec les algèbres de Lie et les systèmes de particules en interaction. Ces sujets sont reliés par une même idée directrice : l'approche algébrique de la dualité, qui permet de construire et d'analyser des processus markoviens exactement solubles. Le séminaire donnera des perspectives algébriques, probabilistes et physiques sur des résultats récents, notamment au sujet des symétries des générateurs markoviens, des interprétations trajectorielles en génétique des populations, et des fluctuations macroscopiques hors d'équilibre.
Les cours et exposés de cette journée seront présentés par :
Cristian Giardinà (Università di Modena e Reggio Emilia)

Frank Redig (TU Delft)

8cfff265b2847517.title: Rigorous identification of dynamics from data
8cfff265b2847517.speaker: Konstantin Mischaikow
8cfff265b2847517.abstract:
It is well established that there is no algorithm that given countable data can identify up to conjugacy the global dynamics of nonlinear system. Thus, if we wish to systematically and rigorously understand data driven dynamics we need a courser characterization of dynamics that still capable capturing essential features, e.g., fixed points, periodic orbits, chaotic dynamics, bifurcations, etc.
With this in mind I will focus on two topics.
1. I will describe a combinatorial/algebraic topological approach to dynamics based on ideas of Conley and show that at this level dynamics can be learned given enough data and enough computing power. In addition, I will show that for low dimensional examples this approach is computationally tractable and requires relatively little data.
2. I will show how using encoders and latent dynamics this approach can give rigorous results about high dimensional systems. I will present examples that show that experimental results are much more promising than theory suggests.

Recent trends at the interface between information theory, probability, statistics and high-dimensional geometry raise new questions on the role and importance of entropy in the understanding of both asymptotic and finite range phenomena, in particular towards discrete structures and applications to areas such as quantum information, percolation and random matrices. Recent fruitful developments warrant imminent blossom of new ideas and results in this area in the near future.
Another central theme at the interface of High-Dimensional Probability and Convexity is the study of isoperimetric properties of log-concave measures (including isoperimetric-type questions related to convex bodies). This is not a mere curiosity: convexity and isoperimetry play an important role in the study of concentration of measure phenomena which is crucial for harnessing various high-dimensional effects in Probability as well as several applied fields.
The scope of the semester includes developing further connections between Information Theory and Convexity, in all of the different directions described above. The semester will aim to strengthen these powerful interdisciplinary methods, aiming towards challenging issues and applications, including the isoperimetry questions for log-concave measures, and super-concentration properties of models from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics.
The semester’s objective is to foster cross-fertilization between probability, analysis, information theory and convex geometry (continuous and discrete). By organizing two thematic pre-schools, we will ensure active participation by junior researchers, which should have a lasting effect on their careers, as well as influence the routes along which these research areas will be developed in the future. Our two workshops will further provide opportunities for many re- searchers from across the globe to interact and collaborate. We believe that close interactions between these disciplines are a necessary condition to address many mathematical challenges raised in the last decades, and that the timing is optimal to bring together all these powerful ideas which have been recently developed in several communities. Therefore, our proposed semester program will have a strong and lasting impact on High-Dimensional Probability, Convexity and Analysis as a whole.

8de6607c53900f8d.title: Torus actions on compactified braid varieties and polytopality of subword complexes
8de6607c53900f8d.speaker: Mikhail Gorsky
8de6607c53900f8d.abstract:
Every cluster variety admits a faithful regular group action scaling all cluster variables. Given a partial compactification of a cluster variety, a natural question is whether this action extends to a regular action on the compactification. I will explain that, in the case of braid varieties for simple Lie groups, the answer is affirmative for brick compactifications. If the braid variety is an open Richardson variety in the flag variety, the same result holds for the corresponding closed Richardson variety. In the latter case, the faithfully acting group is a torus of rank the Kazhdan-Lusztig d-invariant. The same result holds for projected Richardson varieties. I will also explain that, in general, a braid variety is a torus if and only if each of its brick compactifications is a toric variety with respect to this extended action, if and only if the polar dual of the moment polytope for this action realizes the corresponding subword complex. The braid words satisfying this property turn out to be precisely the double root free words of V. Pilaud and C. Stump. This provides a novel approach to the longstanding open question of the polytopality of spherical subword complexes asked by A. Knutson and E. Miller in 2004, and in particular gives infinite families of subword complexes admitting polytopal realizations in dimension higher than the rank of the corresponding Coxeter group. The talk is based on joint work with Lara Bossinger and José Simental, arXiv:2609.12414.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.

Operator algebras are self-adjoint subalgebras of the bounded operators on a Hilbert space and divide into two main classes: C∗-algebras and von Neumann algebras, according to whether one demands that they are closed in the norm topology or the weak operator topology. When one first meets these algebras, they might look quite similar, but they have different natures as exemplified by the commutative case: via the Gelfand transform, abelian C∗-algebras are algebras of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on a locally compact Hausdorff space, while abelian von Neumann algebras are essentially bounded measurable functions on a measure space. These flavours persist in general. Topological concepts such as dimension and invariants such as K-theory pervade the study of C∗-algebras, while measure-theoretic style methods are often used to study von Neumann algebras.
The long thematic program OA will focus on operator algebras and its still evolving interactions with ergodic theory, topological dynamics, discrete subgroups of semisimple Lie groups, analytic, ergodic and geometric group theory, quantum information theory and random matrices.

8f10de0ff45c5eb1.title: Un degré de différentiabilité peut tout changer
8f10de0ff45c5eb1.speaker: Hélène Eynard-Bontemps
8f10de0ff45c5eb1.abstract:
Par lisse, certains entendent de classe $C^1$, d’autres $C^\infty$, alors que pour l’analyse élémentaire, la mécanique Newtonienne ou les questions de courbure, $C^2$ semble plus naturel… Les mathématiques regorgent d’exemples de problèmes ou de techniques qui sont extrêmement sensibles à la régularité dans laquelle on travaille, souvent pour des raisons profondes et intéressantes. J’illustrerai cette affirmation à l’aide d’exemples tirés de la dynamique unidimensionnelle (qui s’intéresse aux difféomorphismes de l’intervalle et du cercle) mais aux origines bien géométriques : le célèbre théorème de Denjoy et le bijou moins connu qu’est le lemme de Nancy Kopell.

8f822d7a3777c5a9.title: Moduli of vector bundles: from K3 surfaces to higher dimensional irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds of higher dimension.
8f822d7a3777c5a9.speaker: Kieran O'Grady
8f822d7a3777c5a9.abstract: After a quick review of the main results on moduli spaces of semistable sheaves on K3 surfaces we will recall a fundamental theorem of Verbitsky. The latter result opens the way to an extension to higher dimensional IHSM's of one key result valid for K3 surfaces, provided we consider vector bundles with certain characteristic classes. Lastly we will illustrate this principle by stating a recent result of ours on moduli spaces of stable vector bundles on IHSM's of Type K3^[2] (deformations of the Hilbert square of a K3 surface). If time permits I will sketch the proof.

8fe97fd51029ffcd.title: A Dieudonné theory for analytic p-divisible groups
8fe97fd51029ffcd.speaker: Lucas Gerth
8fe97fd51029ffcd.abstract: We prove a classification of families of analytic p-divisible groups on adic spaces S over Qp in terms of Hodge–Tate triples on S, generalizing a theorem of Fargues. From this, for S a perfectoid space, we construct an analytic Dieudonné theory with values in mixed characteristic shtukas. As applications, we obtain moduli descriptions of local Shimura varieties of EL and PEL type. We also explain how to derive generalizations of the fundamental exact sequence of Colmez--Dospinescu--Nizio? on smooth Stein spaces.

905168b43bf26504.title: Lagrangian Klein bottles in S^2 x S^2
905168b43bf26504.speaker: Nikolas Adaloglou
905168b43bf26504.abstract:
The study of Lagrangian submanifolds is a central theme in symplectic geometry. In this talk, after a brief introduction on the basics of symplectic geometry, we are going to study Lagrangian submanifolds in \(S^2\times S^2\), equipped with standard symplectic forms. Our goal is to understand which symplectic forms on \(S^2\times S^2\) carry Lagrangian Klein bottles. We will focus mainly on constructing the Klein bottles, using certain techniques from the theory of Lagrangian torus fibrations. This theory effectively reduces many constructive problems into problems of classical affine geometry of the plane.
Afterwards, I will explain how to obstruct the existence of some Lagrangian Klein bottles, using pseudoholomorphic curve techniques.
Together, the obstructive part and the constructive part completely determine which symplectic forms in \(S^2\times S^2\) carry a Lagrangian Klein bottle.

925a4c8748c5b99e.title: [mini-cours] Combinatorics and Geometry: Crossing paths—in the age of AI. (Part 2)
925a4c8748c5b99e.speaker: János Pach
925a4c8748c5b99e.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
925a4c8748c5b99e.abstract:
What makes the chromatic number of a graph large?
There have been many attempts to answer this question. The
most natural approach is to look for unavoidable substructures in
graphs of large chromatic number. In 1943, Hadwiger made the
conjecture that every graph of chromatic number r can be
transformed into a complete graph of r vertices by a series of
edge contractions and vertex and edge deletions. This is one of
the most important unsolved problems in graph theory. After giving
a somewhat biased survey of the problem, I plan to report on some
related recent results, joint with Fox and Suk.

92c76a615e013520.title: Points critiques stationnaires pour un modèle champ de phase en mécanique de la rupture
92c76a615e013520.speaker: Martin Rakovsky
92c76a615e013520.abstract: Cette thèse est consacrée à la fonctionnelle de Mumford-Shah, utilisée pour modéliser les fissures fragiles dans un matériau élastique, et plus particulièrement à son approximation par la fonctionnelle d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli. Nous nous intéressons notamment à l'analyse asymptotique des points critiques de la fonctionnelle d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli, afin d'étendre aux points critiques la convergence des minimiseurs globaux obtenue par $Gamma$-convergence. Nous commençons par présenter les fonctionnelles de Mumford--Shah et d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli et le principe de l'approximation champ de phase. Ensuite, en dimension $1$, nous établissons la convergence des points critiques dans le cas où l'on rajoute à la fonctionnelle d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli une condition d'obstacle. En dimension quelconque, la convergence des points critiques est connue sous l'hypothèse supplémentaire que l'énergie d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli converge. En dimension $2$, nous montrons ce résultat en ne supposant qu'une partie de la convergence de l'énergie. Enfin, nous étudions le système parabolique associé aux équations vérifiées par les points critiques d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli. Nous établissons l'existence, les conditions d'unicité et la régularité des solutions de ce système, et obtenons en particulier leur régularité maximale en toute dimension.

9308b264c7e8a5bc.title: Algebraic Theory of Indefinite Theta Functions
9308b264c7e8a5bc.speaker: Kenz Kallal
9308b264c7e8a5bc.abstract:
Séminaire de géométrie arithmétique
Jacobi's theta function $\Theta(q) := 1 + 2q + 2q^4 + 2q^9 + \cdots $, and more generally the theta functions associated to positive-definite quadratic forms, have the property that they are modular forms of half-integral weight. The usual proof of this fact is completely analytic in nature, using the Poisson summation formula. However, $\Theta$ is also related to diffusion of heat on a uniform circle-shaped material: it is a restriction of the fundamental solution to the heat equation on a circle. By algebraically characterizing the heat equation as a specific flat connection on a certain bundle on a modular curve, we produce a completely algebraic technique for proving modularity of theta functions. More specifically, we produce a refinement of the algebraic theory of theta functions due to Moret-Bailly, Faltings--Chai, and Candelori. As a consequence of the algebraic nature of our theory and the fact that it applies to indefinite quadratic forms / non-ample line bundles (which the prior algebraic theory does not), we also generalize the Kudla--Millson analytic theory of theta functions for indefinite quadratic forms to the case of torsion coefficients. This is joint work with Akshay Venkatesh.

9318d88da2514dc2.title: IHP School: Artificial Intelligence for Mathematicians and Theoretical Physicists
9318d88da2514dc2.abstract:
Recent breakthroughs have shown that AI can now prove theorems. At the same time, many of the deepest open questions about AI are, at heart, questions of mathematics and physics: high-dimensional geometry, non-convex optimisation, the statistical mechanics of learning. AI is becoming both a tool for and a subject of research in our fields, and a working knowledge of it is fast becoming essential for every young researcher.
This one-week school, funded by Qube Research & Technologies, will introduce the fundamental concepts of modern AI. It is designed for PhD students and early-career researchers in mathematics and theoretical physics with no prior specialisation in AI. The programme combines lectures with hands-on lab sessions.
