934cdfe8c21f0d30.title: Kinetic theory: from long-range interactions to turbulence and quantum simulators, Paris
934cdfe8c21f0d30.abstract:
This is a thematic trimester programme with short courses, seminars and workshops on Kinetic theory: from long-range interactions to turbulence and quantum simulators.
January 18 to April 9, 2027 at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris
REGISTRATION IS MANDATORY AND FREE
IMPORTANT WARNING: Scam / Phishing / SMiShing! Note that ill-intentioned people may be trying to contact some of participants by email or phone to get money and personal details, by pretending to be part of the staff of the conference center. IHP and the organizers will NEVER contact you by phone on this issue and will NEVER ask you to pay for accommodation/ board / possible registration fee in advance.
Deadline for financial support request has been extended to: June 30th, 2026.
Summary
The program centers on the development of a unified understanding of kinetic theory in systems with long‑range interactions, with a particular emphasis on the quantum regime. Long‑range interacting quantum systems—realized experimentally in cold atoms, trapped ions, and polar molecules—exhibit rich dynamical behavior such as metastability, collisionless dynamics, anomalous transport, critical scaling, and turbulence‑like phenomena. These effects are often linked to the Vlasov equation, the collisionless kinetic equation that emerges in the thermodynamic limit. While Vlasov theory is conceptually well established in classical plasma physics, its systematic extension to quantum many‑body systems remains incomplete.
A key scientific motivation of the program is that different communities—mathematical physics, quantum many‑body theory, and AMO physics—address similar non‑equilibrium long‑range phenomena using different methods, preventing the emergence of a unified framework. The program aims to bridge these approaches and clarify conceptual connections between classical and quantum kinetic theories.
The scientific agenda spans several interconnected themes. One major theme is the analysis of classical transport, Vlasov dynamics, and their differences from Boltzmann kinetic theory, including how turbulence, chaos, and long‑range correlations emerge in classical systems. Another theme concerns the quantum generalizations of Vlasov theory, focusing on rigorous derivations and effective equations for quantum gases, including mean‑field and Gross–Pitaevskii limits, and the treatment of finite‑size effects in quantum simulators.
The program will explore non‑equilibrium many‑body dynamics in quantum systems, including quantum turbulence, cascade processes, ergodicity breaking, and anomalous scaling. A related line of inquiry concerns the dynamics of quantum correlations and entanglement, the onset of quantum chaos, and the characterization of universal quasi‑static dynamics in isolated systems. Another scientific direction is the study of effective theories in quantum matter, connecting renormalisation‑group methods with kinetic descriptions and identifying the regimes where classical scaling concepts can illuminate quantum behavior.
On the mathematical side, the program emphasizes rigorous derivations of macroscopic equations from microscopic many‑body dynamics, particularly in long‑range systems, and the formulation of effective transport equations, scaling limits, and mean‑field theories. Renormalisation‑group tools are highlighted both in their rigorous and approximate forms, with the aim of connecting microscopic models to emergent large‑scale behavior in many‑body systems.
Finally, the proposal identifies a scientific need to synthesize current insights into a coherent and predictive quantum kinetic theory for long‑range interactions, and to outline a roadmap of open problems invol

March 1 to 5 - Workshop 1 at IHP, Paris: Classical Transport and Dynamical Evolution in the Statistical Physics of Long-Range Interaction Systems

957bd11bbe483012.title: Conférence de Stéphanie Debette, « Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle »
957bd11bbe483012.abstract:
« Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle »
La santé cérébrale est un enjeu majeur du XXIᵉ siècle, qui dépasse le seul domaine médical pour toucher aux dimensions sociétales, économiques et stratégiques. Plus d'une personne sur trois sera concernée par une maladie cérébrale au cours de sa vie. Ces maladies sont la première cause de handicap et la deuxième cause de décès dans le monde. Le vieillissement de la population augmente le poids des pathologies liées à l'âge, et les troubles de santé mentale progressent chez les jeunes.
La présentation se concentrera sur les maladies vasculaires cérébrales, particulièrement fréquentes et graves. Parmi elles, la maladie des petits vaisseaux cérébraux est la plus répandue. On peut la repérer tôt en imagerie.
Nous évoquerons les progrès récents dans la compréhension de ses mécanismes biologiques et dans l’analyse d'images cérébrales par intelligence artificielle
Cette conférence hybride sera suivie d'un moment convivial.

95db7503a93ba418.title: Defects in skein theory
95db7503a93ba418.speaker: Juan Ramón Gómez García
95db7503a93ba418.abstract:
Skein theory forms a once-extended categorified TQFT that assigns skein algebras to surfaces and skein modules to 3-manifolds.
These algebras and modules are defined in terms of generators of topological flavor, namely a certain class of graphs embedded in the 3-manifold,
modulo the relations induced by evaluating (locally) these graphs in an underlying ribbon category. In this talk I will explain how this picture
can be extended to stratified manifolds with strata of codimension 1 and 2 (called defects). Using the appropriate algebraic structures,
we can define evaluation functors around defects, yielding notions of stratified skein modules and algebras. Examples of these structures
are provided by the formalism of parabolic restriction. As an application, we use an interpolating version of parabolic defects to construct
a categorification of the Turaev coproduct in the HOMFLY skein algebra.

965960f6ccbd08e9.title: The Doubly Conformal Dispersion Relation
965960f6ccbd08e9.speaker: Balt van Rees
965960f6ccbd08e9.abstract:
We provide a simple derivation of the conformal dispersion relation of Carmi and Caron-Huot which reconstructs a CFT four-point function from its double discontinuity. We exhibit a hidden conformal symmetry which explains the appearance of the "magic variable" x as a simple cross-ratio, built from four physical cross-ratios. We also introduce a regulator in the double discontinuity operation and then prove that one subtraction suffices for all integrals to converge.

96ebc0808993dd3e.title: Ruben Haalebos - Portfolio Decarbonization under Incomplete Carbon and Transition Information
96ebc0808993dd3e.abstract: We study dynamic portfolio decarbonization under incomplete information about firms' carbon intensities and the underlying transition state. The investor maximizes expected utility of terminal wealth net of a penalty on perceived cumulative financed emissions. Asset returns and carbon intensities depend on a stochastic transition factor, while the investor may need to infer the current transition state, its long-run mean and firms' carbon intensities from market observations and periodic noisy disclosures. The optimal strategy combines a Merton-type component with climate-dependent expected-return adjustments, a direct carbon intensity penalty and intertemporal hedging demands associated with stochastic carbon intensities and learning. In a numerical application, incomplete information has limited effects on welfare and target satisfaction when prior beliefs are well specified. By contrast, biased beliefs generate welfare losses in either direction but asymmetric environmental consequences: optimistic and pessimistic beliefs induce opposite portfolio tilts and therefore affect the probability of exceeding the cumulative emissions target differently.

970c7dbfcd1f9463.title: Colloquium : "Nielsen meets Weil"
970c7dbfcd1f9463.speaker: Maxim Kontsevich
970c7dbfcd1f9463.abstract: A hundred years ago Jacob Nielsen proposed a lower bound on the number of fixed points of a self-map, utilizing the action on the fundamental group. The natural bookkeeping device is the Reidemeister trace, a linear combination of twisted conjugacy classes. I will review the classical theory and propose an analogue for varieties over finite fields, in the spirit of the rationality part of the Weil conjectures, where the self-map is replaced by the Frobenius automorphism. The resulting conjecture can be checked in non-trivial examples.

9817b8cf32f5e5d2.title: On the undecidability of the QWEP for C*-algebras
9817b8cf32f5e5d2.speaker: Isaac Goldring
9817b8cf32f5e5d2.abstract: In his landmark 1993 paper, Kirchberg introduced a property of C*-algebras called the QWEP, which stands for “quotient of the weak expectation property”. As the name suggests, the property is defined by the fact that the algebra is a quotient of a C*-algebra with the weak expectation property, which was a property introduced by Lance years earlier in connection with the theory of tensor products of C*-algebras. While at first glance this seems to be a strange property, Kirchberg showed that whether or not every C*-algebra has the QWEP is equivalent to the famous Connes Embedding Problem (CEP) from von Neumann algebra theory. The CEP remained open for nearly 50 years until its recent refutation in 2020 via a result in quantum complexity theory (as well as the equivalence with Kirchberg’s QWEP conjecture). Several years ago, I showed that the QWEP is an axiomatizable property of C*-algebras. In this talk, I will present joint work with Aruseelan and Hart where we show that the QWEP does not have an effective axiomatization and, in fact, there can be no effectively axiomatizable satisfiable theory of C*-algebras all of whose models have the QWEP (modulo some nontrivially conditions). The proofs uses the connection with the quantum complexity results mentioned above as well as other techniques from C*-algebra theory. No prior knowledge of continuous logic, operator algebras, or quantum complexity will be assumed.

This workshop will bring together experts in string theory and quantum field theory to discuss recent advances in these fields, and also to foster collaboration between the Korean and French theoretical and mathematical physics communities.

9a45aa9c03af67e7.title: On the Wasserstein Geodesic Principal Component Analysis of probability measures
9a45aa9c03af67e7.speaker: Alice Le Brigant
9a45aa9c03af67e7.abstract:
The GdT OT-PDE-ML is a research seminar organized by the ParMA team. It brings together researchers to discuss recent theoretical and numerical developments at the crossroads of Optimal Transport theory, Partial Differential Equations and Machine Learning.
Abstract: In this talk we discuss how to perform Principal Component Analysis (PCA) of a dataset whose elements are probability distributions, compared using the Wasserstein distance. The goal is to identify geodesic curves in the space of probability measures that best capture the modes of variation of the underlying dataset. To achieve this, we leverage the Riemannian interpretation of the Wasserstein metric. We first address the case of a collection of centered Gaussian distributions, and show how to lift the computations in the space of invertible linear maps using Bures-Wasserstein geometry. For the more general setting of absolutely continuous probability measures, we use Otto-Wasserstein geometry and neural networks to parameterize geodesics in Wasserstein space. Finally, we compare to classical tangent PCA through various examples and provide illustrations on real-world datasets.

9baffe2d745b97da.title: Development of new post hoc methods for structured data
9baffe2d745b97da.speaker: Romain Périer
9baffe2d745b97da.abstract: Cette soutenance présentera certaines de mes contributions à la théorie des tests multiples. Je présenterai notamment de nouvelles méthodologies pour contrôler les fausses découvertes grâce à des bornes de confiance et des procédures de contrôle du False Discovery Rate (FDR). Ces procédures assurent un recouvrement post hoc, ce qui signifie qu'elles préservent les garanties statistiques même après l'intervention du praticien --- comme le p-hacking ou le HARKing --- et offrent une plus grande flexibilité en lui permettant de sélectionner l'ensemble de rejets de manière adaptative. De plus, ces méthodes exploitent également la structure des données ; elles vont au-delà de l'hypothèse i.i.d. traditionnelle en prenant en compte l'hétérogénéité des données afin d'améliorer la puissance statistique.

9cf62b913497ab87.title: Fomin-Kirillov algebras
9cf62b913497ab87.speaker: Leandro Vendramin
9cf62b913497ab87.abstract:
Fomin-Kirillov algebras EnE_nEn​ are quadratic algebras introduced by Fomin and Kirillov in the late 1990s to study the combinatorics of Schubert polynomials. They contain a commutative subalgebra isomorphic to the cohomology ring of the flag manifold, and they are related to Nichols algebras over the symmetric group. It has been known for some time that Fomin-Kirillov algebras EnE_nEn​ are finite-dimensional for n≤5n\leq 5n≤5, but whether this holds for n>5n>5n>5 has remained open since the algebras were introduced. In this talk, I will review basic properties of Fomin-Kirillov algebras and present joint work with Andruskiewitsch, Angiono, Heckenberger, Lentner, and Reiher, in which we prove that Fomin-Kirillov algebras EnE_nEn​ are infinite-dimensional for all n>5n>5n>5.
This talk will take place on Zoom only.

9f79361b0f0772b7.title: De la modélisation aux problèmes inverses : une méthodologie pour les systèmes dynamiques en biomédecine.
9f79361b0f0772b7.speaker: Pierre Monmarché
9f79361b0f0772b7.abstract:
Oratrice : Annabelle Collin (Université de Nantes)
Résumé : Les systèmes dynamiques constituent un cadre naturel pour décrire l'évolution temporelle et spatiale de nombreux phénomènes rencontrés en biologie, et en médecine. Qu'ils soient formulés sous la forme d'équations différentielles ordinaires (EDO) ou d'équations aux dérivées partielles (EDP), ces modèles permettent de formaliser des mécanismes biologiques, physiologiques ou épidémiologiques et d'étudier leur dynamique.
Dans cet exposé, nous présenterons les principales étapes d'une démarche de modélisation mathématique appliquée à des problématiques biomédicales : construction et formalisation du modèle, étude de ses propriétés théoriques, approximation numérique, puis confrontation du modèle aux données à travers la résolution de problèmes inverses. Une attention particulière sera portée à l'estimation de paramètres et d'états non directement observables, ainsi qu'aux difficultés associées à l'identifiabilité, aux incertitudes et au caractère potentiellement bruité ou incomplet des observations.
Nous nous intéresserons plus particulièrement aux approches séquentielles, qui permettent de mettre à jour progressivement l'estimation de l'état du système et de ses paramètres au fur et à mesure de l'acquisition de nouvelles données.
Cette démarche sera illustrée sur un exemple volontairement simple, permettant de mettre en évidence les principales étapes méthodologiques tout en montrant comment des modèles relativement parcimonieux peuvent déjà conduire à des résultats quantitatifs pertinents et exploitables dans un contexte de santé publique.

a0e4a946883cae1d.title: FAMED triangulations will live forever
a0e4a946883cae1d.speaker: Antonin GUILLOUX
a0e4a946883cae1d.abstract:
I will present a joint work with Fathi Ben Aribi and Ka Ho Wong around volume conjectures. Roughly, a volume conjecture describes a link between the semiclassical limit of a quantum invariant of a triangulated hyperbolic knot complement and the hyperbolic geometry of its complement. There are several flavors and we will focus of a version by Andersen and Kashaev.
Recently, arguments by Fathi and Ka Ho reduce essentially this conjecture to a combinatorial property of the triangulation, called FAMED. I will explain this condition and how to extensively test this condition, and a path toward a proof of the volume conjecture.

a160eee0f090d283.title: Around the Pearcey Process
a160eee0f090d283.speaker:
Thomas Chouteau
Pierre Lazag
a160eee0f090d283.abstract:
I. Pierre Lazag (Université Catholique de Louvain-la-Neuve) - "An introduction to the Pearcey point process and number rigidity"
The Pearcey point process is a universal determinantal point process appearing in the scaling limit of a random integrable model near a cusp singularity of its limit shape. In this talk, I will introduce the Pearcey point process and describe how it arises in models such as non-intersecting Brownian motions and random skew-plane partitions. If time permits, I will discuss its analytic and probabilistic properties such as number rigidity.
II. Thomas Chouteau (Université de São Paulo) - "Multiplicative Statistics of the Pearcey Process and the Boussinesq Hierarchy"
The Pearcey process is a universal point process that arises in the study of various integrable models. In this talk, we investigate its multiplicative statistics through three distinct representations of deformed Pearcey kernels: an IIKS integrable representation, a finite-temperature representation, and a representation for a conditionally thinned process. These three frameworks provide complementary viewpoints to analyze multiplicative statistics and yield several new results. From an integrable systems perspective, we show that the logarithmic derivative of the multiplicative statistics with respect to one of the deformation parameters solves the first two equations of the Boussinesq hierarchy, and we determine the associated initial conditions. Finally, we connect these multiplicative statistics to a pair of auxiliary functions satisfying a coupled system of integro-differential equations.

a30b364eaa318fa2.title: ProofTree: Structured Representations for Human-Centred Mathematical Exploration
a30b364eaa318fa2.speaker: Carl Jontza
a30b364eaa318fa2.abstract:
If formal proofs become abundant, how can we help people find mathematics they care about and explore it in ways that are understandable and engaging? I will present ongoing work on ProofTree, investigating a persistent, versioned graph of goals, assumptions, and alternative arguments as an intermediate representation connecting human-readable reasoning with formal proofs. The aim is to support discovery, understanding, and human guidance at levels of abstraction suited to a person’s background, interests, and objectives.
A case study from Lean-based proof hierarchies, involving confusion between an induction hypothesis and a proof obligation, will motivate technical questions about preserving logical scope, revising arguments, and maintaining links to checked proofs. I will discuss what records of exploration should preserve for subsequent reuse, and outline an evaluation agenda that considers mathematical relevance, understanding, and user experience alongside proof completion and human and computational cost.

a329e1844f0ce445.title: Reprojections des pavages par le Spectre et motifs hexagonaux

On peut associer naturellement aux pavages par le spectre un relevé à $\mathbb{R}^4$ du graphe des arêtes du pavage. On peut faire de même avec un autre graphe, issu d'une décoration particulière de la tuile. En reprojetant ces graphes vers le plan selon différentes directions, on observe des motifs intéressants. J'ai effectué une analyse détaillée de l'un d'entre eux.

a54947280dbc198b.title: Régulateur cyclosyntomique des corps de nombres ~~ Transfer principles and the Kato–Kuzumaki conjecture
a54947280dbc198b.speaker: Quentin Gazda, Felipe Gambardella
a54947280dbc198b.abstract:
Felipe Gambardella (Orsay), 2-3pm
Transfer principles and the Kato–Kuzumaki conjecture.
Seeking a Diophantine characterisation of cohomological dimension of fields, Kato and Kuzumaki introduced the C_i^q property for every pair of non-negative integers i and q. These properties are inspired by Lang’s notion of a C_i field and Bloch-Kato’s conjecture relating Milnor K-theory with Galois cohomology. An interesting property of C_i fields is that they satisfy a transfer principle with respect to equicharacteristic complete discrete valuations – i.e. if a field k is C_i, then the field of Laurent series k((t)) is C_{i+1}. However, for the C_i^q property, no such transfer result is known to hold and the situation is more subtle than the one of C_i fields. For instance, the optimistic statement “k((t)) satisfies C_{i+1}^q whenever k satisfies C_i^q ” is false. This talk reports on joint work with Konstantinos Kartas. I will present a transfer principle for C_i fields with respect to non-discrete valuations. This principle has as a corollary a transfer principle for a variant of the Kato-Kuzumaki properties. Moreover, this is enough to establish the Kato-Kuzumaki conjecture for several fields of arithmetic interest such as the perfection of Fp((t_1)) . . . ((t_n)) or C(x_1, . . . , x_n)((t_1)) . . . ((t_m)) and to establish a strengthening of the C_1^1 property for Q_p introduced by Wittenberg.
Quentin Gazda (IMJ-PRG), 3.30-4.30pm
Régulateur cyclosyntomique des corps de nombres
Dans cet exposé, nous présenterons un travail en commun avec Tess Bouis où nous construisons une version q-déformée du régulateur de Dirichlet p-adique des corps de nombres. De manière surprenante, notre construction ne nécessite ni la complétion en p, ni que p soit premier. Nous interpréterons ce régulateur à travers la notion de q-Gauges, objets globaux ayant vocation à interpoler les structures de Hodge p-adiques en chaque p.

a5b13a77b85fcc84.speaker: Hartmut Monien

a6590d9b3aadaf36.title: Constructing actions with Fraïssé limits
a6590d9b3aadaf36.speaker: Paolo Boldrini
a6590d9b3aadaf36.abstract: Given an action of a countable group on the Cantor space, clopen subsets can be compared by cutting and moving through the action or by evaluating them on invariant measures. Dynamical comparison asserts that the measure-theoretic notion controls the dynamical one. Since its first appearance, dynamical comparison has been verified for a wide variety of actions. In this talk, I will survey some recent positive results in this direction and present the construction of the first examples of topologically free minimal actions that fail dynamical comparison, obtained in a joint work with Akshara Prasad. The construction is based on an algebraic invariant known as the type semigroup and involves Fraïssé limits of Boolean algebras equipped with monoid-valued measures.

a7356c5a669739dc.title: Horizon flux-balance laws in the multiscale perturbation
a7356c5a669739dc.speaker: Ali M. Seraj
a7356c5a669739dc.speaker_affiliation: Institute for Research in Fundamental Sciences (IPM), Tehran
a7356c5a669739dc.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
I study the evolution of the event horizon in a “two-timescale” perturbative expansion around a stationary black hole. This leads to strong constraints on the “coarse-grained” horizon dynamics. At leading order, the horizon exhibits an “adiabatic rigidity”: the leading corrections to its angular velocity and inaffinity remain uniform on each horizon cut, while evolving on the slow timescale. We then provide a systematic procedure for transforming a perturbative bulk solution, given for example in Lorenz gauge, to an ingoing Newman--Unti gauge adapted to the horizon, allowing the perturbed horizon geometry to be extracted directly from the metric. Finally, we formulate “horizon conservation laws” associated with horizon symmetries, including energy, dynamical entropy, and angular momentum. We expand the charges through second order and their fluxes through third order in perturbation theory, providing a framework for future applications to horizon absorption and backreaction in extreme mass-ratio inspirals.

a86834f7cca1d9cc.title: Empirical distribution of ancestral lineages in populations with density-dependent interactions
a86834f7cca1d9cc.speaker: Madeleine Kubasch
a86834f7cca1d9cc.abstract: We study a density-dependent Markov jump process describing a population where each individual is characterized by a type, and reproduces at rates depending both on its type and on the population type distribution. We are interested in the empirical distribution of ancestral lineages in the population process. First, we exhibit a time-inhomogeneous Markov process, which allows to capture the behavior of a sampled lineage in the population process. This is achieved through a many-to-one formula, which relates the expected value of a functional evaluated over the lineages in the population process to the expectation of the functional evaluated along this time-inhomogeneous process. This provides a direct interpretation of the underlying survivorship bias. Second, we consider the large population regime, when the population size grows to infinity. Under classical assumptions, the population type distribution converges to a deterministic limit. Here, we focus on the empirical distribution of ancestral lineages in this large population limit, for which we establish a many-to-one formula. Using coupling arguments, we further quantify the approximation error which arises when sampling in this large population approximation instead of the finite-size population process.

a9a6db6006a869d8.title: Canopies for Generalized Persistence
a9a6db6006a869d8.speaker: Barbara Giunti
a9a6db6006a869d8.abstract: In this talk, we provide a new construction for studying parameterized persistence, called a canopy. We do this by making a simple but major modification in the persistence bundle representation information: namely, rather than tracking a point in the persistence diagram, we instead track some choice of pairs of simplices that created said point. This viewpoint is a combinatorial version of tracking the chain complex information rather than just the output of persistence. We show how to construct the canopies from any filtered filtration function, proving, using the algebraic structure of filtered chain complexes, that different choices of pairs result in homeomorphic structures. Finally, we showcase the power of our approach by using canopies to define vines even in the presence of points with multiplicity; to discuss monodromy; and to obtain some immediate results linking non-trivial monodromy in the persistent homology transform with the existence of non-Hausdorff points in the canopy.

a9e4d70457516f82.title: Classical Transport and Dynamical Evolution in the Statistical Physics of Long-Range Interaction Systems
a9e4d70457516f82.abstract:
Kinetic theory: from long-range interactions to turbulence and quantum simulators
Workshop 1: Classical Transport and Dynamical Evolution in the Statistical Physics of Long-Range Interaction Systems
March 1 to 5, 2027 - IHP, Paris
Summary
This workshop aims to synthesize established paradigms from classical transport with the overlapping frameworks of quantum dynamics, forging a coherent pathway toward understanding transport phenomena, turbulence, and chaos in strongly correlated quantum matter. Of central observable importance is the interferometric comparison between the mean-field Vlasov description and the collisionally decohered Boltzmann equation—highlighting the nonlocal phase-space structures endemic to long-range interacting systems, in stark contrast with the short-range statistical closures of local theories.

aab9afc48fbbe470.title: Théorie de Morse, pantalons et jupes
aab9afc48fbbe470.abstract:
Lorsque l’on tient un pantalon droit, on observe qu’il possède un trou en haut et deux en bas. Le bord supérieur du pantalon est donc un cercle tandis que le bord inférieur est composé de deux cercles : les deux bords sont différents. En imposant que les deux bords soient simplement connexes on obtient une jupe (qui n’est rien d’autre qu’un cylindre). Tous les pantalons de dimension au moins 6 ayant 2 bords connexes sont en fait des jupes.
Dans cet exposé j’introduirai plusieurs outils de la théorie de Morse (points critiques, lemme de Morse, fonctions de Morse) et je définirai alors l’homologie de Morse. J’énoncerai ensuite comme application le théorème de h-cobordisme qui formalise mon affirmation sur les pantalons de grande dimension et donnerai selon le temps restant les idées de la preuve.

ab68331d49c277ea.title: !!!!!(Seance Reportée)!!!! The local non-archimedean pluripotential theory and continuity of envelopes for singular polarized varieties
ab68331d49c277ea.speaker: Lyuhui Wu
ab68331d49c277ea.abstract:
Abstract: The envelope property (a.k.a. continuity of envelopes) is a fundamental in non-archimedean pluripotential theory and its applications to complex geometry. While this property was established in the seminal work of Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson for smooth polarized varieties over discretely valued fields of residue characteristic zero, its extension to the singular setting had remained open for more than a decade.
In this talk, I will discuss my recent work establishing the envelope property for normal polarized varieties over discretely valued fields of residue characteristic zero. The proof relies on a study of local non-archimedean pluripotential theory, adapting ideas of Chambert-Loir–Ducros, followed by the establishment of a non-Archimedean analogue of the Fornæss–Narasimhan theorem.
I will conclude by discussing some applications of the envelope property to complex geometry.

ab90d0673c0b4101.title: Two Applications of the Arithmetic Margulis Lemma
ab90d0673c0b4101.speaker: Marc Burger
ab90d0673c0b4101.abstract:
This course has two parts. In the first we will define a general notion of integer point in a higher Teichmüller space and two invariants thereof, the arithmetic dimension and the arithmetic height. The aim is to show finiteness, modulo the mapping class group action, of the number of integer points for which both invariants are bounded.
In the second part we will give the main steps leading to the recent result of Frączyk, Hurtado and Raimbault, stating that the topological complexity of an arithmetic locally symmetric space is bounded by its volume.
Both parts rely on the arithmetic Margulis lemma proven by the same authors as a consequence of Breuillard's height gap theorem.

ac3dc592d1d47701.title: A Reider Theorem for Hilbert Schemes of Points on a Surface
ac3dc592d1d47701.speaker: Aaron Bertram
ac3dc592d1d47701.abstract: Reider's Theorem on very ampleness of divisors of the form \(K_S + D\) on a non-singular surface has a natural generalization to ampleness of divisors of the form \((K_S + D)_d - \Delta\) on the Hilbert schemes of d points on \(S\). The boundary case, where we can prove the divisor is nef but not ample, is a very natural generalization of the pull-back of \(2\Theta\) under the Abel-Jacobi map for curves. In light of Mumford's theorem for surfaces with \(p_g\) different from zero, these nef divisors surprised us. In this talk I will explain some interesting geometry for particular surfaces and also sketch the proof, which relies on results of Bayer-Macrì and Toda on Bridgeland stability conditions on surfaces.

ade3d2050fc674b0.title: Monodromy in Radial Persistence Vineyards and visualizing with Bouquet2D
ade3d2050fc674b0.speaker: Rohit Roy
ade3d2050fc674b0.abstract:
Given a manifold M without boundary, the Radial Persistence Transform (RPT) assigns to each point x in R^2 the persistence diagram of the squared Euclidean distance function d_E^2(., x) restricted to M. As x moves along a closed loop gamma, these diagrams form a periodic vineyard. The RPT is a variant of the persistent homology transform (PHT) introduced by Turner and collaborators, and is more sensitive, see Onus et al. Both the RPT and PHT can exhibit monodromy; after a full traversal of gamma, points of the persistence diagram return permuted. Monodromy obstructs feature tracking and complicates downstream analysis in TDA pipelines, and understanding when and why it occurs is an open problem. Arya et al. gave an example with monodromy for the PHT and the geometric conditions that exclude monodromy, both in 2 dimensions.
Chambers et al. showed that monodromy and knotting of arbitrary complexity can occur for the RPT. We are exploring the relation between the monodromy in a vineyard and the topology of the vineyard for the RPT on one hand and the symmetry and focal set (the bifurcation set for distances) on the other. Classical results of Bruce, Giblin and Gibson, and of Porteous, show that the Morse decomposition of the distance function changes only when x crosses the symmetry set or the focal set of M. We prove that for curves in R^2, the vineyard of a sufficiently small loop gamma cannot exhibit monodromy unless gamma encloses a specific singularity of the symmetry set. This yields a local classification of the causes of monodromy in 2 dimensions, which we are currently expanding to a global classification. This opens the door to algorithmic criteria for detecting and then exploiting or avoiding it.
Our investigation has been informed and corroborated by experimentation with Bouquet2D, an interactive web-based tool for exploring this phenomenon. The tool allows the user to define M as a spline curve and draw a loop gamma, and the tool displays the symmetry and focal sets of M together with the vineyard as x moves along gamma. Deforming M updates all of these in real time, so one can directly observe how bifurcations of the symmetry and focal sets appear as events in the vineyard, and where monodromy arises. Bouquet2D is available for everyone to experiment with vineyard topology at: https://bouquet2d.rohitroy.me/.

ae962c76bf6437f0.title: Irreducibility of random reciprocal polynomials
ae962c76bf6437f0.speaker: David Hokken
ae962c76bf6437f0.abstract: Let $P = a_m T^m + \sum_{j=0}^{m} a_j (T^{m-j} + T^{m+j})$ be a monic reciprocal polynomial of even degree n, with the $a_j$ drawn independently and uniformly at random from $\{1, 2, \ldots, H\}$ for some fixed integer $H \geq 35$. In joint work with Dimitris Koukoulopoulos, building on prior work of Bary-Soroker—Koukoulopoulos—Kozma, we show that $P$ is irreducible over the rationals, and has large Galois group, with probability tending to 1 as $n$ tends to infinity. This is in line with the long-held belief going back in various forms to Hilbert, Van der Waerden, Odlyzko—Poonen and Konyagin that a typical polynomial is irreducible and has Galois group as large as possible. I will discuss some recent, related developments in the field of probabilistic Galois theory before discussing aspects of the proof, which draws from classical polynomial theory, Fourier analysis, probability theory and group theory.

af9c44e02345c816.title: Dynamical Tidal Response of Neutron Stars from Scattering Amplitudes
af9c44e02345c816.speaker: Muddu Venkata Sai Saketh
af9c44e02345c816.speaker_affiliation: International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS-TIFR), Bengaluru, India
af9c44e02345c816.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
In this talk I will describe an amplitude-based framework for extracting the frequency-dependent tidal response of neutron stars while preserving the tidal resonances associated with their normal modes. The response is obtained by matching the amplitude for gravitational-wave scattering off a neutron star, equivalently gravitational Compton scattering, computed using relativistic stellar perturbation theory, to the corresponding amplitude in worldline effective field theory. The tidal contribution is isolated through the difference between the neutron-star and black-hole scattering phases. Unlike conventional treatments, the construction allows for a post-Newtonian expansion without Taylor expanding the response in frequency or assuming a harmonic-oscillator model for the internal dynamics.
I will present the tidal response through relative third post-Newtonian (3PN) order and use currently available numerical results to illustrate its frequency dependence. The results reproduce the known static Love numbers in the low-frequency limit, exhibit resonances at the expected stellar mode frequencies, and capture their damping through gravitational-wave emission. I will also discuss the renormalisation of the tidal response required through 3PN order. Time permitting, I will outline how the resulting response can be incorporated into binary dynamics and ultimately into gravitational waveforms.

b029985993a2d7ec.speaker: Andrei Negut
b029985993a2d7ec.abstract: Together with Alexander Tsymbaliuk, we propose a blueprint for constructing shuffle realizations of various quantum loop (super)algebras; this is a valuable tool for the study of these important algebraic structures and their representation theory. We apply this framework to the case of classical super-types A,B,C,D, which leads us into new combinatorics: higher order wheel conditions on one hand, and on the other hand certain generalizations of Young diagrams that we call shrubs (in types A) and asps (in types B,C,D).

We will first review Bar-Natan's construction for even Khovanov homology and then describe a modification of this framework that produces the odd Khovanov invariant. If time permits, we will also briefly discuss the functorial properties of this construction.
This is a joint work in progress with Shun Ming Samuel Lee and Léo Schelstraete.

b21032da43b2e91e.title: Informative Trains: A Memory-Efficient Journey to a Self-Stabilizing Leader Election Algorithm in Anonymous Graphs
b21032da43b2e91e.speaker: Sylvain Gay
b21032da43b2e91e.abstract:
We study the self-stabilizing leader election problem in anonymous n-nodes networks. Achieving self-stabilization with low space memory complexity is particularly challenging, and designing space-optimal leader election algorithms remains an open problem for general graphs. In deterministic settings, it is known that Ω(log log n) bits of memory per node are necessary [Blin et al., Disc. Math. & Theor. Comput. Sci., 2023], while in probabilistic settings the same lower bound holds for some values of n, but only for an unfair scheduler [Beauquier et al., PODC 1999]. Several deterministic and probabilistic protocols have been proposed in models ranging from the state model to the population protocols. However, to the best of our knowledge, existing solutions either require Ω(log n) bits of memory per node for general worst-case graphs, or achieve low state complexity only under restricted network topologies such as rings, trees, or bounded-degree graphs.
In this paper, we present a probabilistic self-stabilizing leader election algorithm for arbitrary anonymous networks that uses O(log log n) bits of memory per node. Our algorithm operates in the state model under a synchronous scheduler and assumes knowledge of a global parameter N = Θ(log n). We show that, under our protocol, the system converges almost surely to a stable configuration with a unique leader and stabilizes within O(poly(n)) rounds with high probability.
Our algorithm is inspired by the uniform constant-state leader election protocol in [Vacus and Ziccardi, PODC 2025] for the beeping model (without self-stabilization). A novel component of our approach is the introduction of an information train mechanism that propagates O(log n)-bit information across the network while requiring only O(loglog n) local memory per node. We believe this mechanism may be of independent interest for the design of space-efficient self-stabilizing distributed algorithms.

b22eaa44c92b9f1a.title: Cinquième rencontre de probabilités intégrables
b22eaa44c92b9f1a.abstract:
La Cinquième rencontre de probabilités intégrables aura lieu le vendredi 20 novembre 2026 à l'Institut Henri Poincaré.
Titles and Abstracts
Mini-course (2x1h) by Cédric Boutillier
Title:
Abstract:
Seminar talk (1h) by Elia Bisi (Università degli Studi di Firenze)
Title: Matrix Whittaker processes
Abstract: The log-gamma polymer is a prominent integrable model in the KPZ class: the law of its partition function is a marginal of a Whittaker measure, a positive-temperature analogue of the Schur measure. I will present a non-commutative generalisation, in which the “particles” are positive definite matrices. These evolve as interacting multiplicative random walks with inverse Wishart increments, arranged in a triangular array with push-and-block interactions. Using intertwining relations, we show that, for suitable random initial configurations, the bottom edge of the array evolves as an autonomous Markov process, with a kernel built from Whittaker functions of matrix arguments. For a singular initial state, its fixed-time law is a matrix Whittaker measure. Consequently, the matrix log-gamma polymer partition function is distributed as the first marginal of this measure.
Joint work with Jonas Arista and Neil O’Connell.

b3a1f693246fd183.title: Séminaires de doctorants
b3a1f693246fd183.speaker: Marius Kjaersgaard, Changjiang Du, Lucrezia Bertoletti, Marc Coulomb
b3a1f693246fd183.abstract:
14h - 14h25: Marius Kjaersgaard
Title: Local constancy of the Betti automorphic category over the moduli of curves
Abstract: Nadler and Yun have defined a relative notion of Betti automorphic sheaves and conjectured that they form a locally constant sheaf of categories over the moduli space of curves. We give a brief overview of the conjecture and work in progress, joint with Joakim Færgeman, towards proving the conjecture.
14h30 - 14h55: Changjiang Du
Title: Multivariable (phi,Gamma)-modules associated to p-adic Galois representations
Abstract: Let K be a finite unramified extension of Q_p. In a series of works by Breuil, Herzig, Hu, Morra, and Schraen, a multivariable coefficient ring A was constructed, together with two functors: D_A^{\otimes}, which sends mod p Galois representations to étale (phi,Gamma)-modules over A, and D_A, which sends admissible smooth mod p representations of GL_2(K) to étale (phi,O_K*)-modules over A. In this talk, we will explain how to construct the p-adic analogue of D_A^{\otimes}. This construction relies on two descent arguments: the pro-étale descent for perfectoid spaces and the Frobenius descent for phi-modules.
15h - 15h25: Lucrezia Bertoletti
Title: Finite length for unramified GL2: beyond multiplicity one.
Abstract: For K a finite unramified extension of Qp, a natural place to look for a conjectural mod p Langlands correspondence for GL2(K) are Hecke eigenspaces in the mod p cohomology of a tower of Shimura curves, which are expected to be a direct sum of copies of a representation (i.e. depending only on the input at p of the global setting) of GL2(K). The expected number of copies, called the multiplicity, should then be computed by counting Serre weights in the socle.
In the multiplicity one case, a recent work of Breuil, Herzig, Hu, Morra and Schraen establishes the finite length of the above Hecke eigenspaces, under mild genericity assumptions.
In this talk we will discuss how to extend this finite length result when the multiplicity one assumption is removed.
15h30 - 15h55: Marc Coulomb
Titre : Développement asymptotique explicite et matrices de Stokes des E-fonctions hypergéométriques.
Résumé : La famille des E-fonctions hypergéométriques généralise les fonctions de Bessel, de Kummer, et est liée à de nombreuses fonctions spéciales. Le résultat principal est une formule close, explicite, donnant le développement asymptotique de ces fonctions dans tout grand secteur angulaire autorisé. De cette formule découlent la sommation explicite de Borel-Laplace des fonctions hypergéométriques divergentes, ainsi que les matrices de Stokes associées.

b3c985794d5d65de.title: Commensurating actions, amenabilty, and the Sierpiński carpet
b3c985794d5d65de.speaker: Nicolas Matte Bon
b3c985794d5d65de.abstract:
Group actions on CAT(0)-cube complexes play an important role in geometric group theory. A group G has Property FW if every such action has a fixed point. This property is a combinatorial weakening of Kazhdan’s property (T).
I will give an introduction to this property through the point of view of commensurating actions, developed by Cornulier. Then, I will explain that there exist groups with Property FW that are amenable (thus very far from being Kazhdan).
These examples arise from the theory of iterated monodromy group, a class of groups of dynamical origin associated to certain expanding maps on compact spaces. They are related to the classical square Sierpińki carpet.
Joint work with Volodia Nekrashevych and Tianyi Zheng.

b50629e2ea8e03dc.title: Une inégalité isopérimétrique quantitative dans l'espace
b50629e2ea8e03dc.speaker: Gisella Croce
b50629e2ea8e03dc.abstract:
Dans ce séminaire nous allons étudier un problème de stabilité pour l'inégalité isopérimétrique dans $\mathbb{R}^3$, faisant intervenir une asymétrie de type Hausdorff. Pour un corps convexe $F \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ de volume $4\pi/3$ (c'est-à-dire le volume de la boule unité dans l'espace), nous considérons la fonctionnelle \[ Q^*(F) := \frac{\delta(F)\log\bigl(\delta(F)+\delta(F)^{-1}\bigr)P(F)^3} {\lambda^*(F)^2}, \] o\`u $\delta(F)$ d\'esigne le déficit isop\'erim\'etrique, c'est-à-dire la différence entre le périmétre $P(F)$ et le périmètre de la boule unité, et $\displaystyle \lambda^*(F):=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^3} d_H(F,B+x)$
la distance de Hausdorff à la famille des boules unit\'es. Le facteur logarithmique reflète l'échelle capacitaire optimale au voisinage de la boule en dimension trois, tandis que le facteur $P(F)^3$ assure la coercivité. Notre résultat principal est l'existence du minimum de $Q^*$ dans la classe des corps convexes de volume $4\pi/3$.
Ce travail est en collaboration avec S. Bove et G. Pisante.

b535918fd371b710.title: A Cartan Geometry from a Correspondence Space in Riemannian Geometry
b535918fd371b710.speaker: Rodrigo MORÓN SANZ
b535918fd371b710.abstract: Cartan geometries are curved analogues of homogeneous spaces, and the correspondence space construction produces, from a Cartan geometry of one type, another of a different type over a larger base manifold. The unit tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold is, in this language, a Cartan geometry of type (Euc(n), O(n-1)) obtained in this way; we study Cartan geometries of this type in general, whether or not they arise as correspondence spaces. We show that every such geometry induces on its base manifold an almost contact metric structure, together with an orthogonal splitting of the tangent bundle and a compatible linear connection; conversely, these data determine the geometry, so that the correspondence is a bijection. Moreover, we single out a distinguished Cartan connection, which we call normal, by a condition on its torsion formulated in terms of the Spencer differential. This normalization is dictated by the correspondence space construction: the Cartan connection induced on the unit tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold is normal.
b535918fd371b710.organizer: G. Franz, L. Hauswirth, P. Laurain, R. Petrides, R. Souam

b55a4e6cb646027e.title: Two Applications of the Arithmetic Margulis Lemma
b55a4e6cb646027e.speaker: Marc Burger
b55a4e6cb646027e.abstract:
This course has two parts. In the first we will define a general notion of integer point in a higher Teichmüller space and two invariants thereof, the arithmetic dimension and the arithmetic height. The aim is to show finiteness, modulo the mapping class group action, of the number of integer points for which both invariants are bounded.
In the second part we will give the main steps leading to the recent result of Frączyk, Hurtado and Raimbault, stating that the topological complexity of an arithmetic locally symmetric space is bounded by its volume.
Both parts rely on the arithmetic Margulis lemma proven by the same authors as a consequence of Breuillard's height gap theorem.

b5a6c6683d78c1da.abstract: In markets with transaction costs, can super-hedging prices and strategies be explicitly characterized and computed directly from real market data, without relying on dual formulations? This talk presents a constructive approach based on conditional supports and dynamic programming, leading to explicit recursive formulas for super-hedging prices and strategies. The approach is illustrated using real market data.

b5c4e29174571cbe.title: Well-typed program generation, with prenex polymorphism
b5c4e29174571cbe.speaker: Gabriel Scherer
b5c4e29174571cbe.abstract:
Fuzzing” is a popular testing approach where we throw random inputs at a program and check that it respects some expected properties on all inputs. Fuzzing a metaprogram such as a compiler requires producing random input programs. To exercise interesting behaviors of the compiler, we want our input programs to be well-formed in a strong sense, in particular to be well-typed. Generating random well-typed program is difficult when the type-system is powerful, there is a whole scientific literature on the topic, see for example [Testing an Optimising Compiler by Generating Random Lambda Terms, Pałka, 2012].
Most existing generators integrate a large part of the implementation of a type-checker, “inverted” to assist in top-down random term generation by efficiently discarding choices that result in ill-typed programs. Scaling this approach to a full language would result in implementing two sophisticated type-checkers, once in the compiler and once in the program generator. This is one type-checker too many!
We present preliminary work on reusing the constraint-based type inference approach [The Essence of ML-based type inference, Pottier and Rémy, 2004] to write a single type-checker that can be used for both purposes: to check types of user-provided programs, and to efficiently guide a random program generator. This only requires a fairly simple modification to constraint generators: parametrizing them over a search monad. We have succesfully implemented a generator of simply-typed terms in this style, and are in the process (almost done) of scaling it to Hindley-Milner type inference.
(Relevant previous work is [Making Random Judgments: Automatically Generating Well-Typed Terms from the Definition of a Type-System, Fetscher, Claessen, Pałka, Hughes, Findler]. They start from Redex, a Racket DSL to implement simple type systems, and derive a random program generator. The limitation of this approach is that Redex only works with fairly simple type systems, in particular we do not expect it to scale to ML-style type inference with polymorphism, which is the part that hand-crafted generators also struggle on.)
Note: I gave a Formath talk on a preliminary version of this work in March 2024. At the time my prototype only supported the simply-typed lambda-calculus. The extension to Hindley-Milner is follow-up joint work with my 2025 intern Hugo Barreiro. I will also discuss optimizations to the search monad that are necessary to effectively generate terms of larger size.

b767edfc4e552ec3.title: F-CohFTs, their Givental group and tautological relations
b767edfc4e552ec3.speaker: Paolo Rossi
b767edfc4e552ec3.abstract: F-CohFTs are the natural generalization of cohomological field theories (CohFTs) when moving from the Deligne- Mumford compactification of the moduli space of stable curves given by nodal stable curves to the partial compactification given by curves with only separating nodes. They are natural under various viewpoints and were inspired by integrable systems considerations. As it happens for CohFTs, F-CohFTs can be used to probe the cohomology of this partial compactification, based on an analogue of the Givental-Teleman classification of semisimple CohFTs and similar nonsemisimple limiting techniques.

b98f19cd1bde90a5.title: Théorème de l’image directe de Grauert et superconnexions antiholomorphes
b98f19cd1bde90a5.speaker: Shu Shen
b98f19cd1bde90a5.abstract:
Les faisceaux cohérents sont des objets fondamentaux en géométrie complexe. En 1960, Grauert a démontré
que la cohérence est préservée par une application holomorphe propre entre espaces analytiques complexes.
*Dans cet exposé, j’expliquerai comment les superconnexions antiholomorphes permettent de construire une résolution
globale de faisceaux cohérents, conduisant ainsi à une nouvelle démonstration du théorème de l’image directe de Grauert.
Ce travail est en collaboration avec Jianqing Yu.

b9f065779fb1bf55.title: Geometry and arithmetic of special functions
b9f065779fb1bf55.speaker: Kevin Kwan
b9f065779fb1bf55.abstract: There is no universally agreed definition of special functions, but they are generally viewed as the useful functions that arise frequently and naturally in mathematics and broader sciences, with numerous tabulated identities that help solve practical problems. Efforts to bring structure to this seemingly chaotic world have varied in scope and success. In this talk, based on joint work with Akshay Venkatesh and Griffin Wang, I will discuss yet another (partial) attempt that brings geometry and arithmetic of algebraic groups into the study of special functions.

ba7528b34045622d.title: Séparer les composantes des variétés algébriques réelles par des invariants cohomologiques.
ba7528b34045622d.speaker: Samuel Lerbet
ba7528b34045622d.abstract: Si X est une variété algébrique complexe, il suit du théorème de comparaison de M. Artin que X et son lieu complexe X(C) ont le même nombre de composantes connexes, la première pour la topologie de Zariski, le second pour la topologie analytique ou forte. Au contraire, si X est une variété algébrique réelle connexe, son lieu réel X(R) est disconnexe pour la topologie forte en général. On peut néanmoins se demander si l'on peut séparer les composantes connexes de X(R) par des invariants algébriques de X. On peut pour cela utiliser des invariants de nature cohomologique : ainsi, E. Witt a montré que le signe des classes dans le groupe de Brauer d'une courbe algébrique réelle lisse séparent les composantes connexes de son lieu réel. La possibilité d'une telle séparation par un invariant cohomologique de degré donné dépend cependant de la relation entre ce dernier et la dimension : cela motive l'étude de l'optimalité de ce degré pour une dimension donnée. Le but de l'exposé est d'expliquer des résultats autour de cette question pour la séparation par la cohomologie et par son raffinement non ramifié et, si le temps le permet, des applications à la signature globale des formes quadratiques. Il s'agit d'un travail en commun avec Olivier Benoist.

bd3fba0cb87bd7c8.title: Curve counting through intrinsic mirror symmetry
bd3fba0cb87bd7c8.speaker: Michel van Garrel
bd3fba0cb87bd7c8.abstract: According to Mirror Symmetry, the generating function of curve counting Gromov-Witten invariants of a Calabi-Yau threefold is conjectured to equal the integral over the positive real locus of a mirror-dual family of Calabi-Yau threefolds. In this joint work with Siebert, we prove that this conjecture holds as stated in the case of the canonical bundle of the projective plane with its mirror family constructed via the intrinsic mirror construction of Gross-Siebert. A key feature of the proof is that at no point do we calculate any invariants. Instead, we work with the punctured Gromov-Witten invariants that govern the intrinsic mirror construction.

bddfccf00e52b245.title: Torseurs sur la droite affine sous des groupes lisses
bddfccf00e52b245.speaker: Alexis Bouthier
bddfccf00e52b245.abstract:
Si G est réductif sur un corps, un théorème de Raghunathan-Ramanathan énonce que
tout G-torseur sur la droite affine, trivial sur la clôture séparable, est trivial.
Le cas non-réductif avait été écarté d'emblée par les auteurs comme "rather complicated".
On montre qu'un tel énoncé vaut pour tout k-groupe lisse (et même pas lisse du tout).
On discutera également d'autres extensions et généralisations à l'étude des G-torseurs sur des espaces affines.
Travail en commun K. Cesnavicius et F. Scavia.

beb708d5ed3076f7.title: Representation theory of quantum aﬃne algebras via tensor products of modules over hereditary algebras
beb708d5ed3076f7.speaker: Elie CASBI
beb708d5ed3076f7.abstract:
We introduce new families of monoidal structures suited to categorifying important invariants arising in the representation theory of quantum affine algebras and in the theory of cluster algebras. Our framework builds on Auslander--Reiten theory and higher homological algebra; namely, for each finite acyclic quiver QQQ, we construct a monoidal category RQ\mathcal{R}_QRQ​ whose indecomposable objects are tensor products of modules over the path algebra of QQQ. We show that to each indecomposable object XXX in RQ\mathcal{R}_QRQ​ corresponds a (unique up to homotopy) chain complex C∙(X)C_{\bullet}(X)C∙​(X) satisfying remarkable homological properties. These complexes are constructed using some iterated mapping cone procedure, which yields a collection of distinguished triangles in the bounded homotopy category of RQ\mathcal{R}_QRQ​. We then prove that in the case where QQQ is a Dynkin quiver, the Euler characteristics of (the image under a suitable functor of) C∙(X)C_{\bullet}(X)C∙​(X) can be identified with the (truncated) qqq-character of a standard module over the quantum affine algebra Uq(gQ^)U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{g}_Q})Uq​(gQ​​). We also show that the above mentioned distinguished triangles categorify certain exchange relations in the finite type cluster algebra AQ\mathcal{A}_QAQ​. If time allows, we will discuss perspectives towards monoidal categorifications of more general cluster structures.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.
beb708d5ed3076f7.organizer: J. Alev, D. Hernandez, B. Keller, Th. Levasseur, et S. Morier-Genoud.

becf056d0121d7e5.title: Can you compute the operator norm in group C*-algebras?
becf056d0121d7e5.speaker: Isaac Goldbring
becf056d0121d7e5.abstract:
A paper by Fritz, Netzer, and Thom from 2012, titled "Can you compute the operator norm?", in essence initiated the computable structure theory for C*-algebras. The primary question involved is: given some "standard" presentation of a C*-algebra, is there an algorithm for computing the norm on the algebra? In this talk, I will focus on the case of C*-algebras arising from groups. In fact, most of the talk will focus on the case of the following four group C*-algebras: C^*(F_2), C^*(F_2\times F_2), C^*_r(F_2), C^*_r(F_2\times F_2). Here, for a group G, C^*(G) and C^*_r(G) denote the universal and reduced group C*-algebras associated to G, and F_2 denotes the free group on two generators. The answers to the question about computability of the norm for these four group C*-algebras turn out to be: yes, no, yes, and yes. The first is a result of FNT, the second a result due to myself and Thomas Sinclair from a year ago (answering a question of FN,T using recent results from quantum complexity theory), and the third and fourth recent results of mine (answering a question of Sinclair). Time permitting, I will discuss a potential generation of the latter results to wider classes of groups.
No prior knowledge of C*-algebra theory will be assumed.

bfccd867d483b32d.title: Exact-Solvability of Superintegrable Systems
bfccd867d483b32d.speaker: Alexander Turbiner
bfccd867d483b32d.speaker_affiliation: ICN-UNAM, Mexico – Stony Brook Univ., USA – CRM, Canada
bfccd867d483b32d.abstract:
All, so far known explicitly two-dimensional quantum superintegrable systems in flat space are exactly solvable with spectra linear in quantum numbers (in agreement with the Montreal Conjecture by Tempesta-Turbiner-Winternirz (2001)). Their eigenfunctions are bivariate orthogonal polynomials in invariants of the (discrete) symmetry group. It includes the Smorodinsky-Winternitz potentials I-IV (or the Holt potential), the Fokas-Lagerstrom model, the 3-body Calogero (equivalently, A2 rational) and the Wolfes (equivalently, G2 rational, or I6) models, and the Tremblay-Turbiner-Winternitz system with integer index k=1,2,3,4. They have hidden (Lie) algebraic structure g(k) with various k, and they possess a (finite order) polynomial algebras of integrals generated by the Hamiltonian, two algebraically-independent integrals and their commutator.

c02b8c5019c87888.title: Limit of archimedean heights and Ceresa cycles
c02b8c5019c87888.speaker: Souvik Goswami
c02b8c5019c87888.speaker_affiliation: IISER - Indian Institute of Science Education and Research
c02b8c5019c87888.abstract: For a smooth, projective and complex variety $X$, and a pair of algebraic cycles $Z$ and $W$ that are homologous to zero and are in complementary codimensions, the archimedean height pairing is a real number that can be interpreted as a secondary intersection pairing that measures how far a certain cohomology group of the pair $(X\setminus |Z|, |W|)$ is from being real split. This interpretation makes it suitable for variational study: Let $\Delta := \{t\in \mathbb{C};\,|t|<1\}$, and $\Delta^{\ast}=\Delta\setminus \{0\}$. Given a family $\{X_t\}_{t\in \Delta}$ of projective and complex varieties that are smooth for $t\in \Delta^{\ast}$, while $X_0$ is a simple normal crossing divisor, and a family $\{Z_t, W_t\}_{t\in \Delta^{\ast}}$ of algebraic cycles in complementary codimensions that are homologous to zero, the function $h := \Delta^{\ast}\to\mathbb{R}$, with $h(t)$ being the archimedean height pairing of the pair $(Z_t, W_t)$, is smooth. But $h$ does not extend to $t=0$. R.~Hain, G.~Pearlstein, P.~Brosnan et al. have shown that the asymptotic function $\widetilde h(t)= h(t)+\mu \log|t|$ extends continuously to $t=0$, where $\mu\in\mathbb{Q}$ depends on the monodromy of the variation of mixed Hodge structures associated with these pairings. Fixing a parameter $t$, one can ask if $\widetilde h(0)$ is given by the archimedean height pairing of algebraic cycles associated with the central fiber $X_{0}$. In a joint work with Dr. Irene Spelta, I have shown that this question has an affirmative answer in case of height pairings of Ceresa cycles (arxiv.org/abs/2604.01842). The purpose of this talk will be to explore this result and some interesting questions that still remains unanswered.

c08df0626f41e567.title: Combinations of Non-Archimedean Discrete Groups
c08df0626f41e567.speaker: Konstantinos Tsouvalas
c08df0626f41e567.abstract: Chatterji and Venkataramana, motivated by Nori's problem, asked for a real algebraic semisimple Lie group G and a simple Lie subgroup H of G, whether a Zariski-dense discrete subgroup of G, intersecting H in a lattice, is itself a lattice in G. After discussing what is known related to this question and Nori's problem, we will address a similar version of this question for the k-points of semisimple groups defined over a non-Archimedean local field k, and provide examples for which a positive answer fails. This is based on a combination theorem for discrete subgroups of matrix groups over discretely valued fields. We will also discuss a construction of non-Fuchsian hyperbolic groups that quasi-isometrically embed as subgroups of matrix groups over a discretely valued field.

c1f9ef6befcf4e98.title: An affirmative solution to the generalized Busemann-Petty problem with subspaces dimensions 2 and 3
c1f9ef6befcf4e98.speaker: Cheng Lin
c1f9ef6befcf4e98.abstract: The generalized Busemann--Petty problem asks whether two origin-symmetric convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^n$ having larger volume of all $m$-dimensional sections necessarily have larger volume. When $m\geq 4$, this is known to be false, but the cases $m=2, 3$ for $n\geq 5$ have remained open since the 1990s. In this work, we resolve these cases. Together with the known results, the generalized Busemann--Petty problem is completely solved: the answer is affirmative for $m=1, 2, 3$, and negative for $m\geq 4$. This talk is based on the joint work with Yu-de LIU and Ge XIONG.

c364de33b1bcf9f9.title: Finiteness and Density Problems for (Positive) Integral Points on Mordell–Schinzel Surfaces
c364de33b1bcf9f9.speaker: Robin Zhang
c364de33b1bcf9f9.abstract:
Séminaire de géométrie arithmétique
In 1952, Mordell erroneously claimed that the surface xyz = G(x,y) has infinitely many integral points for any G ∈ ℤ[x,y]. I will discuss a classification for finiteness and Zariski density of (positive) integral points on these log K3 surfaces when the coefficients of G are non-negative. This combines a dynamical argument proposed by Mordell, the theory of generalized cluster algebras, and the Killing–Cartan classification of semisimple Lie algebras. This talk is partially based on joint work with Antoine de Saint Germain.

c368155abf23a658.title: On the Euler characteristic and simplicial volume of convex projective manifolds
c368155abf23a658.speaker: Grazia Rago
c368155abf23a658.abstract:
A famous conjecture of Gromov states that, for a closed oriented aspherical manifold, the vanishing of the simplicial volume implies the vanishing of the Euler characteristic.
In this talk, we prove this conjecture for closed oriented real convex projective manifolds by explicitly constructing a bounded cocycle representing their Euler class.
The talk is based on joint work with Michelle Bucher and Stefano Francaviglia.

c4864fa17f638a07.title: Zeta values as moments: A random matrix theory
c4864fa17f638a07.speaker: Hartmut Monien
c4864fa17f638a07.abstract: Values of the Riemann zeta-function $\zeta\left(\alpha+\beta n\right)$ with $\alpha>1$, $\beta>0$ and $n$ a positive integer can be obtained as moments of a certain probability distribution. In my talk I will construct the corresponding random matrix model and determine its asymptotic spectral curve, which exhibits an unusual feature, the complete asymptotics of its partition function and uniform approximations to its correlation functions using a discrete version of Riemann-Hilbert problem with Airy and Bessel asymptotics. This relates a problem in number theory to ideas of Vershik and Okounkov in representation theory of the symmetric group.

c511733100dec7a5.title: A Two-Scale System and Ambient Constructions
c511733100dec7a5.speaker: Mikhail MARKOV
c511733100dec7a5.abstract: Geometric structures can often be understood by realising them in a higher-dimensional space. The Fefferman–Graham ambient construction in conformal geometry and the Eisenhart–Duval lift in nonrelativistic mechanics are two examples of this idea. In this talk, I will describe a common framework for these constructions based on a conformal metric and two scales satisfying the almost-Einstein equation. Besides bringing familiar constructions into a common setting, this approach leads to an ambient description of the spatial and temporal infinities of Ricci-flat spacetimes. I will discuss the geometry behind this description and explain how conformal compactification also brings null infinity into the picture.

c5e5cda85abd7fa5.title: Topological localization in unentangled random braids
c5e5cda85abd7fa5.speaker: Sergei Nechaev
c5e5cda85abd7fa5.abstract: In 2015, P. Serna, G. Bunin, and A. Nahum numerically investigated fluctuations in a bunch of unentangled random threads. They showed that fluctuations of an individual tread in a braid are qualitatively different from those of a thread embedded in a medium of fixed parallel lines. In particular, they observed a logarithmic increase in the transverse span, D, of a thread with its length, N. Studying this problem both numerically and analytically, we propose the following interpretation: the logarithmic regime is an intermediate one, and sufficiently long threads exhibit topological localization, where span D approaches a finite limit at N >> 1. Unlike localization induced by quenched external disorder, this phenomenon arises solely from collective topological constraints, giving rise to topological microphase separation. We study braids within a locally free approximation and confirm the localization by analytical investigation of Brownian bridges on the asymptotic Cayley graph of a locally free group LF_n which approximates the braid group B_{n+1}. We conjecture that topologically induced localization emerges as a phase transition: for a small number of threads, n ~ 3 -- 5, the span, D, grows algebraically with N (N>>1), as D ~ N^{1/4}. By contrast, for large n, each thread in a long braid asymptotically localizes, approaching D ~ const.

c699519255a59a3d.title: Combinatoire des mots, combinatoire énumérative et combinatoire algébrique autour de la forme normale alternante des tresses
c699519255a59a3d.speaker: June Roupin
c699519255a59a3d.abstract:
Les tresses sont des objets topologiques qui possèdent de très bonnes propriétés combinatoires, et peuvent en particulier être représentées et étudiées comme des classes d’équivalence de mots sur l'alphabet des transpositions. Un concept naturel dans ce contexte est la notion de forme normale : le choix d’un représentant unique pour chaque tresse. La forme normale alternante, dont l’étude a initialement été motivée par ses liens avec l’ordre standard des tresses, associe à chaque tresse sur n fils une séquence unique de tresses sur n-1 fils, appelés des blocs, permettant de définir récursivement un unique représentant.
Dans cet exposé, je vais présenter quelques propriétés combinatoires et algébriques importante de la forme normale alternante, notamment la régularité et l'automaticité du langage associé. Je vais ensuite aborder plusieurs applications de ces résultats couvrant divers domaines de combinatoires : énumération des tresses ; bon ordre totale sur le monoïde de tresse ; généralisations aux monoïdes d'Artin-Tits.

c9e0f6e753a79da8.title: Gelfand-Kirillov dimensions and the p-adic Langlands program
c9e0f6e753a79da8.speaker: Reinier SORGDRAGER
c9e0f6e753a79da8.abstract:
This thesis' main results are upper bounds to the Gelfand-Kirillov dimension of certain p-adic representations and some applications of such bounds.
The Gelfand-Kirillov dimension is a generalization of the Krull dimension of modules ovef commutative rings to modules over completed group rings of p-adic Lie groups -- also known as Iwasawa algebras. These Iwasawa algebras act on the duals of p-adic Banach representations or smooth mod p representations of such groups.
The main result is, for p>2 a prime number, that an admissible p-adic Banach representation of GL_2 of a p-adic field K has Gelfand-Kirillov dimension at most the degree [K:Q_p] as soon as its locally analytic vectors admit an infinitesimal character.
The second main result is a generalization of this statement to families of Banach representations with infinitesimal characters in families in the sense of Dospinescu-Paškūnas-Schraen. This result yields a generalization of the GK-bound of Breuil-Herzig-Hu-Morra-Schraen beyond K unramified for the smooth mod p representation given by a Galois isotypic component in the mod p cohomology of Shimura varieties.
The method of proof for both results is much in the spirit of the filtrations of fixed ``radius of analyticity'' of Schneider-Teitelbaum on the duals of the representations and the study of their associated gradeds. The second main result required a generalization of these filtrations to double radii.
Finally, this thesis has two more results. The most important one being that (in the setting of K unramified, only needing the results of Breuil-Herzig-Hu-Morra-Schraen) the GK-bound for mod p cohomology of Shimura varieties allows one, via miracle flatness of the patched module over R_\infty, to compute the derived pro-p Iwahori invariants of the mod p representation as complex over the non-derived pro-p Iwahori Hecke algebra, up to quasi-isomorphism. This derived module turns out to depend only on the mod p Galois representation (and a multiplicity) and not on the global choices that go into the construction of the smooth mod p representation of GL_2.

ca840c48a45a8c70.title: Grid Minors in planar graphs
ca840c48a45a8c70.speaker: Eileen Robinson
ca840c48a45a8c70.abstract:
In 1984, Robertson and Seymour showed that the treewidth of a planar graph with no t × t grid as minor is bounded by a function g(t). Together with Thomas, they later proved that g(t) can be taken to be linear. The current best known bound, due to Gu and Tamaki (2012), is g(t) ≤ 9/2 t − 11/2. In this talk, I will show an improved bound of g(t) ≤ 4t + O(1), which is within a factor 2 of optimal.
This talk is based on joint work with Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Quentin Claus, Gwenaël Joret, Robin Petit and Jean-Florent Raymond.

cd93bd9dd7a3b7b1.title: Conférence de Stéphanie Debette : « Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle »
cd93bd9dd7a3b7b1.abstract:
Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle
La santé cérébrale est un enjeu majeur du XXIᵉ siècle, qui dépasse le seul domaine médical pour toucher aux dimensions sociétales, économiques et stratégiques. Plus d'une personne sur trois sera concernée par une maladie cérébrale au cours de sa vie. Ces maladies sont la première cause de handicap et la deuxième cause de décès dans le monde. Le vieillissement de la population augmente le poids des pathologies liées à l'âge, et les troubles de santé mentale progressent chez les jeunes.
La présentation se concentrera sur les maladies vasculaires cérébrales, particulièrement fréquentes et graves. Parmi elles, la maladie des petits vaisseaux cérébraux est la plus répandue. On peut la repérer tôt en imagerie.
Nous évoquerons les progrès récents dans la compréhension de ses mécanismes biologiques et dans l’analyse d'images cérébrales par intelligence artificielle.
Cette conférence gratuite, sera suivie d’une discussion informelle autour d’un verre de l’amitié

ce5e0a79b4e1c60f.title: Quadratic terms, Lie brackets and local controllability
ce5e0a79b4e1c60f.speaker: Karine Beauchard
ce5e0a79b4e1c60f.abstract:
We study the small-time local controllability, in the vicinity of an equilibrium, of a nonlinear scalar-input system. A natural strategy consists in proving the controllability of the linearized system at the equilibrium and conclude with a local inversion argument. When this linearized system is not controllable, it is necessary to study the quadratic term.
In this talk, we link several recent results on this subject. We also propose a unified methodology to prove quadratic obstructions to local controllability, that relies on systematic drift estimates.
For finite-dimensional control systems, quadratic terms only generate obstructions to controllability: they introduce coercive drifts in the dynamics, quantified by negative integer Sobolev norms of the control, linked to Lie brackets.
In infinite dimension, the same obstructions persist, but two new behaviors occur. First, quadratic obstructions can be due to drifts quantified by other norms (for instance fractional Sobolev norms); their geometric interpretation is challenging. Second, and more strikingly, small-time local controllability can sometimes be recovered from the quadratic expansion.
The tools developed for these studies are also used to understand the influence of higher order terms on the small-time local controllability, for single or multi-input systems, and in other research areas.

d01b4db8ace39d0b.speaker: Felipe Gambardella, Lyuhui Wu, Lucas Mann
d01b4db8ace39d0b.abstract:
14h00-14h40: Felipe Gambardella
Title: Some diophantine and cohomological aspects of fields
Abstract: Over the years, cohomological tools such as Galois cohomology or the Brauer—Manin obstruction have shown to be fruitful in the study rational points and others Diophantine properties. Conversely, Diophantine features such as Tsen's C_1 property or the property of being PAC determine the cohomology of a field partially. In spite of the positive results, the precise relationship between Cohomology and Diophantine properties is not fully understood. In this talk, I will present some Diophantine and Cohomological invariants with a particular focus on their interaction and the variety of tools appearing in their computation.
14h45-14:25: Lyuhui Wu
Title: Theory of non-archimedean plurisubharmonic functions
Abstract: Understanding the asymptotic behavior of Kähler metrics along degenerating families of complex projective manifolds is a fundamental problem in complex geometry. Non-archimedean pluripotential theory, that is, the theory of plurisubharmonic functions in the non-archimedean setting, provides a powerful framework for investigating this problem. In this talk, I will give an overview of non-Archimedean pluripotential theory and discuss some of its applications to complex geometry.
15h30-16h10: Lucas Mann
Title: Six-functor formalisms and representation theory
Abstract: Six-functor formalisms are a powerful tool to capture the formal properties of a cohomology theory. In recent years, the development of abstract six-functor formalisms has shown that they capture a surprising amount of constructions and results, including well-known finiteness conditions and dualities. Even more, six-functor formalisms can be applied in places outside traditional cohomology theories, for example in representation theory. In this talk I will survey the theory of six-functor formalisms and discuss its applications to representations and the local Langlands program.

d29de5a33174494b.title: Delocalisation of the disordered long-range discrete Gaussian chain
d29de5a33174494b.speaker: Corentin Faipeur
d29de5a33174494b.abstract:
The long-range discrete Gaussian chain (DGC) is a 1D height function model with $1/r^\alpha$ interactions between pairs of sites at distance $r$. The DGC is known to delocalise at every temperature when $\alpha>2$ (i.e. the typical height at the origin diverges when the size of the system goes to infinity), to localise when $1<\alpha<2$, and to present a localisation/delocalisation phase transition at $\alpha=2$.
In this talk, we will consider a disordered version of the long-range DGC, obtained by adding an external random field. We will show that this disordered model becomes delocalised at all temperatures for all $\alpha>3/2$, and provide quantitative estimates of this delocalisation phenomenon. If time permits, I will also present a central limit theorem for the height at the origin. Joint work with Christopher Chalhoub, Paul Dario and Arnaud Le Ny.
