rec.title: Using AI in mathematical research
rec.speaker: Andrew Pearce-Crump
rec.abstract: AI systems have recently contributed to new results across mathematics, several of them in number theory. This talk is about the everyday version: how a working mathematician can use AI for a research project. I will go back to a paper from my PhD with Chris Hughes, about the moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function at its zeros, and ask how I would have worked on it had AI been available then. The emphasis is on habits that mathematicians already have, and how they apply to mathematical research in the age of AI.

rec.title: The first moment of symmetric cube $L$-functions and applications
rec.speaker: Anders Södergren
rec.abstract: In this talk I will present joint work with Bingrong Huang in which we establish an asymptotic formula for the first moment of symmetric cube central $L$-values over Hecke-Maass forms in short spectral windows. Applications include a quantitative non-vanishing result and an almost-all Lindelöf bound.

rec.title: Modular symbols in arithmetic progressions
rec.speaker: Svenja Zur Verth
rec.abstract: Motivated by conjectures of Mazur, Rubin and Stein, the distribution of modular symbols has received a lot of attention in recent years. Notably, Petridis and Risager showed that modular symbols are asymptotically normally distributed when averaged over all denominators. A natural next step is to restrict the denominators to sparser sets, such as squarefree numbers. This requires understanding modular symbols in arithmetic progressions. Using spectral methods for Eisenstein series twisted by modular symbols, we make the dependence on the modulus explicit in the first two terms of all even moments, and in the full main term of the fourth moment. As an application, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the fourth moment over squarefree denominators.

rec.title: An affirmative solution to the generalized Busemann-Petty problem with subspaces dimensions 2 and 3
rec.speaker: Cheng Lin
rec.abstract: The generalized Busemann--Petty problem asks whether two origin-symmetric convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^n$ having larger volume of all $m$-dimensional sections necessarily have larger volume. When $m\geq 4$, this is known to be false, but the cases $m=2, 3$ for $n\geq 5$ have remained open since the 1990s. In this work, we resolve these cases. Together with the known results, the generalized Busemann--Petty problem is completely solved: the answer is affirmative for $m=1, 2, 3$, and negative for $m\geq 4$. This talk is based on the joint work with Yu-de LIU and Ge XIONG.

rec.title: IHP School: Artificial Intelligence for Mathematicians and Theoretical Physicists
rec.abstract:
Recent breakthroughs have shown that AI can now prove theorems. At the same time, many of the deepest open questions about AI are, at heart, questions of mathematics and physics: high-dimensional geometry, non-convex optimisation, the statistical mechanics of learning. AI is becoming both a tool for and a subject of research in our fields, and a working knowledge of it is fast becoming essential for every young researcher.
This one-week school, funded by Qube Research & Technologies, will introduce the fundamental concepts of modern AI. It is designed for PhD students and early-career researchers in mathematics and theoretical physics with no prior specialisation in AI. The programme combines lectures with hands-on lab sessions.

rec.title: Exact curve counting on the once-punctured torus
rec.speaker: Mingkun Liu
rec.abstract: Two closed curves on a surface are said to have the same topological type if they lie in the same mapping class group orbit. Mirzakhani first showed that, on a hyperbolic surface, the number of closed geodesics of a given topological type of length at most L is asymptotically proportional to L^{6g-6}. In this talk, we will focus on the case of the once-punctured torus. Rather than using hyperbolic length, we will count curves according to their word length. In this setting, it turns out that exact counting formulas can be obtained. This is joint work with Filippo Baroni and David Fisac.

rec.title: An Introduction to D-Modules
rec.speaker: Raoul Hallopeau
rec.abstract: The theory of D-modules had initially been developed for complex (algebraic and analytic) varieties in the 1970's, and allows for an algebraic approach of partial differential equations. There are lots of applications; for instance, in the 1980's Masaki Kashiwara and Zoghman Mebkhout have used it to generalize the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. D-modules are also an invaluable tool in less expected areas, such as Representation Theory. In more recent years, D-modules have also found applications to the world of arithmetic varieties.

rec.title: The p-adic Riemann-Hilbert Correspondence
rec.speaker: Enguerrand Moulinier
rec.abstract: In this talk, I will introduce differential equations on p-adic analytic varieties. We will see how the ultrametric p-adic topology is an obstruction to a Cauchy-Lipschitz-type result. I will then show, following Scholze, how the pro-étale topology and the introduction of new numbers called "periods" provide a workaround to this issue.

rec.title: De la modélisation aux problèmes inverses : une méthodologie pour les systèmes dynamiques en biomédecine.
rec.speaker: Pierre Monmarché
rec.abstract:
Oratrice : Annabelle Collin (Université de Nantes)
Résumé : Les systèmes dynamiques constituent un cadre naturel pour décrire l'évolution temporelle et spatiale de nombreux phénomènes rencontrés en biologie, et en médecine. Qu'ils soient formulés sous la forme d'équations différentielles ordinaires (EDO) ou d'équations aux dérivées partielles (EDP), ces modèles permettent de formaliser des mécanismes biologiques, physiologiques ou épidémiologiques et d'étudier leur dynamique.
Dans cet exposé, nous présenterons les principales étapes d'une démarche de modélisation mathématique appliquée à des problématiques biomédicales : construction et formalisation du modèle, étude de ses propriétés théoriques, approximation numérique, puis confrontation du modèle aux données à travers la résolution de problèmes inverses. Une attention particulière sera portée à l'estimation de paramètres et d'états non directement observables, ainsi qu'aux difficultés associées à l'identifiabilité, aux incertitudes et au caractère potentiellement bruité ou incomplet des observations.
Nous nous intéresserons plus particulièrement aux approches séquentielles, qui permettent de mettre à jour progressivement l'estimation de l'état du système et de ses paramètres au fur et à mesure de l'acquisition de nouvelles données.
Cette démarche sera illustrée sur un exemple volontairement simple, permettant de mettre en évidence les principales étapes méthodologiques tout en montrant comment des modèles relativement parcimonieux peuvent déjà conduire à des résultats quantitatifs pertinents et exploitables dans un contexte de santé publique.

rec.title: Limit of archimedean heights and Ceresa cycles
rec.speaker: Souvik Goswami
rec.speaker_affiliation: IISER - Indian Institute of Science Education and Research
rec.abstract: For a smooth, projective and complex variety $X$, and a pair of algebraic cycles $Z$ and $W$ that are homologous to zero and are in complementary codimensions, the archimedean height pairing is a real number that can be interpreted as a secondary intersection pairing that measures how far a certain cohomology group of the pair $(X\setminus |Z|, |W|)$ is from being real split. This interpretation makes it suitable for variational study: Let $\Delta := \{t\in \mathbb{C};\,|t|<1\}$, and $\Delta^{\ast}=\Delta\setminus \{0\}$. Given a family $\{X_t\}_{t\in \Delta}$ of projective and complex varieties that are smooth for $t\in \Delta^{\ast}$, while $X_0$ is a simple normal crossing divisor, and a family $\{Z_t, W_t\}_{t\in \Delta^{\ast}}$ of algebraic cycles in complementary codimensions that are homologous to zero, the function $h := \Delta^{\ast}\to\mathbb{R}$, with $h(t)$ being the archimedean height pairing of the pair $(Z_t, W_t)$, is smooth. But $h$ does not extend to $t=0$. R.~Hain, G.~Pearlstein, P.~Brosnan et al. have shown that the asymptotic function $\widetilde h(t)= h(t)+\mu \log|t|$ extends continuously to $t=0$, where $\mu\in\mathbb{Q}$ depends on the monodromy of the variation of mixed Hodge structures associated with these pairings. Fixing a parameter $t$, one can ask if $\widetilde h(0)$ is given by the archimedean height pairing of algebraic cycles associated with the central fiber $X_{0}$. In a joint work with Dr. Irene Spelta, I have shown that this question has an affirmative answer in case of height pairings of Ceresa cycles (arxiv.org/abs/2604.01842). The purpose of this talk will be to explore this result and some interesting questions that still remains unanswered.

rec.title: Exposés de Marco Di Marco et Jean-François Babadjian
rec.abstract:
Marco Di Marco :
Title: Quantization of measures in Carnot groups
Abstract: The aim of the talk is to present a sub-Riemannian analogue of the celebrated Zador theorem, a cornerstone of the theory of quantization of measures. After a brief introduction to sub-Riemannian geometry and Carnot groups, I will outline the key ideas behind the proof of the Euclidean Zador theorem and its sub-Riemannian version. Talk based on a joint work with Mikaela Iacobelli.
Jean-François Babadjian :
Titre : Energies de surfaces anisotropes, courbure et approximation champ de phase
Résumé : Dans cet exposé, je présenterai des résultats obtenus en collaboration avec Blanche Buet (LMO, Orsay) et Michaël Goldman (LAMA, Créteil) concernant les effets régularisants de termes de type courbure moyenne pour les modèles avec interface en présence d'anisotropie. Lorsque la tension superficielle est une fonction convexe de la normale, l'anisotropie est dite faible. Ceci assure généralement la semi-continuité inférieure de l'énergie associée. En revanche, si la tension superficielle dépend de la normale de manière non convexe, cette forte anisotropie peut engendrer des instabilités liées à l'absence de semi-continuité inférieure de la fonctionnelle. Nous étudions les effets régularisants de l'ajout d'un terme d'ordre supérieur de type Willmore à l'énergie. Nous considérons deux types de problèmes : une généralisation anisotrope non convexe du périmètre et une fonctionnelle aux discontinuités libres de Mumford-Shah, anisotrope non convexe. Dans les deux cas, nous établissons les propriétés de semi-continuité inférieure des énergies, ainsi qu'une approximation par Gamma-convergence par des modèles de champ de phase. L'un des aspects originaux de notre travail dans le cadre des problèmes à discontinuités libres est le traitement des énergies de points qui repose sur un résultat de type Gauss-Bonnet pour les varifolds.

rec.title: An equivariant version of Gabber’s lemma
rec.speaker: Filippo Belfiori
rec.abstract: Gabber’s preparation lemma is a fundamental result in algebraic geometry, originally established by Gabber in 1994 in his work on the exactness of certain Gersten complexes. Following the work of Morel, Gabber’s lemma has become a cornerstone of motivic homotopy theory over fields, the homotopy theory of algebraic varieties. When algebraic varieties are equipped with an action of an algebraic group G, one can similarly define an equivariant motivic homotopy category, providing a framework for studying the homotopy theory of varieties with G-action. In this talk, I will first recall Gabber’s preparation lemma and discuss some of its main consequences. I will then propose and study an equivariant version of Gabber’s lemma for a finite constant abelian group G, based on the C2-equivariant version introduced by Bachmann. If time permits, I will also discuss some applications of this equivariant version of Gabber’s lemma.
rec.location_text: Salle Pierre Grisvard, IHP - Bâtiment Borel

rec.title: Good complexifications of nonnegatively curved manifolds
rec.speaker: Ethan Peng
rec.abstract: A closed manifold M admits a good complexification if it is diffeomorphic to the set of real points of a real affine variety X such that the embedding X(R) -> X(C) is a homotopy equivalence. We will give examples of such closed manifolds, including classical ones (spheres, RP2, homogeneous spaces, Cheeger manifolds), as well as a class of closed Riemannian manifolds with non-negative sectional curvature constructed by B. Totaro using plumbing techniques. We will also discuss topological constraints on closed manifolds admitting a good complexification, such as the classical non-negativity of its Euler characteristic, and vanishing of some Betti numbers and Pontryagin numbers as proved by Totaro. An effort will be made to explain how the curvature constraints interplay with the algebro-geometric aspects. If time permits, we will also discuss how good complexifications pass to quotients by nice group actions, giving ways to "algebraicize" various familiar manifolds.

rec.title: Zeta values as moments: A random matrix theory
rec.speaker: Hartmut Monien
rec.abstract: Values of the Riemann zeta-function $\zeta\left(\alpha+\beta n\right)$ with $\alpha>1$, $\beta>0$ and $n$ a positive integer can be obtained as moments of a certain probability distribution. In my talk I will construct the corresponding random matrix model and determine its asymptotic spectral curve, which exhibits an unusual feature, the complete asymptotics of its partition function and uniform approximations to its correlation functions using a discrete version of Riemann-Hilbert problem with Airy and Bessel asymptotics. This relates a problem in number theory to ideas of Vershik and Okounkov in representation theory of the symmetric group.

rec.title: Topological localization in unentangled random braids
rec.speaker: Sergei Nechaev
rec.abstract: In 2015, P. Serna, G. Bunin, and A. Nahum numerically investigated fluctuations in a bunch of unentangled random threads. They showed that fluctuations of an individual tread in a braid are qualitatively different from those of a thread embedded in a medium of fixed parallel lines. In particular, they observed a logarithmic increase in the transverse span, D, of a thread with its length, N. Studying this problem both numerically and analytically, we propose the following interpretation: the logarithmic regime is an intermediate one, and sufficiently long threads exhibit topological localization, where span D approaches a finite limit at N >> 1. Unlike localization induced by quenched external disorder, this phenomenon arises solely from collective topological constraints, giving rise to topological microphase separation. We study braids within a locally free approximation and confirm the localization by analytical investigation of Brownian bridges on the asymptotic Cayley graph of a locally free group LF_n which approximates the braid group B_{n+1}. We conjecture that topologically induced localization emerges as a phase transition: for a small number of threads, n ~ 3 -- 5, the span, D, grows algebraically with N (N>>1), as D ~ N^{1/4}. By contrast, for large n, each thread in a long braid asymptotically localizes, approaching D ~ const.

rec.title: Introduction to crystalline cohomology
rec.speaker: Livia Grammatica
rec.abstract: Arithmetic geometers study problems from number theory using tools inspired by differential geometry or topology. To achieve this they have defined, over the years, many algebraic counterparts to the classical cohomology groups of topology. Crystalline cohomology is one of these counterparts, and it is extremely useful for studying varieties in positive and mixed characteristic. In this talk, we will present its fundamental properties and show how to compute it using the de Rham cohomology of lifts to characteristic 0.
rec.location_text: Salle Pierre Grisvard, IHP - Bâtiment Borel

rec.title: Beyond crystalline cohomology, rigid cohomology
rec.speaker: Thomas Serafini
rec.abstract: Crystalline cohomology is not a "good" cohomology for non-proper varieties - for instance, the crystalline H1 of the affine line is not finite-dimensional. Following ideas from Monsky and Washnitzer, Berthelot defined rigid cohomology on general varieties in characteristic p > 0, which provides the "right" extension of crystalline cohomology to arbitrary varieties. The central idea is that of overconvergence, i.e. considering analytic functions that converge not on a p-adic lifting of the variety, but rather on a neighborhood of it. Following and detailing the example of the affine line, we will build to the definition of rigid cohomology and explain its relation to p-adic differential equations.

rec.title: Conférence de Stéphanie Debette, « Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle »
rec.abstract:
« Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle »
La santé cérébrale est un enjeu majeur du XXIᵉ siècle, qui dépasse le seul domaine médical pour toucher aux dimensions sociétales, économiques et stratégiques. Plus d'une personne sur trois sera concernée par une maladie cérébrale au cours de sa vie. Ces maladies sont la première cause de handicap et la deuxième cause de décès dans le monde. Le vieillissement de la population augmente le poids des pathologies liées à l'âge, et les troubles de santé mentale progressent chez les jeunes.
La présentation se concentrera sur les maladies vasculaires cérébrales, particulièrement fréquentes et graves. Parmi elles, la maladie des petits vaisseaux cérébraux est la plus répandue. On peut la repérer tôt en imagerie.
Nous évoquerons les progrès récents dans la compréhension de ses mécanismes biologiques et dans l’analyse d'images cérébrales par intelligence artificielle
Cette conférence hybride sera suivie d'un moment convivial.

rec.title: Origami Tori
rec.speaker: Richard Schwartz
rec.abstract:
An origami torus is a piecewise affine isometric embedding of a flat torus into R3. It is surprising that these things exist, but thanks to the work of Burago and Zalgaller in 1960 they do. 30 years later, B&Z proved that every flat torus is realized as an origami torus. In 2023, Lazarus and Tallerie proved that you can realize all flat tori using a single underlying triangulation with about 2500 vertices.
The question remained: how many vertices do you need to make an origami torus? In this talk I will prove that the minimum number of vertices needed is 8. I will also discuss joint work, with Peter Doyle, proving that almost every flat torus is represented by an 8-vertex origami torus. Finally, I will explain work-in-progress with Doyle, Fabian Lander, and Steve Trettel, which shows that in fact every flat torus is represented by an 8-vertex origami torus. If I have time, I will also discuss hyperbolic versions of this business.

rec.title: Families of Discrete Representations from Incidence Theorems
rec.speaker: Jean-Philippe Burelle
rec.abstract: Motivated by a family of examples constructed by R. Schwartz based on Pappus's theorem, we explore constructions of representations of discrete groups arising from incidence theorems in projective spaces. Schwartz recently proved that his construction parametrizes the boundary of a connected component of Anosov representations in a certain moduli space of representations of PSL(2,Z) into Isom(SL(3,R)/SO(3)). We use a generalized version of Pappus's theorem to define a higher dimensional analogue of this family, and we prove that in RP3 these representations are "extended geometrically finite", a notion of relative Anosov representation introduced by T. Weisman. This is joint work in progress with W. Dimoune.

rec.title: Nonrelativistic Conformal Collider Physics of Multiparticle Point Production
rec.speaker: Dam Thanh Son
rec.abstract:
Motivated by nuclear experiments where a few neutrons are produced by a local source, we develop a formalism of "nonrelativistic conformal collider physics." We define detector operators in the nonrelativistic conformal field theory describing fermions at unitarity. We reduce the problem of computing the momentum distribution and correlation between final particles produced by a local source ("point-produced") to the computation of correlation functions involving the detector operators. The general formalism is applied to the point production of three unitary fermions, where we find the momentum and angular distribution of final particles, and point production of a large number of fermions. We discuss a nonrelativistic version of celestial holography, which maps the asymptotic out-state to a quantum wave function in the so-called "oscillator frame." Based on arXiv:2608.18202 with Cyuan-Han Chang, Subham Dutta Chowdhury, and Ian Moult.

rec.title: On the Wilson-Fisher Fixed Point in the Limit of Integer Spacetime Dimensions
rec.speaker: Bernardo Zan
rec.abstract:
The Wilson–Fisher (WF) fixed point, a scalar field theory with a quartic interaction in $d = 4 - \epsilon$ dimensions, is the textbook example of a weakly coupled CFT. The epsilon expansion accurately reproduces the critical exponents of the $d = 3$ and the $d = 2$ Ising model. This has led to the common view that WF defines a continuous family of CFTs in non-integer dimensions, interpolating between the free theory at $d=4$ and the Ising model at $d = 3$ and $d = 2$. In this talk I will look at what happens to the WF CFT when the number of dimensions approaches an integer value. Identifying the $d\to 2$ limit of WF as the $2d$ Ising CFT raises some issues, related to the fact that the $d=2$ CFT has infinitely many conserved currents that the $d>2$ theory does not have. I will propose a scenario, inspired by some exactly solved two-dimensional models, where the $d\to 2$ limit of WF contains the $d=2$ Ising CFT as a subsector, but contains more operators which do not completely decouple from the Ising subsector. I will explain why this makes the task of obtaining a $d= 2 + \epsilon$ expansion for the Ising model harder.

rec.title: The Messy Story of Crossing Dispersion Relations
rec.speaker: Andrea Guerrieri
rec.abstract:
In this talk I will discuss an attempt of unifying under a simple geometric picture, the plethora of crossing symmetric dispersion relations existing in literature.
Each dispersion is valid on a different finite window in energy, but none of them could be extended to infinity.
I will explain how they can all be understood from a simple choice of a foliation of the kinematics space.
This geometric viewpoint also suggests the existence of a particular (but not so nice) foliation that naturally covers all energies. Unfortunately, this example turns out to be impractical for phenomenological and bootstrap applications. I will comment why, and what teaches us about the dual bootstrap.

rec.title: Proliferation Transitions for Non-Abelian Anyons
rec.speaker: Andrea Antinucci
rec.abstract:
Phases of matter and the transitions between them are famously characterized within the Landau paradigm and Landau–Ginzburg theory: phases are labeled by broken or unbroken symmetries, while phase transitions are described in terms of scalar order parameters. There are, however, phases beyond the standard Landau paradigm that are distinguished not by the realization of ordinary symmetries, but by that of generalized global symmetries. Among these, topologically ordered phases in (2+1)d possess non-invertible 1-form symmetries described by anyon lines. In this talk, I will present a framework for describing transitions between topologically ordered phases related by anyon proliferation, which can be viewed as a non-invertible generalization of the choice of the unbroken symmetry. The resulting theories involve scalar fields coupled to gauge fields. A crucial ingredient in this construction is the (3+1)d Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), which allows to separate symmetry from dynamics and will be employed in a rather unconventional way.

rec.title: AI for Math: From Group Theory to Discrete Holography
rec.speaker: Fedor Levkovich-Maslyuk
rec.abstract: I will describe how one can use modern machine learning methods to attack open problems in group theory. I will show how ideas from AI, pure math, integrability, string theory and quantum information meet here in a highly productive way. I will focus on much-studied Cayley graphs of permutation groups, which are often very hard to explore due to their enormous size. I will describe how a modern ML approach overcomes this challenge and provides efficient pathfinding on these huge graphs. The outcome is a large set of new results and conjectures that in particular sharpen famous bounds on the diameters of these graphs. These results also hint at the existence of a novel, discrete string-like duality for this setting. It provides a realisation of the paradigm "complexity = volume" from AdS/CFT holography, and may potentially be applicable to a wider range of AI tasks. Lastly I will outline some new results for combinatorics of quantum periods and how this could help in improving these ML approaches. Based on arXiv:2509.19162, 2603.22195 and work to appear. Our code is publicly available as the CayleyPy library.

In this talk, we consider an analogue for the p-adic period spaces introduced by Rapoport and Zink. We give a partial criterion for the existence of a Siegel domain and discuss its expected applications.

rec.title: The Pentagram Map and Ramifications
rec.abstract:
October 12-15, 2026
at IHES - Marilyn and James Simons Conference Center
How to get to IHES
This workshop explores the mathematics connected to the pentagram map and its generalizations.
With 3 talks per day, spread out over 4 days, leaving time for individualized interactions, it will not be confined to the special topic of the pentagram map, but rather an exploration of the kind of mathematics that it relates to: integrable systems, algebraic dynamics, projective geometry and cluster algebras.
The pentagram map is a geometrically flavored dynamical system defined on polygons by a simple and projectively natural straight-line construction.
Starting with a polygon, one intersects the shortest diagonals in cyclic order to produce a new polygon with the same number of vertices.
Though quite elementary to define, the pentagram map turns out to have a deep structure connected to completely integrable systems, symplectic geometry, cluster algebras, dimers, algebraic dynamics, and moduli spaces.
The same goes for the many generalizations of the pentagram map, some of which are still quite mysterious.

rec.title: Dynamical Tidal Response of Neutron Stars from Scattering Amplitudes
rec.speaker: Muddu Venkata Sai Saketh
rec.speaker_affiliation: International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS-TIFR), Bengaluru, India
rec.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
In this talk I will describe an amplitude-based framework for extracting the frequency-dependent tidal response of neutron stars while preserving the tidal resonances associated with their normal modes. The response is obtained by matching the amplitude for gravitational-wave scattering off a neutron star, equivalently gravitational Compton scattering, computed using relativistic stellar perturbation theory, to the corresponding amplitude in worldline effective field theory. The tidal contribution is isolated through the difference between the neutron-star and black-hole scattering phases. Unlike conventional treatments, the construction allows for a post-Newtonian expansion without Taylor expanding the response in frequency or assuming a harmonic-oscillator model for the internal dynamics.
I will present the tidal response through relative third post-Newtonian (3PN) order and use currently available numerical results to illustrate its frequency dependence. The results reproduce the known static Love numbers in the low-frequency limit, exhibit resonances at the expected stellar mode frequencies, and capture their damping through gravitational-wave emission. I will also discuss the renormalisation of the tidal response required through 3PN order. Time permitting, I will outline how the resulting response can be incorporated into binary dynamics and ultimately into gravitational waveforms.

rec.title: Zeta Values as Moments: A Random Matrix Theory
rec.speaker: Hartmut Monien
rec.abstract: The values of the Riemann zeta-function $\zeta\left(\alpha+\beta n\right)$ with $\alpha>1$, $\beta>0$ and $n$ a positive integer can be viewed as moments of a probability distribution. In my talk I will construct the corresponding random matrix model and determine its asymptotic spectral curve, which exhibits an unusual feature, the complete asymptotics of its partition function and uniform approximations to its correlation functions using a discrete version of Riemann-Hilbert problem with Airy and Bessel asymptotics. This relates a problem in number theory to ideas of Vershik and Okounkov in the representation theory of the symmetric group.

rec.title: Gravitational Sommerfeld Effects: Framework and Applications
rec.speaker: Chia-Hsien Shen
rec.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
Sommerfeld effects describe long-distance corrections to radiation emitted by a short-distance source. They play an important role in atomic physics and dark matter phenomenology, but the same mechanism also arises in gravitational-wave radiation from compact binaries. In this talk, I will develop a systematic framework for gravitational Sommerfeld effects by combining worldline effective field theory with black hole perturbation theory. A key advantage of this framework is that it organizes high-order perturbative calculations without requiring any nontrivial loop integration, allowing us to compute the waveform to tenth order in the perturbative expansion and beyond. The formulation also reveals an exact connection between the radiation waveform and Compton scattering, as well as the underlying structures of the classical renormalization group of the multipoles and tidal Love numbers. I will conclude by discussing how these results can be incorporated into waveform resummation models for gravitational-wave signals. This talk is based on arXiv:2604.14112 with Chih-Hao Chang and Zihan Zhou, and work in progress.

rec.title: The Doubly Conformal Dispersion Relation
rec.speaker: Balt van Rees
rec.abstract:
We provide a simple derivation of the conformal dispersion relation of Carmi and Caron-Huot which reconstructs a CFT four-point function from its double discontinuity. We exhibit a hidden conformal symmetry which explains the appearance of the "magic variable" x as a simple cross-ratio, built from four physical cross-ratios. We also introduce a regulator in the double discontinuity operation and then prove that one subtraction suffices for all integrals to converge.

rec.title: Conférence de Stéphanie Debette : « Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle »
rec.abstract:
Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle
La santé cérébrale est un enjeu majeur du XXIᵉ siècle, qui dépasse le seul domaine médical pour toucher aux dimensions sociétales, économiques et stratégiques. Plus d'une personne sur trois sera concernée par une maladie cérébrale au cours de sa vie. Ces maladies sont la première cause de handicap et la deuxième cause de décès dans le monde. Le vieillissement de la population augmente le poids des pathologies liées à l'âge, et les troubles de santé mentale progressent chez les jeunes.
La présentation se concentrera sur les maladies vasculaires cérébrales, particulièrement fréquentes et graves. Parmi elles, la maladie des petits vaisseaux cérébraux est la plus répandue. On peut la repérer tôt en imagerie.
Nous évoquerons les progrès récents dans la compréhension de ses mécanismes biologiques et dans l’analyse d'images cérébrales par intelligence artificielle.

rec.title: Horizon flux-balance laws in the multiscale perturbation
rec.speaker: Ali M. Seraj
rec.speaker_affiliation: Institute for Research in Fundamental Sciences (IPM), Tehran
rec.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
I study the evolution of the event horizon in a “two-timescale” perturbative expansion around a stationary black hole. This leads to strong constraints on the “coarse-grained” horizon dynamics. At leading order, the horizon exhibits an “adiabatic rigidity”: the leading corrections to its angular velocity and inaffinity remain uniform on each horizon cut, while evolving on the slow timescale. We then provide a systematic procedure for transforming a perturbative bulk solution, given for example in Lorenz gauge, to an ingoing Newman--Unti gauge adapted to the horizon, allowing the perturbed horizon geometry to be extracted directly from the metric. Finally, we formulate “horizon conservation laws” associated with horizon symmetries, including energy, dynamical entropy, and angular momentum. We expand the charges through second order and their fluxes through third order in perturbation theory, providing a framework for future applications to horizon absorption and backreaction in extreme mass-ratio inspirals.

rec.title: Maximal functions, Nikodym sets and local smoothing estimates
rec.speaker: Chen Mingfeng
rec.abstract:
Séminaire d'Analyse
I will discuss some recent works related to maximal operators and Nikodym sets in the plane. Nikodym constructed a measure-zero Borel set in the plane that contains a line segment passing through each point in the unit square. Fenton and Falconer asked whether a similar construction is possible when “lines through a point” are replaced by ”circles with a prescribed center.” This was answered in the negative by Bourgain and Marstrand. We study a generalization of this question, in which “lines through a point” or “circles with prescribed center” are replaced by general analytic families of plane curves.
Using decouping, we prove new maximal function and local smoothing estimates for families of curves satisfying a multi-parameter analogue of Sogge's cinematic curvature condition. Combining with a recent nonlinear generalization of Falconer's prescribed projection theorem to construct Nikodym-type sets, we characterize when Nikodym-type sets exist for analytic families of plane curves.

rec.title: Near-horizon Collisions at the Extreme: Naturalness and Observability of Critical Near-horizon Collisions around Near-extremal Black Holes
rec.speaker: Delilah Gates
rec.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
In principle, rapidly rotating black holes could naturally act as particle colliders because geodesics particles that collide can exhibit center-of-mass (CM) energies that diverges in the limit that the black hole approaches extremality and the collision radius approaches the horizon, provided that one particle has a critically tuned angular momentum. In this talk, I present work to understand the naturalness and observability of these critical-particle collisions around near-extremal BHs. I will highlight 1) the landscape of conditions under which these critical-particle collisions occur, 2) the CM energy achievable for critical-particle collision where one particle falls from in from infinity and the other particle is part of an accretion disk, and 3) the observability as measure by the escape probability and expected energy of emission born of a critical-particle collision.

rec.title: The Stratified Shape
rec.speaker: Marco Volpe
rec.abstract:
In this talk, I will try to address the question of how to do algebraic topology with stratified spaces and schemes in a meaningful way. I will begin by recalling and motivating some of the main historical attempts to approach this question, both in topology and in algebraic geometry, passing through the work of Nash, Quinn, Siebenmann, Edwards–Hastings, Deligne, and, more recently, Lurie and Barwick–Glasman–Haine. I will then propose my own answer, based on a construction I call the stratified shape.
Time permitting, I will discuss some applications of the stratified shape to proper homotopy theory (joint with Georg Lehner), homology manifolds (joint with Markus Land), and a generalization of Lurie's exodromy equivalence (joint with Peter Haine and Guglielmo Nocera).

rec.title: Algebraic Theory of Indefinite Theta Functions
rec.speaker: Kenz Kallal
rec.abstract:
Séminaire de géométrie arithmétique
Jacobi's theta function $\Theta(q) := 1 + 2q + 2q^4 + 2q^9 + \cdots $, and more generally the theta functions associated to positive-definite quadratic forms, have the property that they are modular forms of half-integral weight. The usual proof of this fact is completely analytic in nature, using the Poisson summation formula. However, $\Theta$ is also related to diffusion of heat on a uniform circle-shaped material: it is a restriction of the fundamental solution to the heat equation on a circle. By algebraically characterizing the heat equation as a specific flat connection on a certain bundle on a modular curve, we produce a completely algebraic technique for proving modularity of theta functions. More specifically, we produce a refinement of the algebraic theory of theta functions due to Moret-Bailly, Faltings--Chai, and Candelori. As a consequence of the algebraic nature of our theory and the fact that it applies to indefinite quadratic forms / non-ample line bundles (which the prior algebraic theory does not), we also generalize the Kudla--Millson analytic theory of theta functions for indefinite quadratic forms to the case of torsion coefficients. This is joint work with Akshay Venkatesh.

Depuis bientôt une quinzaine d’années l’axe math-physique de la FMJH organise un séminaire Itzykson tous les ans à l’IHES. Il s’agit d’une journée consacrée à un thème de physique mathématique, avec un cours et deux ou trois exposés spécialisés (en français ou en anglais selon le choix des orateurs).
Le prochain séminaire Itzykson portera sur la dualité markovienne, et ses liens avec les algèbres de Lie et les systèmes de particules en interaction. Ces sujets sont reliés par une même idée directrice : l'approche algébrique de la dualité, qui permet de construire et d'analyser des processus markoviens exactement solubles. Le séminaire donnera des perspectives algébriques, probabilistes et physiques sur des résultats récents, notamment au sujet des symétries des générateurs markoviens, des interprétations trajectorielles en génétique des populations, et des fluctuations macroscopiques hors d'équilibre.

rec.title: Scattering and Smoothing for the Two-Dimensional Cubic Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation
rec.speaker: Muyuan Lyu
rec.abstract:
Séminaire d'Analyse
Scattering theory describes the large-time behavior of nonlinear evolution equations through comparison with a linear flow. This raises a further question: can the nonlinear correction to the asymptotic state be smoother than the initial data?
I will begin with an introduction to scattering for nonlinear Schrödinger equations, highlighting several developments that motivate this question. I will then present a deterministic smoothing result for the two-dimensional cubic equation. Assuming that a solution scatters in the harmonic Sobolev space $(\mathcal H^s)$, with $(s>0)$, the difference between its scattering state and its initial datum belongs to $(\mathcal H^{s+\sigma})$ for every $(0<\sigma<\min{2s,1})$. The proof combines the lens transform, which turns the large-time problem into a finite-time endpoint problem, with bilinear Strichartz estimates and harmonic spectral analysis. The emphasis will be on the mechanism behind the regularity gain.

rec.speaker: Thomas Mordant
rec.abstract:

AI and the Future of Mathematics and Physics
The Jacobian conjecture states that for any polynomial map from to itself, if it is everywhere a local diffeomorphism, then it admits a polynomial global inverse. In this talk, I will present the three-dimensional counterexample to this conjecture posted by L. Alpöge on and credited to Claude.
After stating the conjecture and the counterexample, I will explain the geometric interpretation of the counterexample which was posted by A. Jiang and credited to ChatGPT. Finally I will give some observations about the history of the conjecture and its significance.
We answer this problem coming from representation theory using topological tools. On the representation theory side we define extensions of Habiro type rings. On the topological side, we construct a universal Jones link invariant and a universal Alexander link invariant. Putting these together, our universal invariants of geometrical nature take values in the extended Habiro rings that we construct.

rec.title: Two Applications of the Arithmetic Margulis Lemma
rec.speaker: Marc Burger
rec.abstract:
This course has two parts. In the first we will define a general notion of integer point in a higher Teichmüller space and two invariants thereof, the arithmetic dimension and the arithmetic height. The aim is to show finiteness, modulo the mapping class group action, of the number of integer points for which both invariants are bounded.
In the second part we will give the main steps leading to the recent result of Frączyk, Hurtado and Raimbault, stating that the topological complexity of an arithmetic locally symmetric space is bounded by its volume.
Both parts rely on the arithmetic Margulis lemma proven by the same authors as a consequence of Breuillard's height gap theorem.

rec.title: Exact-Solvability of Superintegrable Systems
rec.speaker: Alexander Turbiner
rec.speaker_affiliation: ICN-UNAM, Mexico – Stony Brook Univ., USA – CRM, Canada
rec.abstract:
All, so far known explicitly two-dimensional quantum superintegrable systems in flat space are exactly solvable with spectra linear in quantum numbers (in agreement with the Montreal Conjecture by Tempesta-Turbiner-Winternirz (2001)). Their eigenfunctions are bivariate orthogonal polynomials in invariants of the (discrete) symmetry group. It includes the Smorodinsky-Winternitz potentials I-IV (or the Holt potential), the Fokas-Lagerstrom model, the 3-body Calogero (equivalently, A2 rational) and the Wolfes (equivalently, G2 rational, or I6) models, and the Tremblay-Turbiner-Winternitz system with integer index k=1,2,3,4. They have hidden (Lie) algebraic structure g(k) with various k, and they possess a (finite order) polynomial algebras of integrals generated by the Hamiltonian, two algebraically-independent integrals and their commutator.

rec.title: Boltzmann Equation and Hard Sphere Gas with Singular Initial Data: Well-posedness, Kinetic Limit, and Weak Stability
rec.speaker: Chenjiayue Qi
rec.abstract:
Séminaire d'Analyse
We develop a local well-posedness theory for the spatially inhomogeneous 3-d Boltzmann equation with hard sphere cross-section, accommodating a class of large initial data. This class is an interpolation between the space $L_{x}^{\infty}L_v^{1}$ and $L_{v}^1L_{x}^{\infty}$ (with weight in $v$). It is notable for including data that can have infinite $L_{x,v}^\infty$-norm, entropy density. The core idea of the proof is a homogenization method based on collision geometries. As a key application, we prove the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with initial data in this space, having certain extra conditions. This is the first proof on the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with singular initial data. We also derive weak stability estimates of Boltzmann equation and hard sphere gas within the same functional spaces.

rec.title: Families of G-Curves, Monodromy, and Tannaka Groups
rec.speaker: Irene Spelta
rec.abstract: Maximality results for the monodromy of families of algebraic varieties are widely studied in algebraic geometry. In this talk, we study the monodromy group of families of Galois G-coverings of curves. The action of the Galois group G on cohomology induces a decomposition of the associated variation of Hodge structures. Under suitable assumptions on this decomposition, we discuss results on the maximality of the algebraic monodromy group. We also present ongoing work exploring the relationship between this group and the Tannaka group associated with sheaf convolution on a single fiber of the family.

rec.title: Kneser Graphs: Variations on a Theme
rec.speaker: Matej Stehlik
rec.abstract:
Kneser graphs are a classical family of graphs that play a central role in graph colouring. In 1978, Lovasz determined their chromatic number using topological methods. Schrijver later strengthened this result by identifying vertex-critical induced subgraphs of Kneser graphs, now known as Schrijver graphs.
The talk will survey several recent developments involving these graph families, including constructions of edge-critical subgraphs of Schrijver graphs, a common generalisation of Kneser and Schrijver graphs, and a new family of vertex-critical graphs for which the standard topological lower bounds on the chromatic number are not tight.
The talk is based on joint work with Carmen Arana, Penny Haxell, and Tomas Kaiser.

rec.title: Grid Minors in planar graphs
rec.speaker: Eileen Robinson
rec.abstract:
In 1984, Robertson and Seymour showed that the treewidth of a planar graph with no t × t grid as minor is bounded by a function g(t). Together with Thomas, they later proved that g(t) can be taken to be linear. The current best known bound, due to Gu and Tamaki (2012), is g(t) ≤ 9/2 t − 11/2. In this talk, I will show an improved bound of g(t) ≤ 4t + O(1), which is within a factor 2 of optimal.
This talk is based on joint work with Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Quentin Claus, Gwenaël Joret, Robin Petit and Jean-Florent Raymond.

rec.title: Combinatorial tools for posets topology and simplicial complexes
rec.speaker: Lucas Pouillart
rec.abstract: Topological theory of posets originates from a simple observation : the Möbius function of an interval of a poset P can be interpreted as the Euler characteristic of a simplicial complex. It turned out that in a lot of cases, these complexes hold a lot more information on P and that a lot of interesting examples satisfy the (homotopy) Cohen-Macaulay property, which gives both nice topological and algebraic properties. A lot of techniques were developed by combinatorialists to prove the Cohen-Macaulay property and give interpretations of algebraic and topological problems for posets as enumeration problems, and I will present some of them in this talk.

rec.title: Informative Trains: A Memory-Efficient Journey to a Self-Stabilizing Leader Election Algorithm in Anonymous Graphs
rec.speaker: Sylvain Gay
rec.abstract:
We study the self-stabilizing leader election problem in anonymous n-nodes networks. Achieving self-stabilization with low space memory complexity is particularly challenging, and designing space-optimal leader election algorithms remains an open problem for general graphs. In deterministic settings, it is known that Ω(log log n) bits of memory per node are necessary [Blin et al., Disc. Math. & Theor. Comput. Sci., 2023], while in probabilistic settings the same lower bound holds for some values of n, but only for an unfair scheduler [Beauquier et al., PODC 1999]. Several deterministic and probabilistic protocols have been proposed in models ranging from the state model to the population protocols. However, to the best of our knowledge, existing solutions either require Ω(log n) bits of memory per node for general worst-case graphs, or achieve low state complexity only under restricted network topologies such as rings, trees, or bounded-degree graphs.
In this paper, we present a probabilistic self-stabilizing leader election algorithm for arbitrary anonymous networks that uses O(log log n) bits of memory per node. Our algorithm operates in the state model under a synchronous scheduler and assumes knowledge of a global parameter N = Θ(log n). We show that, under our protocol, the system converges almost surely to a stable configuration with a unique leader and stabilizes within O(poly(n)) rounds with high probability.
Our algorithm is inspired by the uniform constant-state leader election protocol in [Vacus and Ziccardi, PODC 2025] for the beeping model (without self-stabilization). A novel component of our approach is the introduction of an information train mechanism that propagates O(log n)-bit information across the network while requiring only O(loglog n) local memory per node. We believe this mechanism may be of independent interest for the design of space-efficient self-stabilizing distributed algorithms.

rec.speaker: Sylvain Douteau
rec.abstract: Dans cette exposé, j'exposerai dans les grandes lignes la notion de "enhanced categories" introduite par Kaledin. Celle-ci est très inspirée de la théorie des dérivateurs, et vise à remplacer à la fois le formalisme 1-catégorique des catégories modèles et les raisonnements homotopiques des infinies catégories

rec.title: Les polygraphes réguliers et leur théorème de recollement homotopique
rec.speaker: Clémence Chanavat
rec.abstract:
Je commencerai par présenter deux (ou trois) manières de régulariser les polygraphes, que j'appellerai méthode-Hadzihasanovic, méthode-Steiner et, si le temps le permet, méthode-Henry.
J'expliquerai pourquoi la méthode-Hadzihasanovic ne produit pas toujours des polygraphes, à moins que l'on impose aux ∞-catégories strictes des lois d'échange supplémentaires, dictées par des égalités de topologie combinatoire.
Je terminerai par un théorème de recollement, issu de mes derniers travaux, qui assure que certains de ces polygraphes sont librement générés en un sens homotopique, ce qui signifie que ce sont aussi des polygraphes dans la théorie des (∞, n)-catégories.

rec.title: Combinatoire des mots, combinatoire énumérative et combinatoire algébrique autour de la forme normale alternante des tresses
rec.speaker: June Roupin
rec.abstract:
Les tresses sont des objets topologiques qui possèdent de très bonnes propriétés combinatoires, et peuvent en particulier être représentées et étudiées comme des classes d’équivalence de mots sur l'alphabet des transpositions. Un concept naturel dans ce contexte est la notion de forme normale : le choix d’un représentant unique pour chaque tresse. La forme normale alternante, dont l’étude a initialement été motivée par ses liens avec l’ordre standard des tresses, associe à chaque tresse sur n fils une séquence unique de tresses sur n-1 fils, appelés des blocs, permettant de définir récursivement un unique représentant.
Dans cet exposé, je vais présenter quelques propriétés combinatoires et algébriques importante de la forme normale alternante, notamment la régularité et l'automaticité du langage associé. Je vais ensuite aborder plusieurs applications de ces résultats couvrant divers domaines de combinatoires : énumération des tresses ; bon ordre totale sur le monoïde de tresse ; généralisations aux monoïdes d'Artin-Tits.

rec.title: Well-typed program generation, with prenex polymorphism
rec.speaker: Gabriel Scherer
rec.abstract:
Fuzzing” is a popular testing approach where we throw random inputs at a program and check that it respects some expected properties on all inputs. Fuzzing a metaprogram such as a compiler requires producing random input programs. To exercise interesting behaviors of the compiler, we want our input programs to be well-formed in a strong sense, in particular to be well-typed. Generating random well-typed program is difficult when the type-system is powerful, there is a whole scientific literature on the topic, see for example [Testing an Optimising Compiler by Generating Random Lambda Terms, Pałka, 2012].
Most existing generators integrate a large part of the implementation of a type-checker, “inverted” to assist in top-down random term generation by efficiently discarding choices that result in ill-typed programs. Scaling this approach to a full language would result in implementing two sophisticated type-checkers, once in the compiler and once in the program generator. This is one type-checker too many!
We present preliminary work on reusing the constraint-based type inference approach [The Essence of ML-based type inference, Pottier and Rémy, 2004] to write a single type-checker that can be used for both purposes: to check types of user-provided programs, and to efficiently guide a random program generator. This only requires a fairly simple modification to constraint generators: parametrizing them over a search monad. We have succesfully implemented a generator of simply-typed terms in this style, and are in the process (almost done) of scaling it to Hindley-Milner type inference.
(Relevant previous work is [Making Random Judgments: Automatically Generating Well-Typed Terms from the Definition of a Type-System, Fetscher, Claessen, Pałka, Hughes, Findler]. They start from Redex, a Racket DSL to implement simple type systems, and derive a random program generator. The limitation of this approach is that Redex only works with fairly simple type systems, in particular we do not expect it to scale to ML-style type inference with polymorphism, which is the part that hand-crafted generators also struggle on.)
Note: I gave a Formath talk on a preliminary version of this work in March 2024. At the time my prototype only supported the simply-typed lambda-calculus. The extension to Hindley-Milner is follow-up joint work with my 2025 intern Hugo Barreiro. I will also discuss optimizations to the search monad that are necessary to effectively generate terms of larger size.

rec.title: Remarques autour de la formule U^X = ∑_A:U X^A
rec.speaker: Mathieu Anel
rec.abstract: Cette formule classique de théorie des types est remarquable en ce qu’elle égalise des constructions contravariante et covariante en X. Pour l'étudier, je vais me placer dans la catégorie des algèbres sous la monade polynomiale associée à la famille universelle de types U’—>U. Cette catégorie est additive et monoïdale et on peut y relire la formule en terme de dualité et de formes quadratiques. Cela permet une caractérisation précise des paires (U,X) pour lesquelles la formule est vraie.

rec.title: ProofTree: Structured Representations for Human-Centred Mathematical Exploration
rec.speaker: Carl Jontza
rec.abstract:
If formal proofs become abundant, how can we help people find mathematics they care about and explore it in ways that are understandable and engaging? I will present ongoing work on ProofTree, investigating a persistent, versioned graph of goals, assumptions, and alternative arguments as an intermediate representation connecting human-readable reasoning with formal proofs. The aim is to support discovery, understanding, and human guidance at levels of abstraction suited to a person’s background, interests, and objectives.
A case study from Lean-based proof hierarchies, involving confusion between an induction hypothesis and a proof obligation, will motivate technical questions about preserving logical scope, revising arguments, and maintaining links to checked proofs. I will discuss what records of exploration should preserve for subsequent reuse, and outline an evaluation agenda that considers mathematical relevance, understanding, and user experience alongside proof completion and human and computational cost.

rec.title: Verso Blueprint: Reimagining Blueprints for the AI Era
rec.speaker: Emilio Gallego Arias
rec.abstract:
Large-scale formalization projects have long needed tools to
coordinate contributions, track dependencies, and connect mathematical
exposition with formal proofs. A key example is Lean
Blueprint. Introduced in 2020 for the sphere eversion project, Lean
Blueprint extends plasTeX to provide a shared map of statements,
dependencies, Lean declarations, and progress. Lean Blueprint's model
has been quite influential and has helped shape how mathematicians and
formalizers work together on large-scale formalization projects.
This talk presents recent work on Verso Blueprint, a Lean-native
implementation of the Lean Blueprint concept built on Verso, Lean's
official markup language. Designed for close integration with Lean,
Verso Blueprint maintains a three-layer database linking source
material, informal statements, and their formalized counterparts. The
database is populated from Verso documents, analysis of Lean
declarations, and other user-provided data. Interactive HTML views
provide navigation and previews, connecting mathematical exposition
with the formal development. We have now largely reached our original
goal, with functionality comparable to Lean Blueprint or Lean
Architect.
But matching that functionality is no longer enough: this is an
extraordinary moment for formalisation. The practice is radically
chaining even as we build its tools.
When we began this project, our central use case was for humans to
write detailed statements and dependencies to guide
formalization. Today, coding agents are increasingly writing and
interacting with the blueprints themselves in an autonomous
fashion. Blueprints are taking on the reverse role: not just guiding
the construction of formal proofs, but making AI-generated proofs
intelligible to humans. At the same time, dependency tracking and
organizational information remain essential for coordinating
large-scale autoformalization. For example, Prove2Me, a theorem
database with dependency tracking, played a key coordination role in
the recent Fermat's Last Theorem auto-formalization milestone.
What comes next for blueprints in this extraordinary moment? We are
redesigning Verso Blueprint around the idea of "programmatic
blueprints": human-readable, machine-actionable objects synchronized
with formal developments. Our ambition is for blueprints to become a
*foundational harness for AI-assisted formalization*, maintaining the
shared state of a project and coordinating what happens next across
mathematicians, formalizers, code repository workflows, and agents.

rec.title: Compilation of pattern-matching by small inversion
rec.speaker: W. Ait Moussa
rec.abstract:
Dependent inductive data types are an essential part of type theory based proof-assistant, where they close the gap between theorem proving and functional programming. Their meaning and computational behavior are given by dependent recursors, but those are tedious and unintuitive to work with in a dependent setting. Today, the established practice in dependent settings is to have an expressive high-level dependent pattern matching construct with the same logical power as recursors but which is more natural to work with.
This talk will be split into three parts. First, I will go over the history and established theory of dependent-pattern matching and its correspondence to recursors. Then I will present an alternative translation of the non-recursive part of pattern matching to recursors using small-inversion. Finally, I will present an implementation for Rocq of the latter, written by Thierry Martinez a few years back ; in addition to its value as a basis for a specification for this translation, of particular interest is its extensive use of Ocaml's GADTs in order to formalize a notion of intrinsically well-formed Rocq terms.

rec.title: Dynamics of singularity surfaces for the compressible viscous fluids.
rec.speaker: Marcel Zodji
rec.speaker_affiliation: Laboratoire de Mathématiques et Modélisation d'Évry
rec.abstract:
The motion of a compressible viscous fluid is described by the Navier-Stokes system.
It is a system of hyperbolic-parabolic mixed-type PDEs. In this talk, we will study
the so-called density patch problem: \emph{If we are given a density that is initially "regular"
on both sides of a hypersurface across which it is discontinuous, will this structure
be preserved over time?}
An important quantity in the mathematical analysis of this system is the so-called effective flux,
which was discovered by Hoff and Smoller (1985). More precisely, the mathematical properties
of this quantity play a crucial role in the study of the propagation of oscillations in
compressible fluids [Serre, 1991], in the construction of weak solutions [P-L Lions, 1996] or the
propagation of discontinuity surfaces [Hoff, 2002], to cite just a few examples.
In the case of density-dependent viscosities, the behavior of the effective flux degenerates,
which renders the analysis more subtle.

rec.title: Multi-scale modeling and analysis of signal processing in neurons
rec.speaker: Claire Guerrier
rec.abstract: In this talk, I will present models for signal propagation in neurons, ranging from the macro- to the micro-scale, with various applications to neuronal signalling. The first application concerns myelin plasticity, and the influence of neuronal myelin geometry on signal transmission. We investigate the evolution of the maximum of a signal in a damped heat equation on x>0, with a Dirichlet boundary condition representing the signal, which models signal transmission in a myelinated internode. We derive an expression of the solution, and derive the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator at x=0. We then investigate the max. At a more refined scale, to investigate signal summation in the neuronal dendritic tree, we consider the Poisson-Nernst Planck system of equations representing ionic electrodiffusion in an electrolyte. This system expresses a sharp boundary layer of the size of the Debye length at the boundary, where the extra-charges accumulates. In particular, we derive an asymptotic approximation of the solution at steady state, in the regime of small Debye length.

rec.title: Mosquito borne disease outbreak : Climate change impact to Physics Informed Neural Network use
rec.speaker: Aniket Banerjee
rec.abstract:
Dengue, Zika and chikungunya are expanding across new
territories as their vector, the tiger mosquito _Aedes albopictus_,
tracks a warming climate. Forecasting where and when outbreaks will
occur requires models that are both mechanistically faithful to mosquito
ecology and disciplined by real observational data — yet the
biological parameters that govern transmission, such as the biting rate,
the extrinsic incubation period and mosquito survival, are precisely the
ones we cannot measure directly in the field.
In this talk, I present a national -scale furcating framework that
couples a mechanistic _Aedes albopictus_ population model, in the spirit
of the Arbocarto approach, to a vector-to-human transmission layer, and
the use of Neural Network use to predict diffusion pattern in
epidemiological systems. I will explain the modelling choices behind the
population and transmission layers, the structure of the inverse
problem, and how PINNs let a mechanistic model "speak" to messy,
heterogeneous data.

rec.speaker: Mohamed Boubekeur
rec.abstract: >Ce travail porte sur les WE-PINNs, une architecture d'apprentissage profond conçue pour la résolution des lois de conservation hyperboliques. L'approche combine une formulation faible et des contraintes d'entropie physiques pour modéliser avec précision les chocs et les discontinuités (Burgers, Euler 1D/2D), surmontant ainsi les limites des méthodes classiques sans recourir à une viscosité artificielle.

rec.title: Lissage par peignes et trivialité locale pour les espaces homogènes au-dessus d’une courbe relative
rec.speaker: Margot Bruneaux
rec.abstract:
Soit $R$ un anneau local hensélien, de corps résiduel $\kappa$, soit $C$ une courbe projective lisse sur $R$, à fibres géométriquement connexes, soit $G$ un $C$-groupe réductif dont le tore radical $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, et soit $E\to C$ un $G$-torseur.
Nous montrons que, si le noyau de l'isogénie centrale
\[
G_{\mathrm{sc}}\times_C \operatorname{rad}(G)\longrightarrow G
\]
est étale sur $C$, ou bien si $\kappa$ est un corps suffisamment grand, alors la trivialité de $E_\kappa\to C_\kappa$ pour la topologie de Zariski implique la trivialité de $E\to C$ pour cette même topologie.
Nous démontrons également une version « moyennée » de ce résultat, en supposant seulement que $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, ainsi qu'une variante concernant les espaces homogènes projectifs, sans aucune hypothèse restrictive sur $G$.
Ces résultats ont notamment pour conséquences un principe local-global pour les torseurs sur les corps de fonctions de courbes au-dessus d'anneaux de valuation discrète henséliens, renforçant des travaux de Gille--Parimala--Suresh, ainsi qu'une version hensélienne d'un théorème de Drinfeld--Simpson.
Nos démonstrations sont de nature géométrique. Elles reposent sur des compactifications de torseurs et sur une technique de lissage par peignes, dans une version relative et arithmétique que nous développons en détail, en nous appuyant sur les travaux de Kollár et de Graber--Harris--Starr.
En collaboration avec Federico Scavia.

rec.title: Torseurs sur la droite affine sous des groupes lisses
rec.speaker: Alexis Bouthier
rec.abstract:
Si G est réductif sur un corps, un théorème de Raghunathan-Ramanathan énonce que
tout G-torseur sur la droite affine, trivial sur la clôture séparable, est trivial.
Le cas non-réductif avait été écarté d'emblée par les auteurs comme "rather complicated".
On montre qu'un tel énoncé vaut pour tout k-groupe lisse (et même pas lisse du tout).
On discutera également d'autres extensions et généralisations à l'étude des G-torseurs sur des espaces affines.
Travail en commun K. Cesnavicius et F. Scavia.

rec.title: Mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties
rec.speaker: Martin Ortiz
rec.abstract: The weight part of Serre's conjecture studies the modularity of certain spaces of mod p automorphic forms. In the case of Shimura varieties, this is usually done by considering their etale cohomology, with Serre weights as coefficients. One can also propose a similar conjecture for mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties, and I conjecture that the two approaches are equivalent. I can prove this generically for G=GL3, and some cases in GSp4. Moreover, for GSp4 this approach produces a generic entailment of Serre weights, which is completely invisible from the etale cohomology perspective.

rec.speaker: Diego Izquierdo
rec.abstract: Dans cet exposé, je partirai de certaines conjectures de Kato et Kuzumaki reliant la dimension cohomologique des corps à l'existence de certains zéro-cycles sur des hypersurfaces de petit degré. On verra qu'en remplaçant les hypersurfaces de petit degré par des espaces homogènes il est possible d'obtenir des caractérisations de nature diophantienne de la dimension cohomologique. Il s'agit de travaux en commun avec Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche.

rec.title: A Dieudonné theory for analytic p-divisible groups
rec.speaker: Lucas Gerth
rec.abstract: We prove a classification of families of analytic p-divisible groups on adic spaces S over Qp in terms of Hodge–Tate triples on S, generalizing a theorem of Fargues. From this, for S a perfectoid space, we construct an analytic Dieudonné theory with values in mixed characteristic shtukas. As applications, we obtain moduli descriptions of local Shimura varieties of EL and PEL type. We also explain how to derive generalizations of the fundamental exact sequence of Colmez--Dospinescu--Nizio? on smooth Stein spaces.

rec.title: Le principe d'incertitude fort sur les groupes abéliens finis
rec.speaker: Emma Weschler
rec.abstract:
En mécanique quantique, le principe d'incertitude d'Heisenberg stipule qu'on ne peut connaître simultanément avec précision la position et la vitesse d'une particule. Cette célèbre inégalité relie en réalité une fonction et sa transformée de Fourier.
En 1989, motivés par des applications en traitement du signal, Donoho et Stark donnent un nouveau principe d'incertitude, non plus pour des fonctions définies sur les réels mais sur un groupe abélien fini. Ce dernier a ensuite été significativement amélioré : en 2006, Tao prouve ce qu'on peut appeler un principe d'incertitude fort pour des fonctions définies sur Z/pZ, où p est premier.
Plus récemment, en 2021, Garcia, Karaali et Katz généralisent ce principe aux corps finis, pour des fonctions vérifiant une certaine condition de symétrie qu'on détaillera.
Dans cet exposé, on présentera une généralisation du principe d'incertitude fort pour des groupes abéliens finis quelconques et nous verrons ce que donne l'étude de ce dernier sur les groupes cycliques.

rec.title: Numerical semigroups, conjectures, algorithms, and applications.
rec.speaker: Maria Bras-Amorós
rec.abstract:
A numerical semigroup is a subset of N containing zero, with finite complement, and such it is closed under addition. We will introduce the main results on the topic, the connection with algebraic geometry, and the construction of different trees for their classification by different parameters.
Some open conjectures will be presented relating the parameters of a numerical semigroup as well as concerning their growth with respect to the maximum gap, i.e. the Frobenius number, and with respect to the number of gaps, i.e., the genus. We will expose the partial known results and the state of the art of the algorithms for counting semigroups. >
We will finally get a glimpse into the role that numerical semigroups have in the area of error-correcting codes and in music theory.

rec.title: Biased random walk on dynamical percolation
rec.speaker: Nina Gantert
rec.abstract:
As an example for a random walk in random environment, we
study biased random walk for dynamical percolation on the
d-dimensional lattice. We establish a law
of large numbers and an invariance principle for this random walk
using regeneration times.
Moreover, we verify that the Einstein relation holds, and we
investigate the speed of the walk
as a function of the bias. While for d = 1 the speed is
increasing, we show that in general this
fails in dimension d ? 2. As our main result, we establish two
regimes of parameters, separated
by a critical curve, such that the speed is either eventually
strictly increasing or eventually
strictly decreasing. This is in sharp contrast to the biased
random walk on a static supercritical
percolation cluster, where the speed is known to be eventually
zero.
Based on joint work with Sebastian Andres, Dominik Schmid and
Perla Sousi.

rec.title: Percolation de premier passage brochette
rec.speaker: Maxime Marivain
rec.abstract:
Nous étudions un nouveau modèle de percolation de premier passage, appelé percolation de premier passage brochette, dans lequel les temps de passage associés aux arêtes situées sur une même droite sont égaux. Nous établissons tout d'abord un théorème de convergence point à point, où la constante de temps est identifiée. En particulier, nous étudions le cas où cette constante de temps est nulle et mettons en évidence l'existence d'une grande variété de comportements possibles.
Nous démontrons ensuite un théorème de forme, montrant que la forme limite est le diamant L^1. Nous étendons ensuite l'analyse en établissant un théorème de convergence point à point dans le cadre où les temps de passage peuvent prendre la valeur infinie. Enfin, nous nous intéressons à la déviation transversale maximale des géodésiques par rapport à la ligne droite. Nous démontrons l'existence de géodésiques sous des hypothèses faibles et déterminons l'ordre de grandeur de leur déviation par rapport à la ligne droite en fonction du comportement de la distribution des temps de passage au voisinage de son infimum.

rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: À propos de la tessellation de Poisson-Delaunay : quelques techniques classiques et de nouveaux résultats de loi
rec.speaker: Cecilia d'Errico
rec.abstract:
Dans cet exposé, nous présentons la tessellation de Delaunay issue d’un processus ponctuel de Poisson homogène sur Rd. Dans une première partie, nous parlerons de la cellule typique et montrerons comment obtenir sa loi à l’aide d’une technique 'combo'
classique : la formule de Mecke + changement de variable de Blaschke-Petkantschin. Dans la deuxième partie, nous étudions le volume de cette cellule : nous voyons comment obtenir ses moments, puis nous résolvons le problème des moments pour déterminer la loi
du volume de la cellule typique. Enfin, nous présenterons d’autres résultats de loi de fonctionnelles de la cellule typique que nous avons obtenus en étendant ces techniques.

rec.title: Delocalisation of the disordered long-range discrete Gaussian chain
rec.speaker: Corentin Faipeur
rec.abstract:
The long-range discrete Gaussian chain (DGC) is a 1D height function model with $1/r^\alpha$ interactions between pairs of sites at distance $r$. The DGC is known to delocalise at every temperature when $\alpha>2$ (i.e. the typical height at the origin diverges when the size of the system goes to infinity), to localise when $1<\alpha<2$, and to present a localisation/delocalisation phase transition at $\alpha=2$.
In this talk, we will consider a disordered version of the long-range DGC, obtained by adding an external random field. We will show that this disordered model becomes delocalised at all temperatures for all $\alpha>3/2$, and provide quantitative estimates of this delocalisation phenomenon. If time permits, I will also present a central limit theorem for the height at the origin. Joint work with Christopher Chalhoub, Paul Dario and Arnaud Le Ny.

rec.title: [mini-cours] Combinatorics and Geometry: Crossing paths—in the age of AI. (Part 1)
rec.speaker: János Pach
rec.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
rec.abstract:
Crossing numbers: Dead or alive. The crossing
number of a graph G, denoted by cr(G), is the smallest number of
edge crossings in any drawing of G in the plane. Clearly, cr(G)=0
if and only if G is planar. Garey and Johnson proved that
determining cr(G) is an NP-complete problem. Over the past forty
years, crossing numbers have proven to play a vital role in
various fields, including discrete and computational geometry,
number theory, and circuit layout (such as providing lower bounds
on the chip area required for a graph's physical layout). Yet,
many of the foundational questions that inspired research in this
area remain open, and new mysteries continue to emerge. Quo
vadis?
rec.location_text: Salle B107
rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: [mini-cours] Combinatorics and Geometry: Crossing paths—in the age of AI. (Part 2)
rec.speaker: János Pach
rec.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
rec.abstract:
What makes the chromatic number of a graph large?
There have been many attempts to answer this question. The
most natural approach is to look for unavoidable substructures in
graphs of large chromatic number. In 1943, Hadwiger made the
conjecture that every graph of chromatic number r can be
transformed into a complete graph of r vertices by a series of
edge contractions and vertex and edge deletions. This is one of
the most important unsolved problems in graph theory. After giving
a somewhat biased survey of the problem, I plan to report on some
related recent results, joint with Fox and Suk.

rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: Catalan sums, infinite noodle and 1/Pi
rec.speaker: Paul Thévenin
rec.abstract:
We investigate a family of infinite sums of products of Catalan numbers, indexed by trees.
These sums naturally appear in the study of the infinite noodle, which is an infinite random discrete planar graph.
This infinite noodle is the limit, in a local sense, of large uniformly random meandric systems,
which are configurations of non-crossing loops in the plane.
In particular, we show that our sums are all polynomials in 1/Pi with rational coefficients, and provide an algorithm to compute them.
This is joint work with Alin Bostan and Valentin Féray.

rec.title: Empirical distribution of ancestral lineages in populations with density-dependent interactions
rec.speaker: Madeleine Kubasch
rec.abstract: We study a density-dependent Markov jump process describing a population where each individual is characterized by a type, and reproduces at rates depending both on its type and on the population type distribution. We are interested in the empirical distribution of ancestral lineages in the population process. First, we exhibit a time-inhomogeneous Markov process, which allows to capture the behavior of a sampled lineage in the population process. This is achieved through a many-to-one formula, which relates the expected value of a functional evaluated over the lineages in the population process to the expectation of the functional evaluated along this time-inhomogeneous process. This provides a direct interpretation of the underlying survivorship bias. Second, we consider the large population regime, when the population size grows to infinity. Under classical assumptions, the population type distribution converges to a deterministic limit. Here, we focus on the empirical distribution of ancestral lineages in this large population limit, for which we establish a many-to-one formula. Using coupling arguments, we further quantify the approximation error which arises when sampling in this large population approximation instead of the finite-size population process.

rec.title: Height one phenomena in p-adic Hodge theory
rec.speaker: Tasos MOULINOS
rec.abstract:
The syntomification of the integers (Z_p^syn) acts as a parameter space for p-adic cohomology theories. By the work of Drinfeld and others, it is known to carry a canonical formal group, and hence a map to the moduli stack of formal groups. Pulling back along this map gives rise to a certain line bundle equipped with a distinguished section "v_1". On the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups, the nonvanishing of v_1 defines the substack parametrizing "height-1" formal groups. Yet the preimage of this locus on Z_p^syn, when computed in p-adic formal stacks, is empty. There is a mismatch here because inverting v_1 on syntomic cohomology gives p-adic étale cohomology, but inverting it on the stack itself before passing to global sections gives nothing.
I will explain how passing to analytic stacks brings this missing locus into view. By realizing the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups as an analytic stack, we construct an algebro-geometric shadow of K(1)-localization. Applied to syntomification, this produces an analytic stack whose dualizable quasi-coherent sheaves recover p-adic Galois representations, and more generally lisse étale sheaves on the generic fiber of a p-adic formal scheme. I will explain how a perfected version of this construction depends only on the generic fiber, providing a geometric counterpart to purity results for K(1)-localized K-theory.
This is joint work in progress with Greg Andreychev.
rec.location_text: Salle B405, bâtiment B, LAGA, Institut Galilée, Université Paris 13

rec.title: Minimal model for localization of topological Fukaya categories of surfaces
rec.speaker: Pierre BODIN
rec.abstract:
In the first half of this talk, I will present the construction of the topological Fukaya category of a graded marked surface, as introduced by Haiden, Katzarkov, Kontsevich, and present some of its main properties.
In the second half, I will present a minimal model for the localization of this category at a spherical object corresponding to a simple closed curve on the surface. This new description will then be used to describe the indecomposable objects of the localization in terms of graded curves on the singular surface obtained by collapsing the simple closed curve to a point.
