We give an expression for the cohomology of the Orlik--Solomon algebra that we show holds for Schubert matroids as well as for simple, complex-realizable rank-$3$ matroids that do not support multinets.

arxiv:2611.01259.title: Clique counts under degree and matching constraints
arxiv:2611.01259.summary: We study the maximum number of $t$-cliques in graphs with maximum degree at most $D$ and matching number at most $M$, with no restriction on the number of vertices. For $t\ge 3$, we determine this maximum whenever $D\ge 2M-1$ and characterize all extremal graphs when the maximum is positive. Up to isolated vertices, these are complete or complete split graphs for $D\ge 2M$, while $K_{2M}$ is uniquely extremal when $D=2M-1$.

arxiv:2611.01260.title: Gromov-Witten theory of the local model of the standard flop
arxiv:2611.01260.summary: We conjecture that the generating series of equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants of the local Calabi-Yau $(2n-1)$-fold $\operatorname{Tot} \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{n-1}} (-1)^{\oplus n}$ at fixed genus can be presented as a linear combination of polylogarithms, generalising a well-known property of the resolved conifold. We prove this conjecture for two specialisations of the equivariant parameters. In the first, the parameters are specialised to roots of unity and the proof proceeds via Givental-Teleman reconstruction.

arxiv:2611.01273.title: Artinian reduction applied to the Largest Intersection Problem
arxiv:2611.01273.summary: Suppose we have $r$ hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{P}^m$ of degree $d$, whose defining polynomials are linearly independent and whose intersection is zero-dimensional. What is the maximum number of points in their intersection? This problem is motivated by computing the generalized Hamming weights of projective Reed-Muller codes, and a conjectured formula for this maximum was given in [21].

arxiv:2611.01291.title: Contact multiplicity and a sharp six-map bound for collinear self-similar dendrites
arxiv:2611.01291.summary: Let $K\subset\mathbb{C}$ be the attractor of $n\ge2$ similarities $z\mapsto\lambda z+b_k$, $0<|\lambda|<1$, whose fixed points are evenly spaced on a line, and suppose that $K$ does not lie in a line. We prove that $K$ can be a dendrite only if $n\le6$, and that such dendrites exist for every $2\le n\le6$; no separation or finite-intersection hypothesis is imposed. Hence, for $n\ge7$, every connected $K$ of this kind has interior points or separates the plane.

arxiv:2611.01338.title: Threshold existence for random NAE-$k$-SAT and random hypergraph $2$-colourability
arxiv:2611.01338.summary: The existence of limiting threshold densities for random hypergraph $2$-colourability and random NAE-$k$-SAT was conjectured in earlier work, including Achlioptas and Moore [RANDOM 2002] and Coja-Oghlan and Panagiotou [STOC 2012]. We prove these conjectures for all $k\geq 3$. We also show that $\alpha^{\mathrm{2-col}}_k \leq \alpha^{\mathrm{NAE}}_k$ for each $k\geq 3$.

arxiv:2611.01340.title: Graceful supertrees with at most $2m-\mathrm{diam}(T)$ edges
arxiv:2611.01340.summary: A graceful labeling of a tree with $m$ edges is a bijection from its vertices to $\{0,1,\ldots,m\}$ whose edge differences are pairwise distinct. The Graceful Tree Conjecture asserts that every tree admits such a labeling; equivalently, the smallest graceful tree containing a given $m$-edge tree has $m$ edges. For this embedding problem, Sethuraman, Ragukumar and Slater proved that fewer than $4m$ edges suffice, while Sethuraman and Ragukumar observed that in practice fewer than $2m$ appear to suffice.

arxiv:2611.01350.title: Lehmer's number is not an orientable stretch factor in genus six
arxiv:2611.01350.summary: Let $\lambda_L \approx 1.17628$ be Lehmer's number. We prove that no pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus six with orientable invariant foliations has stretch factor $\lambda_L$. This gives a negative answer to a question of Lanneau and Thiffeault on the minimal stretch factor in even genus.

arxiv:2611.01368.title: An $\mathsf{FPRAS}$ for Mixed Volumes
arxiv:2611.01368.summary: We design the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme ($\mathsf{FPRAS}$) to estimate the mixed volume of $n$ arbitrary compact convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ specified by weak membership oracles. This disproves a longstanding conjecture of Gurvits (2009). $\textbf{AI Disclosure}$ The main ideas were generated entirely by GPT 6 Astra.

arxiv:2611.01379.title: Decay of Correlations for Multiplicative Functionals of Determinantal Point Processes
arxiv:2611.01379.summary: The main result of this paper is an upper bound on the correlations of multiplicative functionals of determinantal point processes. In particular, for the sine process, the correlations of a multiplicative functional associated with a rapidly decaying function decay quadratically. It follows that the spectral density of such functionals belongs to the Sobolev space $H_1$.

arxiv:2611.01418.title: Topological transcendence degree and the dimension problem for perfectoid spaces
arxiv:2611.01418.summary: Let $K$ be a perfectoid field of characteristic $p$ with countable value group (for example, $K=\mathbb{C}_{p}^{\flat}$). We study Zariski-closed subsets \begin{equation*}Z\subseteq \mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}\end{equation*}of the $n$-dimensional perfectoid closed unit ball $\mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}$ over $K$. We use an example of Gleason, and its generalization obtained in the authors' previous work, to show that two natural notions of dimension for such Zariski-closed subsets, the Krull dimension $\dim(Z)$ and Huber's iterated transcendence degree $\mathrm{dim.tr}(Z)$, do not coincide, and that the gap between them can be arbitrarily large.

arxiv:2611.01422.title: The Marvelous Meixner Polynomials: Second Kind, First Class
arxiv:2611.01422.summary: Meixner's classification asks which exponential generating functions can generate orthogonal polynomials. We follow the continuous Meixner family from this question to its moments, measures, and continued fractions. A beta integral and a bilinear identity establish positivity and orthogonality; Carlitz's Bernoulli and Euler constructions reveal further connections.

arxiv:2611.01423.title: The classification of Fano contact manifolds revisited
arxiv:2611.01423.summary: We present an account of the classification of Fano contact manifolds based on the proof of OpenAI and the solution of LeBrun-Salamon conjecture by Hu, Liu and Wan. The proof combines their constructions with earlier results on contact lines, with some simplifications.

arxiv:2611.01428.title: Whittaker modules for the principal $W$-algebra $\mathcal W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$ via free field realizations
arxiv:2611.01428.summary: We study Whittaker and generalized Whittaker modules for the universal principal $W$-algebra $\mathcal W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, using two free field realizations: one in the Heisenberg vertex algebra of rank two and the other in the tensor product of the universal Virasoro vertex algebra with the Heisenberg vertex algebra of rank one. Under explicit conditions on the parameters, we construct universal Whittaker modules, establish their ordered bases, and obtain explicit irreducibility criteria. Under an explicit nondegeneracy condition, we also show that the submodules of these tensor products correspond to the submodules of the Virasoro factor.

arxiv:2611.01444.title: Generating the liftable outer automorphism groups of regular cyclic covers
arxiv:2611.01444.summary: Let $R_n = \bigvee_{i=1}^{n} S^1$ be a finite connected one-dimensional CW complex with $n \geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ be the outer automorphism group of the free group $F_n$, where $\pi_1(R_n)\cong F_n$. Let $p_k:\tilde{R}_n\rightarrow R_n$ be the standard $k$-sheeted regular cyclic cover of $R_n$ induced by a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-action on $\tilde{R}_n$ (which is homotopy equivalent to $R_{n_k}$, where $n_k=k(n-1)+1$) generated by a free rotation through $2\pi/k$ of $\tilde{R}_n$. Let $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ be the liftable outer automorphism group associated with a standard $k$-sheeted normal cover $p_k$.
arxiv:2611.01444.authors: Rohan Suresh Mahure, Priyavrat Pandey, Kashyap Rajeevsarathy

arxiv:2611.01445.title: Irreducibility of Full Multivariate Partial-Twuality Polynomials
arxiv:2611.01445.summary: For each nonempty finite simple graph, we study five full multivariate partial-twuality polynomials defined using matrix ranks and coranks over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Over an arbitrary coefficient field $K$, we give a necessary and sufficient criterion for nontrivial factorization in the Laurent polynomial ring by additive separation of the exponent function across a nontrivial vertex partition. For $\bullet\in\{\tau,\delta\tau,\tau\delta,\delta\tau\delta\}$, the full multivariate partial-$\langle\bullet\rangle$ polynomial is irreducible in $K[z^{\pm1},\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected.

arxiv:2611.01453.title: An Odd-Arch Family of Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursions: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws
arxiv:2611.01453.summary: For every integer $p\ge2$, we construct a globally well-defined positive odd sequence $Q_p$ satisfying, after an explicit finite initial block, $Q_p(n)=Q_p(n-Q_p(n-1))+Q_p(n-Q_p(n-2))-(-1)^n$. Its binary block words admit the exact factorization $U_{p,k}=(A_k\overline{A}_{k+1})^{p-1}A_{k+2}$, producing exactly $2p-1$ alternating signed arches per natural block. The elementary word heights converge uniformly to the Gaussian isoperimetric profile $\varphi\circ\Phi^{-1}$.

arxiv:2611.01465.title: Extremal permutations of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ with many good slopes and applications to quantum Latin squares
arxiv:2611.01465.summary: For $n\ge2$, a good slope of a permutation $f$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n=\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is an element $m\in\mathbb{Z}_n$ for which $x\mapsto f(x)+mx$ is a permutation. We prove the sharp upper bound $\varphi(n)$ on the number of good slopes, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function. We classify and count the equality cases for prime powers and products of two distinct odd primes.

arxiv:2611.01482.title: Global straightening of solution manifolds for state-dependent delay equations
arxiv:2611.01482.summary: Let $U$ be an arbitrary open subset of $C^1([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuously differentiable. Suppose that each derivative $Df(\phi)$, $\phi\in U$, admits a continuous linear extension $D_ef(\phi):C([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)\to\mathbb R^n$, such that $D_ef(\phi)\chi$ depends jointly continuously on $\phi\in U$ and $\chi\in C([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$. We construct a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of $U$ onto an open subset of $C^1([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$ which maps the solution manifold of $x'(t)=f(x_t)$ onto an open subset of the closed subspace defined by $\phi'(0)=0$.

arxiv:2611.01497.title: Eynard-Orantin Topological Recursions for Higher Weil-Petersson Volumes on Moduli Spaces of Super Riemann Surfaces
arxiv:2611.01497.summary: We derive an Eynard-Orantin topological recursion for intersection numbers involving Norbury's $\Theta$-class together with $\psi$-classes and higher $\kappa$-classes. These intersection numbers encode higher Weil-Petersson volumes of moduli spaces of super Riemann surfaces. The resulting recursion is a higher-$\kappa$ deformation of the topological recursion associated with the Bessel curve, which encodes the Br\'ezin-Gross-Witten model.

arxiv:2611.01508.title: Du Bois cohomology of noncommutative spaces and the Hodge numbers invariance conjecture for singular varieties
arxiv:2611.01508.summary: We extend the definition of cdh-sheafified Hochschild homology from varieties to stable categories linear over a field of characteristic zero, thereby proving its Morita-invariance. The dimensions of its homology groups give meaningful numerical invariants of a category; we combine them with invariants coming from topological K-theory and Poincar\'e duality to prove equality of mixed Hodge numbers for singular complex projective Fourier--Mukai partners in several classes in dimensions two, three, and four, including normal surfaces and threefolds with rational singularities and equal irregularity. Beyond these applications, we construct Du Bois versions of topological cyclic homology of…

arxiv:2611.01509.title: Every $k$-Quasi-Planar Graph Has Linearly Many Edges
arxiv:2611.01509.summary: For every fixed integer $k\ge2$, we prove that every simple graph on $n$ vertices drawn in the plane with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges has at most $C_kn$ edges, where $C_k$ depends only on $k$. We allow any finite number of proper crossings between two edges, including edges with a common endpoint. For $n\ge3$, removing a small disk around each vertex turns the drawing into a family of arcs on a sphere with $n$ boundary circles.

arxiv:2611.01524.title: From Ghost SICs to SIC-POVMs: A Galois Reduction of Zauner's Conjecture
arxiv:2611.01524.summary: Symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (SIC-POVMs, or SICs) are optimal minimal measurements for quantum state tomography. Problem~1 of Horodecki, Rudnicki and \.Zyczkowski's open problems in quantum information asks for SICs in infinitely many dimensions. By work of Appleby--Flammia--Kopp and Radchenko--Wheeler, ghost SICs, which satisfy the SIC equations with Hermiticity up to parity, exist unconditionally for $d\ge4$.

arxiv:2611.01528.title: The most singular loci of twisted character varieties
arxiv:2611.01528.summary: For any simply connected almost simple group $G$ and any compact Riemann surface of genus $g>1$, we study the singular locus of the character variety which parametrises fundamental group representations with a twist by a central element $z$ of $G$. While for $z=1$ the most singular representations have values in a maximal torus (and are invariant for the Weyl group action) and for generic $z$ every $z$-twisted representation is irreducible, for a general $z$ we find that the most singular representations have values in a particular Levi subgroup $L_z$ up to conjugation. From the explicit Lie-theoretic description of $L_z$, we determine the structure of the maximal stabiliser groups, and…

arxiv:2611.01535.title: A rigidity theorem for edge-connectivity under non-negative Bakry--\'Emery curvature
arxiv:2611.01535.summary: The edge-connectivity $\kappa(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum number of edges whose removal disconnects $G$, and it is bounded above by the minimum degree $\delta(G)$. We classify all connected locally finite simple graphs with nonnegative Bakry--\'Emery curvature satisfying $\kappa(G)<\delta(G)$. All such graphs are infinite.
arxiv:2611.01535.authors: Kaizhe Chen, Shiping Liu, Haotian Yang

arxiv:2611.01546.title: MDS Algebraic Geometry Codes of Square-Root Length on Hyperelliptic Curves
arxiv:2611.01546.summary: For every fixed genus $g\geq2$ and every $0<\rho<1$, we construct maximum distance separable (MDS) algebraic geometry codes over $\F_q$ for all sufficiently large odd squares $q$. Their parameters are $\bigl[n,\lfloor\rho n\rfloor,n-\lfloor\rho n\rfloor+1\bigr]_q$ with $n=\sqrt q+1+O_g(q^{1/4})$. The codes use full Riemann--Roch spaces on genus-$g$ hyperelliptic curves.

arxiv:2611.01554.title: Short Paper No. 1: Relation between integer sequence A319433 and the maximum degrees of finite linear Jaco graphs
arxiv:2611.01554.summary: This short paper presents the interesting relation between integer sequence A319433 in https://oeis.org and the maximum degrees of the family of finite linear Jaco graphs $J_n(x)$ where $n = 1,2,3,\dots$. The result first appeared as a conjecture. Subsequently, a proof through AI-assisted mathematical reasoning came to the fore.

arxiv:2611.01561.title: A log-concavity criterion for finite nonnegative linearization
arxiv:2611.01561.summary: In a 2005 survey, R. Szwarc asked for criteria, stated in the recurrence coefficients, for nonnegative linearization (property (P)) of finite orthogonal polynomial systems such as the Krawtchouk polynomials. For a finite three-term recurrence normalized to have row sums one, whose diagonal and downward coefficients have a constant nonnegative ratio, we prove that property (P) holds for every product, including products beyond the terminal degree, whenever the Newton coefficients of the profile $d_i=b_i+c_i$ are log-concave without internal zeros.

arxiv:2611.01567.title: A sphere-product counterexample to the additivity of homology nilpotency
arxiv:2611.01567.summary: Homology nilpotency need not increase under a product with a sphere. We construct a simply connected, closed smooth manifold $M$ of dimension $53$, rationally elliptic with $\dim_{\mathbb Q}\bigl(\pi_*(M)\otimes\mathbb Q\bigr)=7$, such that $cat_0(M)=10$ and $Hnil(M\times S^2)=Hnil(M)=11$. The inequality $Hnil(X\times Y)\leq Hnil(X)+Hnil(Y)$ can therefore be strict even for a product of a closed manifold with $S^2$ as the second factor.

arxiv:2611.01577.title: Sharp Bounds for Edge Mappings of Graphs
arxiv:2611.01577.summary: The study of extremal problems for set mappings was initiated by Erd\H{o}s and Hajnal in 1958. Alon and Caro, and later Caro, Patk\'os, Tuza and Vizer, studied related problems for edge mappings of graphs. For a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, let $g_0(G)$ be the minimum integer $N$ such that every mapping $f:E(K_N)\to E(K_N)$ satisfying $f(e)\cap e=\varnothing$ for every $e\in E(K_N)$ admits a copy $G^*$ of $G$ in $K_N$ with $f(e)\notin E(G^*)$ for every $e\in E(G^*)$.

arxiv:2611.01588.title: Contractable 2-connected subgraphs in minimally 3-connected graphs
arxiv:2611.01588.summary: We study the 2-connected subgraphs of minimally 3-connected graphs whose contraction preserves 3-connectedness. We show that every minimally 3-connected graph that is not a wheel or a complete bipartite graph $K_{3,n}$ contains a contractable 2-connected induced subgraph that is a cycle, a fan, a $K_{2,n}$ or a $K_{3,n}$. In addition, these subgraphs satisfy certain degree restrictions.

arxiv:2611.01618.title: Haagerup vertex operator algebras at central charge eight
arxiv:2611.01618.summary: Evans and Gannon showed that a positive vertex operator algebra of central charge eight whose representation category is the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category has one of two character vectors, with six or nineteen currents. Call such an algebra, if strongly rational, a Haagerup algebra. We prove that a Haagerup algebra $U$ has six currents, that $U_1 \cong \mathfrak{sl}_2 \oplus \mathfrak{sl}_2$ embeds into $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$ in one of two explicit ways, with levels $(1,39)$ or $(3,13)$, and we determine the lowest weight spaces of its modules and $U_2$ as $U_1$-modules.

arxiv:2611.01654.title: Absolute descent and the B\'enabou--Roubaud theorem
arxiv:2611.01654.summary: We continue the programme developed in Pseudo-Kan extensions and descent theory by studying descent for augmented pseudocosimplicial objects. Let $\mathcal H$ be a $2$-category, and let $\operatorname{suc}=\mathsf{1}+(-)$ be the successor monad on the augmented simplex category. Precomposition with $\operatorname{suc}$ induces the d\'ecalage pseudomonad $\mathbb S$ on the $2$-category of augmented pseudocosimplicial objects with values in $\mathcal H$.

arxiv:2611.01672.title: A faithful representation and profinite completion
arxiv:2611.01672.summary: We exhibit two finitely generated residually finite groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{G_1} \cong \widehat{G_2}$, such that $G_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,\mathbb{C})$ but $G_2$ is not linear. This answers a question of Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain, Alexander Lubotzky, and Martin Bridson negatively. We also present two finitely generated residually finite groups $H_1$ and $H_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{H_1} \cong \widehat{H_2}$ satisfying the following.

arxiv:2611.01674.title: Boolean Rank Nine for Polygons with 35 to 40 Vertices
arxiv:2611.01674.summary: We give a computer-assisted proof that the rectangle covering number, or Boolean rank, of every polygon slack matrix of order 35 through 40 is nine. The upper bound is due to Goucha, Gouveia, and Silva; the new contribution is the matching lower bound. A hypothetical covering by eight rectangles yields a saturated inclusion cycle between two antichains on eight coordinates.

arxiv:2611.01689.title: Partially wrapped contact Fukaya categories of 1-jet spaces
arxiv:2611.01689.summary: We introduce the partially wrapped contact Fukaya category of a 1-jet space equipped with a stop, which is an \(A_\infty\)-category of Legendrians equipped with representations of their Chekanov-Eliashberg algebras. This category is invariant under contact isotopies of the stop. We prove a wrapping exact triangle and a generation theorem.

arxiv:2611.01699.title: Chaotic Dynamics of Charged Particles in Magnetic Fields with Singular Forces
arxiv:2611.01699.summary: We study charged-particle dynamics under a non-Lipschitz velocity-dependent force with magnetic and damping effects, focusing on continuation through zero velocity and chaos in the velocity direction. For a time-independent directional force and fixed parameters, we introduce a $C^1$ regularization. When an unregularized trajectory reaches zero velocity in finite time, inner rescaling yields convergence to a reference orbit within the regularization ball, while the regularized trajectories converge locally uniformly outside it to a unique continuation.
arxiv:2611.01699.authors: Linhao Chen, Yong Li, Weiping Yan

arxiv:2611.01714.title: The Three-Color Generalized Schur Number of \(x+(k-1)y=z\): A Proof for All \(k\) from a Critical Set of 33 Polynomials
arxiv:2611.01714.summary: For an integer \(k\ge 3\), let \(T_k(3)\) be the least positive integer \(N\) such that, for any \(3\)-coloring of \([1,N]\), there exists a monochromatic solution to \(x+(k-1)y=z\). In this paper, we prove that \(T_k(3)=k^3+2k^2-2\) for all \(k\ge 3\). In the notation \(s_a(3)\) of the first author, with \(a=k-1\), this says that \(s_a(3)=a^3+5a^2+7a+1\) for all \(a\ge 2\), which confirms the conjecture proposed in 2020.

arxiv:2611.01716.title: Derived Torelli for Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds
arxiv:2611.01716.summary: We prove that every orientation-preserving Hodge isometry between the integral Mukai lattices of the Kuznetsov components of two smooth cubic fourfolds is induced by an exact equivalence. The proof uses Markman--Mehrotra's comonad reconstruction method to recover both Kuznetsov components from a common Fourier--Mukai comonad on a moduli space of stable objects. As an application, we prove that the Kuznetsov components of two smooth cubic fourfolds are equivalent whenever their Fano varieties of lines are derived equivalent.

arxiv:2611.01719.title: Strict Separation of Antiperiodic Degeneracy Curves for Elliptic Euler and Lagrangian Solutions
arxiv:2611.01719.summary: We prove strict separation of antiperiodic degeneracy curves associated with elliptic Euler and Lagrangian solutions of the planar three-body problem. For every eccentricity $0<e<1$, each Euler pair issuing from a common circular parameter is strictly ordered in the extended family $\beta>0$, and the two Lagrangian curves remain disjoint. Every antiperiodic degeneracy point in these families with $0<e<1$ has a one-dimensional full kernel.
arxiv:2611.01719.authors: Xijun Hu, Li Wu, Ao Zhu

arxiv:2611.01725.title: Uniqueness of SRB measures for stochastic differential equations
arxiv:2611.01725.summary: For a dissipation stochastic differential equation (abbreviated as SDE), exponential ergodicity has been investigated a lot in a wide range of settings. In this paper, we prove that the Markovian measure $\mu$ determined by the unique stationary measure is also the unique invariant measure which satisfies the entropy formula. Consequently, the existence of an SRB measure is completely determined by the sign of the sample top Lyapunov exponent of $\mu$: if $\chi_\mu^1>0$, then $\mu$ is the unique SRB measure, whereas if $\chi_\mu^1\leq0$, then the SDE admits no SRB measure.

arxiv:2611.01745.title: A remark on the AI proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
arxiv:2611.01745.summary: We give a geometric interpretation of the projection and reconstruction underlying the Open AI's characteristic-two proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture. Using the double covering and filling a puncture, we construct a morphism on normalized level-two associators with an explicit inverse on its image. We compute the restricted tangent reconstruction in the pro-2 realization and identify the leading coefficient maps with those of the OpenAI proof, making its implicit reconstruction explicit.

arxiv:2611.01763.title: The Maximum Diagonal Product of a Stochastic Matrix of Bounded Rank
arxiv:2611.01763.summary: Let $A=(a_{ij})$ be a nonnegative row-stochastic or column-stochastic $n\times n$ matrix of rank at most $k$, where $1\le k\le n$. Write $n=qk+s$, where $0\le s<k$. The author conjectured in 2018 that, for every permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $\prod_{i=1}^n a_{i,\sigma(i)}\le q^{-q(k-s)}(q+1)^{-(q+1)s}$.

arxiv:2611.01772.title: An approximate cactus-decomposition for vertex-connectivity
arxiv:2611.01772.summary: The classical cactus theorem of Dinitz, Karzanov and Lomonosov from 1976 states that the minimum edge-cuts of a connected graph are displayed by a cactus. For vertex-separations, Tutte's theorem gives an exact cactus-decomposition for connectivity $2$, but exact cactus-decompositions fail for higher connectivity. Extending earlier approximate cactus-decomposition results for connectivities $3$ and $4$ by Carmesin and Kurkofka [FOCS 2023] and Kurkofka and Planken [SODA 2026] to all connectivities, we prove that for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there is a constant $d=d(k)$ such that every $k$-connected graph $G$ admits a cactus-decomposition displaying $k$-separations such that every $k$-separation…
arxiv:2611.01772.authors: Romain Bourneuf, Johannes Carmesin, Jan Kurkofka, Tim Planken

arxiv:2611.01795.title: Dimension bounds for finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes
arxiv:2611.01795.summary: We prove that a finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter polytope has dimension at most $81$, substantially improving Prokhorov's bound of $995$. A refinement of Prokhorov's method gives the intermediate bound $162$, while an extension of Vinberg's planar-angle comparison to the finite-volume setting yields the sharper bound. Both arguments combine improved weighting functions with estimates using cusp geometry to control weight contributions of angles at ideal vertices or edges incident to them.

arxiv:2611.01803.title: RaFH and CRaFH superalgebras: Frobenius forms, representation theory and respectability
arxiv:2611.01803.summary: We introduce \emph{RaFH superalgebras}, which are Rees affine Frobenius Hecke superalgebras. These algebras are defined by generators and relations, using \emph{Frobenius-tensor superalgebras} to axiomatise tensor powers of Frobenius superalgebras together with their copairing elements. The RaFH superalgebras include, as special cases, the affine and degenerate affine Hecke algebras of type $A$, the affine Sergeev superalgebras, the affine wreath product algebras and quantum affine wreath algebras, as well as the recently introduced quantum wreath product algebras in the special case of the superflip braiding.

arxiv:2611.01807.title: Perfect 1-factorisations of $K_{18}$ with a non-trivial automorphism group
arxiv:2611.01807.summary: A perfect 1-factorisation (P1F) of $K_{2n}$ is a partition of its edges into $2n-1$ perfect matchings, any two of which form a Hamiltonian cycle. Exhaustive classification is known only up to $K_{16}$. We present a method for the exhaustive generation, up to isomorphism, of perfect 1-factorisations with a non-trivial automorphism group, which reduces the search tree far enough to make $K_{18}$ and beyond feasible.
arxiv:2611.01807.authors: Andrei V. Ivanov, Leonid M. Tertitski

arxiv:2611.01808.title: An infinite family of graphs with \v{S}olt\'es fraction uniformly above one half
arxiv:2611.01808.summary: The Wiener index $W(G)$ of a connected graph $G$ is the sum of the distances between all unordered pairs of vertices. A vertex $x$ is a \v{S}olt\'es vertex if $G-x$ is connected and $W(G-x)=W(G)$. We construct an infinite family of graphs in which the proportion of \v{S}olt\'es vertices is strictly greater than $(\sqrt{21}-3)/3=0.5275\ldots>1/2$ and decreases to this value from $2/3$.

arxiv:2611.01833.title: Braided Multisections and Aspherical Stein Fillings
arxiv:2611.01833.summary: We construct Stein fillings diffeomorphic to complements of a connected symplectic unbranched multisection and a regular sphere fiber in the ruled surface $\Sigma_g\times S^2$. For every $g\geq2$ and every multisection degree $p\geq4$, a fixed contact three-manifold admits infinitely many pairwise nonhomeomorphic aspherical fillings of this form. Their first and second integral homology groups are $\Z^{2g}\oplus\Z/p$ and $\Z^{(2g-1)(p-1)}$, respectively, and their intersection pairings vanish.

arxiv:2611.01838.title: Integral saturation of adjacency-degree lattices
arxiv:2611.01838.summary: Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of $G\sim G(n,1/2)$, let $D=\operatorname{diag}(A\mathbf{1})$, and let $\Lambda_G=\mathbb{Z}\langle A,D\rangle\mathbf{1}$. We prove $\Pr[\Lambda_G\ne\mathbb{Z}^n]\le n^{-3/20+o(1)}$. Thus two dependent graph operators generate the entire vertex lattice from the constant vector, simultaneously over every prime field.

arxiv:2611.01841.title: Graphic matroids with connectivity constraints
arxiv:2611.01841.summary: In 1959, Tutte proved that a matroid can be realised by a graph if and only if it does not have a minor isomorphic to $U_{2,4}$, $F_7$, $F_7^*$, $M^*(K_5)$ or $M^*(K_{3,3})$. In this paper, we extend this theorem to determine when it is possible to find a graphic realisation $G$ of a matroid $M$, subject to a list of additional constraints of the following form: a subset $F$ of the elements of $M$ must induce a connected subgraph of $G$. We prove that a connected matroid with such constraints---called a `constraint matroid'---is realisable as a graph satisfying those constraints if and only if it does not contain as a minor one of the constraint matroids from a given list: that is, the…

arxiv:2611.01871.title: Infinite Generalized Sidon Sets with a Negative Answer to a Problem of Szemer\'edi
arxiv:2611.01871.summary: We construct infinite $B_h$ sets that repeatedly attain the density scale of finite $B_h$ sets. For every integer $h\geq2$ and every finite $B_h$ set $F$ of positive integers, we obtain an infinite $B_h$ set $A\supseteq F$ such that $$ \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)}{x^{1/h}}=\frac1h, \qquad \liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)}{x^{1/h}}=0. $$ The key is to preserve density while preventing additive relations between successive blocks.

arxiv:2611.01875.title: Approximation Algorithms for Maximum-Weight Degree-Bounded Forests
arxiv:2611.01875.summary: In the maximum-weight degree-bounded forest problem, we are given a graph with nonnegative edge weights and a degree upper bound on each vertex. The objective is to find a maximum-weight forest satisfying the degree bounds. We show that this problem admits a simple $2$-approximation via the greedy algorithm.
arxiv:2611.01875.authors: Theophile Thiery, Vera Traub, Nicola Widmer

arxiv:2611.01882.title: Convergence of the Calabi flow on K\"ahler surfaces with bounded Sobolev constants
arxiv:2611.01882.summary: We study global Calabi flows $g(t)$ on compact K\"ahler surfaces with a uniform Sobolev constant. For any sequence $t_j\to\infty$, set $g_j(t):=g(t_j+t)$. After passing to a subsequence, these flows converge to an eternal Calabi flow on a compact extremal K\"ahler orbifold surface.
arxiv:2611.01882.authors: Haozhao Li, Bing Wang, Kai Zheng

arxiv:2611.01895.title: Optimal asymptotic bounds for design curves on manifolds
arxiv:2611.01895.summary: A spherical $t$-design is a finite set of points on the $d$-dimensional unit sphere such that averaging any polynomial of degree at most $t$ over these points gives its exact spherical average. We study the corresponding notion for curves, where point averages are replaced by normalized arclength integration. For fixed $d\ge 2$, the length of such curves is known to be bounded below by a positive multiple of $t^{d-1}$ as $t\to\infty$.

arxiv:2611.01896.title: The Brin-Katok local entropy formula for non-compact random dynamical systems and an application
arxiv:2611.01896.summary: In this paper, we establish the classical Brin-Katok local entropy formula for $C^1$ random dynamical systems on a complete Riemannian manifold (possibly non-compact) under a mild integrability condition. The proof depends on the constructions of measurable partitions adapted to asymptotically varying radii and finite measurable partitions with null-boundaries. As an application, under additional integrability assumptions, we obtain the Margulis-Ruelle inequality for $C^2$ random dynamical systems on complete non-compact Riemannian manifolds.

arxiv:2611.01906.title: Improved lower bounds for the kissing number in dimensions 49 to 61
arxiv:2611.01906.summary: We give explicit kissing configurations in R^d for every d = 49, ..., 61. The lower bound is improved over the best previously published value in all thirteen dimensions, by margins from 232 to 159,220 points and by 506,461 points in total. The configurations are obtained from the antipodal block lift of Yang et al. applied to the 52,416,000-point minimal shell of the extremal even unimodular lattice P_48p, using a class of 7,193 minimal lines and, in each dimension, a kissing configuration of R^k (k <= 15) with the largest available number of antipodal pairs.

arxiv:2611.01915.title: Quadratic bounds for intersecting hypergraphs: An affirmative answer to a question of Duke and Erd\H{o}s
arxiv:2611.01915.summary: Let $m(k,b)$ denote the minimum number of edges in an intersecting $k$-uniform hypergraph in which every $(k-1)$-set of vertices is disjoint from at least $b$ edges, with $m(k,b)=+\infty$ if no such hypergraph exists. Duke and Erd\H{o}s [Congressus Numerantium (1980)] asked whether $m(k,k)=o(k^4)$ is possible. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively and determine the order of growth of $m(k,k)$ by proving that $k^2+1\leq m(k,k)\leq Ck^2$ for all sufficiently large $k$, where $C$ is an absolute constant.
arxiv:2611.01915.authors: Guoqing Wang, Linlin Wang, Jun Yue

arxiv:2611.01916.title: On closed symmetric monoidal enriched $\infty$-categories
arxiv:2611.01916.summary: We show that a closed symmetric monoidal V-enriched $\infty$-category can be described by a lax symmetric monoidal functor to V from its underlying $\infty$-category.

arxiv:2611.01919.title: Alternating Sums in Compositions
arxiv:2611.01919.summary: Motivated by the recent asymptotic formula for the moment of the alternating sum of parts in partitions by Craig and Li, we study the moment of the alternating sum of parts in compositions. We establish closed formulas for this moment using techniques involving generating functions, matrix diagonalization, Krawtchouk polynomials, differential equations, and Fa\`a di Bruno's formula. Our result is connected with some known integer sequences in the OEIS and admits a combinatorial interpretation by coin flipping.

arxiv:2611.01928.title: Boundary fibers of the holonomy map for complex projective structures
arxiv:2611.01928.summary: We study the Morgan--Shalen boundary of holonomy representations of complex projective structures on a compact Riemann surface of genus at least two. We prove that every direction defined by a holomorphic quadratic differential with a multiple zero admits distinct projective marked length limits. Together with Dumas's uniqueness theorem for simple zeros, this gives a complete characterization of directions with unique limits.

arxiv:2611.01957.title: Theoretical relations between basic centrality measures in real-world networks
arxiv:2611.01957.summary: We establish new relationships among several fundamental measures of real-world networks, including the average clustering coefficient, the global clustering coefficient, the average shortest-path length and degree centrality, closeness centrality, betweenness centrality and ksi-centrality. We further develop the theory of $j$-neighborhood centrality, which encompasses degree centrality and ksi-centrality as special cases.

arxiv:2611.01961.title: Moduli spaces of rank 2 sheaves on $\mathbb P^3$ via Quot schemes
arxiv:2611.01961.summary: We study the Gieseker--Maruyama moduli space $M_{c_3}$ of stable rank 2 torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^3$ with Chern classes $c_1=-1$, $c_2=1$, and odd $c_3 \le 1$. Every such sheaf $E$ has reflexive hull $E^{\ast\ast}$ parametrised by $M_1$, and the quotient $E^{\ast\ast}/E$ is a 0-dimensional sheaf of length $n = (1-c_3)/2$. We prove that $M_{c_3}$ is isomorphic to the relative Quot scheme $\mathsf{Quot}_{\mathbb{P}^3 \times M_1/M_1}(\mathscr{R},n)$, where $\mathscr{R}$ is the universal reflexive sheaf over $M_1$.
arxiv:2611.01961.authors: Charles Almeida, Nicol\`o Bignami, Marcos Jardim, Andrea T. Ricolfi

arxiv:2611.01963.title: The Erd\H{o}s--Hajnal property for paths
arxiv:2611.01963.summary: The well-known Erd\H{o}s-Hajnal conjecture states that for any graph $H$, there is a constant $c=c(H)>0$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with no induced copies of $H$ contains a clique or an independent set of size at least $n^{c}$. In this paper, we prove that the Erd\H{o}s-Hajnal conjecture holds for every path.
arxiv:2611.01963.authors: Shenwei Huang, Yidong Zhou, Yuwen Zhou

arxiv:2611.01969.title: Finite tests and low-rank excluded minors for matroid path-width two
arxiv:2611.01969.summary: The path-width of a matroid is the minimum, over all orderings of its ground set, of the maximum value of its connectivity function on an initial segment. For any two connected rooted matroids whose roots are neither loops nor coloops, we form the 2-sum of each with a third such rooted matroid by identifying their roots and deleting the common element. The two original rooted matroids are equivalent when these sums agree on whether their path-width is at most two for every choice of the third rooted matroid.

arxiv:2611.01971.title: On Bykov Cycles in Filippov Systems
arxiv:2611.01971.summary: We introduce two types of Bykov cycles for Filippov systems: crossing Bykov cycles, which retain the main dynamical features of their smooth counterparts, and sliding Bykov cycles, whose dynamics intrinsically involves the switching manifold. We construct explicit piecewise linear examples of both configurations. For crossing Bykov cycles, we prove the existence of hyperbolic invariant sets carrying symbolic dynamics, as in the classical smooth setting.
arxiv:2611.01971.authors: Matheus G. C. Cunha, Paulo R. da Silva

arxiv:2611.01972.title: The equality $s(G)=\eta(G)+\exp(G)-1$ fails for $G=C_2^7\oplus C_6$
arxiv:2611.01972.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. The Erd\H{o}s-Ginzburg-Ziv constant $\mathsf{s}(G)$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length at least $\ell$ contains a zero-sum subsequence of length $\exp(G)$. The short zero-sum constant $\eta(G)$ is defined similarly, with the requirement that the zero-sum subsequence is nonempty and has length at most $\exp(G)$.

arxiv:2611.01979.title: Covariant Calculus and Hamiltonian Flows for Nonlocal Wasserstein Metrics
arxiv:2611.01979.summary: In this paper, we study nonlocal metrics on smooth positive probability densities on a closed manifold, induced by symmetric jump kernels and density-dependent mobilities. First, we introduce the density-variation operator to express the density derivatives of the Dirichlet form and kinetic energy. Second, we construct density and velocity-field representations of the tangent space and prove their isometric equivalence.
arxiv:2611.01979.authors: Yuanke Chen, Jinqiao Duan, Qiao Huang

arxiv:2611.01980.title: Finite-Regularity Counterexamples to Katok's Periodic-Point Conjecture
arxiv:2611.01980.summary: For any $r>1$ and any nonnegative sequence $\omega(n)=o(n)$, we construct a $C^r$ sphere diffeomorphism $f$ with $h=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)>0$ such that \begin{equation*} \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log\#\Fix(f^n)=h, \qquad \sum_{n\geqslant1}e^{-hn+\omega(n)}\#\Fix(f^n)<\infty. \end{equation*} Every ergodic invariant probability measure is hyperbolic, and, apart from finitely many fixed points, all periodic points lie in a single topologically mixing homoclinic class of entropy $h$. This shows that the logarithmic periodic-point lower bound is optimal in finite regularity.

arxiv:2611.01985.title: Fixed points via tilting
arxiv:2611.01985.summary: In this article we initiate the study of perfect commutative $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras in the non-connective setting. As an application we show that given a finite $C_p$-space $X$ the $\mathbb{F}_p$-cochains on $X^{C_p}$ can be recovered as a base-change of the tilt of the Tate construction on cochains on $X^e$.

arxiv:2611.01994.title: Unfolding of symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories
arxiv:2611.01994.summary: We prove Lurie's proposed description of left rigid symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories in terms of purely $\infty$-categorical data. More precisely, unfolding gives an equivalence between left rigid symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories and complete categorical chain complexes of rigid symmetric monoidal $\infty$-categories. More generally, unfolding identifies skeletal sequences with categorical chain complexes without the completeness condition.

arxiv:2611.02000.title: A Reider-type theorem for syzygies of cyclic covers of anticanonical rational surfaces
arxiv:2611.02000.summary: Let $\pi\colon X\to S$ be a smooth ramified cyclic cover of an anticanonical rational surface, with $\kappa(X)\geq0$, and let $A$ be a divisor on $S$. We prove a Reider-type theorem for syzygies: for every integer $p\ge 0$, the adjoint divisor $K_X+\pi^*A$ satisfies Property $\mathrm{N}_p$ provided that $A\cdot C\geq p+3$ for every curve $C\subseteq S$ with $C^2\le 1$. One ingredient is a syzygy criterion for finite covers that reduces the weight-two Koszul vanishing on $X$ to weight-one vanishing for the nontrivial character modules on $S$.

arxiv:2611.02005.title: A complete characterization of graphs with second largest eigenvalue at most $(\sqrt5-1)/2$
arxiv:2611.02005.summary: In 1993, Cao and Hong posed the problem of characterizing graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is greater than $1/3$ and less than $(\sqrt5-1)/2$. Subsequent work extended the question to the non-strict bound. We give a complete structural characterization of connected graphs $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge2$ satisfying $\lambda_2(G)\le(\sqrt5-1)/2$.
arxiv:2611.02005.authors: Chaohui Chen, Hangxi Cha, Haiying Shan, Muhuo Liu

arxiv:2611.02010.title: Volume Doubling and Geometric Inequalities on Graphs with Bakry-\'Emery Curvature
arxiv:2611.02010.summary: We consider irreducible reversible Markov chains whose nonzero off-diagonal transition probabilities are bounded below by $\epsilon>0$ and whose reversible measure satisfies $m_-\le m(x)\le\kappa m_-$. Under the Bakry--\'Emery curvature condition $\mathrm{CD}(K,\infty)$, with $K\in\mathbb{R}$, we establish Wang's log-Harnack inequality $$ P_t(\log f)(x)\le\log P_tf(y) +\frac{C\mathrm{dist}(x,y)^2}{\int_0^t e^{2Ks}\mathrm{d} s}, $$ for bounded positive $f$ bounded away from zero and all $x,y\in V$, where $C$ is a constant dependent only on $\varepsilon$. Building upon this inequality, we further prove volume doubling property: let $K_-:=\max\{-K,0\}$ $$ \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,2R))\le…
arxiv:2611.02010.authors: Yanlong Ding, Shiping Liu, Chiyu Zhou

arxiv:2611.02013.title: The Coxeter-Todd abelian sixfold, Gamma00, and big Schottky
arxiv:2611.02013.summary: We recall the construction of the Coxeter-Todd principally polarized abelian sixfold, and study its special properties. We show that the base locus of the Gamma00 linear system on the Coxeter-Todd sixfold consists of 253 points, disproving the stronger version by Donagi and Beauville--Debarre of the Gamma00 conjecture of van Geemen and van der Geer. This also leads us to construct explicit indecomposable 7-dimensional principally polarized abelian varieties that are not Jacobians, but lie in the so-called Big Schottky locus, thus disproving the corresponding conjecture from the Schottky-Jung approach to the Schottky problem.

arxiv:2611.02043.title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
arxiv:2611.02043.summary: We prove the D\'iaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp.

arxiv:2611.02046.title: On Guarding Line Arrangements
arxiv:2611.02046.summary: We study the problem of guarding a set of straight lines in the plane by selecting a minimum-cardinality set of points such that every line contains at least one selected point. This problem is known to be strongly NP-hard \cite{megiddo}. We investigate approximation algorithms for the problem and analyze their performance guarantees under various structural assumptions on the underlying line arrangement.

arxiv:2611.02063.title: Extremal zero-sum sequences without elements of maximal order
arxiv:2611.02063.summary: Let $\mathsf D(G)$ denote the Davenport constant of a finite abelian group $G$, the maximal length of a minimal zero-sum sequence over $G$. Gao and Geroldinger conjectured that every minimal zero-sum sequence of length $\mathsf D(G)$~\cite[Conjecture~6.1]{GG99} and every zero-sumfree sequence of length $\mathsf D(G)-1$~\cite[Conjecture~4.1]{GG06} contains an element of order $\exp(G)$. We disprove both conjectures by proving a density-one theorem: for every fixed finite abelian group $H$ of exponent $M=2^ap^b$, where $a\ge2$, $b\ge1$, and $p$ is an odd prime, the set of integers $r\ge0$ for which $G_r=C_2^r\oplus H$ admits a minimal zero-sum sequence of length $\mathsf D(G_r)$ with no term…

arxiv:2611.02070.title: Classical and Quantum Logics with Multiple Non-Equivalent and Non-Isomorphic Models
arxiv:2611.02070.summary: Both quantum and classical logics have several mutually non-equivalent and non-isomorphic models as has repeatedly been proved in the literature. Yet, several authors have recently come with criticisms of this result. In this paper, we show that the criticisms are either unfounded or wrong.

arxiv:2611.02072.title: Enumeration of $k$-convex polyominoes by semi-perimeter
arxiv:2611.02072.summary: We prove the Conway--Guttmann formula for the generating function of $k$-convex polyominoes by semi-perimeter, for every $k\ge2$. A decomposition according to the two diagonal directions reduces the enumeration to convex polyominoes satisfying a one-bend condition in one diagonal direction. Splitting these polyominoes at the right endpoint of the top row leaves an initial part followed by columns whose vertical intervals decrease by inclusion.

arxiv:2611.02080.title: Koszul duality for boundary categories
arxiv:2611.02080.summary: We study how Koszul duality relates two kinds of boundary constructions associated with a smooth category and a proper category. For a smooth category with a proper Koszul-dualizing subcategory, we construct a fully faithful functor from its categorical neighborhood of infinity to the singularity category associated to the proper category. We prove that this functor is an equivalence precisely when the smooth category is reflexive, meaning that it can be reconstructed from its finite-dimensional module theory.

arxiv:2611.02097.title: On the representability of actions of algebras with several bilinear multiplications
arxiv:2611.02097.summary: We study the representability of actions in varieties of algebras with $n \geq 1$ not necessarily associative bilinear multiplications. We first prove that, for homogeneous varieties, action accessibility is equivalent to being an Orzech category of interest. For an action accessible, operadic variety we then construct the external weak actor $\mathcal{E}(X)$ of an algebra $X$, an algebra with $n$ bilinear partial operations together with a natural monomorphism encoding the actions on $X$.

arxiv:2611.02098.title: Characterizing $k$-Naples parking functions and refining bounds via obstructed parking functions
arxiv:2611.02098.summary: The Naples parking functions are a major generalization of the classical parking functions, where cars have more options to park because they are allowed to check (and possibly park) backward up to a fixed number of spots before driving forward as in the classical case. In a previous work, using involutions we established an injection from the Naples parking functions to a special set of obstructed parking functions, which we referred to as \textit{left obstructed}, thereby immediately obtaining a crude upper bound on the former set. We continue that work here by identifying the image of this injection, providing a characterization of Naples parking functions as a certain (smaller) set of…

arxiv:2611.02100.title: Electrical quantum groups
arxiv:2611.02100.summary: We give a construction of electrical quantum group and its superpartner as coideal subalgebras in $U_q(\mathfrak{gl}(N))$ and, respectively, in $U^u_q(\mathfrak{gl}(1|N-1))$, where the latter is an "ungraded" (non-standard) quantum general linear supergroup. We derive them as quantum isotropy subgroups of triangular twisted K-matrices found in one of our recent papers.
arxiv:2611.02100.authors: D. Algethami, A. Mudrov, V. Stukopin

arxiv:2611.02106.title: Ergodicity of geodesic flows on Aravinda-Farrell twisted doubles
arxiv:2611.02106.summary: The announced rank-one ergodicity theorem of Rodriguez Hertz, Rodriguez Hertz, and Wu includes the nonpositively curved metrics considered here on Aravinda--Farrell twisted doubles. For these construction metrics, a direct geometric argument identifies the singular set. Their singular geodesics are precisely those tangent to the torus sections of finitely many flat product collars, so their initial vectors have Liouville measure zero.

arxiv:2611.02111.title: Cohomology of regular spherical actions
arxiv:2611.02111.summary: We study regular spherical actions, namely, actions of a connected compact Lie group G on a manifold M with equidimensional orbits, some of which are spheres. These spherical orbits are diffeomorphic to homogeneous spaces G/H, and there is a list of nine possible families of pairs (G, H). The normalizer N of H in G plays an important role in our calculations, as does the Weyl group W = N/H.
arxiv:2611.02111.authors: Jos\'e Ignacio Royo Prieto, Martintxo Saralegi-Aranguren, Robert Wolak

arxiv:2611.02116.title: Complete Topological Invariant and Coding of Homoclinic Flows on the Two-Dimensional Sphere
arxiv:2611.02116.summary: We study codimension one homoclinic flows on closed surfaces and introduce a complete topological invariant based on the structural graph of the flow and the distinguishing graphs of its atoms. This invariant completely determines the topological equivalence class of a homoclinic flow. For flows on the two-dimensional sphere, we construct a canonical coding algorithm that avoids the global renumbering required in the classical coding of Morse flows and substantially reduces the computational complexity.

arxiv:2611.02128.title: A hitting-time version of Kotzig's conjecture in random graphs
arxiv:2611.02128.summary: A family of perfect matchings on the same vertex set is said to have the Kotzig property if the union of any pair of matchings forms a Hamilton cycle. Kotzig famously conjectured that, when $n$ is even, the complete graph on $n$ vertices can be decomposed into $n-1$ perfect matchings with the Kotzig property. A closely related conjecture of Wormald states that, for fixed $d \ge 3$, whp a random $d$-regular graph contains $d$ perfect matchings with the Kotzig property.
arxiv:2611.02128.authors: Stefan Glock, Lyuben Lichev, Amedeo Sgueglia

arxiv:2611.02167.title: On a hybrid trilinear Hilbert transform
arxiv:2611.02167.summary: In this paper we study the boundedness properties of a \emph{hybrid} trilinear Hilbert transform characterized by a \emph{dual regime} which simultaneously exhibits 1) \emph{resonant} (zero curvature) features, \emph{i.e.}, modulation invariance properties, and 2) \emph{non-resonant} (non-zero curvature) features. Specifically, given $a\in(0,\infty)\setminus \{1,2\}$ and $\vec{\lambda}:=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\lambda_4)\in (\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\})^4$ with $\lambda_1\neq \lambda_2$ and $\lambda_3\neq \lambda_4$, we provide wide-range $L^p$ bounds for the trilinear operator $$ HTHT^a_{\vec{\lambda}} (f_1,f_2,f_3)(x):= p.v. \int_{\mathbb R} f_1(x-\lambda_1 t)\,f_2(x-\lambda_2…
arxiv:2611.02167.authors: Cristina Benea, Fr\'ed\'eric Bernicot, Victor Lie

arxiv:2611.02168.title: Minimal cellular resolutions of complementary edge ideals
arxiv:2611.02168.summary: We construct an explicit minimal cellular resolution for every squarefree monomial ideal generated in degree $n-2$ in the polynomial ring $S=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. Such an ideal is the complementary edge ideal $I_c(G)$ of a simple graph $G$ on $[n]$, and the resolution is supported on a labeled regular CW complex $X_G$ of dimension at most $2$. This yields closed formulas for the differentials and for the multigraded Betti numbers of $I_c(G)$ in terms of graph invariants.

arxiv:2611.02187.title: An $L\log L$ theory of sparse graph convergence
arxiv:2611.02187.summary: Borgs, Chayes, Cohn and Zhao developed a limit theory for sparse graphs based on $L^p$ upper regularity with $p>1$, where Holder's inequality controls small sets. We develop the analogous theory in the Orlicz class $L\log L$, replacing Holder by the Young-Fenchel inequality for $\Psi(u)=(1+u)\log(1+u)-u$ and $\Psi^*(v)=e^v-1-v$. We prove a weak regularity lemma for upper $\Psi$-regular graphons with $4^{O(1/\varepsilon^2)}$ parts, using the modular $\int\Psi$ as the energy; that upper $\Psi$-regular sequences have cut-metric convergent subsequences; that convergent sequences with $L\log L$ limits are upper $\Psi$-regular; and that $L\log L$ balls are cut-metric compact.

arxiv:2611.02191.title: Graphs versus loopless digraphs with a given degree sequence, and convergence of uniformly random graphs at every density
arxiv:2611.02191.summary: For a degree sequence d on n vertices with M edges, let G(d) be the number of simple graphs and D(d) the number of loopless digraphs with in-degree = out-degree = d. We conjecture that G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log(2+M/n)) for every graphical d, a single inequality across all densities, and prove it up to an extra factor log n: G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log n log(2+M/n)) for every graphical d. The proof compares pairs of graphs with Eulerian digraphs by alternately colouring closed trails; the failure of injectivity is measured exactly, shared edges cancel against 2-cycles, and parity is handled by merging trails and by a parity argument on Eulerian circuits of odd components.

arxiv:2611.02194.title: The real eigenvalues of the non-backtracking Laplacian
arxiv:2611.02194.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $N$ nodes and $M$ edges, with minimum degree at least $2$. We prove that the non-backtracking Laplacian of $G$ has at least $2M-2N+2c+2b$ real eigenvalues, counted with algebraic multiplicity, where $c$ is the number of connected components of $G$ and $b$ is the number of bipartite ones. More precisely, at least $M-N+2c$ of them lie in $[0,1)$ and at least $M-N+2b$ lie in $(1,2]$.

arxiv:2611.02210.title: A Quasisymmetric Analogue of the Bruhat Order
arxiv:2611.02210.summary: We define a quasisymmetric analogue of the Bruhat order on indexed binary forests using the multiplicity-free Monk rule for forest polynomials. For the finite window $\mathcal{P}_n$ of forests supported in $[1,n]$, we construct an explicit partition into saturated chains terminating at the top rank, proving that $\mathcal{P}_n$ is strongly Sperner. We also recover the known Catalan ballot formula for its rank numbers.

arxiv:2611.02237.title: Nonreciprocal Spherical Attention and Retrieval: Sharp Coarsening Clocks and Certified Score Correction
arxiv:2611.02237.summary: We develop nonreciprocal spherical attention as a mathematical framework for coarsening and compressed nearest-neighbor retrieval. For two shrinking acute blocks whose centers have zero skew pairing and whose total mass ratio is subexponential in inverse temperature, we prove $\lim_{\beta\to\infty}\beta^{-1}\log T_\beta=1-\cos\phi$, without restricting particle-count growth. An explicit three-body flow has two rigorously separated metastable exponents.

arxiv:2611.02246.title: Direct and Indirect Competition in a Two-Prey-One-Predator System : Global Dynamics, Chaos, and the Paine Conjecture
arxiv:2611.02246.summary: This paper studies the global dynamics of a three-dimensional Lotka-Volterra system of two prey, with direct competition between them, and one predator. Under a symmetry assumption, the rescaled parameter space is sorted into four generic categories, which yield a complete classification of the global dynamics into 56 meaningful subcases. We determine the existence and stability of the boundary and positive equilibria, including global asymptotic stability and bistability of boundary equilibria, and necessary and sufficient conditions for local asymptotic stability of the positive equilibrium.

arxiv:2611.02249.title: How the eigenvalue region of standardized Laplacians leaves the 2005 polygon
arxiv:2611.02249.summary: Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of $n\times n$ standardized Laplacian matrices, and let $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$ be the polygon introduced in 2005, with upper vertices $\lambda_0=0,\dots,\lambda_{n-1}=1$. It is now known that $\Lambda_n=S_n$, and that $\Lambda_n$ is convex, if and only if $n\le4$. We study how $\Lambda_n$ leaves $S_n$ near an edge $[\lambda_m,\lambda_{m+1}]$, $2(m+1)<n$.

arxiv:2611.02261.title: Normality of closures of conormal bundles to Schubert cells for $\operatorname{GL}_n$
arxiv:2611.02261.summary: We prove normality of closures of the conormal bundle to certain Schubert cells in the flag variety for $\operatorname{GL}_n$ coming from Grassmannians. Our argument uses a Zelevinsky-type resolution of singularities, and through a sequence of cohomological computations based on the Borel--Weil--Bott theorem, we reduce normality to a problem about Kronecker coefficients, which we solve by applying results of Knutson and Tao from honeycomb theory.

arxiv:2611.02320.title: Motivic Eilenberg--Mac Lane spaces at the characteristic
arxiv:2611.02320.summary: We provide a novel, homotopy theoretic model for the motivic Eilenberg--Mac Lane spaces $K(Z_{(p)}(n), 2n) \in Spc(k)$ over fields of characteristic p. Using this, we determine their motives and, consequently, determine the motivic Steenrod algebra at the characteristic. Applications include the Hopkins--Morel isomorphism over arbitrary base schemes as well as the computation of the p-completed motivic stable stems and algebraic cobordism groups of fields of characteristic p.

arxiv:2611.02388.title: Construction of stability conditions on some Kuznetsov components
arxiv:2611.02388.summary: We construct Bridgeland stability conditions on the Kuznetsov components of smooth Fano hypersurfaces of degrees three, four, and six and dimension at least three, smooth quartic double fivefolds, and smooth Fano complete intersections of three quadrics. For odd-dimensional cubic hypersurfaces and quartic double fivefolds, every connected component of the numerical stability manifold is biholomorphic to $\mathbb C\times\mathbb H$. For general cubic sevenfolds and quartic double fivefolds, spherical twists produce infinitely many distinct connected components.

arxiv:2611.02394.title: On Lattice Tilings by Symmetric Limited Magnitude Error Balls: Q-polynomials and Ideal Characterization
arxiv:2611.02394.summary: In this paper, we study the lattice tilings of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ by the symmetric limited magnitude error balls $\mathcal{B}(n,t,k,k)$, which play a crucial role in flash memory applications. Using generating functions and complete Bell polynomials, we derive an explicit formula for the $r$-th Q-polynomial associated with $\mathcal{B}(n,t,k,k)$. Then, an ideal-theoretic characterization of the lattice tiling condition is developed: for an odd prime $p$ dividing $|\mathcal{B}(n,t,k,k)|$ exactly once, a lattice tiling would force a certain polynomial to lie outside a certain ideal of $\mathbb{F}_p[Y_1,\dots,Y_{\frac{p-1}{2}}]$.

arxiv:2611.02398.title: A Global Generic Locus for Elementary Abelian p-covers of P^1 with two Ramification Points
arxiv:2611.02398.summary: In this paper, we study elementary abelian $p$-covers of $P^1$ totally ramified at exactly two points and unramified elsewhere. Such covers are isomorphic to the rank-$\ell$ Artin--Schreier curves $ X_{f, \ell} : y^{p^\ell} - y = f(x), $ where $f \in \bar{F}_p[x^{\pm 1}]$ has a pole of order $d_1>0$ at $0$ and order $d_2>0$ at $\infty$. After fixing $d_1$ and $d_2$, the cover $X_{f, \ell}$ is generic if its Newton polygon is minimal as $f$ varies over all Laurent polynomials with pole orders $d_1$ and $d_2$.

arxiv:2611.02399.title: Minimum net-saturated graphs of even order
arxiv:2611.02399.summary: Let \(F\) be the net, consisting of a triangle with one distinct degree-one vertex attached to each of its vertices. A graph is \(F\)-saturated if it contains no copy of \(F\), but adding any missing edge creates one. Zhao, You and Zhang determined the minimum number of edges and conjectured that the minimum graph is unique at every sufficiently large even order.

arxiv:2611.02417.title: Calogero-Moser Polynomial Approximations and Dwork Congruences for Complete Flags
arxiv:2611.02417.summary: We construct $p$-adic polynomial approximations to the zero-framing cohomological quasimap vertex of cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties from the trigonometric Calogero--Moser system. Negative integer couplings give regular staircase Jack polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients. We compare them with complete-flag master polynomials extending the construction of Smirnov--Varchenko.

arxiv:2611.02424.title: Around the Clock. New Twists on Fitch Cheney's Five-Card Trick
arxiv:2611.02424.summary: Fitch Cheney's five-card trick is one of the purest two-person effects in card magic, and it has attracted mathematicians for more than seventy five years. This article retells the effect and its classic method, surveys how far it can be pushed, and presents several new results that matter to performers. We give a version of Cheney's method that needs no fixed first suit and no fixed ``lowest card'': shifting every card one step in rank and one step in suit shifts the display in the same way.

arxiv:2611.02429.title: The Hubbard-Wigner model: from Aubry-Mather theory to Fractional Quantum Hall Effects
arxiv:2611.02429.summary: The Hubbard-Wigner model describes binary lattice configurations with convex repulsive pair interactions. We give a unified classification of its periodic minimizers, minimizing invariant measures, and Aubry sets through a positive block-count identity, recovering explicit plateau widths and a complete devil's staircase for the minimizing density. This variational structure parallels Aubry-Mather theory and the authors' work on Aubry's completeness conjecture, where the staircase is related to the sliding and pinning mechanisms underlying the conducting and insulating interpretations of particle chains.

arxiv:2611.02465.title: Pointwise Ergodic Theorems Along $\lfloor p^c\rfloor$ for Every $c>1$
arxiv:2611.02465.summary: Let $c>1$ be noninteger, and let $\Lambda$ denote the von Mangoldt function. The averages \[ A_N^{c} f(x):=\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^{N} \Lambda(n)f\bigl(T^{\lfloor n^c\rfloor}x\bigr) \] satisfy the variational estimate \[ \bigl\|\mathcal{V}^r(A_N^{c} f:N\in\mathbb{N})\bigr\|_{L^p(X)} \lesssim_{c,p,r}\|f\|_{L^p(X)} \] for every $1<p<\infty$ and $r>2$, on every $\sigma$-finite measure-preserving system. In particular, the normalized averages along fractional powers of primes converge almost everywhere.

arxiv:2611.02483.title: Large independent sets via neighborhood block dynamics, Glauber dynamics, and local occupancy
arxiv:2611.02483.summary: Local occupancy can be used to bound the expected size of a hard-core independent set. The framework of locally stationary distributions shows that for triangle-free graphs, despite slow mixing at the relevant fugacity parameter, standard Glauber dynamics can be used to find sets close to the local occupancy guarantee. We improve the application of this framework to the hard-core model by replacing a conditional mixing argument with a more direct approach based on a short sequence of single-site updates that, from every initial configuration, achieves the required occupancy inequality.

arxiv:2611.02494.title: Relative trisection maps on 4-manifolds
arxiv:2611.02494.summary: We show that for an arbitrary compact orientable smooth $4$--dimensional manifold $M$ with a given open book structure on the boundary $\partial M \neq \emptyset$, which may be disconnected, there exists a generic smooth map of $M$ onto the $2$--disk which gives a relative trisection on $M$ consistent with the given open book structure on $\partial M$. This gives a new proof to the existence of a relative trisection on $M$. In fact, it turns out that every relative trisection can be obtained in this way.

arxiv:2611.02496.title: The topology of the amoeba map and maximal volume
arxiv:2611.02496.summary: For a smooth complete intersection $V\subset(\C^*)^n$ of dimension $k$, $n\ge2k$, we bound the volume of its amoeba by $\pi^{2k}$ times a sum of mixed volumes, divided by the order of any finite group $\Gamma$ of symmetries commuting with the logarithmic map. For $n=2k\ge4$ almost every fibre of the amoeba map has a number of points divisible by $2|\Gamma|$. For $n=2k$ we characterise the varieties of maximal volume, show that for $k\ge2$ they are not real, and prove that no plane in general position in $(\C^*)^4$ has maximal volume.

arxiv:2611.02515.title: Summing over Seifert Manifolds in Narain Ensemble Averages
arxiv:2611.02515.summary: The ensemble average of Narain conformal field theories over their moduli space is a real-analytic Eisenstein series, whose Poincar\'e expansion can be interpreted as a sum over lens spaces weighted by the partition functions of Abelian Chern-Simons theory. In this paper we extend this correspondence from lens spaces to Seifert manifolds, which gives an example of a restricted sum over topologies of the kind that arises in three-dimensional quantum gravity. A Seifert manifold is obtained from a fixed core, a punctured surface times a circle, by gluing solid tori to its boundary tori, and we place a copy of the Narain theory on each of these tori.

arxiv:2611.02523.title: Substrate hypergraph cycles: unique steady states and persistence for every enzyme assignment; oscillations enabled by enzyme sharing
arxiv:2611.02523.summary: We associate a directed substrate hypergraph with an enzymatic reaction system. The hypergraph records which substrates each composite reaction consumes and produces, and each composite reaction is realized by a Henri--Michaelis--Menten (HMM) module whose enzyme may be distinct, shared with other reactions, or absent. We call the hypergraph a cycle when it is strongly connected and every substrate is produced by exactly one reaction and consumed by exactly one reaction, each time with coefficient one; equivalently, its dual is a strongly connected ordinary directed graph.

arxiv:2611.02535.title: Noncommutative extensions of an ergodic theorem of Breiman
arxiv:2611.02535.summary: Let $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra, $T:L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)\to L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ be induced by a normal $\tau$-preserving $*$-automorphism of $\mathcal{M}$, and $x\in L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)$. We will prove the bilaterally almost uniform convergence of averages of the form $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}T^k(x_k),$$ generalizing an ergodic theorem proven by Breiman in \cite{Breiman57}, where $(x_k)_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is an element of the noncommutative vector-valued $L_p$-space $L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau;\ell_\infty)$ such that there exists $x\in L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ with $(x_k-x)_{k=0}^{\infty}\in L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau;c_0)$. A generalization to semifinite…

arxiv:2611.02544.title: Counterexamples to a Cubic Nondegeneracy Conjecture
arxiv:2611.02544.summary: Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko conjectured that a cubic Boolean generating function satisfying an ordered separation condition on its second polar must be equivalent to one of two symmetric normal forms. Two infinite families of counterexamples are constructed and proved analytically; both are direct sums of small seeds, and neither is equivalent to the proposed forms even after linear functions are added. The first adjoins a nondegenerate quadratic block to a ternary cubic seed and is distinguished from the proposed forms by the radical of its third polar.

arxiv:2611.02564.title: Central pivot point control of a body-attached spring-mass runner: periodic gaits, stabilization, template embedding and approximate analytic return maps
arxiv:2611.02564.summary: The spring-loaded inverted pendulum (SLIP) describes the center-of-mass (COM) motion of runners but has no trunk. In trunk models, the hip torque couples posture and COM motion and destroys the central-force structure on which SLIP analysis relies. As a result, trunk models have been studied almost only numerically.
arxiv:2611.02564.authors: \.Izel Sever, O. Kaan Karag\"oz, M. Mert Ankaral{\i}

arxiv:2611.02577.title: $S_n$-equivariant $L$-classes of Cartesian powers of Witt spaces and the Hodge index conjecture for symmetric products
arxiv:2611.02577.summary: For a compact oriented even-dimensional Witt pseudomanifold $X$, we compute the $S_n$-equivariant Banagl--Zagier $L$-classes of $X^n$ in terms of the Goresky--MacPherson $L$-classes of $X$ and the intersection cohomology Euler characteristic of $X$. This generalizes a theorem of Zagier for manifolds. Our approach is based on analyzing the equivariant structure of the signature operator of $X^n$ using equivariant $KK$-theory and power operations in analytic $K$-homology.

arxiv:2611.02582.title: Quantum 6j-symbols arising from a subfactor of finite index and finite depth and the zipper condition for 4-tensors in two-dimensional topological order
arxiv:2611.02582.summary: We study 3-tensors satisfying the ``zipper condition,'' which play an important role in tensor network approaches to two-dimensional topological order. In our previous work, we identified the 4-tensors appearing in these approaches with bi-unitary connections in the Jones theory of subfactors in operator algebras. These bi-unitary connections give rise to subfactors of finite index.

arxiv:2611.02586.title: Dynamics of Transversal Matroids
arxiv:2611.02586.summary: We propose a way of generating matroids by randomly picking indicator vectors, and since we will see that it mostly gives uniform matroids, which are transversal, we then look at randomly generated transversal matroids. In both models we also investigate threshold phenomena of certain monotone increasing properties. Non-monotone properties of transversal matroids will also be investigated.

arxiv:2611.02614.title: Indecomposable Uniform Families on the Adams 4-Line
arxiv:2611.02614.summary: We show that the $f_j$, $p_j$, $D_3(j)$, and $p_j'$ families on the 4-line of the classical Adams spectral sequence all conform to the Uniform Doomsday Conjecture. We do so by first using Bruner's formula to establish uniform families of differentials on these classes. We then study the Burklund-Xu and Cartan-Eilenberg spectral sequences to ensure that the differential targets are nonzero.

arxiv:2611.02615.title: Spectral radius and size conditions for 1-tough balanced bipartite graphs to contain a $k$-factor with $k\ge 3$
arxiv:2611.02615.summary: The largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix $A(G)$ of a graph $G$ is called the spectral radius $\rho(G)$ of $G$. If $S$ is a vertex cut of a connected graph $G$, then $c(G-S)$ denotes the number of connected components of $G-S$. The toughness $t(G)$ of a graph $G$ is defined as $t(G) = \min\left\{\frac{|S|}{c(G-S)}: S \subset V(G), \text{ and } c(G-S) > 1\right\}$.
arxiv:2611.02615.authors: Jinxuan Ren, Jiayao Song, Ligong Wang

arxiv:2611.02638.title: Hereditary lowerability of diagonal entropy scales
arxiv:2611.02638.summary: Let $T$ be a continuous self-map of a compact metric space. For each integer $p\geq2$, we consider the upper capacity entropy scale obtained by dividing the $p$-fold logarithm of an orbit covering number by the $(p-1)$-fold logarithm of time. We prove that every nonempty compact set contains a compact subset realizing any value between zero and its own scale entropy.

arxiv:2611.02714.title: Triangle Relation Planar Algebras: Cohomology, Classification, and New Families
arxiv:2611.02714.summary: We establish a finite system of consistency equations for triangle relation planar algebras. Within the Yang--Baxter relation class, we characterize triangle relations by $H^2(K;\mathbb C)=0$, where $K$ is the fusion complex recording the support of the fusion coefficients. Together with a reconstruction theorem, this gives an algebraic classification procedure.

arxiv:2611.02717.title: Universal Curve Counting in Calabi-Yau 4-folds
arxiv:2611.02717.summary: Recently, Pardon introduced a universal curve counting framework, which allows him to show that curve counting on 3-folds is "generated" by local curves (in a precise sense). We implement this universal curve counting program for Calabi-Yau 4-folds, where a significant technical difficulty comes from the dependence of the virtual dimension on the genus, which leads to more complicated generators than just local curves. Our main techniques are combinations of deformation-theoretic and homotopy-theoretic methods with an adaptation of Pardon's generic transversality results, which allow us to establish a full set of (computable) generators for CY4 curve counting.

arxiv:2611.02724.title: All-Disorder Localization for the One-Dimensional Anderson Model with Power-Law Hopping
arxiv:2611.02724.summary: We consider the one-dimensional random operator \[ (H_{\lambda,\omega}u)(n) = \sum_{m\ne n}\frac{u(m)}{|n-m|^r} +\lambda\omega_nu(n), \] where the random variables $\omega_n$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $[-1,1]$ (i.e., \mbox{$\omega_n\stackrel{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[-1,1]$}). For every $\lambda>0$ and $r>3/2$, we prove that $H_{\lambda,\omega}$ almost surely has pure point spectrum and admits an orthonormal eigenbasis $\{\psi_j\}$ satisfying \[ \sum_{n\in\bbZ}(1+|n|)^{2\tau}|\psi_j(n)|^2<\infty \qquad \text{for every }j\text{ and }0\le\tau<r-\frac32. \] These conclusions establish spectral localization, thereby rigorously confirming the prediction of…

arxiv:2611.02742.title: k-uniform l-Eulerian hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.02742.summary: We consider $l$-Euler trails and $l$-Euler circuits in finite $k$-uniform directed multihypergraphs, where $k\geq 2$ and $1\leq l<k$. Let $D$ be such a directed multihypergraph. The notions of $l$-connectivity and $l$-balance are defined in terms of the $l$-tails and $l$-heads of its hyperarcs.
arxiv:2611.02742.authors: Yiming Lei, Chenxi Lv, Bing Dai

arxiv:2611.02743.title: Two-point residual step size gradient methods for linear systems
arxiv:2611.02743.summary: Kaczmarz-type methods often converge slowly when the coefficient matrix is ill-conditioned. In particular, when the smallest singular value is small, every row of the coefficient matrix is nearly orthogonal to the corresponding right singular direction, so that the iteration stalls along that direction. To break this slow-convergence regime, we borrow the delayed-step-size idea of the Barzilai-Borwein (BB) method and, within the framework of the residual-based surrogate-hyperplane Kaczmarz method, propose two new step sizes for gradient-descent-type methods solving linear systems: a delayed residual step size \(\alpha_k^{\mathrm{DR}}\) and a residual-difference step size…

arxiv:2611.02749.title: Generalized parabolic Demazure modules and the N!/2-conjecture for two-row diagrams
arxiv:2611.02749.summary: We study a family of generalized parabolic Demazure modules, i.e. of gl[x]-submodules of tensor products of integrable representations of the affine Lie algebra generated by tensor products of extremal vectors, and describe these modules by generators and relations. Realizing the Garsia--Haiman modules of two-row diagrams as fusion products of two local Weyl modules, we show that their y-graded components admit filtrations whose associated graded modules are isomorphic to tensor products of these generalized parabolic Demazure modules with the cohomology rings of Grassmannians. As a consequence, the Garsia-Haiman modules of two-row diagrams of a fixed size generate a distributive lattice,…

arxiv:2611.02760.title: Every tournament $T$ of order at least 3 admits infinitely many $T$-irregular oriented graphs
arxiv:2611.02760.summary: Let $F$ be a fixed graph. A graph $G$ is $F$-irregular if any two distinct vertices of $G$ belong to a different number of subgraphs of $G$ isomorphic to $F$. In this paper, we settle the strong conjecture about $F$-irregular oriented graphs (Dovzhenok, Lukashenko, and Filiuta, 2026) for the case of tournaments.

arxiv:2611.02762.title: Colorings breaking prescribed families of graph automorphisms
arxiv:2611.02762.summary: We prove that for every continuous action of a compact group on a discrete set, each finite-color template admits a coloring from arbitrary lists of the same size whose stabilizer is contained in a conjugate of the template stabilizer. Consequently, the ordinary and list parameters coincide whenever the ordinary parameter is finite. In particular, we answer the question of Ferrara, Flesch and Gethner negatively for finite graphs, and establish the finite case of the conjecture of Kwa\'sny and Stawiski whenever a distinguishing edge coloring exists.
arxiv:2611.02762.authors: Hui Lei, Yu Wang, Yueyue Zhao

arxiv:2611.02781.title: Hyperbolic scattering in the planar n-body problem
arxiv:2611.02781.summary: For the planar $n$-body problem with homogeneous strong force potentials, given an arbitrary pair of normalized collision-free configurations $(a, b)$, we prove that for any positive energy $h$, there are infinitely many $h$-energy scattering orbits between $a$ and $b$.

arxiv:2611.02789.title: Closed energy formulas on tensor squares of perfect crystals of types $D_4^{(3)}$ and $G_2^{(1)}$
