arxiv:2611.02789.summary: For each integer $l\ge1$, we give closed formulas for the local energies on tensor squares of the level-$l$ perfect crystals of types $D_4^{(3)}$ and $G_2^{(1)}$, normalized to vanish at the all-zero coordinate tensors. The $D_4^{(3)}$ energy is the maximum of three defects, equivalently of nine linear forms in parameters of classical highest-weight elements. Eliminating these parameters yields the maximum of nine piecewise-linear functions of the twelve input coordinates.

arxiv:2611.02795.title: Correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble on a General Interval and Hurwitz Numbers
arxiv:2611.02795.summary: We study correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble $\mathbf J(p,q,\alpha,\beta,N)$ of Hermitian matrices with spectrum in an arbitrary real interval $[p,q]$. For $(p,q)=(0,1)$, Gisonni, Grava and Ruzza expressed the large-$N$ expansion of the correlators $\langle\prod_j \mathrm{tr}\,X^{\lambda_j}\rangle$ through triple monotone Hurwitz numbers. We extend this genus expansion to arbitrary $p,q$ with $\alpha/N$ and $\beta/N$ fixed.

arxiv:2611.02838.title: Characterization of the boundary zero set of stable polynomials in $\mathbb B_2$
arxiv:2611.02838.summary: Given a polynomial $p\in \mathbb{C}[z,w]$ whose zeros lie outside the unit ball $\mathbb{B}_2$ of $\mathbb{C}^2,$ we study its local Weierstrass polynomial--obtained via the Weierstrass Preparation Theorem--and provide a strong version of the Nash curve selection lemma. These results lead to a characterization of the intersection of the zero set of $p$ with the unit sphere: $\mathcal{Z}(p)\cap\mathbb{S}_{2}.$

arxiv:2611.02847.title: Quasimorphisms and bounded cohomology of transformation groups of nonorientable surfaces
arxiv:2611.02847.summary: Let $N_g$ be a closed connected nonorientable surface of genus $g\ge1$, let $\omega$ be a smooth positive density, and let $\mu$ be a good measure. In this paper we generalize the Gambaudo--Ghys construction using homogeneous quasimorphisms on the central quotients of the braid groups of $N_g$. We prove injectivity of this map for density-preserving diffeomorphisms.

arxiv:2611.02885.title: Stability and exact extremal colourings for the Alon--Frankl--Lov\'asz bound
arxiv:2611.02885.summary: The Alon--Frankl--Lov\'asz theorem states that every $q$-colouring of the edges of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains a monochromatic matching of size $\lfloor(n+q-1)/(r+q-1)\rfloor$. For fixed uniformity $r$ and number of colours $q$, we prove a stability theorem: every colouring whose largest monochromatic matching has size at most $n/(r+q-1)+o(n)$ differs from a threshold extremal colouring on only $o(n^r)$ edges. We also give a necessary and sufficient structural characterization of all extremal colourings for sufficiently large $n$.
arxiv:2611.02885.authors: Tianhong Kan, Hongliang Lu, Feihong Yuan

arxiv:2611.02888.title: A Universal Policy Wrapper With Guarantees
arxiv:2611.02888.summary: Many control tasks require driving the system into a prescribed goal set and subsequently keeping it there. The considered setting assumes that a working controller is available that provably reaches and maintains the goal, albeit with suboptimal performance. This controller is referred to as the fallback policy.
arxiv:2611.02888.authors: Georgiy Malaniya, Anton Bolychev, Pavel Osinenko

arxiv:2611.02901.title: Antidiagonal and square averages for amenable groups
arxiv:2611.02901.summary: We prove that, for commuting unitary representations $U,V$ of a countable amenable group $G$, the averages $$ D_F=\frac1{|F|}\sum_{g\in F}U_g^*V_g $$ have a common selfadjoint weak operator limit along all left and right \Folner{} sequences, with strong* convergence along two-sided sequences. This answers Bergelson's question on commuting actions. For any unitary representation $\pi$, we also prove that $A_F=|F|^{-1}\sum_{g\in F}\pi(g^2)$ converges strongly along right \Folner{} sequences to a selfadjoint central operator supported on the finite type~I part of $\pi(G)''$; the adjoints $A_F^*$ converge strongly along left \Folner{} sequences.

arxiv:2611.02925.title: Buildings governed by twisted Bruhat orders
arxiv:2611.02925.summary: This paper introduces the notion of a twisted building associated to a Coxeter system and an initial section of a reflection order. These are pairs of buildings and a map between them which depends on a twisted Bruhat order. It is proved that projection maps exist between components and that the common apartment property holds for a suitable notion of an apartment, generalising what is known for twin buildings.

arxiv:2611.02939.title: Singularities of Separation Coordinates
arxiv:2611.02939.summary: We study singularities of separation coordinates for geodesic flows of real-analytic two-dimensional (pseudo-)Riemannian metrics. We obtain a complete local classification of these singularities using the Nijenhuis operator associated with a quadratic first integral. The singular set is locally a smooth curve, an isolated point, or two transversely intersecting curves.

arxiv:2611.02954.title: High-order fractional linear differential equations do not describe stochastic processes with finite state space
arxiv:2611.02954.summary: The replacement of the classical derivative in the governing equation of a continuous-time Markov process with finite state space by a fractional derivative of arbitrary order $\alpha>1$ produces solutions that are mathematically incompatible with the theory of stochastic processes.

arxiv:2611.02963.title: Full-Rank Constructions of Explicit Lossless Expanders and Good Small-Set qLTCs
arxiv:2611.02963.summary: We construct explicit two-sided lossless expanders whose binary adjacency matrices have full rank, and use them to obtain explicit asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes whose specified X- and Z-check matrices have full row rank and satisfy small-set soundness, or confinement, on a linear range. Our lossless expanders are a variant of those of Hsieh, Lubotzky, Mohanty, Reiner, and Zhang, with a free action of a finite 2-group. Under such an action, injectivity and surjectivity of the adjacency matrix are detected on a fixed-size matrix indexed by vertex orbits.
arxiv:2611.02963.authors: Yali Aharon-Holzman, Michael Ilan, Assaf Reiner, Amnon Ta-Shma

arxiv:2611.02967.title: Operator Fej\'{e}r--Riesz Theorems with Gaps and Degree Bounds
arxiv:2611.02967.summary: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of the real line, and let $S$ be a saturated scalar description of $K$. We prove that every hermitian polynomial with bounded-operator coefficients that is positive semidefinite on $K$ belongs to the operator quadratic module generated by $S$. We also show that if such a polynomial has degree at most $\tt{d}$, then it admits a certificate of weighted degree at most $\tt{d}+c_S$, where $c_S$ depends only on $S$, not on the polynomial or the coefficient Hilbert space.

arxiv:2611.02986.title: On local spectra of classical distance-regular graphs with $b = 2$
arxiv:2611.02986.summary: Using a combination of spectral techniques and combinatorial counts, we prove a number of non-existence results for putative distance-regular graphs with classical parameters, focusing on the case $b=2$. Among those, the case $(d,b,\alpha,\beta)=(d,2,1,2^d-2)$ passed all known feasibility conditions and required a deeper combinatorial analysis, from which nonexistence has been derived whenever $d \ge 9$. In doing so, we constructed a new family of regular graphs with four distinct eigenvalues which would have been local graphs in such a distance-regular graph.

arxiv:2611.03010.title: Strong Borel-Cantelli laws and clusters of visits for random intermittent maps
arxiv:2611.03010.summary: Near the neutral fixed point of an intermittent map, a single entrance into a small target can be followed by a long run of consecutive visits, so the number of visits need not follow its mean. We study targets $[0,u_n]$ for iid random compositions of Liverani-Saussol-Vaienti maps with a bounded parameter law that is regularly varying at its minimum $\alpha\in(0,1)$; this includes a single map. For $u_n=cn^{-g}L(n)$, where $c>0$, $0<g\leq1$ and $L$ is slowly varying, the visit count is almost surely asymptotic to its mean if and only if $\sum_n n^{-1}(nu_n)^{-(1-\alpha)/\alpha}<\infty$.

arxiv:2611.03028.title: The computational capacity of the Logistic family
arxiv:2611.03028.summary: Viewing computing machines as symbolic dynamical systems is a powerful idea which has led to many important results. However, the standard setting of symbolic Turing dynamics is not well suited for studying questions of typicality, genericity, or robustness. Such natural questions, for example, as "what is the computational power of a typical computer program?", "how common is poly-time computability", or "how common is universal computation among all algorithms?" require a different approach.

arxiv:2611.03036.title: Positive integral points on Mordell-Schinzel surfaces
arxiv:2611.03036.summary: We apply the theory of generalised cluster algebras to classify the finiteness of positive integral points on the class of log K3 surfaces defined by $xyz = G(x,y)$ where $G$ has positive coefficients. We furthermore establish results on Zariski density, number of orbits and asymptotic growth of such points. These provide a Diophantine realisation of the finite-affine-indefinite trichotomy of rank-two root systems.
arxiv:2611.03036.authors: Antoine de Saint Germain, Robin Zhang

arxiv:2611.03064.title: Higher Groupoids of Gauge Potentials in Higher Gauge Theories admitting Weights
arxiv:2611.03064.summary: We construct an explicit small model for the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances of higher gauge curvatures by algorithmically trivializing their nonlinear Bianchi identities. More precisely, for a finite-type Sullivan minimal Bianchi algebra equipped with positive integer weights, we organize weighted potentials and higher gauge parameters at each fixed curvature into an $\infty$-groupoid whose gauge transformations are linear in the parameters. We prove that this model is naturally equivalent to the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances through an intermediate total-form model, with explicit projection and section maps and simplicial homotopies.

arxiv:2611.03083.title: An optimal $\chi$-bound for $\{P_7, \text{diamond}\}$-free graphs
arxiv:2611.03083.summary: A $\textit{diamond}$ is a graph obtained by removing an edge from the complete graph on four vertices. A graph is $\{P_7, \text{diamond}\}$-$\textit{free}$ if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to a seven-vertex path or a diamond. Schiermeyer (2020) asked whether there is a constant $c$ such that $\chi(G)\leq\omega(G)+c$ for every $\{P_7, \text{diamond}\}$-free graph $G$.

arxiv:2611.03088.title: Optimal Configurations for Mordell's Problem
arxiv:2611.03088.summary: Mordell's problem asks for the largest product of squared pairwise distances among $n$ points in the complex plane with a prescribed sum of squared distances from the origin. When this sum equals $n$, the maximum for $2\le n\le5$ is known to be $n^n$, attained precisely by the $n$th roots of unity up to rotation and relabeling. For $n\ge6$, Chalk showed that a regular polygon together with its center gives a larger product than the regular $n$-gon.
arxiv:2611.03088.authors: Xiang Ji, Tiancheng Xu, Wensheng Yu

arxiv:2611.03096.title: Non-simple Arrangements of Lines and Pseudolines with Many Triangles
arxiv:2611.03096.summary: We study affine arrangements of an even number $n$ of lines and pseudolines with many triangles. For simple ones, Blanc's bound limits the number of triangular faces to $\lfloor n(n-5/2)/3\rfloor$. Adapting the Bartholdi-Blanc-Loisel doubling to the even case, we construct an infinite series of arrangements of $n=6\cdot2^t+2$ ($8,14,26,50,\ldots$) straight lines with two triple points and $(n(n-5/2)+1)/3$ triangles, one more than the simple bound allows.

arxiv:2611.03124.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
arxiv:2611.03124.summary: We study Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary, sequential, and weak $m$-positive real $(1,1)$-forms in complex dimension $d$. For ordinary $m$-positive forms, we prove the fully mixed relations in every permitted bidegree without assuming semipositivity, generalizing results by Xiao. As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant.

arxiv:2611.03145.title: Reed-Muller Codes are Optimal Binary Linear 3-Query LCCs
arxiv:2611.03145.summary: We prove that any linear $3$-query locally correctable code $C \colon \mathbb{F}_2^k \to \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with constant correction radius must have length $n \geq 2^{\Omega(\sqrt{k})}$. This improves on the prior best lower bound of $2^{\Omega(\sqrt{k/\log k})}$, due to [AG24], and shows that the folklore construction of linear $3$-LCCs from Reed-Muller codes, which achieve length $n = 2^{O(\sqrt{k})}$, is optimal up to constant factors in the exponent. Our proof builds on the approach of [KM24a], further refined in [Yan24,KM24b], that uses "chain derived equations" in combination with Kikuchi graphs.

arxiv:2611.03151.title: Counterexamples to Relaxed Multiplication in List Coloring
arxiv:2611.03151.summary: Jiang and Zhu [J. Combin. Theory Ser.

arxiv:2611.03169.title: An Erd\H{o}s-Pach-Pollack-Tuza theorem for oriented diameter
arxiv:2611.03169.summary: The oriented diameter of a bridgeless graph is the minimum diameter of its strong orientations. Erd\H{o}s, Pach, Pollack and Tuza proved that every connected graph of order $n$ and minimum degree $\delta\ge 2$ has diameter at most $3n/(\delta+1)-1$, which is sharp up to an additive constant. Cochran and Wang conjectured that the oriented diameter obeys the same bound up to an absolute additive constant.
arxiv:2611.03169.authors: Jiangdong Ai, Bin Chen, Yaokun Feng

arxiv:2611.03174.title: Final coalgebras over R-modules
arxiv:2611.03174.summary: Final coalgebras and the coinduction principle for coalgebras over $R$-modules, where $R$ is a commutative ring, are essential in determining the denotational behaviour of various types of linear weighted automata. The goal of this paper is to provide lower and upper bounds on the ordinals that are needed to construct final coalgebras over $R$-modules as the limit of a transfinite sequence of functor iterations. We give an example of a binary intersection preserving finitary functor on the category of abelian groups, which is the category of modules over integers, that fails to converge in $\omega \cdot 2$ steps, thus settling an open problem of Ad\'{a}mek, Milius, and Moss.
arxiv:2611.03174.authors: Ois\'{i}n Flynn-Connolly, Henning Basold, Chase Ford

arxiv:2611.03176.title: A Topology-Based Approach to Representative Volume Element Assessment in Solid Oxide Cell Anodes Using Large Volume Tomography and Persistent Homology
arxiv:2611.03176.summary: Determining the representative volume element is essential for establishing statistically meaningful microstructure-property relationships. Conventional approaches rely on the convergence of selected geometric descriptors, which may yield different estimates of the representative volume. Here, we propose a topology-based framework for assessing the representative scale of a nickel-yttria-stabilized zirconia solid oxide cell anode reconstructed using plasma focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (121.8 um x 83.97 um x 45.99 um).
arxiv:2611.03176.authors: Aleksandra Kukie{\l}ka, Maksym Szemer, Szymon Buchaniec, Katarzyna Berent, Grzegorz Brus

arxiv:2611.03190.title: Asymptotically Optimal Weighted Edge Colorings via Local Bin Packing
arxiv:2611.03190.summary: We study weighted edge coloring, where each edge of a graph $G$ has a weight in $(0,1]$, and colors are assigned so that the incident weight of each color at every vertex is at most one. The objective is to minimize the number of colors, denoted by $\chi'_w(G)$. This generalizes classical edge coloring (all weights are one) and bin packing ($G$ is a star).

arxiv:2611.03204.title: Hammock coordinates for silting subcategories of derived-discrete algebras
arxiv:2611.03204.summary: We introduce hammock coordinates to study the combinatorial structure of partial silting configurations in the bounded derived category of a derived-discrete algebra $\Lambda(r,n,m)$. By extracting exact integer inequalities from the Bobi\'nski--Gei\ss{}--Skowro\'nski Hom-hammock formula, we establish a closed-form criterion for pairwise partial silting both within any $\mathcal Z$-component and across distinct components. Using this coordinate framework, we establish three primary results.

arxiv:2611.03225.title: Human Variations on AI Mathematics
arxiv:2611.03225.summary: This article is motivated by the OpenAI manuscripts "Minimal metrics and interior injectivity for nef adjoints" and "Log abundance in characteristic zero". We establish a jet comparison for metrics with minimal singularities and use it to prove a dlt-type extension theorem. Combined with geometric arguments from the latter manuscript, this yields an alternative analytic proof of its Theorem~3.1.

arxiv:2611.03236.title: The strong fractional choice number can exceed the choice number
arxiv:2611.03236.summary: Erd\H{o}s, Rubin and Taylor asked whether every $(a,b)$-choosable graph is $(am,bm)$-choosable for all positive integers $a,b,m$. Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni disproved this by constructing a $4$-choosable graph that is not $(8,2)$-choosable, and asked whether a $3$-choosable graph can fail to be $(6,2)$-choosable. As a weakening, Li and Zhu asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(kb+1,b)$-choosable for all positive integers $k,b$.

arxiv:2611.03252.title: Conformal dimension of Bedford-McMullen carpets
arxiv:2611.03252.summary: We show that the Hausdorff dimension of a Bedford-McMullen carpet with non-uniform fibres can be lowered with a quasisymmetry, provided that the defining iterated function system does not have a full column. We prove this by constructing explicit dimension lowering metrics which are quasisymmetrically equivalent to the Euclidean metric.

arxiv:2611.03253.title: Normalizers in the category of topological groups
arxiv:2611.03253.summary: We show that the category of morphisms of topological groups admits split extension classifiers and hence the category of topological groups admits normalizers. We give explicit descriptions of both normalizers and of split extension classifiers of morphisms of topological groups in terms of split extension classifiers of topological groups.
arxiv:2611.03253.authors: Maria Manuel Clementino, James Richard Andrew Gray

arxiv:2611.03261.title: Exact Agreement Expansion up to the Top via Non-polarity
arxiv:2611.03261.summary: Agreement expansion asks whether local assignments to faces of a poset that usually agree on a sampled common face must agree with a single global function on most faces. Agreement expansion is exact (approximate) if local assignments need to exactly (approximately) agree with the global function. We suggest a new proof technique for agreement expansion that enables agreement expansion in settings which were previously beyond reach, such as: exact agreement expansion for Grassmannian posets (before only simplicial complexes support exact agreement expansion); agreement expansion based on assignments to top faces of the a complex (before agreement expansion is generally proven only for…

arxiv:2611.03265.title: Multivariable Alexander polynomials of twisted torus links via Dehn surgery
arxiv:2611.03265.summary: Let $T(p,q;r,s)$ be the twisted torus link obtained from the torus link $T(p,q)$ by adding $s$ full twists to $r$ adjacent strands, and let $C$ be an unknotted circle encircling those strands. For all $p$, $q$, and $r$ we compute the multivariable Alexander polynomial of $T(p,q)\cup C$ in closed form. A relation of Silver and Williams between the Alexander polynomials of a link and of its $1/n$ Dehn fillings then gives a closed formula for the multivariable Alexander polynomial of every twisted torus link $T(p,q;r,s)$, answering a question of Adnan and Park.

arxiv:2611.03287.title: Homological reduction and entropy of discontinuous interval maps
arxiv:2611.03287.summary: We develop a homological approach to the topological entropy of discontinuous interval maps with arbitrary branch orientations. Relations among the one-sided images of discontinuities reduce the kneading determinant, while symmetries yield further simplifications. We determine the smallest possible dimension of this reduction for each orientation pattern and show that this minimum can coexist with maximal entropy.

arxiv:2611.03292.title: Selection principle for Weak KAM solutions on $\mathbb{R}^n$ via large deviation principle for diffusions
arxiv:2611.03292.summary: Stationary Hamilton-Jacobi equations generally admit many weak KAM solutions. The question is how to select one weak KAM solution that reflects a meaningful physical principle. In this paper, we propose a selection principle for Hamilton-Jacobi equations arising from the large deviation principle of general drift-diffusion processes on $\mathbb{R}^n$ based on the exponential asymptotics of invariant measures.

arxiv:2611.03311.title: The Universal Nilpotent Cone and a Canonical 1-form
arxiv:2611.03311.summary: We construct a canonical Du Bois 1-form on the nilpotent cone in the dual Lie algebra of any reductive group. Using this 1-form we give an intrinsic construction of Nadler and Yun's universal global nilpotent cone. In particular, we obtain a moduli interpretation of the universal nilpotent cone.

arxiv:2611.03336.title: Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction for periodic orbits of implicit discrete dynamical systems
arxiv:2611.03336.summary: We derive bifurcation equations for periodic orbits of autonomous and periodically non-autonomous implicit discrete systems in arbitrary finite dimension. Cyclic Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction gives recursive coefficients and nondegeneracy and transversality conditions at the multipliers +1 and -1. We prove equivalence under regular changes of implicit representation and exact invariance under cyclic relabelling when the reduction data are transported consistently.

arxiv:2611.03348.title: Quaternionic and Octonionic Frameworks for Quantum Computation: Mathematical Structures, Models, and Fundamental Limitations
arxiv:2611.03348.summary: We develop detailed quaternionic and octonionic frameworks for quantum computation grounded on normed division algebras. Our central result is to prove the polynomial computational equivalence of quaternionic and complex quantum models: Computation over $\mathbb{H}$ is polynomially equivalent to the standard complex quantum circuit model and hence captures the same complexity class BQP up to polynomial reductions. Over $\mathbb{H}$, we construct a complete model---quaternionic qubits on right $\mathbb{H}$-modules with quaternion-valued inner products, unitary dynamics, associative tensor products, and universal gate sets---and establish polynomial equivalence with the standard complex…
arxiv:2611.03348.authors: Johan Heriberto R\'ua Mu\~noz, Jorge Eduardo Mahecha G\'omez, Santiago Pineda Montoya

arxiv:2611.03355.title: Rate-selective synchronization in switching networks: when timing meets structure
arxiv:2611.03355.summary: Switching networks arise across physics, biology, and engineering, where interactions turn on and off due to communication limits, control protocols, failures, or scheduling. Most synchronization theory for switching networks of continuous-time oscillators relies on the fast-switching approximation, yet many systems operate outside this regime, where switching can produce unexpected and counterintuitive collective dynamics. We develop the first analytical framework for synchronization in non-fast-switching networks of saddle-focus continuous-time oscillators.
arxiv:2611.03355.authors: Russell Jeter, Angelo Boateng, Maurizio Porfiri, Igor Belykh

arxiv:2611.03364.title: Maximizing Crossword Grids with a Fixed Minimum Clue Length
arxiv:2611.03364.summary: In an American-style crossword puzzle, the grid must be connected, 180-degree symmetric, and have minimum word length 3. Ferland and Pratt construct $n\times n$ crossword grids with many clues satisfying these conditions and prove their construction is maximal when $n\equiv 1$ or 3 $\pmod{4}$. In this paper, we explore American-style crosswords in which the minimum word length is 4.

arxiv:2611.03366.title: Finite groups with all involutions fused
arxiv:2611.03366.summary: We characterize finite groups whose involutions form a single fusion class. In the solvable case, we show that the $2$-length is $1$, extending Thompson's theorem which states that a solvable group with all involutions conjugate has $2$-length $1$. For a nonsolvable group $G$, we prove that if its involutions are fused then they are conjugate; moreover, $G/\mathbf{O}_{2'}(G)$ is almost quasisimple.

arxiv:2611.03380.title: Centralizers of maps as automorphism groups of Yang--Baxter solutions
arxiv:2611.03380.summary: For a partition $X = Y \sqcup Z$ of a set $X$ and an arbitrary map $g \colon Y \to {\rm Hom}_{\rm Set} (Z, \, Z)$, we construct a solution $R_g \colon X \times X \to X \times X$ of the braid equation. We characterize intrinsically the solutions which are isomorphic to some $R_g$ and we give a necessary and sufficient condition for two solutions $R_g$ and $R_{g'}$ to be isomorphic. Consequently, the number of isomorphism classes of the solutions $R_g$ on a set with $n$ elements is $1 + \sum_{k = 1}^{n-1} \widetilde{o} (n - k, \, k)$, where $\widetilde{o} (m, \, k)$ is the number of orbits of the symmetric group $S_m$, acting by conjugation, on the set of multisets with $k$ elements of maps…

arxiv:2611.03402.title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Non-Hopfian Baumslag--Solitar Groups
arxiv:2611.03402.summary: We study the singular loci of the reduced $\SL_2(\CC)$-representation varieties $R_{m,n}$ of non-Hopfian Baumslag--Solitar groups $B(m,n)=\langle a,b\mid b^{-1}a^m b=a^n\rangle$. We determine their dimensions and profile functions, which list the numbers of irreducible components in descending order of dimension. The components have dimensions three or five.

arxiv:2611.03427.title: Proving the Koml\'os conjecture slowly
arxiv:2611.03427.summary: The Koml\'os conjecture was a long-standing open problem in discrepancy theory until it was recently solved in a flurry of AI developments. We give a motivated exposition of an elementary proof of the conjecture due to Karingula and Lovett, as well as a counterexample to the strong Koml\'os conjecture due to Kintali, aiming to introduce the ideas in a gentle and explained manner in order to ease the understanding of the proofs. We conclude with several problems which remain open.

arxiv:2611.03444.title: A nearly tight bound on the probability $G(n,p)$ is even-degenerate
arxiv:2611.03444.summary: A graph is even-degenerate if we can order its vertices as $v_1,\dots,v_n$ so that the number of edges from $v_i$ to $v_1,\dots,v_{i-1}$ is even for all $i>2$. We show that the probability $G(n,p)$ is even-degenerate is $e^{-\Omega(n/\log\log n)}$, which is only a factor of $\log\log n$ away, in the exponent, from the trivial lower bound $2^{-O(n)}$.

arxiv:2611.03464.title: Spectral pairs of Newton non-degenerate polynomials with isolated singularities
arxiv:2611.03464.summary: We give a formula for the spectral pairs of Newton non-degenerate polynomials with isolated singularities. This is a revised version of a conjecture proposed by Steenbrink fifty years ago. Although this conjecture fails in the non-simplicial Newton polytope case, we can find the correction term using the intersection complexes and the primitive intersection cohomologies of toric varieties associated with non-simplicial compact faces.
arxiv:2611.03464.authors: Seung-Jo Jung, In-Kyun Kim, Morihiko Saito, Youngho Yoon

arxiv:2611.03468.title: The Optimizer's Windfall: Bounding Hindsight Gain under Random Restrictions
arxiv:2611.03468.summary: Suppose an optimization problem is randomly restricted, independently on each variable, and re-optimized after the restriction is revealed. For multilinear objectives, every fixed solution is unbiased after rescaling, but re-optimizing introduces an upward bias. We bound this excess, the hindsight gain, over products of arbitrary compact local domains in Euclidean unit balls.

arxiv:2611.03505.title: Hyperbolic periodic orbits and optimal $1/t$ convergence of the Lax--Oleinik semigroup
arxiv:2611.03505.summary: Let $M$ be a closed manifold and $H:T^*M\to\mathbb{R}$ a $C^k$ ($k\geq2$) Tonelli Hamiltonian whose Aubry set consists of finitely many hyperbolic orbits, each of which is either a periodic orbit or a fixed point. We construct a $C^k$ critical subsolution that is quadratically strict outside the projected Aubry set. We then use this subsolution to establish an $O(1/t)$ rate of convergence for the associated Lax--Oleinik semigroup and the minimal action functions.

arxiv:2611.03514.title: Quantitative finiteness for maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of non-arithmetic ball quotients
arxiv:2611.03514.summary: We prove that the number of maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of a smooth finite-volume non-arithmetic ball quotient is bounded linearly by its volume, with a constant depending only on the complex dimension. This gives a quantitative strengthening of the finiteness theorems of Bader--Fisher--Miller--Stover (Invent. Math., 2023) and Baldi--Ullmo (Ann. of Math., 2023).

arxiv:2611.03515.title: The proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: a detailed exposition and an extension to rotation systems
arxiv:2611.03515.summary: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number $\ucr{K_n}$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is $Z(n):=\frac{1}{4}\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\rfloor$ for all $n\ge 3$. In October 2026 OpenAI uploaded to GitHub a proof of this conjecture. The proof is very short, but it relies on polynomial methods that are not part of the standard techniques used by many combinatorialists, and it is written with very little motivation or explanation.

arxiv:2611.03519.title: Stability of negative-regularity mixing and applications to stochastic fluids
arxiv:2611.03519.summary: We consider mixing for a scalar advected by random vector fields, such as solutions to stochastic fluid equations. Our main abstract result is that contraction in expectation of a negative Sobolev norm of the scalar (negative-regularity mixing) is stable under perturbations of the joint scalar-velocity process. We apply the result in three settings: mixing for a hyperviscous Boussinesq-type system where the scalar actively drives the velocity, mixing for a passive scalar advected by two-dimensional Navier-Stokes driven by smooth-in-time stochastic forcing, and a black-box proof that negative-regularity mixing implies enhanced dissipation.
arxiv:2611.03519.authors: Antonio Agresti, William Cooperman, Patrick Flynn

arxiv:2611.03522.title: Koopman-von Neumann formalism meets contact Hamiltonian systems
arxiv:2611.03522.summary: The present work develops a Koopman--von Neumann (KvN) formulation of contact Hamiltonian dynamics on the Hilbert space defined by the contact volume. The resulting generator includes the divergence correction required for unitary evolution. We establish symmetry and, for complete contact Hamiltonian vector fields, essential self-adjointness and a strongly continuous unitary evolution; we also describe covariance under contactomorphisms.

arxiv:2611.03539.title: $C^1$-rigidity of $\mathbb{H}^{p,q}$-convex cocompact representations of Gromov hyperbolic groups
arxiv:2611.03539.summary: Let $p>3$ and let $\Gamma$ be a non-elementary Gromov hyperbolic group with $\partial_\infty\Gamma\cong\mathbb S^{p-1}$. We prove that every $\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$-convex cocompact representation $$ \rho:\Gamma\longrightarrow \mathrm{PO}_{p,3} $$ whose proximal limit set $\Lambda_\rho\subset\partial_\infty\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$ is a $C^1$ submanifold preserves a totally geodesic copy of $\mathbb{H}^p\subset\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$. Consequently, $\Gamma/\ker \rho$ is virtually a cocompact lattice in $\mathrm{Isom}(\mathbb{H}^p)$.

arxiv:2611.03553.title: Higher-order many-sorted categorial algebras via generalized hep-derivors
arxiv:2611.03553.summary: Higher-order many-sorted categorial algebras are many-sorted algebras whose carriers are strict higher-order categories and whose operations are higher-order functors. They admit a homogeneous and a heterogeneous presentation, both by partial algebras whose operation domains are given by existence equations. To relate these presentations and their dimensions, we introduce generalized hep-derivors between hierarchical equationally partial signatures.
arxiv:2611.03553.authors: J. Climent Vidal, E. Cosme Ll\'opez, R. Ruiz Mora, M. Vago Marzal

arxiv:2611.03560.title: Haagerup symmetries of the $E_8$ theory and conformal nets at central charge eight
arxiv:2611.03560.summary: A Haagerup algebra is a positive strongly rational vertex operator algebra $U$ of central charge eight with $\mathrm{Rep}(U)$ braided equivalent to the Drinfeld center $Z(\cal H_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category. Such an algebra has been proposed by Jiao, with a computer-assisted proof, and announced by Riesen and by Huang. We show that $U$ has exactly three holomorphic extensions, each isomorphic to $V_{E_8}$, and that the categories of modules over the corresponding Lagrangian algebras are the three Haagerup fusion categories of Grossman and Snyder.

arxiv:2611.03566.title: GW/PT-correspondence for CY $4$-fold-II: Virtual Classes
arxiv:2611.03566.summary: Let $B$ be a complex manifold and $f:\bX\to B$ a derived \textit{complex-analytic} (not necessarily \textit{algebraic}) space with an oriented relative $(-2)$-shifted symplectic structure. We suppose that the closed symplectic form is locally exact in the completed relative de Rham complex, and construct a derived smooth manifold over $B$, independent of additional choices. When $f$ is proper and oriented, this gives integral virtual fundamental classes on its fibres.

arxiv:2611.03572.title: Counterexamples to the Jacobian Conjecture from the viewpoint of lineability
arxiv:2611.03572.summary: Algebraic genericity in the family of polynomial counterexamples to the recently solved Jacobian Conjecture for $N\ge3$ is investigated. The notion of affine-coneability is introduced and it is shown that this family is affine-coneable and 1-lineable, but not 2-lineable. Semigroupability is further studied with respect to coordinatewise multiplication and composition.
arxiv:2611.03572.authors: L. Bernal-Gonz\'alez, M. C. Calder\'on-Moreno, J. A. Prado-Bassas

arxiv:2611.03578.title: Uniform Sampling of Linear Codes with Prescribed Hull Dimension
arxiv:2611.03578.summary: We give exactly uniform samplers for linear codes with prescribed hull dimension, for the Euclidean, Hermitian, and symplectic inner products and over finite fields of every characteristic. Except for the Euclidean form over fields of odd characteristic, these are the first uniform samplers for arbitrary prescribed hull dimension. Each sample costs an expected $O(k^2 N + k \log q)$ field operations for codes of dimension $k$ in a space of dimension $N$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ or $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$.

arxiv:2611.03606.title: Isogeny rigidity under algebraic group actions and finite translation orbits
arxiv:2611.03606.summary: We study finite orbits generated by fibrewise translations on varieties carrying two abelian fibrations. Under natural dominance and generation hypotheses, non-isotriviality of the first family forces points with finite orbit to lie over proper closed subsets of both bases. This extends results of Corvaja, Tsimerman and Zannier to complex families of arbitrary, possibly different relative dimensions, including torsors.
arxiv:2611.03606.authors: Paolo Dolce, Francesco Tropeano, Ekaterina Amerik

arxiv:2611.03609.title: On ill-distributed $B_3$ and $B_4$ sets
arxiv:2611.03609.summary: We show that, for $k\in\{3,4\}$, a $B_k$-set $A\subseteq[N]$ has size $o(N^{1/k})$ if it omits a fixed positive proportion of the residue classes modulo every prime in a fixed family whose reciprocals have divergent sum.
arxiv:2611.03609.authors: Andr\'e Hisatsuga, Rafael Miyazaki, Cosmin Pohoata

arxiv:2611.03611.title: Associated Varieties of Finite-Group Orbifolds
arxiv:2611.03611.summary: Let $V$ be a simple, strongly finitely generated vertex algebra with a connected nonnegative integer grading, and let $G$ be a finite group of grading-preserving automorphisms. In this paper, we prove that $X_{V^G}\cong X_V/G$ as reduced Poisson varieties. More precisely, the canonical surjection $R_{V^G}\longrightarrow (R_V)^G $ has nilpotent kernel.

arxiv:2611.03612.title: Efficient Closure Learning in Dynamical Systems: A Comparison of Data-Assimilated and Embedded Approaches
arxiv:2611.03612.summary: Increased computing power has transformed computational science and improved predictive capabilities for complex systems, but many phenomena still exceed current simulation capabilities or require rapid evaluations for fast design iterations. Closure models address this challenge by approximating unresolved effects in reduced or incomplete dynamical systems. Data-driven closures offer a flexible mechanism for improving model accuracy and applicability, but approaches that embed the closure within a computational model for construction and training phases can be computationally expensive and cause numerical instabilities in the computational model during training.
arxiv:2611.03612.authors: Rileigh Bandy, Teresa Portone, Mohammad Khalil, Eric Crislip, Kyle Neal

arxiv:2611.03636.title: Get Permanent Results Faster by Counting Stars
arxiv:2611.03636.summary: We show that $n \times n$ permanents can be computed with $O^*{(2-\varepsilon)^n}$ arithmetic operations over every commutative ring, for $\varepsilon = 10^{-40}$. This solves a problem stated in Knuth's The Art of Computer Programming. Our algorithm implements the classical Binet--Minc identity with dynamic programming and careful bookkeeping.

arxiv:2611.03682.title: New lower bounds for kissing numbers in dimensions 32-35 and 37-39
arxiv:2611.03682.summary: We show that the kissing numbers in dimensions 32, 33, 34, 35, 37, 38 and 39 are at least 352320, 370240, 390980, 415308, 499816, 605322 and 768916, improving the previous bounds 347584, 364736, 384836, 409676, 498024, 591900 and 763668. Except in dimension 38, the configurations are those of Edel, Rains and Sloane with new binary constant-weight codes of weight 8 and minimum distance 8 in the middle layer; each additional word adds 128 points. In dimension 38 we add 6855 antipodal pairs of vectors of the second shell of the Leech lattice to the empty equator of Kravatskiy's 591612-point configuration, where 144 pairs were known; this is an independent set problem in a regular graph of…

arxiv:2611.03688.title: The nonexistence of nine-point crescent configurations
arxiv:2611.03688.summary: A planar crescent configuration consists of $n$ points, no three collinear and no four concyclic, whose distinct distances have multiplicities $1,2,\ldots,n-1$. We prove by exact computation that no such configuration exists for $n=9$. The three pairs carrying the two least frequent distances yield a six-point subset with at most six distances.

arxiv:2611.03695.title: On Gallai $d$-colored circulants
arxiv:2611.03695.summary: A $d$-graph is a complete graph whose edges are colored with colors from $[d]$. It is Gallai if it contains no triangle whose three edges have distinct colors. We prove that every Gallai $d$-circulant is an iterated lexicographic product of circulants using at most two colors.

arxiv:2611.03701.title: Naturalization of Vinti's intermediary orbit---or how to get rid of small divisors in Brouwer's satellite solution
arxiv:2611.03701.summary: A naturalization, in the sense of Deprit, of Vinti's dynamical system makes the construction of a first order analytical satellite perturbation solution without critical divisors possible. The process gives hints on how to recast Brouwer's classical solution in a form that is free from small divisors too. The functionality of classical perturbation solutions is in this way extended to the close vicinity of the critical inclination.

arxiv:2611.03711.title: Spectral Dynamics and Fuglede--Kadison Determinants for Wreath Products
arxiv:2611.03711.summary: We investigate connections between operator spectra, complex dynamics, and determinants for wreath product groups. For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, the natural action of $G\wr\mathbb Z$ on a rooted tree produces a family of operators with a recursive structure. Applying Schur complements to this family yields a rational map on complex projective space.
arxiv:2611.03711.authors: Penghui Wang, Xumin Wang, Rongwei Yang

arxiv:2611.03714.title: Grid triples, link cobordisms in $\CPbar$ and the computation of Heegaard-Floer TQFT
arxiv:2611.03714.summary: We give a combinatorial description of the Heegaard--Floer link-cobordism maps associated with pointed triple grid diagrams in the complement of three $4$-balls in complex projective plane with reverse orientation. Every contributing index-zero holomorphic triangle decomposes into Euclidean triangular sheets. We characterize the compatible collections of sheets that contribute by an explicit geometric separation criterion, expressed as a lattice-point test, and prove that each has mod-\(2\) count one.

arxiv:2611.03745.title: Large deviation of preimages of points under the dynamics of a holomorphic correspondence
arxiv:2611.03745.summary: Our main objective in this paper is to prove a large deviation result for the distribution of preimages of a point under the iteration of a holomorphic correspondence with respect to the unique equilibrium state associated to a H\"{o}lder continuous potential defined on the support of the Dinh-Sibony measure of the correspondence. As a consequence, we obtain a convergence result which generalises the result on equidistribution of preimages by Dinh and Sibony. We also study a situation where the Dinh-Sibony measure happens to be the unique measure of maximal entropy for an appropriate holomorphic correspondence and also record some comments that connect this work with some recent works in…

arxiv:2611.03758.title: Generating Forbidden Words and Measures of Maximal Entropy for Subshifts
arxiv:2611.03758.summary: We prove that if the entropy of generating forbidden words of a subshift over a finite alphabet is strictly smaller than its topological entropy, then the subshift has only finitely many ergodic measures of maximal entropy, each of which is Bernoulli up to a finite period, and admits a characteristic measure of maximal entropy. In particular, these conclusions hold when the entropy of minimal forbidden words is strictly smaller than the topological entropy, giving a negative answer to a question of Buzzi.

arxiv:2611.03763.title: Circular flows and bisections of random regular graphs
arxiv:2611.03763.summary: Jaeger conjectured that, for every positive integer $p$, every $4p$-edge-connected graph admits an orientation with congruent indegree and outdegree modulo $2p+1$. We prove a stronger probabilistic counterpart: a uniformly random simple $(4p+1)$-regular graph has a strongly connected orientation with all outdegrees in $\{p,3p+1\}$ with probability tending to one as its even order grows. More generally, for every fixed odd $d\ge9$, there is $\varepsilon_d>0$ such that its circular flow number is less than $2+4/(d-1)-\varepsilon_d$ with probability tending to one.

arxiv:2611.03797.title: Seshadri constants of singular loci of line arrangements with at most twelve lines
arxiv:2611.03797.summary: Let ${\mathcal L}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in the complex projective plane and let $Z={\operatorname{Sing}}({\mathcal L})$. A question of Pokora asks whether the multipoint Seshadri constant of ${\mathcal O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1)$ at $Z$ is always computed by a line of the arrangement containing the largest number of points of $Z$. We prove that the answer is affirmative for every arrangement of at most twelve lines.
arxiv:2611.03797.authors: Marcin Dumnicki, {\L}ucja Farnik, Krishna Hanumanthu, Brian Harbourne, Piotr Pokora, Joaquim Ro\'e, Halszka Tutaj-Gasi\'nska

arxiv:2611.03830.title: Bayesian Filters via the Stochastic Category
arxiv:2611.03830.summary: We extend the categorical treatment of Bayesian filters to models with feedback, whose transitions and observations may depend on the past observations. We work in the stochastic category, whose objects are measurable spaces and whose morphisms are Markov kernels, which we refer to as stochastic morphisms. We systematically parameterize stochastic morphisms by a measurable space, and develop the calculus of conditioning in a notation intuitively compatible with classical probability theory, requiring neither string diagrams nor densities.

arxiv:2611.03838.title: A King for Almost Everyone
arxiv:2611.03838.summary: A tournament is an orientation of a complete graph. A vertex $v$ controls a vertex $u\neq v$ if there is a directed path of length at most two from $v$ to $u$, and a $\delta$-king is one that controls at least $\delta(n-1)$ vertices. In the query complexity model, each query reveals the orientation of an edge.
arxiv:2611.03838.authors: Ziad Ismaili Alaoui, Oded Lachish, Nikhil S. Mande

arxiv:2611.03843.title: The Iterated Local Transitivity Model for oriented graphs
arxiv:2611.03843.summary: Transitivity in social and other complex networks describes the tendency for two nodes with a common neighbor to become adjacent. We propose a new model for complex networks based on transitivity, called the Iterated Local Transitivity Model for Oriented Graphs (ILTO). The model generalizes the Iterated Local Model for Tournaments (ILMT).
arxiv:2611.03843.authors: Anthony Bonato, MacKenzie Carr, Ketan Chaudhary, Trent G. Marbach, Teddy Mishura

arxiv:2611.03847.title: Combination Theorems and the Farrell--Jones Conjecture for Graph Products of Pairs
arxiv:2611.03847.summary: We study the Farrell--Jones conjecture for graph products of pairs and for fundamental groups of polyhedral products. We introduce a pair-deletion decomposition and a local notion of FJ-admissibility, and prove a vertexwise combination theorem for graph products of pairs. The criterion applies, in particular, to ordinary graph products, free-factor pairs, suitable normal pairs, and classes controlled by acylindrical Bass--Serre actions.

arxiv:2611.03855.title: A surface-group action on real-hyperbolic space with no Cannon--Thurston map
arxiv:2611.03855.summary: We present discrete, faithful and purely loxodromic representations of a closed surface group of genus 431, and of a free group, into the group of isometries of a finite-dimensional real-hyperbolic space for which no Cannon--Thurston map exists. The construction combines three ingredients: the small-cancellation strategy employed by Baker--Riley to construct a subgroup of an ambient hyperbolic group with no Cannon--Thurston map, the realization of these groups by octagon complexes, and a theorem of Desgroseilliers--Haglund that supplies a convex cocompact faithful representation of the ambient hyperbolic group on a real-hyperbolic space. These examples admit ray Cannon--Thurston maps, as…

arxiv:2611.03863.title: Statistical Stability and Linear Response for Suspension Measures under Base and Roof Perturbations
arxiv:2611.03863.summary: We study the dependence of canonical invariant probability measures of suspension semiflows on simultaneous perturbations of the invariant base density and the roof function. We compare two natural representations of the suspension measure: physical-height coordinates, in which the support depends on the roof function, and normalised-height coordinates, in which all measures are defined on a fixed cylinder. In physical-height coordinates, we obtain an exact fibrewise formula for the $L^1$ discrepancy between suspension densities and derive quantitative total-variation estimates.

arxiv:2611.03866.title: Curve-Supported Concentrations of Vortices and Screw Dislocations Subject to Confinement
arxiv:2611.03866.summary: We study the concentration of logarithmically interacting defects, such as Ginzburg--Landau vortices and screw dislocations, on closed curves in two dimensions, subject to a confining field. We prove that a measure supported on a smooth closed curve solves the mean-field transport equation exactly when, in Lagrangian labels, the curve moves with the negative induced velocity and each label keeps its mass. This contour law is a gradient flow of the mean-field energy.

arxiv:2611.03878.title: On the lower- and upper bounds of three-colored anti-Ramsey numbers
arxiv:2611.03878.summary: In this paper we study a relatively new Ramsey type graph parameter introduced by my Bachelor's thesis supervisor N\'ora Alm\'asi, and her Master's thesis supervisor Maria Axenovich. The parameter $\xi(G)$ denotes the largest natural number $n$, such that there is a red-blue-green edge coloring of $K_n$, such that in the edge coloring all copies of $G$ represent all three colors. After a brief recap on Ramsey numbers, we precisely define $\xi(G)$, and take a look at its relations to the Ramsey numbers.

arxiv:2611.03879.title: Lemmas and Conjectures in Spectral Graph Theory
arxiv:2611.03879.summary: The corpus of Elie Duhamel and Tristan Cazenave~\cite{dc} contains $305{,}755$ automatically generated conjectures relating spectral and metric invariants of connected graphs. A pipeline generated with Claude Code (numerical refutation, proof by the SMT solver \textsf{z3} from a library of lemmas, discovery of new lemmas, formalisation in \lean~4/Mathlib) refuted $162{,}964$ conjectures and proved $117{,}390$ without any unproved hypothesis, of which $79{,}505$ are verified end to end in \lean{} for every connected graph. This document collects, with proofs written for mathematicians, the most interesting lemmas that were discovered and proved, the ten most useful lemmas, the ten hardest…

arxiv:2611.03896.title: Min-plus Bruhat decomposition
arxiv:2611.03896.summary: We study min-plus Bruhat cells $B_{trop}^{(n)} \odot p\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}$, where $B_{trop}^{(n)}$ denotes the set of all upper-triangular matrices over $\RR \cup \{\infty\}$, and $p$ is a permutation. It is proved that $\dim (B_{trop}^{(n)} \odot p \odot B_{trop}^{(n)})= \frac{n(n+1)}{2} + l(p)$, where $l(p)$ is the length of $p$ in Coxeter generators. Also we provide an explicit description of the cell $B_{trop}^{(n)}(\RR) \odot p_0\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}(\RR)$ (up to a subset of dimension less than $n^2$) for the highest in Bruhat order permutation $p_0$.

arxiv:2611.03906.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring on Structured Graph Classes: Bounds, Exact Algorithms, and Hardness
arxiv:2611.03906.summary: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper vertex coloring in which every non-isolated vertex has a neighbor whose color appears exactly once in its open neighborhood. We study this coloring on chordal and ordered bipartite graph classes. For well-partitioned chordal graphs, we prove the tight bound $\omega(G)\leq\pcf(G)\leq\omega(G)+1$ and give an $O(n^2)$ construction from a partition tree.

arxiv:2611.03907.title: The Askey-Wilson Function is the Laplace Transform of a Positive Measure
arxiv:2611.03907.summary: The Askey-Wilson function $\phi(x, \gamma)$ is a meromorphic continuation of the Askey-Wilson polynomials in their spectral variable off the lattice $\gamma = \tilde{a} q^m, m \in \mathbb{Z}_+$. We show that the analytic part of the Askey-Wilson function $\phi^{an}(x, \tilde{a} q^\gamma)$ is the Laplace transform of a positive measure of total measure $\phi^{an}(x, s_0) < \infty$, under certain conditions on the parameters governing the function. We deduce log-convexity of this function, as well as positive-definiteness and an integral formula for a certain intertwining operator associated with the Askey-Wilson operator $L$.

arxiv:2611.03956.title: Well-Covered Powers: Cartesian Products and Cayley Graphs
arxiv:2611.03956.summary: We study graphs whose powers are well-covered, with an emphasis on Cartesian products and Cayley graphs. We first establish necessary conditions and sufficient criteria for Cartesian products, provide examples showing that a factor need not be well-covered and that two noncomplete factors can have the well-covered powers property, and classify several structured product families. In particular, we construct graphs satisfying the well-covered powers property for arbitrarily large diameters.
arxiv:2611.03956.authors: Haobo Ma, Thanh Vu, Wenlin Zhang

arxiv:2611.03960.title: Invariant random subgroups of the finitary special linear group over a finite field
arxiv:2611.03960.summary: An invariant random subgroup of a discrete group is a conjugation-invariant probability measure on the space of its subgroups. We confirm a conjecture of Simon Thomas and classify the invariant random subgroups of the finitary special and general linear groups over a finite field. These are shown to be stabilizers of random tuples of vectors and functionals.

arxiv:2611.03989.title: Binomial Artin-Schelter Regular Algebras and Twisted Monoid Algebras
arxiv:2611.03989.summary: We study four-dimensional binomial Artin-Schelter regular algebras and their connection with twisted monoid algebras. Starting with $23$ examples up to permutation of generators, we investigate the associated monoids of I-type and the structure of their groups of fractions. We determine the corresponding finite permutation groups and compute the second group cohomology $H^2(G(M),k^\times)$.

arxiv:2611.03991.title: Balance in Inequality: Testing the Physical Equilibrium, Precession, and Structural Stability of Magic Gems
arxiv:2611.03991.summary: A magic square exemplifies balance in inequality: its $n^2$ entries $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ are distinct, yet every row, column, and main diagonal sums to $\mu_n=n(n^2+1)/2$. Lifting centred grid cells into $\mathbb{R}^3$ as radial vectors $\mathbf{p}_{ij}(\lambda)=(x_j,y_i,\lambda z_{ij})$ and taking their convex hull---the Magic Gem $\mathcal{G}_\lambda(S)$---asks: when does line-sum equality suffice for equilibrium in 3D, and when a nonlinear realization breaks balance, how can an opposing inequality restore it? We test this across all $880$ order-$4$ magic squares in four regimes.

arxiv:2611.04013.title: Toward Quillen stratification for the odd primary Steenrod algebra
arxiv:2611.04013.summary: Fix an odd prime $p$ and let $A$ be the mod $p$ Steenrod algebra. There is a normal sub-Hopf algebra $D$ of $A$, and we show that the cohomology of $A$ is $F$-isomorphic to the subalgebra of the cohomology of $D$ which is invariant under the $A$-action. We also show that the sub-Hopf algebras of $A$ with bounded profile function detect nilpotence in cohomology.

arxiv:2611.04020.title: Automatic partition identities
arxiv:2611.04020.summary: We encode certain sets of partitions by regular languages of boundary words, so that their generating functions become rational series in the quantum plane $RU=qUR$. An equality between two partition counts is certified by writing the difference of their series as $(1-U)a+b(1-R)$, with $a,b$ converging $q$-adically. We show that $a,b$ may be chosen as solutions of finite holonomic systems of $q$-difference equations computed from the automata, and describe finite certificates of their convergence, together with bounded searches for such certificates; the searches need not succeed, but a false identity is always detected.

arxiv:2611.04089.title: On nearly Lefschetz fibrations and spinal open books
arxiv:2611.04089.summary: We survey the recent development of spinal open books and nearly Lefschetz fibrations. The focus is on explaining past and new results regarding the detection of symplectic fillability and classification of symplectic fillings of contact 3-manifolds in light of the new machinery. We give many examples and a list of open questions.
arxiv:2611.04089.authors: Hyunki Min, Agniva Roy, Luya Wang

arxiv:2611.04095.title: Universal bounds for decompositions of PL manifolds
arxiv:2611.04095.summary: The geometric dimension of a nonempty compact PL manifold $N$ is the smallest nonnegative integer $d$ for which $N$ admits a handle decomposition with all handles of index at most $d$. A PL filling of a compact PL manifold is a decomposition into compact codimension $0$ PL submanifolds, called sectors, with pairwise disjoint interiors and intersections described by standard local models. We advance Singhof's program of simplifying the sectors of a filling and their intersections.

arxiv:2611.04118.title: D-equivalence conjecture for hyperk\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type
arxiv:2611.04118.summary: We show that birationally equivalent hyperk\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type are derived equivalent, confirming the D-equivalence conjecture in this case. Combined with recent results of other authors, this settles the conjecture for all known deformation types of hyperk\"ahler varieties. The kernel is built from an equivariant Fourier-Mukai kernel on the sum-zero loci of powers of an abelian surface.
arxiv:2611.04118.authors: Will Donovan, Chengxi Wang, Nantao Zhang

arxiv:2611.04127.title: Algorithmic Non-dimensionalisation of Polynomial Dynamical Systems with CRNNondim
arxiv:2611.04127.summary: Although non-dimensionalisation is a fundamental step in modelling, it is rarely obvious, especially for large dynamical systems, how to systematically construct optimal non-dimensionalisations. In this work, we develop a general mathematical framework for non-dimensionalising polynomial ODEs by interpreting them as chemical reaction networks (CRNs) and characterise the space of admissible scalings. Within this viewpoint, admissible scalings of time and species are encoded by Laurent monomials, and we derive exact formulae for the minimal number of multiplicative dimensionless parameters required by the reaction-channel coefficients and by the full initial value problem, together with…

arxiv:2611.04130.title: Global vector fields and the automorphism group of regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties
arxiv:2611.04130.summary: For a connected regular semisimple Hessenberg variety other than the full flag variety, we prove that the identity component of its automorphism group is an algebraic torus. The argument uses equivariant local coordinates and weight-homogeneous coefficient functions of vector fields.
arxiv:2611.04130.authors: Mikiya Masuda, Takashi Sato, Haozhi Zeng

arxiv:2611.04131.title: Schrodinger group along the horocycles and Egorov's theorem on compact hyperbolic surfaces
arxiv:2611.04131.summary: In this paper, we study Egorov's theorem for Laplacian eigenfunctions on compact hyperbolic surfaces in Zelditch's quantization. In this quantization, the remainder in Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is given explicitly by the second derivatives of the symbols along the weak stable foliation of the geodesic flow. Forward in time, we show that Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is valid to all logarithmic times, far beyond the Ehrenfest time T_E=|log h|/2, where h going to 0 is the semiclassical parameter.

arxiv:2611.04145.title: Admissible extremal rays and the anticanonical minimal model program
arxiv:2611.04145.summary: We develop an anticanonical minimal model program for projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial klt pairs $(X,\Delta)$ such that $-(K_{X}+\Delta)$ is pseudoeffective. We first prove the cone and contraction theorems for potentially klt triples and establish the existence of flips for such triples. Using these results, we introduce the notion of admissible extremal rays and show that $(K_{X}+\Delta)$-positive admissible extremal rays are precisely the rays that are to be contracted by $-(K_{X}+\Delta)$-MMP.
arxiv:2611.04145.authors: Sung Rak Choi, Sungwook Jang, Dae-Won Lee

arxiv:2611.04154.title: A Bubble Compactification of KSBA Moduli Space of Surfaces of General Type
arxiv:2611.04154.summary: We construct a bubble-tree enhancement of the KSBA moduli space of surfaces of general type using index-one-cover Deligne--Mumford stacks. The construction is inspired by bubbling phenomena for K\"ahler--Einstein metrics. Non-klt semi-log-canonical singularities are replaced by admissible simple-normal-crossing configurations: the cusp and degenerate-cusp components are rational, while the simple-elliptic case also contains elliptic ruled components.

arxiv:2611.04161.title: Categorical and Floer-theoretic entropies: comparison and counting conjugacy classes in symplectic mapping class groups
arxiv:2611.04161.summary: Let $W$ be a Weinstein manifold and let $f: W \to W$ be a compactly supported symplectic automorphism. Using Floer theories, one can define two different entropies of $f$, called "Floer-theoretic" entropy and "categorical" entropy. The current article compares these two entropies and show that the former bounds the latter from below.

arxiv:2611.04167.title: Higher zeroes in pointed infinity-categories
arxiv:2611.04167.summary: We construct an endofunctor on (small) simplicial sets which freely adjoins a zero object to a (small) infinity-category, as the co-cone construction freely adjoins a terminal object. We then prove that this endofunctor induces a left adjoint to the inclusion of the infinity-category of (small) pointed infinity-categories and morphisms that preserve zero objects into the infinity-category of (small) infinity-categories. This adjunction, in turn, leads to the definition of a coherent choice of nullhomotopies on a pointed infinity-category.

arxiv:2611.04184.title: Short permutation pattern waves: The complete length-five classification
arxiv:2611.04184.summary: For a permutation pi in Sk, a pi-wave is an increasing sequence of integers whose consecutive gaps have relative order pi. Let g(pi, n) be the maximum cardinality of a pi-wave-free subset of [n], and let P(pi, r) be the least integer N such that every r-coloring of [N] contains a monochromatic pi-wave. We determine the asymptotic orders of both functions for every permutation of length at most five.
arxiv:2611.04184.authors: Lihong Qiu, Minglei Mao, Yaping Mao

arxiv:2611.04190.title: Quadratic Hubbard trees, automata, and ray connections
arxiv:2611.04190.summary: We describe an algorithm that, given a postcritically finite quadratic polynomial, outputs a finite state machine whose regular language is the set of external arguments for all points on the Hubbard tree, generalizing an example of Milnor. We do this by extracting orbit portraits from angled internal addresses, and constructing a suitable Markov partition of angle intervals. A main application is computing direct ray connections between Hubbard trees in matings of quadratic polynomials.

arxiv:2611.04210.title: Rational points on loxodromic K3 surfaces and complex dynamics
arxiv:2611.04210.summary: We establish an analogue of the Hilbert irreducibility theorem for all K3 surfaces over number fields that admit an automorphism of positive entropy. Our method draws ingredients from both algebraic geometry and complex dynamics.
arxiv:2611.04210.authors: Dami\'an Gvirtz-Chen, Zhizhong Huang, Zhuchao Ji, Junyi Xie

arxiv:2611.04232.title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings
arxiv:2611.04232.summary: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.

arxiv:2611.04243.title: Smooth and Topological Nonorientable Four-Genera of Low-Crossing Knots
arxiv:2611.04243.summary: We compare linking-form bounds with the smooth and locally flat nonorientable 4-genera of low-crossing knots. For every prime knot with at most 13 crossings whose Witt-level linking-form bound is at least 2, this bound equals both genera. We also exhibit 41 prime knots with 12 or 13 crossings that bound locally flat M\"obius bands but no smooth ones, and whose smooth nonorientable 4-genus is 2.

arxiv:2611.04245.title: Limit cycles of singular algebraic foliations on the real projective plane
arxiv:2611.04245.summary: In this paper we consider cycles of singular algebraic foliations on the real projective plane. Our first result shows that there exists a limit cycle of singular algebraic foliations such that the limit cycle cannot be realized in any affine chart, that is, it fails to appear in any affine plane via the usual dehomogenization. On the other hand, under an appropriate convexity assumption, we verify that a cycle becomes fully visible, lying entirely in some affine chart.
arxiv:2611.04245.authors: Tianwei Gan, Hongjin He, Dongmei Xiao

arxiv:2611.04258.title: A note on the BRST-BV Formalism Explanation of Deformation Quantization and Algebraic Index Theorem
arxiv:2611.04258.summary: In this note, we begin with considering the simple one-dimensional field theory describing a single free particle on manifold, and apply the BRST formalism and BV quantization to this model following the standard procedures in physics. Through calculations that, while not fully rigorous, have a more transparent physical interpretation, then subsequent geometric identifications, we recover the deformation quantization and algebraic index theorem on symplectic manifold. This note thus elucidates the physical origins and mechanisms of these mathematical results.

arxiv:2611.04265.title: The $p$-local topologoical period-index problem in dimensions $2p+2$ and below
arxiv:2611.04265.summary: For any odd prime number $p$, we solve the topological period-index problem for a $p$-primary element of the Brauer group of a CW-complex of dimension not greater than $2p+2$.

arxiv:2611.04276.title: Testing Implies Distance Estimation with Polynomial Loss
arxiv:2611.04276.summary: A tester decides whether a graph has a property or is far from having it. A distance estimator asks for more: it must approximately determine how many edges need to be changed. A property is said to be testable if there is a tester with a number of queries bounded independently of the graph's order for each conceivable distance.

arxiv:2611.04290.title: An example of universal braiding in Links--Gould topological quantum computation
arxiv:2611.04290.summary: We construct a universal quantum computational encoding via braiding in Links--Gould fusion spaces associated to $U_q^H(\mathfrak{sl}(2|1))$ where $q$ is on the unit circle and is not a root of unity. The construction uses only neglectons and is realized in the morphism spaces $\mathrm{Hom}_{U_q^H}(V(0,\alpha),V(0,-\frac{1}{2})^{\otimes 2N}\otimes V(0,\alpha)).$ Under explicit positivity and arithmetic constraints these spaces admit a $2^N$-dimensional computational subspace with a positive definite Hermitian form. We prove single-qubit density in $\mathrm{U}(2,1)$ and approximate arbitrary unitary operators on $N$-qubit computational subspaces with arbitrarily small leakage.

arxiv:2611.04293.title: Conjecture B for $X_{10}$ and its genus-two mirror
arxiv:2611.04293.summary: We prove Conjecture B of Akhtar--Coates--Corti--Heuberger--Kasprzyk--Oneto--Petracci--Prince--Tveiten unconditionally for the normalized family of maximally mutable Laurent polynomials with prescribed $T$-binomial edge coefficients associated with the degree-10 orbifold del Pezzo hypersurface $X_{10}\subset\mathbb{P}(1,2,3,5)$. An explicit $S$-extended quantum-period calculation determines the affine mirror map $\lambda=a-346$ and proves that the regularized quantum period equals the classical period as a formal power series throughout the family.

arxiv:2611.04297.title: Fractional colorings of $K_r$-free graphs with local demands
arxiv:2611.04297.summary: We study fractional coloring with local demands, a framework introduced by Kelly and Postle in which one seeks a probability distribution on the independent sets of a graph such that each vertex $v$ is included with probability at least a prescribed target $\phi(v)$. For $K_r$-free graphs, Kelly and Postle conjectured that such a distribution exists provided $\phi(v)\le c_r\frac{\log d(v)}{d(v)}$ for a fixed \(c_r>0\), where $d(v)$ is the degree of $v$, and they established this up to a factor of $(\log\log d(v))^2$. In this paper, we prove their conjecture, showing that \[ \phi(v)\le\frac{c}{r}\frac{\log(d(v)+2)}{d(v)+1} \] suffices for an absolute constant $c>0$.
arxiv:2611.04297.authors: Ewan Davies, Abhishek Dhawan, Abhishek Methuku, Huy Nguyen, Jaehyeon Seo

arxiv:2611.04314.title: Canonical Projectivization of Algebraic Varieties in Characteristic Zero
arxiv:2611.04314.summary: We construct a canonical projectivization of every smooth proper algebraic variety $X$ in characteristic zero. Once a principalization procedure is fixed, the construction gives a finite sequence of blowups in smooth centers with smooth projective endpoint, natural under semilinear isomorphisms and preserving the quasi-projective core, the intersection of all maximal quasi-projective open subsets. At each stage we select finitely many ideals near the generic points of the image in $X$ of the boundary of a maximal quasi-projective open.

arxiv:2611.04326.title: Reflective algebras over factorizable Hopf algebras
arxiv:2611.04326.summary: The reflective algebra $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$, introduced by Laugwitz, Walton and Yakimov, is a quasitriangular left $H$-comodule algebra constructed from a quasitriangular Hopf algebra $(H,R)$ and a left $H$-comodule algebra $A$. We study the structure and factorizability of finite-dimensional reflective algebras. When $(H,R)$ is factorizable, we show that $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$ is isomorphic, as a quasitriangular left $H$-comodule algebra, to $A\otimes H$ equipped with the trivial left $H$-coaction on $A$ and the universal $K$-matrix induced by $R_{21}R$.

arxiv:2611.04328.title: Compatible gradings on dg models and cluster equivalence
arxiv:2611.04328.summary: Let $\La_1$ and $\La_2$ be finite-dimensional $\ta_2$-finite complex algebras of global dimension at most two. We prove that, if they are cluster equivalent, then they admit $\bbZ$-gradings for which the bounded derived categories of graded modules are triangle equivalent. The equivalence is not required to commute with the internal grading shifts.

arxiv:2611.04339.title: Optimal no-feedback card guessing after a fixed number of riffle shuffles
arxiv:2611.04339.summary: An ordered deck of $n$ cards is subjected to $k$ independent Gilbert--Shannon--Reeds riffle shuffles. A player then guesses each card without feedback, with repeated guesses allowed. For every fixed $k\ge1$, we prove that, once $n$ is sufficiently large, an optimal guess at position $i$ in the top half of the deck is $\lfloor i/2^k\rfloor+1$; the bottom-half strategy is obtained by reflection.

arxiv:2611.04384.title: Infinitely Many Almost-Uniform 3-Qualitative Independence Hypergraphs are Cores
arxiv:2611.04384.summary: Qualitative independence is a property associated with the column vectors of well-known combinatorial designs known as covering arrays and qualitative independence hypergraphs characterize the existence of covering arrays on hypergraphs. The core of a hypergraph $H$ is an interesting structural characteristic to study, as it is the unique (up to isomorphism), minimal subhypergraph $H^\bullet \subseteq H$ which is homomorphically equivalent to $H$. We use the vertex transitivity and strong independence number of almost-uniform $3$-qualitative independence hypergraphs, $3\text{-}AUQI(2n+1,2)$, to show that $3\text{-}AUQI(2n+1,2)$ are cores for infinitely many $n$.

arxiv:2611.04398.title: Remarks on the Farthing--Muhly--Yeend inverse semigroup of a finitely aligned higher-rank graph
arxiv:2611.04398.summary: Given a finitely aligned higher-rank $k$-graph $\Lambda$, Farthing, Muhly and Yeend (Semigroup Forum 2005) constructed an inverse semigroup $S_\Lambda$ to provide a groupoid model for the $C^*$-algebra of $\Lambda$. In this paper, we extend some of the existing results related to the semigroup structure of a graph inverse semigroup to the more general setting of the inverse semigroup $S_\Lambda$. We obtain geometric descriptions of the Green's relations on $S_\Lambda$, which effectively generalize the existing characterization of Green's relations on a graph inverse semigroup.

arxiv:2611.04404.title: Ergodic full measures and entropy spectrum for countable observables on compact spaces
arxiv:2611.04404.summary: We investigate conditions and obstructions for the existence of ergodic full measures in the context of countable observables on compact spaces. Extending the theory in a unified way, we are able to show a complete picture via thermodynamic formalism for symbolic, uniformly hyperbolic and related systems. We prove conditional variational principles for the topological entropy, showing good approximations by ergodic full measures, and we give conditions where we precisely get ergodic full measures.

arxiv:2611.04471.title: Algebraicity, Hodge Gradings, and the Geometry of Period Images
arxiv:2611.04471.summary: We prove the algebraicity of period images in arithmetic quotients without using o-minimality. The proof uses infinitesimal neighborhoods and formal algebraization to recover the images and the maps from their algebraic sources. Hodge positivity and an algebraic ampleness criterion yield the Griffiths polarization and quasi-projectivity.

arxiv:2611.04502.title: Upper Bounds on the Strassen CP Rank Gap and Symmetric Rank Gap of Third-Order Tensors
arxiv:2611.04502.summary: For two third-order tensors over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, we define the Strassen CP rank gap as the sum of their CP ranks minus the CP rank of their direct sum. For arbitrary third-order tensors, we derive explicit upper bounds on this gap in terms of CP rank excess and dimension. For symmetric third-order tensors, we similarly define the Strassen symmetric rank gap using symmetric rank and establish explicit upper bounds in terms of symmetric rank excess, CP rank excess, and dimension.

arxiv:2611.04523.title: Binary Codes with a Forbidden Distance
arxiv:2611.04523.summary: The maximum size of a t-intersecting code in the set of words of length n over an alphabet of size m, a problem posed by Frankl and F\"uredi, was determined independently by Ahlswede and Khachatrian and by Frankl and Tokushige. Extending this result to the forbidden-intersection setting, Keevash, Lifshitz, Long and Minzer proved that, for m greater than two and n sufficiently large in terms of t, (t minus one)-avoiding codes have the same maximum size and the same extremal ball constructions as t-intersecting codes. They also raised the binary case.

arxiv:2611.04530.title: Star-shaped periodic solutions of a system of delay differential equations: A computer-assisted proof
arxiv:2611.04530.summary: In this paper, we consider a planar system of nonlinear delay differential equations and prove the existence of the star-shaped periodic solutions conjectured by Hara (Nonlinear Analysis: Theory, Methods \& Applications, 30:4555--4563 (1997)) for seven parameter values. These solutions cannot be obtained by a direct application of the standard Fourier spectral method, since the corresponding linearized operator is degenerate. From numerical observations of the Fourier coefficients, we derive an ansatz that writes a star-shaped periodic solution as a periodic profile in a rotating frame.

arxiv:2611.04541.title: Exotic Dehn twists on sums of 4-manifolds, nuclei, and exotic structures
arxiv:2611.04541.summary: For closed 4-manifolds $X_1, X_2$, we give a sufficient condition, in terms of the Seiberg-Witten invariants of $X_i$, for the Dehn twist on $X_1\#X_2$ along the neck to be smoothly nontrivial. This provides a broad generalization of the result of Kronheimer-Mrowka for $K3\#K3$. We also show that the boundary Dehn twists on the punctured connected sums of many pairs of elliptic surfaces are smoothly nontrivial.

arxiv:2611.04551.title: Good slopes, congruence preservation, and gaps over residue rings
arxiv:2611.04551.summary: For $n\ge2$, a good slope of a permutation $f$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n=\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is an element $m\in\mathbb{Z}_n$ for which $x\mapsto f(x)+mx$ is a permutation. We call $f$ congruence-preserving if it preserves congruences modulo every divisor of $n$. For odd prime powers $n$, we classify all permutations with more than $n/2$ good slopes.

arxiv:2611.04560.title: Morse homology of nonsingular Morse-Smale foliations and its duality theorem
arxiv:2611.04560.summary: We define a Morse homology of the foliation which is defined by a general nonsingular Morse-Smale flow, applying the framework of the Conley index theory. In fact, we define a chain and a boundary homomorphism, therefore, a cochain and a cohomology are obtained as well. Furthermore, we prove a duality theorem on the homology and the cohomology.

arxiv:2611.04564.title: Fat base schemes and unexpected hypersurfaces of type $(d+k,d)$
arxiv:2611.04564.summary: We study hypersurfaces of degree $d+k$ containing a prescribed zero-dimensional fat point scheme $Z\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ and having multiplicity at least $d$ along a general codimension-two linear subspace. We associate with this interpolation problem a vector bundle on $\mathbb{P}^1$ whose splitting type determines the dimensions of all linear systems of type $(d+k,d)$. For a fat point of multiplicity $m$, we determine the exact number of conditions detected by this bundle and introduce the corresponding effective length.

arxiv:2611.04575.title: Polynomial configurations and pointwise averages along Piatetski--Shapiro primes
arxiv:2611.04575.summary: For every \(c>1\) sufficiently close to \(1\), we prove that there is \(\kappa>0\) such that every sufficiently large \(A\subset[N]\) of density at least \((\log N)^{-\kappa}\) contains \[ x,\ x+(p-1),\ x+(p-1)^2,\ldots,\ x+(p-1)^k, \qquad p=\lfloor n^c\rfloor\in\mathbb P. \] We also prove pointwise almost-everywhere convergence of the corresponding multiple ergodic averages.

arxiv:2611.04577.title: The Lov\'asz Local Lemma Is Sharp for the Hat Guessing Number
arxiv:2611.04577.summary: In the hat guessing game on a graph $G$, each vertex is occupied by a player wearing a hat whose color is chosen from a set of $q$ colors. Each player knows the graph and their position in it and sees only the hat colors of their neighbors. The players may agree on a strategy beforehand but must simultaneously try to guess their own hat colors without communicating.

arxiv:2611.04581.title: Finiteness properties of centralisers in $\mathrm{Out}(F_N)$ and automorphisms of free-by-cyclic groups
