arxiv:2611.04581.summary: Let $F$ be a finitely generated free group. We prove that the centraliser of any element of $\mathrm{Out}(F)$ or $\mathrm{Aut}(F)$ is of type $\rm{VF}$. We also prove that the (outer) automorphism group of any free-by-cyclic group $M=F\rtimes_\varphi\mathbb{Z}$ is of type $\rm{VF}$, and so are the McCool subgroups of $\mathrm{Out}(M)$.
arxiv:2611.04581.authors: Naomi Andrew, Yassine Guerch, Camille Horbez, Richard D. Wade

arxiv:2611.04602.title: K3 Categories and Mukai Homomorphisms for Debarre-Voisin Varieties
arxiv:2611.04602.summary: Let $M=X_6^\sigma$ be a smooth Debarre-Voisin hyperk\"ahler fourfold and $X=X_3^\sigma$ the associated smooth hyperplane section of $\operatorname{Gr}(3,10)$. Using the incidence correspondence between $X$ and $M$, we construct a family $\mathcal E$ of objects in the Kuznetsov component $\operatorname{Ku}(X)$. We write $v$ for the common Mukai vector of its fibers.

arxiv:2611.04630.title: Isolated symplectic singularities admitting symplectic resolutions
arxiv:2611.04630.summary: We give a proof that an isolated algebraic symplectic singularity of dimension $2n\ge 4$ admitting a projective symplectic resolution is analytically isomorphic to the minimal nilpotent orbit closure in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$ at the origin.

arxiv:2611.04644.title: Additive energy, Freiman's lemma, and an edge-isoperimetric problem on the boolean cube
arxiv:2611.04644.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite, non-empty set not contained in any translate of a hyperplane. We show that there exists a subset $S \subseteq A$ such that $d \ll |S| \ll d$ and \[E(A,S) := |\{(a_1,a_2,s_1,s_2)\in A\times A\times S\times S:a_1+s_1=a_2+s_2\}|\ll\lvert A\rvert\lvert S\rvert.\] This can be interpreted as a robust, analytic generalisation of the classical Freiman's lemma, and recovers Freiman's lemma up to a constant multiplicative factor. In the process of proving this result, we also show that for any integer $1 \leq m \leq d$ and any set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $|A| \leq \binom{d}{m}$, one has \[ E(A, B) \leq 4(m + 1/m) |A||B|,\]…
arxiv:2611.04644.authors: Akshat Mudgal, Carl Schildkraut, Dmitrii Zakharov

arxiv:2611.04655.title: Long-time behaviour and bifurcation analysis of a non-reciprocal two-species aggregation-diffusion system on the torus
arxiv:2611.04655.summary: A two-species aggregation-diffusion system on the one-dimensional torus with antisymmetric cross-interactions modeling pursuit-evasion dynamics is studied. The self-interaction strength is used as a bifurcation parameter, and the linear stability of the homogeneous state is characterized by Fourier analysis. It is shown that non-reciprocal coupling enlarges the stability region.

arxiv:2611.04658.title: Co-Decompositions and FO Model Checking
arxiv:2611.04658.summary: Tree decompositions describe large graphs as gluings of smaller component parts. Here we study their categorical duals, tree co-decompositions, which construct large graphs via fibered products of small constituent parts. Co-decompositions are compressed representations of graphs or relational structures: the decomposed object can be exponentially larger than the space required to specify the co-decomposition.
arxiv:2611.04658.authors: Benjamin Merlin Bumpus, Guilherme C. M. Gomes, Laura Larios-Jones, Will J. Turner

arxiv:2611.04674.title: Online packing of the three largest trees
arxiv:2611.04674.summary: For every $n\ge4$, arbitrary trees of orders $n,n-1,n-2$ can be packed into $K_n$ online, in decreasing order of size: each tree must be embedded before the next is revealed, and earlier embeddings cannot be changed. This strengthens the classical three-tree packing theorem of Hobbs, Bourgeois and Kasiraj (1987). In particular, the second tree is embedded without knowing the third, and the resulting pair of copies can be extended to accommodate every possible third tree.

arxiv:2611.04688.title: Resolvent comparison for Hermitian block matrices and Kelmans transformations
arxiv:2611.04688.summary: A Kelmans transformation increases or preserves the largest eigenvalue of a symmetric nonnegative matrix. We determine when this comparison holds for Hermitian block extensions with a fixed coupling and an arbitrary common complementary block. An orthogonal change of basis and Schur complementation give an exact formula for the compressed resolvent difference as a difference of two rank-one matrices.
arxiv:2611.04688.authors: Xianhao Meng, Zhijun Xu, Zhiyuan Zhang

arxiv:2611.04690.title: A Relative Telescope-Type Conjecture: Support and Generation in Half-Bounded Derived Categories
arxiv:2611.04690.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative noetherian ring. We ask whether complexes with finitely generated cohomology and a fixed support can be generated by relatively compact objects, using coproducts which exist in the half-bounded derived category. We prove that $\mathbf D^+_{\mathrm{fg},W}(R)=\operatorname{Loc}_{\mathrm{ex}}(\mathbf D^b_{\mathrm{fg},W}(R))$ whenever $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec} R$ is specialization closed and has finite dimension.

arxiv:2611.04691.title: Two-block paths in oriented graphs under the Ore-type condition
arxiv:2611.04691.summary: Stein conjectured that for every positive integer $k$, every oriented graph with minimum semi-degree greater than $k/2$ contains every oriented path of length $k$ [Springer Optim.Appl. 165 (2020), 459--486]. For directed paths this is a classical result of Jackson (1981). The two-block case of the conjecture was established by Chen, Hou and Zhou (2025).
arxiv:2611.04691.authors: Ke Zhao, Jia Zhou, Yunshu Gao

arxiv:2611.04699.title: Glauber Dynamics for Sampling Colorings: Rapid Mixing above $(1+1/\mathrm{e})\Delta$ via Hidden Hard-Core Models
arxiv:2611.04699.summary: We show that for every $\gamma>0$ and every sufficiently large $\Delta$, the Glauber dynamics for proper $q$-colorings of any $n$-vertex graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has spectral gap $\Omega_\gamma(1/n)$, and hence mixing time $O_\gamma(n^2\log q)$, whenever $q\ge(1+1/\mathrm{e}+\gamma)\Delta$. Our proof establishes a Bochner-type inequality by exploiting the spectral gaps of hard-core models hidden in the color classes. The constant $1+1/\mathrm{e}\approx1.368$ comes from the uniqueness threshold $\approx\mathrm{e}/\Delta$ of the hard-core model on the infinite $\Delta$-regular tree.

arxiv:2611.04723.title: Local resolution of the second log-Fitting ideal
arxiv:2611.04723.summary: Logarithmic Fitting ideals encode the complexity of the corresponding morphisms in a natural and intrinsic way, and their principalisation offers a new perspective on problems such as the resolution of cotangent sheaves and the monomialisation of morphisms. In this paper, we give a local resolution theorem for log-rank adapted morphisms: after finite sequences of smooth local blow-ups, the first two log-Fitting ideals \mathcal{F}\_{n--1}(\sigma) and \mathcal{F}\_{n--2}(\sigma) become principal monomial ideals.

arxiv:2611.04737.title: Profinite approach to S-adic shift spaces II: Invertible directive sequences
arxiv:2611.04737.summary: This paper is the second in a series about (relatively) free profinite semigroups and S-adic representations of minimal shifts. The first installment introduced the key notions of profinite images and saturating properties. The present paper examines the relationship between relative invertibility conditions (on a directive sequence) and charging properties (of a shift).
arxiv:2611.04737.authors: Jorge Almeida, Alfredo Costa, Herman Goulet-Ouellet

arxiv:2611.04778.title: On the Haagerup Vertex Operator Algebras
arxiv:2611.04778.summary: Three constructions of vertex operator algebras realizing the Haagerup center were announced independently and almost simultaneously. The relations between these constructions are studied in this paper. The generators are expressed in a common lattice basis for $E_6\oplus A_2$.
arxiv:2611.04778.authors: Chongying Dong, Xiangyu Jiao, Feng Xu

arxiv:2611.04801.title: Pushforwards of lc pairs under morphisms to abelian varieties
arxiv:2611.04801.summary: Let $f$ be a morphism from a log canonical pair $(X,\Delta)$ to an abelian variety $A$ and $D\sim_{\mathbb Q}m(K_X+\Delta)$ a Cartier divisor on $X$ with $m>1$ a rational number. We prove that $f_*\mathcal{O}_X(D)$ is globally generated after pullback by an isogeny. Our methods involve birational geometry, mixed Hodge modules and singular Hermitian metrics with the minimal extension property.

arxiv:2611.04823.title: The $\mathbb{Z}/2$-equivariant Seiberg--Witten Floer cohomology of the $(2, 1)$-cable is an unknot detector
arxiv:2611.04823.summary: We prove that a knot $K \subset S^3$ is the unknot if and only if the $\mathbb{Z}/2$-equivariant Seiberg--Witten Floer cohomology of the double cover branched along the $(2, 1)$-cable of $K$ has no $\mathbb{F}_2[Q]$-torsion. The proof combines the Thom--Gysin exact sequence, the Montesinos trick, and the genus bound for $L$-space surgeries.

arxiv:2611.04837.title: Enumerative geometry of conics and double covers on projective complete intersections
arxiv:2611.04837.summary: We compare genus zero degree two Gromov--Witten invariants with the number of embedded conics on general projective complete intersections whose conic space has expected dimension zero. Their difference comes from double covers of lines. We compute this contribution as an integral of Chern classes over the Fano scheme of lines, using an explicit obstruction bundle on the compactified space of double covers.
arxiv:2611.04837.authors: Dang Tuan Hiep, Ha Thi Thao Tram

arxiv:2611.04844.title: Derived Equivalences for Terminal Threefold Flops via Local Index-One Covering Models
arxiv:2611.04844.summary: Inspired by the quadratic involutions of Corti-Pukhlikov-Reid and Gavin Brown's description of hypersurface flips via toric GIT, we apply similar symmetries to local covering models of terminal threefold flops. We recover the derived equivalence of their canonical stacks by pullback and pushforward along the fibre product over the canonical stack of the contraction target, revisiting the local picture in Kawamata's work.

arxiv:2611.04851.title: Pseudo-Einstein Structures on Links of Isolated Singularities
arxiv:2611.04851.summary: We study Jack Lee's conjecture that, for a compact strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold $M$, the condition $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{R})$ implies the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure. For links of isolated singularities, we construct counterexamples in every odd dimension at least three, with $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{Z})$ and $b_1(M)=0$. For isolated algebraic singularities of log canonical type and complex dimension at least three, we prove that the real Chern class condition is equivalent to $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartierness of the canonical divisor, log canonicity, and the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure.
arxiv:2611.04851.authors: Yoshinori Gongyo, Kengo Hirachi, Shuya Matsumoto, Yuya Takeuchi

arxiv:2611.04856.title: Boundary determination from the anisotropic elastic Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
arxiv:2611.04856.summary: We show that the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of the elastic wave equation determines the density and the anisotropic stiffness tensor on the boundary for generic density and stiffness tensor fields. The proof builds on an interplay between microlocal analysis and algebraic geometry. Microlocal analysis yields a construction of special solutions, valid for many real principal type systems, that concentrate near a boundary point.
arxiv:2611.04856.authors: Joonas Ilmavirta, Mikko Salo, Hj{\o}rdis Schl\"uter, Daniel Windisch

arxiv:2611.04862.title: On Douglas' conjecture for $m$-Kronecker quivers
arxiv:2611.04862.summary: We prove Douglas' conjecture for $m$-Kronecker quivers for each $m \geq 3$ on the normalized logarithms of Euler characteristics of moduli spaces. Also, we state a log-concavity conjecture on Euler characteristics near slope one for the 3-Kronecker quiver.

arxiv:2611.04863.title: Geometric Obstructions and Sharp Genus Dependence in LCD Scalings
arxiv:2611.04863.summary: We study the least pole order of a rational function whose nonzero evaluations scale a prescribed code to a Euclidean LCD code. A residue-one differential yields an obstruction for odd-dimensional one-point AG codes in characteristic two: for $C=C_L(D,aQ)$ with $0\le a<n$ and odd dimension, the threshold is at least $n+2g-a-1$. The obstruction uses alternating Gram matrices and does not require the scaled code to be self-orthogonal.

arxiv:2611.04869.title: Asymptotics for partitions over the Fibonacci numbers and related sequences, II
arxiv:2611.04869.summary: In a recent paper of the same title, we considered nondistinct partitions of integers over the Fibonacci sequence and related linearly recurrent sequences. In this paper, continuing this story, we apply the same method, but consider distinct partitions. In particular, let $q_F(m)$ denote the number of ways of writing $m$ as the sum of distinct Fibonacci numbers.
arxiv:2611.04869.authors: Michael Coons, Simon Kristensen, Mathias L. Laursen

arxiv:2611.04880.title: Automaticity of structural defects in fixed points of block substitutions
arxiv:2611.04880.summary: We study structural defects in fixed points of block substitutions, building on arXiv:2604.12637 and providing its technical supplement. We develop an automata-based framework to characterize their occurrence and derive verifiable combinatorial criteria. We also introduce simplifications for the construction and analysis of these automata, including tensor-product decompositions, that clarify the mechanisms underlying structural defects and their emergence.

arxiv:2611.04942.title: An Ito-Michler type theorem and the prime class graph of weakly integral braided fusion categories
arxiv:2611.04942.summary: In a weakly integral braided fusion category, a prime divides none of the conjugacy-class dimensions if and only if it does not divide the Frobenius-Perron dimension of the adjoint subcategory. We prove that these conditions hold precisely when the corresponding Sylow subgroup of the group of invertible objects generates a braided Deligne factor whose dimension is the largest power of that prime dividing the Frobenius-Perron dimension of the category. We also prove that the prime graph of the conjugacy-class dimensions has at most two connected components.

arxiv:2611.04964.title: Substantially Improved Rate and Distance for Addressable Transversal Phase Gates
arxiv:2611.04964.summary: An important ingredient in fault-tolerant quantum computation is asymptotically good codes with fully addressable transversal non-Clifford gates. Existing constructions, however, provide only small explicit guarantees for rate and relative distance. Here, we substantially improve these guarantees for fully addressable transversal phase gates at every fixed level $h\ge3$ of the Clifford hierarchy, using a cyclic encoding beyond the binary CSS framework.
arxiv:2611.04964.authors: Bujiao Wu, Tongyin Lin, Bin Cheng

arxiv:2611.04983.title: Algebraic ellipticity of double covers of $(\mathbf P^1)^3$
arxiv:2611.04983.summary: We show that every smooth complex double cover of $(\mathbf P^1)^3$ branched along a smooth divisor of tridegree $(2,2,2)$ is algebraically Gromov elliptic. These irrational Fano threefolds form Mori--Mukai family 3-1 and have anticanonical genus seven and Picard rank three. Their three coordinate projections define degree-four del Pezzo fibrations.
arxiv:2611.04983.authors: Alexander Dvorsky, Shulim Kaliman, Mikhail Zaidenberg

arxiv:2611.04990.title: Basic Reproductive Numbers in Host-Parasite Systems with Demographic Bistability
arxiv:2611.04990.summary: The basic reproductive number, $\mathcal{R}_0$, is widely used to determine whether an infectious disease can persist in a population. However, its interpretation may become unclear when the underlying disease-free demographic dynamics exhibit multiple types of stable attractors. In this study, we investigate how demographic bistability between fixed points and periodic cycles affects the calculation and interpretation of $\mathcal{R}_0$.
arxiv:2611.04990.authors: Carli Peterson, Erika Gallo, Christopher Kribs

arxiv:2611.05015.title: The integer spectrum of a superintegrable quantum field theory
arxiv:2611.05015.summary: In our previous article CMP 407 (2026) 131, we explored the rich algebraic structures arising from a specific quantum many-body Hamiltonian quartic in the bosonic creation-annihilation operators. This Hamiltonian originated from the works of G\'erard and Grellier on classical turbulent energy transfer in a Lax-integrable setting, and its quantum version respects hierarchies of polynomial conservation laws all of which possess purely integer spectra, as does the Hamiltonian itself. The latter feature, known from numerical studies, has previously remained unproved.

arxiv:2611.05034.title: A Short Proof and Generalization of the Rainbow Cycle Theorem and Improved Bounds for Binary Even-Query LCCs
arxiv:2611.05034.summary: A \emph{rainbow cycle} in a list-edge-colored graph is a cycle where no color appears more than once. We give a short and simple proof of a result of [ABSZZ] showing that a properly edge-colored $n$-vertex graph with average degree $\Omega(\log n\log\log n)$ always contains a rainbow cycle, and generalize it to weighted graphs with edges list colored with list size at most $\ell$ and where the total weight of all edges containing a given color $i$ incident to a vertex is at most $\Delta$, showing that $\Omega_\ell(\Delta\log n\log\log n)$ average degree guarantees a rainbow cycle. Using the reduction of [AG26] and the new generalized rainbow cycle theorem, we prove that for $r\geq 3$, every…

arxiv:2611.05043.title: A Low-Diameter Nash-Williams--Tutte Theorem
arxiv:2611.05043.summary: The Nash-Williams--Tutte theorem characterizes the existence of $k$ edge-disjoint spanning trees by a condition on every vertex partition. We prove that, for simple graphs, the same condition guarantees $k$ edge-disjoint spanning trees, each of diameter $O(n/\delta)$ and with $O((n/\delta)\log(\delta+1))$ internal vertices, where $n$ is the number of vertices and $\delta$ is the minimum degree. Both bounds hold simultaneously for every tree, with absolute implicit constants independent of $k$, and each is asymptotically optimal in general.
arxiv:2611.05043.authors: Pin-Hsian Lee, Peng-Ting Lin, Meng-Tsung Tsai, Ting-An Wu

arxiv:2611.05045.title: A Wolpert Theorem for shearing coordinates
arxiv:2611.05045.summary: A theorem from Wolpert bounds the Weil--Petersson distance from a hyperbolic surface to a maximally noded surface in terms of the lengths of the underlying pants decomposition. We prove analogues for punctured surfaces both in terms of the lambda-lengths and in terms of the shearing coordinates of an ideal triangulation.

arxiv:2611.05057.title: The Maximum Second Zagreb Spectral Radius of Trees, Unicyclic Graphs and Bicyclic Graphs
arxiv:2611.05057.summary: The second Zagreb matrix of a graph $G$ is $Z(G)=D(G)A(G)D(G)$, where $D(G)$ and $A(G)$ are the degree matrix and the adjacency matrix of $G$. For many degree-based weighted adjacency matrices, the trees, unicyclic graphs and bicyclic graphs with the largest spectral radius have a vertex adjacent to all others, and Mei et al. conjectured this for every such matrix on unicyclic graphs. Jiang et al. showed that $Z(G)$ is a counterexample.

arxiv:2611.05059.title: Rank-metric intersecting codes
arxiv:2611.05059.summary: Intersecting codes are codes in which any two nonzero codewords share a common nonzero coordinate, and they have been extensively studied due to their applications in communication theory, cryptography, and combinatorics. Recently, geometric interpretations have provided new insights into intersecting codes, both in the Hamming metric and, more recently, in the rank metric for linear codes. In this paper, we introduce and study matrix rank-metric intersecting codes.
arxiv:2611.05059.authors: Martino Borello, Martin Scotti, Lune Vila

arxiv:2611.05060.title: Odd-ordered Cayley graphs satisfy Erd\H{o}s--Gy\'arf\'as
arxiv:2611.05060.summary: Erd\H{o}s and Gy\'arf\'as conjectured that every graph with minimum degree at least three contains a power-of-two-length cycle. We prove every Cayley graph of odd order satisfies the conjecture. As a corollary, we find that Cayley graphs of finite nilpotent groups satisfy the conjecture as well.

arxiv:2611.05090.title: A face polynomial invariant for embedded graphs
arxiv:2611.05090.summary: We introduce the face polynomial of a ribbon graph, a generating function for face numbers under the ribbon group action. It addresses the face-count case of the Ellis--Monaghan--Moffatt question on twisted duality. We derive deletion--contraction recursions and prove that this polynomial coincides with the vertex polynomial for \(\langle\delta\rangle\), \(\langle\delta\tau\rangle\), and \(\langle\delta,\tau\rangle\).

arxiv:2611.05096.title: Projective symmetries of Chebyshev polynomials
arxiv:2611.05096.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, and let $\varphi_d$ be the monic Chebyshev polynomial defined by $\varphi_d(t+t^{-1})=t^d+t^{-d}$. For $d>4$ with $p\nmid d$, let $H_d\le\text{PGL}_2(k)$ be the stabilizer of the zero set of $\varphi_d$. We show that \[ H_d\cong \begin{cases} D_d,&\text{if }2d=p^r+1\;\text{ for some integer }\;r\geq 1,\\ S_3,&\text{if }4d=p^r+1\;\text{ for some integer }\; r\geq 1,\\ C_2,&\text{otherwise}.

arxiv:2611.05111.title: Algebraic $\mathbb{A}^{1}$-invariance of K-theory for affinoid Tate adic spaces of good reduction
arxiv:2611.05111.summary: We establish homotopy invariance for connective continuous K-theory of affinoid Tate adic spaces of good reduction with respect to the algebraic affine line, distinct from the adic affine line as analytic stacks. We approach this through an investigation of boundedness of t-structures on nuclear module categories, to which end we also study ultrasolid modules, a variant of solid modules, and their properties.

arxiv:2611.05126.title: Mapping class group actions on the cohomology of configuration spaces of surfaces
arxiv:2611.05126.summary: Let X be a closed oriented surface of genus at least 2 and P a finite subset of X. We bound the action of the mapping class group of (X,P) on the rational cohomology groups of the ordered configuration spaces F_n(X-P) of X-P. In particular, we show that, when #P < 2, the diagonal action of the mapping class group on the direct sum of the H^n(F_n(X-P)) is faithful, and determine its kernel when #P > 1.

arxiv:2611.05146.title: Path Decompositions of Sparse Graphs via Gaussian Sweeps and Faster Exponential Algorithms
arxiv:2611.05146.summary: Using the bisection bound of Monien and Preis, Fomin and H{\o}ie proved in 2006 that every graph of maximum degree 3 on $n$ vertices has pathwidth at most $n/6+o(n)$. We prove that the pathwidth, bisection width and cutwidth of these graphs are at most $c_3 n+o(n)$, where $c_3=\frac{3}{4\pi}\arccos\frac56\approx0.1398$. For bisection width this improves the bound $n/6+o(n)$ of Monien and Preis (2006) and extends to all such graphs the bound that Lichev and Mitsche (2023) obtained for random cubic graphs.

arxiv:2611.05160.title: On partitions with bounded multiplicity restrictions on even parts and with the largest part being odd
arxiv:2611.05160.summary: Andrews and El Bachraoui (\textit{RACSAM} \textbf{119}, \textit{Article Number 4 (2025)}) established identities relating $4$-regular partitions to partitions with distinct even parts whose largest part is odd. As an extension to their work, in this paper we define partitions of a positive integer $n$ with bounded multiplicity restriction on even parts and whose largest part is odd. We prove some identities relating our partition functions and $2r$-regular partition function, and show that identities due to Andrews and El Bachraoui follow as particular cases.

arxiv:2611.05162.title: Uniform asymptotics for the Kleitman-West problem
arxiv:2611.05162.summary: Two distinct $r$-element sets are adjacent if their intersection has size $r-1$. The Kleitman-West problem, equivalently formulated as the edge-isoperimetric problem on the Johnson graph $J(n,r)$, asks for the maximum number $M_r(n,m)$ of unordered adjacent pairs in a family of $m$ $r$-element subsets of an $n$-element set, and for the families attaining this maximum. For every fixed integer $r\ge2$, we determine this maximum asymptotically as $n\to\infty$, uniformly over the entire range of family sizes.

arxiv:2611.05177.title: A Smooth Shioda-Tate Isomorphism for Elliptically Fibered 4-Manifolds
arxiv:2611.05177.summary: This paper studies a subgroup of the mapping class group of an elliptically fibered $4$-manifold $\pi: M\to B$, inspired by number theory. The smooth Mordell-Weil group $\mathrm{MW}(\pi)$ is the group of isotopy classes of smooth sections of $\pi$. We construct a smooth analog of the Shioda-Tate isomorphism, identifying $\mathrm{MW(\pi)}$ with the quotient of $H^2(M;\mathbb{Z})$ by the trivial lattice of $\pi$.

arxiv:2611.05178.title: Weighted Max Cut in Subcubic Graphs
arxiv:2611.05178.summary: For a graph $G$ with nonnegative edge weights, let $\operatorname{mc}(G,w)$ denote the maximum total weight of a cut and let $w(G)$ denote the total edge weight. We prove that every edge-weighted triangle-free subcubic graph satisfies $\operatorname{mc}(G,w)\geq \frac{15}{19}w(G)$, improving the bound of $\frac{8}{11}$ due to Gutin and Yeo. For subcubic graphs of odd girth at least seven and nine, we strengthen this bound to $\frac{47}{59}w(G)$ and $\frac45w(G)$, respectively, establishing the conjecture of Gutin and Yeo for graphs of odd girth at least nine.

arxiv:2611.05183.title: Base change between canonical basis and path basis
arxiv:2611.05183.summary: Almost 30 years ago Littelmann conjectured that there is a unitriangular base change between the dual canonical basis and the path vector basis for all symmetrizable Kac-Moody Lie algebras. In this paper we give a positive answer to the conjecture for the case of classical Lie algebras and type $G_2$, when the path model is given by standard Young tableaux.

arxiv:2611.05187.title: Hopf algebra polynomial identities in the Sweedler algebra
arxiv:2611.05187.summary: Using Mac Lane's PROPs, one can introduce multilinear polynomial identities that involve all the operations of a Hopf algebra: the (co)multiplication, the (co)unit and the antipode. We find bases for polynomial identities and calculate their codimensions for the Sweedler algebra, treating it first as an ordinary associative algebra over a field and second as a Hopf algebra.

arxiv:2611.05209.title: Relative cohomology and base-change
arxiv:2611.05209.summary: In this note we prove a simple generalization of cohomology and base-change which seems to be missing from standard sources. We illustrate its usefulness by providing an alternative proof of a result of Ishimura on descent of vector bundles along blowups at a smooth center.

arxiv:2611.05216.title: Two examples in amplituhedron tilings
arxiv:2611.05216.summary: We give an example of a tiling of the $m=4$ amplituhedron that has fewer cells than that of the magic number conjecture. The tiling uses an injective degree two cell.
arxiv:2611.05216.authors: Evgeniya Akhmedova, Thomas Lam, Calvin Yost-Wolff

arxiv:2611.05217.title: On the $abc$ conjecture
arxiv:2611.05217.summary: Using adelic intersection theory and following the method envisioned by Parshin and Moret-Bailly, we prove a conjecture of Vojta for curves of genus two and a weak form of the $abc$ conjecture

arxiv:2611.05228.title: Beyond the Bochner Method: Optimal Spectral Gaps for Block Dynamics of Spin Systems like the $O(N)$ Model
arxiv:2611.05228.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability distribution on a spin system with $n$ sites and possibly infinite spin spaces. We prove local-to-global spectral-gap bounds for block Glauber dynamics. Given a symmetric, entrywise nonnegative matrix $A$ with zero diagonal and $\lambda_{\max}(A)<1$ encoding local spectral bounds for a spin system, we derive global spectral-gap bounds for block dynamics on its marginal distributions.

arxiv:2611.05247.title: Localisations of rings of weak global dimension at most one
arxiv:2611.05247.summary: We characterise the commutative rings of weak global dimension at most one whose derived categories can be stratified by the Balmer-Favi support theory. For such rings, this yields a bijective correspondence between the class of localising subcategories of the derived category, and the subsets of the Zariski spectrum. For a large class of rings of weak global dimension at most one including all valuation domains, this occurs if and only if the ring is locally strongly discrete, if and only if the Telescope conjecture holds, and if and only if the module category has Gabriel dimension.

arxiv:2611.05254.title: The Connectivity Threshold for Friends and Strangers graphs
arxiv:2611.05254.summary: The concept of the Friends and Strangers graph $FS(G,H)$ associated with two graphs $G$ and $H$ was recently introduced by Defant and Kravitz and has generated significant interest. In a companion article, joint with Alon, they consider the behaviour of $FS(G,H)$ in the case where $G$ and $H$ are Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graphs, and prove that the threshold for connectivity is of the form $n^{-1/2+o(1)}$. In this paper we prove that the threshold is $n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log{n}}$, up to a multiplicative constant, answering a question from Alon, Defant and Kravitz.
arxiv:2611.05254.authors: Bruno Baldissera, Gabriel Dias do Couto, Simon Griffiths, Luiz Moreira

arxiv:2611.05261.title: A near-quadratic lower bound for the Brown--Erd\H{o}s--S\'os $(9,6)$-problem
arxiv:2611.05261.summary: Let $f_3(n,e+3,e)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph containing no $e$ distinct edges spanning at most $e+3$ vertices. It has long been conjectured that $f_3(n,e+3,e)\ge n^{2-o(1)}$ for every fixed $e\ge3$. We prove that $f_3(n,9,6)\ge n^2\exp(-O((\log n)^{2/3}))$, settling the first unsolved case of the conjecture.
arxiv:2611.05261.authors: Xiangliang Kong, Chong Shangguan, Xin Wang

arxiv:2611.05265.title: $K$-theory of finite monoid sets
arxiv:2611.05265.summary: In this paper we classify the algebraic K-theory of sets equipped with an action by a finite abelian monoid. The main tool developed for this purpose is an Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem, which gives a decomposition of monoid sets analogous to the decomposition given by the Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem for G-sets.
arxiv:2611.05265.authors: Maru Sarazola, Brandon T. Shapiro, Inna Zakharevich

arxiv:2611.05267.title: On the van der Corput property for cubes
arxiv:2611.05267.summary: We prove a power-saving form of the van der Corput property for cubes. As a consequence, we obtain a power-saving bound $|A|\ll_\varepsilon N^{59/60+\varepsilon}$ for sets $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no nonzero cube differences.
arxiv:2611.05267.authors: Steve Fan, Andrew Lott, \'Akos Magyar, M\'at\'e Matolcsi, Imre Z. Ruzsa

arxiv:2611.05298.title: The tensor triangular geometry of valuation domains
arxiv:2611.05298.summary: We study the tensor triangular geometry of derived categories of valuation domains, obtaining complete ring-theoretic characterizations of their main structural properties. In particular, although valuation domains are almost always non-noetherian, their derived categories always satisfy the local-to-global principle and hence the detection property. We establish precise criteria for homological detection, stratification, and homological stratification, revealing a clear hierarchy among these properties.
arxiv:2611.05298.authors: Tobias Barthel, Drew Heard, Beren Sanders, Changhan Zou

arxiv:2611.05299.title: Supercritical level-set percolation on finite graphs
arxiv:2611.05299.summary: We continue the study of bond percolation on finite graphs induced by the level-sets of the zero-average Gaussian free field on the associated metric graph. In our previous work Goswami and Pal (2026), we analyzed the critical and near-critical behavior of this model on uniform expanders, focusing on the volume of the largest cluster. In the present paper, we investigate the size of the second largest cluster in the supercritical regime --- the phase where one expects a unique giant component.

arxiv:2611.05300.title: Counterexamples to the Happy Edge Conjecture in Plane Spanning Trees
arxiv:2611.05300.summary: We study the problem of reconfiguring plane, straight-line spanning trees on point sets in the plane. A flip is a reconfiguration step in which one edge of a tree is replaced with another, yielding again a plane spanning tree. For a given point set $P$, the flip graph has a vertex for each plane spanning tree on $P$, and an edge between any two trees that differ by a single flip.
arxiv:2611.05300.authors: Oswin Aichholzer, Joseph Dorfer, Peter Kramer, Christian Rieck, Birgit Vogtenhuber

arxiv:2611.05321.title: On the number of tiles in $[n]^d$
arxiv:2611.05321.summary: Let $\mathcal{T}(n,d)$ denote the set of subsets of $[n]^d$ that tile $\mathbb Z^d$ by translations, and write $T(n,d)=|\mathcal{T}(n,d)|$. We show that almost every tile in $\mathcal{T}(n,1)$ tiles $\mathbb{Z}$ by an arithmetic progression, thus determining $T(n,1)$ asymptotically. In higher dimensions, we prove that $T(n,d)=O_d\!\left(n^{C_d}3^{n^d/3}\right)$, confirming a conjecture of Benjamini, Kozma and Tzalik.
arxiv:2611.05321.authors: Anubhab Ghosal, Jeck Lim, Elad Tzalik

arxiv:2611.05323.title: Associahedra are 12-colourable
arxiv:2611.05323.summary: We present a proper 12-colouring for all associahedra. This gives the first constant upper bound on chromatic number for this family, and disproves a conjecture of Fabila-Monroy et al. from 2009.

arxiv:2611.05331.title: Convex ribbon disks, quasipositivity, and Lagrangian sliceness
arxiv:2611.05331.summary: We introduce a version of convex surface theory for immersed ribbon surfaces with Legendrian boundary. As an application, we establish a special case of K3: Problem 1.70 on sharpness in the slice-Bennequin inequality implying quasipositivity, and a special case of a conjecture of Cornwell, Ng, and Sivek on characterizing Lagrangian sliceness. Specifically, we prove that if $K$ is a knot that bounds a "star-shaped" ribbon disk and satisfies $\overline{\mathrm{sl}}(K) = -1$ (resp.\ $\overline{\mathrm{tb}}(K) = -1$), then $K$ is quasipositive (resp.\ Lagrangian slice).

arxiv:2611.05332.title: Morse accessibility with applications to Coxeter groups
arxiv:2611.05332.summary: In this paper we begin developing a theory of Morse hierarchies for finitely generated groups. Very roughly, a Morse hierarchy is a iterative splitting of a group over subgroups that do not contribute to the Morse boundary of the ambient group. We apply this theory to Coxeter groups, establishing new combinatorial criteria that distinguish certain Coxeter groups from other Coxeter groups as well as right-angled Artin groups up to quasi-isometry.
arxiv:2611.05332.authors: Matthew Cordes, Annette Karrer, Kim Ruane

arxiv:2611.05350.title: Gepner stability conditions on hypersurface categories
arxiv:2611.05350.summary: We construct numerical Bridgeland stability conditions on the category of graded matrix factorizations of every smooth complex projective hypersurface of degree $d\ge2$. These conditions are of Gepner type $(\tau,2/d)$, where $\tau$ is the grading shift autoequivalence. By Orlov's theorem, this gives stability conditions of Gepner type on all Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces and on Kuznetsov components of all Fano hypersurfaces.
arxiv:2611.05350.authors: Anibal Aravena, Peize Liu, Jenia Tevelev

arxiv:2611.05366.title: Transfer of Weisfeiler-Leman equivalence under graph operations
arxiv:2611.05366.summary: The Weisfeiler-Leman algorithms WL(k) for $k\ge1$ form a hierarchy of increasingly powerful tests for graph isomorphism. We study how the equivalence relations they induce on graphs transfer through a graph operation $\Phi$: for a given $k$, what level of WL-equivalence between graphs $H_1$ and $H_2$ guarantees WL(k)-equivalence of graphs $\Phi(H_1)$ and $\Phi(H_2)$? We call the least such level the transfer parameter $\tau_\Phi(k)$ and determine it exactly for the line graph operation $\Phi = L$: $\tau_L(k)=2k+1$ for $k\ge2$, while $\tau_L(1)=1$.

arxiv:2611.05370.title: Geometry of Spaces of Subrings
arxiv:2611.05370.summary: Motivated by examples such as the local rings of projective integral schemes and the Zariski-Riemann space of a field, we develop a geometry for continuously indexed families of subrings of a commutative ring $R$. The indexing spaces are Stone spaces, and continuity is taken with respect to the Zariski topology on the space of subrings. To each such family we associate a subsheaf of the constant sheaf with value $R$ whose stalks are the indexed subrings.
arxiv:2611.05370.authors: Laura Cossu, Bruce Olberding, Giovanni Secreti

arxiv:2611.05421.title: Isosceles sets in Euclidean spaces of dimension nine to twenty-two
arxiv:2611.05421.summary: A finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isosceles if every three of its points form an isosceles triangle. Erd\H{o}s asked in 1946 for the largest size $\mathrm{iso}(d)$ of an isosceles set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The answer was known for $d\le 8$, the last cases being due to Ionin.

arxiv:2611.05423.title: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
arxiv:2611.05423.summary: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree at least $750$ satisfies $\chi(G)\le\max\{\omega(G),\Delta(G)-1\}$. The proof starts with a random partial colouring and completes it on large cliques using a list-colouring condition that remains valid as the rest of the graph is coloured. Disjoint stars provide the required colours.

arxiv:2611.05430.title: On the most informative Boolean function under noise
arxiv:2611.05430.summary: Let $X$ be a uniform random bit string and $Y$ be obtained by flipping each bit of $X$ independently with probability $p$. Let $C$ be a random bit obtained as a function of $Y$. We show that $\mathbf{I}(C:X)\le \mathbf{I}(Y_1:X)$ for all $p\in[0,1]$, which resolves a conjecture posed by Courtade and Kumar in 2013.

arxiv:2611.05433.title: Extremal even-cycle-free subgraphs of the $k$-ary $n$-cube
arxiv:2611.05433.summary: A graph is said to be $H$-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to $H$. The generalized Tur\'{a}n number $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$, a natural extension of the classical Tur\'{a}n number, is defined as the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free spanning subgraph of $G$. For any integer $\ell\geq 2$, let $C_{2\ell}$ denote the even cycle of length $2\ell$.

arxiv:2611.05452.title: On Fujita's Advanced Generalized Mukai Conjecture
arxiv:2611.05452.summary: We prove Fujita's advanced generalized Mukai conjecture for smooth complex Fano varieties. Our starting point is the existence of independent two-point Gromov--Witten correspondences. We show that there are finitely many unsplit families of rational curves whose chains connect $X$.

arxiv:2611.05489.title: Stabiliser codes over prime fields as weighted graphs and as quantum sets of lines
arxiv:2611.05489.summary: We further develop the theory of quantum stabiliser codes and its links with graph theory and finite geometry. We prove that an [[n,k,d]]_p stabiliser code over a finite field with p elements, p prime, gives rise to a graph on n-k vertices together with two disjoint independent sets of size k. Its edges are weighted with elements of a finite field of size p.
arxiv:2611.05489.authors: Simeon Ball, G\"ulizar G\"unay, Robin Simoens, Ricard Vilar

arxiv:2611.05526.title: Quantum error correcting codes from quiver moduli: Grassmannians, cyclic monodromy, and argyle collision divisors
arxiv:2611.05526.summary: Building on aspects of a recent diagrammatic field-theory programme for quantum error correction put forward by the first-named author (arXiv:2607.08911), we construct exact finite-dimensional codes from twisted cyclic and argyle quiver moduli on the projective line. A regular fibre of the node-labelled cyclic Hitchin map records the ways to distribute simple spectral zeroes among the arrows with prescribed degrees. The Hilbert space spanned by these allocations is a Young permutation module.

arxiv:2611.05531.title: Hamilton cycles in bicirculants with non-coprime connection sets
arxiv:2611.05531.summary: A bicirculant is a regular graph that admits an automorphism having two vertex-orbits of the same size. A bicirculant can be described as follows. Given an integer $m \ge 1$ and sets $R, S, T \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_m$ such that $R=-R$, $T=-T$, $0 \not\in R \cup T$ and $0 \in S$, the graph $B(m;R,S,T)$ has vertex set $V=\{u_0,\dots,u_{m-1},v_0,\dots,v_{m-1}\}$ and edge set $E=\{u_iu_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in R\} \cup \{v_iv_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in T\} \cup \{u_iv_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in S\}.$ Some of the well known bicirculants include the generalized Petersen graphs and Cayley graphs of dihedral groups.

arxiv:2611.05532.title: Shotgun Assembly of the Non-Uniform Labeled Lattice Model
arxiv:2611.05532.summary: In this paper, we study the graph shotgun assembly problem in the labeled lattice model, as introduced by Mossel and Ross (2019). We start with a $d$-dimensional lattice of length $n$, where the color of each vertex is sampled i.i.d. from a distribution $\pi$. Then, we ask whether it is possible to reconstruct the coloring of the lattice given the coloring of each subgrid of length $k$.
arxiv:2611.05532.authors: Julia Gaudio, Charlie K. Guan, Andrew Jin

arxiv:2611.05568.title: Non-redundant Independence Atoms
arxiv:2611.05568.summary: Independence atom is a key concept in relational database theory. In the present paper, we prove that the maximum possible size of a non-redundant set of independence atoms on $n$ attributes is asymptotically $(1+o(1))\binom{n}{\floor{n/2}}$. It turns out that this problem is closely related to two extremal set theory problems, the Katona-Tarj\'an question on ``V''-free families of subsets of $[n]$ for the lower bound, and Kleitman's bound on union-free families for the upper bound.

arxiv:2611.05588.title: The Zelevinsky involution, co-standard modules for quantum affine algebras and interval symmetric functions
arxiv:2611.05588.summary: Let $\mathscr{F}_n$ be the subcategory of finite-dimensional representations of the quantum loop algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$ whose simple modules are indexed by multisegments consisting of intervals $[a,b]$, where $a,b$ are integers and $0<b-a\le n$. We define the co-standard module associated to a multisegment $\mathbf{s}$ to be the tensor product of the Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules, associated to the first node of the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$, given by the segments of $\mathbf{s}$. Under a suitable (and necessary) restriction on $n$, we show that its socle is isomorphic to the simple module given by the Zelevinsky dual $\mathbf{s}^\dagger$ of $\mathbf{s}$.

arxiv:2611.05607.title: IC-rigidity and generalizations of a theorem of Mahler
arxiv:2611.05607.summary: Mahler showed that for every irrational $\alpha$ and every base ${b\geq 2}$, there is a single positive integer $n$ such that every digit in $\{0, \dots, b-1\}$ occurs infinitely often in the base-$b$ expansion of $n\alpha$. Furstenberg later observed that dynamical methods can be used to give a different proof. Building on this perspective, we give generalizations of Mahler's theorem in two directions: the multipliers are a syndetic subset of certain multiplicative semigroups, and analogous versions hold in higher dimensions.

arxiv:2611.05621.title: Pointfree convergence approach and pointfree index theory
arxiv:2611.05621.summary: Given a category $\mathsf{C}$ of lattices, we introduce the category $\mathsf{C^{Cap}}$, a pointfree version of the category $\Cap$ of convergence approach spaces, that contains $\Cap$ coreflectively, as well as the category $\mathsf{C^{Conv}}$, of pointfree convergence spaces introduced by Goubault-Larrecq and Mynard, both reflectively and coreflectively. We investigate pointfree counterparts of pseudo-approach, pre-approach, and approach spaces along two natural axes---depth and adherence-determinedness---which coincide in the spatial case but diverge in general lattices, and we determine when the point--powerset adjunction restricts to these subcategories. Unlike in $\mathsf{C^{Conv}}$,…

arxiv:2611.05622.title: Almost All 3-uniform Hypergraphs are Class 1
arxiv:2611.05622.summary: The chromatic index $\chi'(H)$ of a hypergraph $H$ is the smallest number of colors needed to color its edges so that no two adjacent edges share the same color. The chromatic index is trivially bounded below by the maximum degree $\Delta(H)$, and when $\chi'(H)= \Delta(H)$, we say that $H$ is Class 1. It is well known that almost every 2-graph is Class 1, and we extend this result to 3-graphs.
arxiv:2611.05622.authors: Arnab Chaterjee, Asaf Ferber, Marcelo Sales, Mason Shurman

arxiv:2611.05623.title: Partitions with designated summands: $k$-tuples and their congruences
arxiv:2611.05623.summary: Let $A_k(n)$ and $B_k(n)$ be the numbers of ordered $k$-tuples of partitions with designated summands, respectively with designated summands and all parts odd, of total size $n$. Using an exact description of the generating function of designated partitions after a $3$-dissection, we classify for every $e$ the values of $k$ for which $A_k(3n+2)$ is divisible by $3^e$: this happens exactly when $k\equiv0$ or $-5\pmod{3^e}$ if $e\le4$, and when $3^e\mid k$ if $e\ge5$. We obtain the corresponding exact $3$-adic and several $2$-adic results for $B_k$ and for $A_k$ along the progressions $4n+3$, a recursion for the classes $3^b(3n+s)$, and for $k=2$ the congruences $A_2(12n+10)\equiv…

arxiv:2611.05631.title: On Diameter Graphs Problems: A proof of Brass's Conjecture
arxiv:2611.05631.summary: The diameter graph of a finite set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ has vertex set $S$ and two points are adjacent when their distance equals $\operatorname{diam} S$. In this paper we study the following question: given $k$ and $d$, is there a constant $c=c(k,d)$ such that from every finite point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ one can remove at most $c$ points so that the subgraph of the diameter graph induced by the remaining points is $k$-colorable? Brass conjectured that such a constant exists for $d=3$ and $k=3$.

arxiv:2611.05634.title: Linear-length cycles in the supercritical percolated hypercube
arxiv:2611.05634.summary: Let $Q_p^d$ be the random subgraph of the $d$-dimensional binary hypercube obtained by retaining each edge independently with probability $p$. A long-standing folklore conjecture states that the emergence of the giant component in $Q_p^d$, at $p\approx 1/d$, is accompanied by the emergence of cycles of linear length. We confirm this conjecture and determine the order of the longest cycle near the phase transition.

arxiv:2611.05649.title: Linear Cotype Bounds for Nonlinear Spectral Gaps of Scalar Expanders
arxiv:2611.05649.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple $d$-regular graph, $d\geq 3$, whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue satisfies $\lambda_2(G)\leq (1-\delta)d$, where $0<\delta\leq 1$. We prove that the Poincar\'e constant satisfies $$\gamma(G,\|\cdot\|_X)\lesssim \frac{qCK}{\delta}$$ whenever $X$ is a real Banach space with a $K$-unconditional Schauder basis and cotype $q$ with constant $C$. This constant compares the mean distance over all vertex pairs with the mean distance across edges.

arxiv:2611.05672.title: A motivic Vojta inequality for non-CM elliptic curves with unbounded height
arxiv:2611.05672.summary: We study a bounded-degree form of a motivic Vojta inequality for pure Andr\'e motives, arising from a question of Kato. We verify this inequality for infinitely many non-CM elliptic curves with unbounded stable Faltings height. The point is that ramification at the finite poles of the $j$-invariant gives the required discriminant bound.

arxiv:2611.05673.title: Orthogonal polynomials on two or more intervals: the Sprugnoli context
arxiv:2611.05673.summary: We show how the group of Sprugnoli arrays on three elements can be used to define families of polynomials that are orthogonal on two intervals, and we indicate how the group can be extended in the hierarchy of Sprugnoli groups to yield families of orthogonal polynomials with more complex supports. In particular, we examine the defining three term recurrences and the Jacobi matrices of these families of orthogonal polynomials, while detailing the Sprugnoli matrix structure of the coefficient matrices of the polynomial families. We also consider integral representations of the principal moments on the defining intervals.

arxiv:2611.05677.title: The Galois actions on braided fusion categories
arxiv:2611.05677.summary: This note harmonizes two classical topics: minimal modular extensions of braided fusion categories and the Galois action on modular fusion categories. Their common generalizations are Galois-modular extensions, which always exist when a braided fusion category $\mathcal{B}$ is pseudounitary. Each extension induces a Galois action on the simple objects of $\mathcal{B}$.

arxiv:2611.05679.title: Orbit Transversality for Projective Space
arxiv:2611.05679.summary: Let $f\colon \mathbb{P}^n\to \mathbb{P}^n$ be a dominant endomorphism defined over a number field $K$. We show that there is a finite extension $L/K$ such that every proper closed subset of $\mathbb{P}^n$ misses at least one grand $(f,L)$-orbit. Equivalently, $(\mathbb{P}^n,f,K)$ is strongly dense orbit transversal (S-DOT): every set containing exactly one representative of each grand $(f,L)$-orbit is Zariski dense in $\mathbb{P}^n$.

arxiv:2611.05696.title: Quartic polynomial differential systems with three disjoint invariant circles
arxiv:2611.05696.summary: We determine the normal forms of real planar polynomial differential systems of degree at most four with three prescribed pairwise disjoint invariant circles, covering all configurations of their centers. None of the prescribed circles is a limit cycle in the concentric case or in the coaxial case with three distinct centers, where the pairwise radical axes coincide. When exactly two centers coincide, or when the three centers are distinct and collinear and the circles are non-coaxial, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for all three circles to be algebraic limit cycles, which are necessarily hyperbolic.

arxiv:2611.05707.title: Equivariant elliptic cohomology via loop spaces
arxiv:2611.05707.summary: We construct a cohomology theory $H_A(-)$ canonically attached to any 1-dimensional commutative group scheme A over a connective $E_\infty$-ring. The additive group in characteristic zero gives 2-periodic de Rham cohomology, the multiplicative group gives topological periodic cyclic homology, and an elliptic curve gives elliptic cohomology. The construction extends to the G-equivariant setting for an algebraic group G, yielding in the elliptic case a theory of equivariant elliptic cohomology on algebraic varieties with G-action that takes values in sheaves on the stack of G-bundles.

arxiv:2611.05745.title: A toric approach to social choice theory
arxiv:2611.05745.summary: This paper initiates a systematic study of objects in convex geometry and toric algebraic geometry arising from status quo systems in social choice theory. Our main application is to classify all cones arising from a large class of status quo systems that are smooth or simplicial.
arxiv:2611.05745.authors: Ata Poyraz Turna, Ben Y. Wormleighton

arxiv:2611.05786.title: A topological Mundici representation theorem
arxiv:2611.05786.summary: We lift Mundici's equivalence between MV-algebras and abelian $\ell$-groups with a strong unit to the topological setting. To this end, we prove that, for every topological MV-algebra, the associated Mundici group can be endowed with a topology that extends the topology of the MV-algebra and makes it into an abelian topological $\ell$-group. Among such topologies there is a finest one; we identify this topology as the topological-group reflection of the bounded-stage final topology, and construct an explicit zero-neighbourhood base in terms of the original MV-algebra topology.
arxiv:2611.05786.authors: Yifan Meng, Lili Shen, Dexue Zhang

arxiv:2611.05795.title: Non-Pseudo-Arithmetic Hyperbolic 4-Manifolds
arxiv:2611.05795.summary: We give three explicit finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter lattices in dimension four whose adjoint trace fields are not totally real. They are the reflection groups of the Ma--Zheng polytopes $P_{11,6}$, $P_{11,7}$, $P_{11,8}$. The obstruction is contained in two cyclic products of the doubled unit-normal Gram matrix $A=2G$.

arxiv:2611.05809.title: On rational curves relative to a divisor
arxiv:2611.05809.summary: Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety and $D$ a reduced simple normal crossings divisor. We prove that, given a complete curve of negative $(K_X+D)$-degree, through its general points there is a rational curve whose normalization meets $D$ in at most one point. The proof uses ordinary weighted jets of a smooth family constructed from $(X,D)$, a positive parameter line bundle, and an intersection calculation on a ruled surface.

arxiv:2611.05848.title: Cyclotomic factorization and fixed-point insertion in colored permutation groups
arxiv:2611.05848.summary: We extend cyclotomic Euler--Mahonian factorization to colored permutation groups for two inversion statistics: Biagioli--Zeng length and the inversion number of the underlying unsigned permutation. At a primitive $m$th root and rank $n=mk+i$, each normalized enumerator is a Hadamard product of a rank-$i$ colored enumerator and a weighted rank-$k$ type-B enumerator. Separate color variables are retained.

arxiv:2611.05861.title: A Complete Characterization of $q$-Ary $2$-Designs in Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
arxiv:2611.05861.summary: Let $\mathcal{C}_k$ be the doubly-extended Reed--Solomon code with parameters $[q+1, k, q-k+2]_q$. We give a complete characterization of when its codewords of a fixed weight form $q$-ary 2-designs. The main ingredient is an exact criterion showing that the number of $r$-subsets of $\mathbb{F}_q^*$ with a prescribed product is independent of that product if and only if $\gcd(r, q-1)=1$.

arxiv:2611.05898.title: An Asymptotic for E. P. Stein Numbers
arxiv:2611.05898.summary: Epstein's put-or-take-a-square game is an impartial combinatorial game in which a player may, in each turn, add or subtract the largest square not exceeding the current integer. We study E. P.

arxiv:2611.05905.title: Holomorphic flexibility properties of strongly commuting varieties
arxiv:2611.05905.summary: We study holomorphic flexibility properties of the strongly commuting variety of a complex semisimple algebraic group $G$. We prove that the smooth locus of the strongly commuting variety of $G$ is Oka-$1$. We also prove that the smooth locus of the commuting variety of a semisimple complex Lie algebra is Oka-$1$, and that it contains a Zariski dense open subset which is algebraically elliptic.

arxiv:2611.05914.title: Uniform comparison of multiplier and test ideals for polynomials with affinely independent support
arxiv:2611.05914.summary: Let $f\in\Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ have affinely independent exponent vectors. We prove that its test ideals agree with the reductions of its multiplier ideals at all nonnegative real exponents for every sufficiently large prime in one arithmetic progression. The progression depends only on the support of $f$.

arxiv:2611.05915.title: Categorical Torelli and Fourier-Mukai partners of hypersurfaces
arxiv:2611.05915.summary: Let $X\subset\PP^{M-1}$ be a smooth hypersurface of degree $d<M$, and let $\Ku(X)$ be its Kuznetsov component, the orthogonal complement of the line bundles $\OO_X,\dots,\OO_X(M-d-1)$ in the derived category. We prove that $\Ku(X)$ determines $X$ for every smooth quartic in $\PP^{4k+1}$, $k\geq1$; together with earlier work, this gives categorical Torelli for every smooth hypersurface of degree $d<M$ with $d\nmid M$. The same algebraic reconstruction proves the classical generic Torelli theorem for these quartics, which completes generic Torelli for smooth hypersurfaces whose degree does not divide $M$, cubic surfaces excepted.

arxiv:2611.05921.title: Occupation Measures in the ODE Method: Wasserstein Convergence and Rates
arxiv:2611.05921.summary: We study occupation measures associated with stochastic approximation recursions within the ordinary differential equation (ODE) method. Under Lyapunov conditions ensuring that the limiting ODE has a globally exponentially stable equilibrium, we establish that the continuous-time occupation measures associated with the piecewise linear interpolation of the iterates converge almost surely in the $2$-Wasserstein topology to the Dirac mass at the equilibrium, the unique invariant probability measure of the limiting semiflow. The choice of the $2$-Wasserstein distance is naturally aligned with our continuous- and discrete-time Lyapunov drift analysis.

arxiv:2611.05924.title: How to prove equations using diagrams: A categorical and operational semantics for e-graphs
arxiv:2611.05924.summary: E-graphs are a powerful algorithmic technique for automated equational reasoning but have resisted a conceptual understanding independent of issues of presentation and implementation. We propose an operational semantics for e-graphs based on the fundamental category-theoretic concepts of diagrams, limits, and initial functors. We illustrate the formalism through numerous example calculations and establish its soundness and completeness.

arxiv:2611.05949.title: Wandering continua, renormalization, and Lebesgue measure on Julia sets
arxiv:2611.05949.summary: We study the Lebesgue measure of wandering continua and related invariant sets in Julia sets, using the hyperbolic area method recently developed by Ye. For entire functions of finite type, we show that a wandering continuum of positive area must escape to infinity uniformly. For infinitely renormalizable unicritical polynomials, we show that almost every point in the renormalization core (the intersection of the orbits of little Julia sets) is recurrent and contained in the postcritical set.

arxiv:2611.05961.title: One-Vertex Lifts of Looped Circle Graphs: Obstructions and Interlace Polynomials
arxiv:2611.05961.summary: Let $M$ be the adjacency matrix of a looped simple graph over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and let $t=\operatorname{diag} M$. We study the one-vertex lift with adjacency matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}M+tt^T&t\\t^T&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. A looped circle graph is called stable if its lift is a circle graph.

arxiv:2611.05962.title: Exact $3$-Adic Periods of Symmetric Dellac Numbers and Their Polynomial Extensions
arxiv:2611.05962.summary: The odd and even symmetric Dellac numbers are the specializations $a_n=f_n(0)$ and $e_n=f_n(1)$ of the Randrianarivony--Zeng family $f_n(s)=2^{-n}D_n(s)$. Using a finite Stieltjes-fraction truncation, we establish the sharp congruence $v_3(a_n)=1$ for $n\ge2$ and obtain explicit congruences modulo $81$ for both sequences. We also establish universal eventual periodicity modulo arbitrary positive integers.

arxiv:2611.05972.title: Magnitude, path and coarse homology
arxiv:2611.05972.summary: In this article, we introduce Borel--Moore and uniformly finite versions of magnitude homology and path homology for locally finite graphs by allowing possibly infinite chains subject to local finiteness and boundedness conditions. In both settings, we construct magnitude--path spectral sequences extending the spectral sequence studied by the author. Their E^1-pages are given by the corresponding magnitude homologies, their E^2-pages contain the corresponding path homologies on the p-axis, and they converge to coarse homology and uniformly finite homology, respectively, in the sense of Nowak--Yu.

arxiv:2611.05980.title: Coherent configuration on 3-uniform hypergraph over strongly regular graph
arxiv:2611.05980.summary: This paper investigates coherent configurations on 3-uniform hypergraphs constructed from strongly regular graphs. We establish that the hypergraph preserves the automorphism group of the original graph and induces a nonhomogeneous Schurian coherent configuration. Using the case of Petersen graph, we obtain a configuration with two fibers and thirteen basic relations.

arxiv:2611.06003.title: How Unbalanced Must a Latin Rectangle Be?
arxiv:2611.06003.summary: We view a $k\times n$ Latin rectangle as $n$ points in the grid $[n]^k$. Each symbol gives one point, whose coordinates are the columns it occupies. The rectangle is balanced when these points are pairwise equidistant in the $\ell_1$ metric.

arxiv:2611.06014.title: The integral Chow rings of $\mathcal A_3$ and $\mathcal M_3$
arxiv:2611.06014.summary: Over $\mathbb C$, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal A_3$, the moduli stack of principally polarized abelian threefolds. Along the way, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal M_3$, the moduli stack of smooth genus-three curves. The ring $\CH(\mathcal A_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, along with three classes supported on the locus of decomposable abelian varieties, subject to 16 relations.

arxiv:2611.06017.title: Finiteness of Non-decomposable Critically Frustrated Signed Graphs
arxiv:2611.06017.summary: A signed graph $(G,\sigma)$ is a graph $G$ with a signature $\sigma$ labeling each edge with a positive or negative sign. Two signatures of $G$ are switching equivalent if one is obtained from the other by sequentially changing the signs of all edges in an edge-cut. The frustration index of a signed graph $(G, \sigma)$ is the minimum number of negative edges among all signatures switching equivalent to $\sigma$.

arxiv:2611.06030.title: Capelli Operators and the Bernstein-Sato polynomials of Minors
arxiv:2611.06030.summary: For every ideal of minors of a generic complex matrix, we determine all roots and their multiplicities in the Bernstein-Sato polynomial. These roots lie in explicit rational intervals indexed by the rank strata. Every nonintegral root is simple, whereas the multiplicity of each integral root equals the number of labels producing that root.

arxiv:2611.06031.title: Toward Shifted symplectic Chiralization: Deformation of Courant Algebroids
arxiv:2611.06031.summary: We study the chiralization of Poisson--Lie theory through graded symplectic geometry. We compare Courant deformations and classical $r$- and $R$-matrix constructions, obtaining integrable hierarchies and free field realizations. We give a variational description of the obstruction to Lie conformal bialgebra compatibility and recover Liberati's obstruction in the Virasoro case.

arxiv:2611.06077.title: Odd and even fake quadrics isogenous to a product
arxiv:2611.06077.summary: A $\mathbb{Q}$-homology quadric is a smooth compact complex surface which has the same $\mathbb{Q}$-homology as a quadric surface, that is, the product of two $2$-dimensional spheres. It is called fake if it is minimal and not rational. Among them are the fake quadrics which are isogenous to a product of complex curves.
arxiv:2611.06077.authors: Fabrizio Catanese, JongHae Keum, Do Geun Kim, Kyoung-Seog Lee

arxiv:2611.06081.title: On the Cameron-Praeger conjecture for Steiner 6-designs
arxiv:2611.06081.summary: A long-standing and far-reaching conjecture of Cameron and Praeger (1993) asserts that no non-trivial block-transitive $6$-$(v,k,\lambda)$ designs exist. Huber (2010) reduced the Steiner case ($\lambda=1$) to a single infinite family of possible exceptions, where the automorphism group is $G=\PGaL(2,p^e)$ acting on the points of the projective line, with $p\in\{2,3\}$ and $e$ an odd prime power. In this paper, we resolve this final case.
arxiv:2611.06081.authors: Ximin Wang, Zheng Huang, Weijun Liu

arxiv:2611.06091.title: Neighbourhood second Zagreb matrix of graphs: spectral radius bounds and extremal graphs
arxiv:2611.06091.summary: Let $G$ be a connected graph on at least two vertices, and let $\delta(i)$ be the sum of the degrees of the neighbours of a vertex $i$. The \emph{neighbourhood second Zagreb matrix} $\NF(G)$ has $(i,j)$-entry $\delta(i)\delta(j)$ if $i\sim j$ and $0$ otherwise; its spectral radius is denoted by $\rNF(G)$. We prove that $\rNF(G)\ge\rho(G)^{5}$, where $\rho(G)$ is the adjacency spectral radius, with equality if and only if $G$ is regular or bipartite semiregular, and we use this to show that the same graphs are exactly the extremal graphs of a Berman--Zhang--type upper bound.

arxiv:2611.06106.title: PCF All The Way Down
arxiv:2611.06106.summary: We prove that a finite surjective post-critically finite self-map of a variety in characteristic zero remains post-critically finite on every preperiodic integral effective divisor after passing to its periodic image with its return map. Iterating this result proves PCF all the way down. A detailed report on AI usage is contained in the manuscript.
arxiv:2611.06106.authors: Taylor Dupuy, Alon Levy, Thomas Tucker, Zhouran Wang

arxiv:2611.06107.title: Geodesic Transversal of Hypercube and Butterfly networks
arxiv:2611.06107.summary: A geodesic $P$ of a connected graph $G(V,E)$ is called a maximal geodesic if there exists no geodesic $P'$ in $G$ that contains $P$ as its sub-path. The geodesic transversal problem determines a subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ such that every possible maximal geodesic of $G$ includes at least one vertex of $S$. Such a set with minimum number of elements is called a gt-set and its cardinality is the gt-number of $G$.
arxiv:2611.06107.authors: R. Prabha, B. Sandhiya, Paul Manuel

arxiv:2611.06140.title: Highly connected uniquely $k$-linked digraphs
arxiv:2611.06140.summary: Extending a result of Thomassen, we prove that for every choice of positive integers $K\geq k$ there exist a $K$-strong digraph which has two disjoint sets $S,T$ each of size $k$ so that the only linkage from $S$ to $T$ in $D$ is the one whose existence follows from Menger's theorem.

arxiv:2611.06165.title: Koszul duality and homotopy algebras for operads over quivers
arxiv:2611.06165.summary: For a quiver $Q$, we introduce and study $Q$-operads (or operads over $Q$), defined as a special sort of $\mathbf{fc}$-multicategories or virtual double categories, in which the directions of the arrows of $Q$ encode the permitted input orderings. In this higher operadic framework, we construct the bar--cobar adjunction and develop a theory of Koszul duality and homotopy algebras, together with compatibility results under changes of quiver. We treat dg categories and their left modules, right modules, and bimodules as algebras over quiver-operads.

arxiv:2611.06193.title: Rational Torsion and Ramification Constraints on Odd Superelliptic Jacobians
arxiv:2611.06193.summary: Let C: y^d = f(x) be a smooth projective superelliptic curve over Q, where d >= 3 is odd, f(x) in Q[x] is separable of degree n >= 3, and gcd(d,n) = 1. Let J = Jac(C) be its Jacobian. We study the rational torsion subgroup J(Q)_tors through the interaction of ramification geometry, Galois actions, reduction at primes of good reduction, and the geometry of divisors.

arxiv:2611.06199.title: Constructing Cospectral Hypergraphs Using Adjacency Preserving Permutations
arxiv:2611.06199.summary: In this paper, we use permutations of the vertices of hypergraphs that preserve their adjacency matrices defined in banerjee 2021. These permutations form a group which lies between the automorphism group and the full symmetric group $S_n$ where $n$ is the number of vertices. Using elements from that group which are not automorphisms, we construct cospectral non-isomorphic hypergraphs.

arxiv:2611.06201.title: $C_2$-Cofiniteness of Permutation Orbifolds I: Relative $C_1$ Descent
arxiv:2611.06201.summary: We establish a relative $C_1$-cofiniteness criterion for $C_2$-cofiniteness of finite group orbifolds. For permutation actions on a simple, self contragredient, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type, it suffices to check a single relation for a derivative of the conformal vector in the Virasoro vertex operator algebra. This reduces the problem to a calculation depending only on the central charge and tensor degree.

arxiv:2611.06210.title: Accessibility of collapsed Anosov flow
arxiv:2611.06210.summary: We prove that every $C^1$ collapsed Anosov flow on a closed three-manifold with non-virtually-solvable fundamental group is accessible. No transitivity or nonwandering assumption is required, and the collapsing map need not satisfy the strong-collapse conditions. We also prove that every three-dimensional collapsed Anosov flow for which no positive iterate is a discretized Anosov flow is accessible.

arxiv:2611.06211.title: Equilibrium webs and stability for arbitrary families of endomorphisms of projective spaces
arxiv:2611.06211.summary: We consider arbitrary holomorphic families of endomorphisms of a complex projective space. We prove that the existence of an equilibrium web implies the holomorphic motion of all repelling cycles contained in the Julia set, i.e., the support of the unique measure of maximal entropy. Together with previous results of Berteloot, Bianchi, Br\'evard, Buff, and Dupont, this completes the extension of the stability-bifurcation theory to arbitrary families of holomorphic endomorphisms.
arxiv:2611.06211.authors: Fabrizio Bianchi, Zhuchao Ji, Junyi Xie

arxiv:2611.06250.title: A Polynomial Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa bound for Eulerian digraphs
arxiv:2611.06250.summary: In [Combinatorica 1996], Reed, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas proved Younger's conjecture dating back to 1973 that states that directed cycles have the Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa property. Specifically, they showed that every directed graph $D$ contains either $k$ arc-disjoint cycles or a set of at most $f(k)$ arcs that intersect every directed cycle. The function $f$, depending only on $k$, is however notoriously large--in fact, not even elementary.
arxiv:2611.06250.authors: Esther Galby, Roohani Sharma, Bart van der Steenhoven

arxiv:2611.06256.title: From the quantum group $U_{q^{1/2}}( {\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}}}_2 )$ to the Kronecker quantum cluster algebra
arxiv:2611.06256.summary: Let $\mathcal A_q$ be the Kronecker quantum cluster algebra with principal coefficients. We construct an explicit algebra homomorphism from the whole quantum group ${U_{{q^{1/2}}}}( {{{\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}}}_2}} )$ to $\mathcal A_q$, whose images together with either of the two frozen variables generate $\mathcal A_q$. As an application, we obtain algebra homomorphisms from the split $\imath$quantum groups of affine $\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}}_2$ to $\mathcal A_q$.
arxiv:2611.06256.authors: Junyuan Huang, Xueqing Chen, Ming Ding, Fan Xu

arxiv:2611.06261.title: Homology and Topology of Partially Ordered Fields
arxiv:2611.06261.summary: We develop a unified homology theory for directed partial orders (DPOs) and lattice-ordered positive cones on fields of characteristic zero. With the underlying field and its operations fixed, we define order?carrying spaces independently by topological conditions, establish a bijection with DPO positive cones, and characterize lattice orders by intersections of minimal open neighborhoods. A unified comparison theorem identifies graded Ext for region ideals with sheaf cohomology and multiplicative Tor with the reduced singular homology of truncated regions, giving a topological interpretation of the existence and preservation of reduced decompositions.

arxiv:2611.06269.title: Small 5-chromatic unit-distance graphs in disks of radius 3/2, 5/4 and 23/20
arxiv:2611.06269.summary: We give three explicit unit-distance graphs in the plane with chromatic number 5 whose vertices lie in small disks: a graph with 773 vertices inside an open disk of radius 3/2, one with 5713 vertices inside an open disk of radius 5/4, and one with 8168 vertices inside an open disk of radius 23/20. The smallest examples previously reported for these radii have 11725, 11725 and 31171 vertices. All coordinates are exact elements of Q(sqrt3, sqrt5, sqrt11).

arxiv:2611.06275.title: On generalized $k$-token graphs with distinguishable tokens and a maximum capacity of $s$ tokens per vertex
arxiv:2611.06275.summary: Supertoken graphs \(F^s_{k\times1}(G)\), also known as generalized token graphs, model configurations of \(k\) distinguishable tokens on a graph \(G\), with at most \(s\) tokens at each vertex. We study structural and metric properties of these graphs in terms of the base graph. For regular \(G\), we characterize when \(F^s_{k\times1}(G)\) is regular.
arxiv:2611.06275.authors: Yiting Cai, Cristina Dalf\'o, Blas Fern\'andez, Miquel \`Angel Fiol

arxiv:2611.06300.title: Perfect Forms and Torsion Bounds in Algebraic $K$-Theory over Totally Real and CM Fields
arxiv:2611.06300.summary: We extend the method of Van Woerden \cite{woerden} to totally real and CM number fields to obtain an upper bound for the number of $\GLo-$equivalence classes of perfect forms. Moreover, by considering appropriate barycentric subdivisions of the Voronoi tessellation, we extend these estimates to the number of $\GLo$-orbits of $k$-dimensional faces of the Voronoi tessellation. As a consequence, we improve the asymptotic order of the bounds for the torsion part of $K_m(\rint)$ obtained by Soul\'e \cite{soule_hermitian_bounds} and Houriet \cite{Juliet_PHD}.

arxiv:2611.06301.title: Multiple $q$-zeta values as polynomials in partition multiplicities
arxiv:2611.06301.summary: Writing multiple $q$-zeta values as sums over partitions, a conjecture of Bachmann, proved by Hirose, Maesaka and Watanabe by means of a recursion, says that polynomials in the parts and multiplicities can be replaced by polynomials in the multiplicities alone. We make this replacement explicit, derive from it bounds on weight and depth that make Bachmann's conjecture effective, and provide a closed formula for the Drop1 operator of Hirose, Maesaka, Seki and Watanabe.

arxiv:2611.06310.title: Hamiltonicity and cycle factors in k-quasi-transitive digraphs of large diameter
arxiv:2611.06310.summary: A digraph is $k$-quasi-transitive if the endpoints of every directed path of length $k$ are adjacent. In this paper, we prove that every strong non-bipartite $k$-quasi-transitive digraph of diameter at least $k+2$ is Hamiltonian when $k\ge7$ is odd. Moreover, combined with the known even case, for $k\ge6$, we also prove that a strong bipartite $k$-quasi-transitive digraph of diameter at least $k+2$ is Hamiltonian if and only if it has a cycle factor.

arxiv:2611.06314.title: Dolgopyat estimate for partially hyperbolic systems: limit theorems and exponential mixing
arxiv:2611.06314.summary: We prove a Dolgopyat-type estimate for the twisted transfer operators of a class of two-dimensional partially hyperbolic endomorphisms of the torus, not necessarily skew-products. The twist satisfies a quantitative transversality condition on the cotangent dynamics of the associated three-dimensional extension which, in the skew-product case, is related to Tsujii's notions of transversality and partial captivity conditions. We use the main estimate to prove higher order expansions in the central and mixing local limit theorems for the two-dimensional base, including the case of several ergodic absolutely continuous invariant measures, and we prove exponential decay of correlations for the…

arxiv:2611.06340.title: A general L\^e--Siersma formula
arxiv:2611.06340.summary: We consider the comparison between a Milnor fibre of a function $f$ and its section by the zero locus of a second function $s$ in a general ambient variety $\mathcal{X}$. We give a formula that generalizes those of L\^e and Siersma, expressing the difference of their Euler characteristics as a sum of local contributions associated with the critical points of the restriction of $s$. We provide an algebraic formula in the case that $\mathcal{X}$ is {smooth of pure dimension outside $f^{-1}(0)$}, and show some applications and examples.
arxiv:2611.06340.authors: R. Gim\'enez Conejero, J. J. Nu\~no-Ballesteros

arxiv:2611.06357.title: On the (in)finiteness of fixed characters in genus $3$
arxiv:2611.06357.summary: We construct a counterexample to the Putman--Wieland conjecture in genus $3$ and discuss some of its consequences.

arxiv:2611.06362.title: Four-colour counterexamples for monochromatic path partitions
arxiv:2611.06362.summary: In 1989, Gy\'arf\'as conjectured that the vertex set of every $r$-edge-coloured complete graph can be partitioned into at most $r$ monochromatic paths. The case $r=2$ follows from a theorem of Gerencs\'er and Gy\'arf\'as, and Pokrovskiy proved the conjecture for $r=3$. Recently, Li and Wang disproved the conjecture for all sufficiently large $r$, leaving open the smallest number of colours for which it fails.

arxiv:2611.06366.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
arxiv:2611.06366.summary: We provide an algorithm for enumerating ordinary K3 surfaces over a fixed finite field based on Taelman's theorem. We use this algorithm to prove that there exist no K3 surfaces without rational points over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q\geq 13$. For elliptic K3 surfaces, we give a geometric proof of this non-existence without computer assistance.

arxiv:2611.06370.title: Intersection Product Formulas and Integral Dependence
arxiv:2611.06370.summary: We prove the intersection product formulas of Gaffney and Gassler for polar multiplicities and Segre numbers over arbitrary Noetherian local rings. For equidimensional and universally catenary rings, we give a geometric refinement of the Principle of Specialization of Integral Dependence, in which the maximal dimension of the images of exceptional components mapping into the hypersurface determines a precise Segre number that strictly increases.

arxiv:2611.06379.title: Exponential Deviations and H\"older Continuity for Moving-Law Mixed Cocycles
arxiv:2611.06379.summary: We study mixed random-quasiperiodic cocycles whose one-step laws evolve along an ergodic environment. Under mixed-base ergodicity, bounded logarithmic growth, and stationary-value uniqueness, which we characterize by relative quasi-irreducibility, we prove exponential quenched deviations for finite-time directional growth. A renewal example shows that, in general ergodic environments, annealed exponential deviations can fail despite quenched exponential concentration.
arxiv:2611.06379.authors: Zhongmin Liu, Dengdi Chen, Yan Zheng

arxiv:2611.06382.title: From hydrological laws to catchment models: A process-based model matches deep-learning accuracy on three continents
arxiv:2611.06382.summary: Dooge asked whether hydrology has laws at the catchment scale. We ask whether a low-dimensional system built under physical laws can match the accuracy of neural networks that outperform process-based models on the same inputs. Three laws constrain a lumped catchment model.

arxiv:2611.06388.title: Lyapunov spectrum, Harder--Narasimhan filtration and thin monodromy
